PREFACE TO THIS VOLUME.

HIS Fourth Volume of The Statutes of the Realm contains the Acts from the

Beginning of the Reign of King Edward VI. to the End of the Reign of King James I., A.D. 1547- to A.D. 1624., printed from the Inrollment on the Rolls of Parliament in Chancery, when the Acts are found entered thereon. In Default of such Inrollment, all Acts which are contained in any former Printed Collections of the Statutes are here printed from the Original Bills or Acts preserved in the Parliament Office. In Three Instances, where the Inrollments and the Originals are both deficient, Recourse has been had to the early Printed Collections; these are 18 Eliz. Chap. XXIII. the Subsidy of the Temporalty—23 Eliz. Chap. XVI. the Pardon —and 39 Eliz. Chap. XXVI. the Subsidy of the Clergy. In every Instance where any Act is not printed from the Inrollment in the Rolls of Parliament specified at the Commencement of each Year, a Note is annexed referring to the Source from whence it is printed. In one Year, 18 Jac. I., it has happened that the Deficiency arising from the Non-Inrollment of the Two Subsidy Acts could not be supplied by the Original Acts, nor by any Manuscript or Printed Copy, although very diligent Searches were made for the Purpose.

All such Acts as, during the Period above particularized, are found entered in any List of Public Acts at the Head of the Inrollment in Chancery, or as have been uniformly inserted or referred to, as such, in Sessional or other Printed Collections of Statutes, are printed in this Volume. In addition to these, some Acts have been now first printed from the Inrollment in Chancery, which seemed deserving of a Place in this Collection : These are distinguished by a smaller Type, in conformity with the Plan in former Volumes. They are only Seven in Number; viz. 1 Eliz. Chap. XXIII. for the Restoration of Queen Elizabeth in Blood, and declaring her inheritable to her Mother:—Chap. XXIV. for annexing certain Religious Houses to the Crown .—5 Eliz. Chap. XXXII. for defraying the Charges of the Royal Household :— 8 Eliz. Chap. XXI. and XXII. relative to the manufacturing Allum, Copperas, and Salt:— 23 Eliz. Chap. XVII. for abolishing the Tenure of Gavelkind, in Exeter:—and 27 Eliz. Chap. XXXI. for the Government of the City of Westminster.

The same Method has been pursued, in comparing the Inrollment in Chancery with the Original Acts in the Parliament Office, and with the Printed Copies, as was adopted in printing Vol. III. and which is fully explained in the Preface to that Volume.

It is hoped that the Marginal Notes in this Volume will not be found less satisfactory or complete than those in Vol. III. although prepared by only one of the Sub-Commissioners engaged in the Superintendance of that Volume.

This Volume is divided into Two Parts, on Account of its Size, in like Manner as Vol. I. of the New Edition of Rymer’s Fcbdera.

Two Engravings from the Inrolment in Chancery, one of the Act of 1 Eliz. Chap. III., and the other, of the Act 3 Jac. I. Chap. I. are inserted at Pages 358 and 1067 of this Volume.

London,

25 March 1819.

T. E. TOMLINS, Sub-Commissioner.

*•* This Mark ( • ) in the Column of the Chapters signifies that the Act has never been inserted in any former Printed Collection of the Statutes. Where the Page is not specified in the last Column of the Table, the Act is not printed in this Collection.

This Mark (t) before the Title of an Act signifies that, although mentioned in the List of Acts at the Head of the Inrolbnent in Chancery, the Act itself is not entered on the Roll.

Where the Title in Chancery is not specified, the Act is neither mentioned in such List nor inrolled on the Roll.

Where the Title in Parliament is not specified, the Act is missing, and not noticed in the Calendars there.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte against suche as shall unreverentlie speake against the Sacrament of the bodie and bloude of Christe comonlie called the Sacrament of the Altar, and for the receiving therof in bothe Kyndes.

THE Kings moste excellent Ma,ie mynding the govemaunce and order of his moste lovinge Subge&f to be in moste pfitt unitie and concorde in all things and in especiall in the trewe faithe and Religion of God, and wishing the same to be brought to passe w'h all elemeneye and mercye on his Highnes pte towardes them, as his moste pryncelie erenitie and Ma"' hathe allredy declared by evydent proofs, to thintent that his moste lovinge Subge&f provoked by elemeneye and goodnes of their Prynce and King shall studie rather for love then for feare to doo their dewties first to Allmightie God and then to his Highnes and the Comon wealthe, nourisshing concorde and love amonge them selfs ; Yet considerethe and pceiveth that in a multitude all be not on that sorte that reason and the knowledge of their dewties can move them from Offence, but many which had nede have some brydle of feare and that the same be men moste contentious and arrogant for the most pte or ells most blynde and ignorant, By the meanes of which sorte of men manny things well and godlie instituted and to the edificac&n of manny be pverted and abused and turned to their owne and others greate losse and Hynder*unce and sometyme to extreme destruction, the whiche dothe appeare in no thing more or soner then in matters of Religion and in the great and highe misteryes therof as in the moste comfortable Sacrament of the bodye and bloude of our Savyo' Jesu Christe comonlie called the Sacrament of the Altar and in Scripture the Supper and Table of the Lorde, the Comunion and ptaking of the bodie and bloude of Christe ; which Sacrament was instituted of no lesse auctho' then of o' Savio' both God and Man, when at his last Supper amongest his Apostles he did take the breade into his hollie handes and did saye Take youe and eate this is my bodye which is given and broken for youe, and taking upp the Chalice or cupp did give thanckf and saie This is my bloude of the newe Testament which is shede for youe and for manny for the remissyon of Synnes, that when so ever we shoulde do the same we shoulde do it in the remembr*unce of him and to declare and sett furthe his deathe and moste glorious passion [untill ] his cominge. Of the which breade who so ever eateth or of the which Cupp who so ever drynketh unworthelie eateth and drynketh condemnation and judgement to himself making no difference of the Lordes bodye ; The Instituc&n of w<t> Sacrament being ordeyned by Christe as is before saide and the saide wordes spoken of it here before rehearsed being of eternal infallible and undoubted trewthe, Yet the saide Sacrament all this notwithstanding hath ben of late mervelouslie abused by such manner of men before rehearsed, who of wickydnes or ells of ignoraunce and want of Learninge for certaine abuses heretofore edmitted of some in misusing therof have condempned in their harts and speche the whole thing and coiitemptuouslie depraved dispised or reviled the same most holly and blessed Sacrament, and not onlie disputed and reasoned unreverentlie and ungodlie of that most high misterye But also in their sermons preachingf readingf lectures comunicacons argumentf talkes ryines songs playes or gestf name or call it by such Vile and unsemely wordes as Christian eares do abhorre to heare rehersed : For reformac&n wherof Be it enacted by the Kings Highnes with thassent of the Lordes sjSuall and Temporall and of the Comens in this p*nt pliament assembled and by thaudoritie of the same, that what so ever psone or psons from and after the first daye of Maye nexte cominge shall deprave dispise or contempne the saide moste blessed Sacrament in contempte therof by any contemptuouse wordes or by anny wordes of depravinge dispisinge or reviling, or what psone or psons shall advisedlie in anny other wise contempne dispise or revile the saide moste blessed Sacrament contrarie to theffedf and declaration abovesaide ; That then he or theie shall suffer imprisonement of his or their bodies and make fyne and rannsome at the Kings will and pleasure.

And For full and effectuall execuc&n of the premises before devised ordeyned and enacted by this Atte, Be it furthermore enacted by thau&oritie of this p>nt pliament. That Iinediatlye after the first daie of Maie next cominge the Justices of Peaxe or three of them at the least wherof one of them to be of the Quop in everie Shiere of this Realme and Wales and all other Places within the Kings Dominions, shall have full power and auftoritie by vertue of this Act as well to take Informacbn and accusac&n by the othes and depositions of twoo liable honnest and lefull parsones at the least, and after such accusaf&n or Informac&n so had to enquire by the othes of xij men in everie of their foure Quarter Sessyons yerelie to be holden, of all and singuler such accusac&ns or Informac&ns to be had or made of anny of the Offences aboveseid to be comitted or doon after the saide first daie of Maye within the Lymittf of their Commission; and that upon everie such accusac&n or Informac&n, the Offendor and Offendo" shall be enquired of and Indited before the said Justices of Peaxe or three of them at the least as is aforesaid of the saide contemptf and Offences by the verditt of xij honnest and indifferent men yf the matter of the saide accusac&n and Information shall seme to the saide Jurie good and trewe.

And it is also further enacted by thaudoritie aforesaide that the saide Justices of Peace or three of them at the least as is aforesaide before whome any such presentment Information and accusac&n shalbe made or taken as is aforesaide shall examyne the accuso" what other witnes were by and present at the tyme of doing and comitting of thoffence wherof the Informac&n accusac&n and presentment shalbe made and how manny others then the accuso" have Knowledge therof, and shall have [full * ] power and authoritie by their discretions to bynde by Recognis'unce to be taken afore them aswell the saide accuso" as all suche other parsons whom the saide accuso" shall declare to have Knowledge of the Offences by them presented and Informed, everye of them in five pounds to the King to appere before the saide Justices of Peace afore whom the Offendo' or Offendo" shall be tryed at the daye of the Tryall and deliver*unce of suche Offendo".

And it is further enacted by thauftoritie aforesaide that the saide Justices of peaxe or three of them at the least as is aforesaide by vertewe of this Acte shall have full power and au&horitie to make processe against everie parsone and parsons so indicted by twoo Capias and an Exigent and by Capias utlagat aswell within the lymittf of their Comissyon as into all other Shieres and places of this Realme Wales and other the Kings Dominions aswell within the Liberties as withowt, and the same pc esse to be good and effectuall in the lawe to all intentf constructions and purposes; and uppon the apparaunce of any of thoffendo" shall have full power and au&oritie by vertewe of this Ade and the Comission of peaxe to determine the contemptf and offences aforesaide accordinge to the lawes of this Realme and theffedf of this Acte: And that the saide Justices of Peaxe or three of them at the least as is abovesaide shall have full power and au&oritie to lett anny suche psone or parsons so indicted uppon sufficient sureties by their discretions to baill for their appar*unce to be tryed according to the tenor so'me and effede of this Ade.

Provided alluaies and be it enacted that the saide Justices of Peaxe or three of them at the least, at their Quarter Sessions where any offendo' or offendo" shalbe or stande indicted of anny of the contemptf or offences abovesaide, shall direde and award one writt in the Kings name to the Bisshopp of the Diocesse where the saide offence or offences be supposed to be comilted or doon, willing and requiring the saide Bisshopp to be in his owne parsone or by his Ch*uncelor or other his sufficient deputic learned at the Q'ter Sessions in the saide Countie to be holden, when and where the saide offendo' shalbe arraigned and tryed, appointing to them in the saide writt the daye and place of the saide arraignement, which Writt shalbe of this so'me:—Rex &c. Epo L. saltm Precipimus tibi qd tu Cancellar tuus vel alius deputatus tuus sufficient eruditus sitis cum Justiciar nris ad pacem in Coiii nfo B. confvand assignat apud D. tali die ad sessionem nram ad tunc et ibidem tenend ad dand consiliu et advisament eisdem Justiciar nns ad pacem super nrranament et deliberacSem offendenC contra formam statuti concernen sacrosanctum Sacramentum Altaris.

Provided allwaies and be it enacted by thauCloritie aforesaide that no parsone or psons shalbe indicted of anny the contemptf or offences abovesaide but onelie [of suche contemptf or offences as shalbe doon or ppetrated 1 ] within three monethes next after the saide offence or offences so comitted or doon.

And be it further enacted by thaudoritie abovesaide that in all tryallf for anny suche offendo" before the saide Justices as is aforesaide the psone or psons being compleyned on and arrayned shalbe admitted to pourge or trye his or their innocencye, by as manny or more witnesses in nombre and of as good honnestie and credence as the witnesses be which deposed against him or them or anny of them.

And forasmuche as it is more agreable bothe to the first Institucftn of the saide Sacrament of the moste precious bodye and bloude of o' Savyo' Jesus Christe, and also more conformable to the comen use and pradise bothe of Thapostles and of the p'mative Churche by the space of Five hundred yeres and more after Christs assention that the saide blessed Sacrament shoulde be ministred to all Christen people under bothe the kyndes of Breade and Wyne, [then' ] under the so'me of breade onelie; And also it is more agreable to the first Institution of Christe and to thusage of Thapostellf and the primative churche that the people being pnt shoulde receive the same w"’ the preist [then*] that the Priest should receive it alone; Therfore be it enacted by our saide Souvarigne Lorde the King with the consent of the Lordes spuall and teinporall and the Comons in this pnt plament assembled and by thaudoritie of the same, that the saide moste blessed sacrament be hereafter comenlie delivered and ministred unto the people, within this Churche of Englande and Irelande and other the Kings Dominions, under bothe the Kyndes, that is to saie of breade and wyne, excepte necessitie otherwise require: And allso that the preist which shall ministre the same shall at the least one day before exhorte all psons which shalbe present likewise to resorte and prepare themselff to receive the same, and when the daie prefixed comethe after a godlie exhortacftn by the Minister made, wherin shalbe further expressed the benefitt and comforte promised to them which worthelie receive the saide hollie Sacrament, and daunger and indignation of God threatened to them wrh shall presume to receive the same unworthclie, to thende that everie man maye trye and examyii lus owne conscience before he shall receive the same, the saide minister shall not withowt laufull cawse denye the same to any parsone that wool devoutelie and humblie desire it, anny lawe statute orden’nce or custoine contrarie therunto in any wise notwithstanding; not condempninge hereby the usage of anny Churche owt of the Kings Ma"-* Dominions.

CHAPTER VL An Acte for the contynuance of making of Woosted Yame in Norff.

Occasional Necessity of severe Laws

NO thinge being more godlie more sure more to be wisshed and desired betwixte a Prynce the Supreame Hed and Ruler and the Subgectf whose Gouverno' and Hed he is, then on the Prynces pte great clemencye and indulgencye, and rather to muche forgivenes and remission of his royall power and just punishment, then exacte severitie and justice to be shewed, and on the Subjects behalfe that theye shoulde obeye rather for love and for the necessitie and love of a Kinge and Prynce, then for feare of his streight and severe Lawes; CHAPTER XV.

An Act for a General Pardon.

THE Kings moste Royall Ma'\ right well pceiving his loving Subgectf by many and sondrie wayes and meanes to have borne and susteyned the greate adventures charges and busynes of wanes and defences of this Realme, aswell in the tyme of his moste dere father King Henry theight as in his tyme and Reigne, intending of his clemencye and pitye to gratefie his saide Subgectf with his gracyous free and liberall pdone according to his Kingly power, trusting assuredlie that his saide Subgectf will contynue his loving and assured obedyent Subgectf, and hereafter in suche sorte obeye his Highnes Lawes and Statates as to them and everye of them of right apptaynethe, is fullie and resolutelie contented and pleased that it be enacted by aucthoritie of this pnt plament in manner and forme following, That is to saye; that all and everye of his saide Subgectf, aswell spuall as temporall, of this (1 ) Realme of Englande Wales the Isles of Jemesey and Gameseye Barwycke Callyce Guisnes HammeS Bolleyn and Bollonoys and the marches of the same, the Heires successo" executo" and administrato" of them and everye of them, and all and singuler bodyes in anny manner of wise Corporate, Cities Boroughes Shires Ryddingf Hundredes Lathes Rapes Wapentakes Townes Villages and Tythingf and everye of them, and the successo' and successo" of everye of them, shalbe by thauctoritie of this pnt plament acquited pdoned released and discharged, against the Kings Highnes his heires successo" and execute" and everye of them, of all manner of Treasons heresyes fellonies robberyes offencf contemptf trespasses wronges deceiptf misdemeano", forfaictures penaltyes and proffittf somes of moneye paynes of deathe paynes corporall and pecunyarie, and all other things cawses quarrellf suites judgementf and executions, whiche maye be or can be by his Highnes in anny wise or by anny meane pdoned, before and unto the XXVth daye of Decembre in the yere of o' Lorde God a thousande five hundred fburtie and seven ; other then suche as hereafter in this Acte be excepted or forprised, in suche manner and so'me and unto suche tymes as theye be excepted or forprised in this Acte, and other then suche as the Clawses of proviso hereafter mentyoned dothe extende unto.

And allso the Kings Highnes is further contented and pleased that it be enacted by aucthoritie of this pnt plament, that this his saide free pdone shalbe as good and effectuall in the Lawe, to everye of his saide Subgectf bodies corporate and other before rehersed and to everye of them, by the saide generall Wordes before rehersed, in all things which be not hereafter in this pnt Acte excepted or forprised, as the same pdone shoulde have byn yf all Offences contemptf forfaictures cawses matters suits quarrellf judgementf executions penaltyes, and all other things not hereafter excepted nor conteyned in anny clawse of proviso hereafter mentioned, had byn pticulerlie singulerlie speciallye and playnelye named rehersed and specified, and allso pdoned by propre and expresse wordes and names in their Kyndes natures and qualities, by wordes and tearmes therunto requisite to have byn putt in and expressed in this pnt Acte of free pdone: And that his saide Subgectf nor anny of them, nor the Heires executo" or administrato" of anny of them, nor anny of the saide bodies corporate nor anny other parsons bodies politique or corporate before named or anny of them, be nor shall be sued vexed or inquieted in their bodies goods landes or cattallf for anny manner matter cawse contempte misdemeano' forfaicture trespasse offence, or anny other thing suffred done or comitted against his Highnes his Crowne dignitie prerogative lawe or statutes, but onelye for suche matters cawses and offences as be rehersed in the exceptions and clawses of proviso in this pnt Acte hereafter mentioned, in suche manner and so'me as in the same exceptions and clawses of proviso be mentyoned, and for none other : Anny Statute or Statutes Lawes Customes Uses or psident heretofore had made or used to the contrarye in anny wise notwithstanding.

Allso the Kings Highnes, of his bounteous Liberalitye by aucthoritye of this pnt plament gr’untethe and frelye givethe to everye of his saide Subgectf, and to everye of the saide bodies corporate and other before rehersed and to everye of them, all suche Goods cattallf debtes fynes issues proffittf amercyamentf forfaictures and somes of moneye by anny of them forfaicted, w'h to his Highnes do or shoulde belonge or appertayne, by reasone of anny offence contempte trespasse misdemeano' matter cawse or quarrell suffred doon or comitted by them or anny of them, which be not hereafter forprised or excepted in this present Acte; And that all and everye the Kings saide Subgectf, and all and singuler bodyes corporate and other before rehersed, maye by him or them self or by his or their deputie or deputies or by his or their atto'neye or atto'neys, accordinge to the Lawes of this Realme, pleade and minister this pnt Acte of free pardone for his or their dischardge of and for everye thing that is by vertewe of this pnt Acte pdoned discharged given or gr*unted, without anny fee or other thing in anny wise paying to anny parsone or psons for writing or eatreye of the Judgement or other cawse conceminge suche plea writing or entreye, but onelye twelve pence to be paide to the Officer or Clerck that shall entre the plea matter or Judgement for the dischardge of anny the ptie so pleading the same; Anny statute or use to the contrarye in anny wise notwithstanding.

CHAPTER L

An Acte for the Unyformytie of Service and Admynistrac&n of the Sacramentf throughout the Realme.*

WHERE of longe tyme there hathe bene hadd, in this Realme of Englande and in Wales, div’se formes of c5en prayer comonlie called the 9vice of the Churche, that is to saye, the use of Sap, of Yorke, of Bangor and of Lyncolne; And besides the same nowe of late muche more divW and sondrie fourmes & facions have bene used in the Cathedrall and parishe Churches of Englande and Wales, aswell concemynge the Martens or mornynge prayer and the Evensong, as also concerninge the Hollie Comunyon comonlie called the Masse, withe div^se and sondre rytes and ceremonyes concerninge the same, and in the admynistrac&n of other Sacramentf of the Churche; And as the doers and executors of the saide rytes and ceremonyes, in other fourme then of late Yeres they have bene used, were pleased therwithe, so other not usinge the same rytes and ceremonyes were therby greatlie offended; And albeit the Kings Majestie, withe thadvise of his moste entirely beloved Uncle the Lorde Protector and other of his Highnes Counsell, hathe heretofore d$se tymes assayed to staye Innovations or newe rites concerninge the premisses, yet the same hathe not hadd suche good successe as his Highnes required in that behalfe; whereupon his Highnes by the most prudent advise aforesaide, beinge pleased to beare withe the frayltie and weknes of his Subjectes in that behalfe, of his greate clemencye hath not bene onelie content to abstayne from punyshment of those that have offended in that behalf, for that his Highnes taketh that they did it of a good zeale, but also to the intent a unyforme quyett and godlie order shoulde be had concerninge the jPmisses, hath appoynted Tharchebisshopp of Canterburie, and certayne of the most learned and discrete Bisshopps and other learned men of this Realme, to consider and ponder the phnisses, and thereupon havinge aswell eye and respecte to the moste syncere and pure Christian Religion taught by the Scripture, as to the usagf in the Primatyve Churche, shoulde drawe and make one convenient and mete order ryte and facyon of comen and open Praier and admynistrac&n of the Sacramentf, to be had and used in his Majesties Realme of Englande and in Wales; the whiche at this tyme, by the ayde of the Holie Ghooste, with one uniforme agrement is of them concluded set for the and delived to his Highnes, to his greate comforte and quietnes of mynde, in a booke entituled The booke of the Comon Prayer and admynistrac&n of the Sacramentf and other rightes and ceremonyes of the Churche after th? Use of the Churche of Englande: Wherefore the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent Parliament assembled, consideringe aswell the moste godlye travell of the Kinges Highnes of the Lorde Protector and other of his Highnes Counsell, in gatheringe & collectinge the saide Archebishopp Bisshoppes and learned men togither, as the godlie prayers orders rites and ceremonyes in the saide booke mencioned, and the considerac&ns of alteringe those thinges whiche be altered, and reteyninge those thinges which be reteyned in the saide booke, but allso the honor of God and greate quietnes, wch by the grace of God shall ensue upon the one and uniforme ryte and order in suche comon Prayer and rytes and extern ceremonies, to be used throughout England and in Wales at Callice and the Marches of the same, doe give to his Highnes most hartie and lowly thanckes for the same, and humbly prayen that it maye be ordeyned and enacted by his Majestie withe the assent of the Lordes and Comons in this pnt parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same, that all and singuler pson and psons that have offended concerninge the pmisses, other then suche pson and psons as nowe be and remayne in Warde in the Towre of London or in the Flete, maye be pardoned therof: and that all and singuler Ministers in any Cathedrall or Parishe Churche, or other place within this Realme of Englande Wales Calyce and Marches of the same or other the Kinges l>nions, shall from and after the feast of Pentecoste next comynge be bounden to saye and use the Matens Evensonge Celebrac&n of the Lordes Supper cdmonlye called the Masse and adminystrac&n of eche of the Sacramentf, and all their coen and open Prayer, in suche order and fourme as ys mencioned in the saide booke and none other or otherwise.

CHAPTER II.

An Acte towchynge the true Service required in Captaynes and Souldiors.

WHERE before this tyme diPse of the Kinges Majesties lovinge and obedient Subjects, accordinge to their bounden dutyes, have assigned appoynted and sent for the, aswell into the parts beyonde the Seas and to the Seas as also into Scotlande and other places diPse bothe within this Realme and without this Realme, many able psons or Souldiors well furnished with good Horses and hameses mete to serve the Kinge in Warres, to their great charges and costs, yet some of the saide Souldiors see sente [doe *] serve contrarie to their saide Maisters expectation & contrarie to their bounden duties to the Kings Highnes have soldc loste exchaunged or altered their Maisters horse and hames, or otherwise by deceipte or covyne converted the same; by meanc wherof the Kinges Highnes hathe not onelie bene destitute of the same Souldiors in tyme of nede, but also the owners of the saide horses and hames who sent them thither have bene untrulye deceyved of their horses or hameses, being therby lesse able to refurnishe other the like Souldiers withe horse and hameses at suche tyme as they shalbe therunto [comaundinges ] by the Kinges Highnes; and sometyme the Captaynes of suche Souldiers depted have demaunded had and taken of the Kinges Highnes Wages for the same Souldiors soe depted, by n.eane whereof the Kings Majestie hathe susteyned and borne great paymentf and yet his Majestie hathe not bene trulie served for the same; not little to the displeasure of the Kinge and to the great charge of the poore Subjects beinge comaunded to sett for the suche Souldiors: For remedye whereof be it enacted by the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde withe the assent of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this plsent Parliament assembled & thauctoritie of the same, that yf any Souldior hereafter servinge the Kinge in his Warres in any his Dnions, or on the Seas or beyonde the Seas or in Scotlande, after the firste daye of Aprill next comynge, doe sell give awaie or wilifullic purloyne or otherwise exchaunge alter or putt awaye anye horse geldinge or Mare or any Hames wherewithe he shalbe sett for the, That then everie suche Souldier soe offendinge, upon due proofe or testymonye to be taken, before the lyveten'nte highe Admyrall the Kinges Deputic Vice Admyrall Wardeyn or Captayne, and in their absence before anye of their deputyes, shalbe emprisoned, by the same lieveten'nte or any other before named, there to remayne without bayle or maynprise untill he have satisfied to the partie owner of the horse geldinge mare or hames so by him soulde purloyned exchaunged wilfully lost altered or otherwise made awaye: And if suche Souldior soe offendinge fortune to escape from the lyveten'nte and other the foresaide psons without the punyshment [or* ] resticucon aforesaide, That then the same Souldior upon complaynt made by the partie greived, or his executors or admynistrators, upon due proofe thereof to be made to anye Justice or Justicf of Peace in the parts where suche Souldior soe offendinge shalbe founde, shalbe by suche Justice or Justicf comytted to Warde there to remayne without bayle or maynprise untill he have satisfied the Partie grieved his executors or admynistrators, of and for suche horses gelding f or mares and hames so by anye suche Souldior wilfullye loste exchanged altered or otherwise purloyned.

And be it also further enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, that yf anye Souldior servinge as is aforesaid, departe without licence of the lyveten*nte, or anye of the others above named, withe botye or otherwise, beinge in the Enemyes countrie or els where in the Kings Service, or out of any garrison where he or they shalbe appoynted to serve, that then everie suche Souldior soe departinge without licence to be taken and judged as a fellon, and to be executed as in cases of fellonye without havinge any advauntage of his Clergie or Seinctuarye: And that the Justicf of everie Shire where anye suche Souldyor shalbe taken, shall have full power to enquier heare and determyne all and everie the saide offences concemynge everie suche departure as they doe and maye in other cases of fellonye cornytted in the Shire where suche Souldior shalbe taken.

And be it also further enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide. That yf any Comyssioner or Captayne, to whom the Kinge shall directe his comaundement by comyssion or Ires for the levyinge or settinge fourthe of any man to serve the King in his Warres, shall at any tyme after the saide firste daye of Aprill, for any gaine rewarde or other lucre, discharge anye pson or psons by him appoynted to serve the King as a Captayne Souldior or Pyanor, of his Service soe appoynted, and doe assigne any other pson or psons in his or their Stede, for anye lucre or gayne as is aforesaide, that then everie Comyssioner or other pson so offendinge shall forfeyte to the Kinge for everie suche defaulte of everie Man so discharged twentie pounde to be levyed of his goods & catallf.

And be it also enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, that yf any Captayne being appointed to have the ordre of any nombre of Souldiours under anye other higher Officer, doe for anye cause licence any Souldior in his retynewe to departe from the feilde or fortresse where they shalbe appoynted to serve, without the especiall assent and licence in writinge of the lyvetenaunte or the others before named, shall forfeytt and loose for everie suche Souldior so by him licensed to departe twentie powndes to be levyed as is aforesaide to the use of the Kinge.

And be it further enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, That everie lyveten*nte and other before named upon the payne of tenne pounde, shall cause to be pclaymed the hole effecte and contents of this Acte, that is to saye; everie lyveten*nte of any Armye in everie Feild under his charge to pclayme this Acte everie monethe, and that everie of the Kinges Deputyes of everie Fortresse and Captayne of anye other Fortresse to pclayme this Acte within his Chardge ones e$ye quarter of a Yere.

And also be it enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, for the better execuf&n of the pmisses, that everie psone or psones givinge to the lyveten*nte or the others above named true information of anye of the Offences above remembred , shall have for his labour one monethes wags of him that shalbe founde faultie, to be payde by thande of the Treasourer upon Warraunte of the saide lyveten’nte or any of the others aforesaide.

Provided always that nothinge herein conteyned shall in anye wise extende to towche or infringe anye orders established for the govemement of Callyce and the Marches of the same, or any other place of the Kinges nowe governed or hereafter to be governed by the same orders, or by suche orders as maye please his Grace hereafter to sen furthe for the same.

Provided alwaye that this Acte nor nothinge therin conteyned shall extende to chardge anye pson or psones for the takinge or receyvinge of anye guyfte or rewarde of anye (') his or their ten*ntes or frcindes towardes the relief ayde or helpe of the same psons, beinge comaunded by the Kinges Majestie to serve in Warres, or otherwise to fynde men on horseback or on foote as well within this Realme as without; nor for the guyfte rewarde ayde or helpe reserved or covenanted to be payde or given to any pson appoynted to serve in Warres or to fynde horse or men to serve by reason of any graunte coven*nte reservac&n custome or tenure.

CHAPTER m.

An Acte towchinge Purveyors.

THE Kinges moste excellent Majestie ys pleased and contentyd by thadvise of his honorable Counsell, at the humble peticon suyte and complaynte of his lovinge and obedient Subjects, that it be inacted by his Highnes withe consent of the Lordes and Comons in this psent parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same. That from and after the feast of Sainte John the Baptiste whiche shalbe in the yere of our Lorde God one thousande fyve hundred fortye nyne, untill the saide Feast of Sainte John the Baptist whiche shalbe in the yere our Lorde God one thousande five hundred fyftye two, noe purveyor or taker or anye other pson or psons by aucthoritie of anye Comyssion or Comyssions or other Writinge or Writings heretofore graunted or made, or hereafter to be graunted or made by the Kings Majesde, or by any other warrant letter or aucthoritie whatsoever, shall purvey or take for the pvysion of the Kings Majesties moste honorable housholde or for the pvision of the householdes of the Kings Majesties Sisters or any other pson or psons, anye corne grayne make meale calves lambes kyddes hennes chekyns capons wyldfowle butter cheese eggs beyff muttons fyshe tymber woode cole strawe haye or anye other kynde of vyttales, without the full assent and consent of the Owner or Owners of the same, and at suche price and prices for redy money, or money to be payde at suche dayes and places as suche purveyors taker or other pson or psons can and shall agree with the Owner or Owners of the same.

And be it further enacted by thauctoritie of this psent parliament, that from and after the feast of Christemas whiche shalbe in the yere of our Lorde God one thousande fyve hundred forty nyne, untill the feast of Christemas whiche shalbe in the yere of our Lorde God One thousande fyve hundred fyftye twoe, noe purveyor or any other pson or psons by aucthoritie of any Comyssion or Cdmyssions or other Writinge or Writings heretofore graunted or made or hereafter to be made or graunted by the Kings Majestie or by any other warrant tre or aucthoritie whatsoever, shall purveye or take for anye of the Kinges Majesties affayres, or for any other cause or matter concerninge the Warres or otherwise, any goods cattellf trees tymber or other thinges whatsoever, savinge onelye Barges Shippes and other Vessells Carts Carriagf and thinges necessarie for carriage, without thassentf and full agreamentf of the Owner or Owners of the same, and at suche price or prices for redye money or money to be payde at suche dayes and placf as anye suche purveyor taker or other pson or psons can or shall agree withe the Owner or Owners of the same : Anti yf anye purveyor or taker or anye other p6on or psons shall after anye of the saide Feastf of Sainte John Baptist and Christmas next comynge, peure or attempte to take or purvey for the Kings Majestie or for any other pson or psons, any vyttaylls or other things whatsoever contrarie to the true meanynge of this Acte, that then suche taker purveyor or anye other suche peon or psons so offending, shall forfeyte to the partie or parties greived treble the Value or Values of the thinge or thinges soe taken or purveyed, and shall also suffer enprisonement by the Space of one quarter of a yere without Bayle or Mayneprise, and shall make fyne at the Kings will and pleasure; CHAPTER IV.

An Acte for Shiriefff to have certayne Allowaunces upon their Accomptes.

MOSTE humblye besechen the Kinges most excellent Majestie his true and faithefull subjects the Comons in this psent Parliament assembled, that where in the Parliament begonne at Westni the sixtenth daye of Januarye in the xxxiij"' yere of the raigne of our late Soveraigne Lorde of famouse memorie King Henrie theight, and by progacon holden at Westm the xxij"1 daye of Januarye in the xxxiiij,h yere of the raigne of our saide late Soveraigne Lorde, and there contynued untill the twelveth daye of Maye in the fyve and thirtieth yere of the raigne of the saide late Kinge, upon d$se and sondrie considerations there was enacted and made one acte by thauctoritie of the same Parliament conceminge the accompte or accomptf of Shreves to be made in the Eschequyer, as in the same acte more playnelye at large it is conteyned : And albeit yt was ment at the tyme of the makinge of the saide acte as it maye appeare by the wordes of the saide acte, that Sherives should not be charged uppon their accomptf but onelye withe suche somes of money as they might laufullie levye -, And also that the saide Sherives shoulde have allowance not all onelye for suche charges and expences as they shoulde susteyne and beare for the dyettf and charges of the Justices of Assise, but also for other necessarie charges and expences by them susteyned in and aboute thexcisinge of their saide office; Yet nevertheles the saide Sherifff are and have been sithen the makinge of the saide acte more and sorer charged vexed and troubled then they weare before, to the great ympoverishement of men of worshippe and Gentilmen within this Realme that have been Sherives, and so it is verie like to be to all suche as hereafter shalbe Sherives yf remedye be not pvided in this behalfe: It maye therefore please the Kinges moste excellent Majestie that it maye be enacted and established withe thassent of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent Parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same, That the saide former acte and all clauses and sentenses in the same conteyned shalbe from henceforthe clerelye frustrate and voyde to all intentf & purposes, other then hereafter in this acte shalbe specified.

And that it maye be enacted by this psent Parliament, that the Sherives whiche shalbe made from henceforthe within all the Shires of Englande, and also suche as have not made and fynished their accompte or accomptf, shall have suche and lyke tayles of rewarde and all suche other allowauncf as they had before the makinge of the saide former acte, or ells the same Sherives whiche shalbe or heretofore have bene, to be at their eleccon and choyce to accompte and all other things to doe accordinge to the aforesaide former acte: And that they and everie of them that soe shall accompte and take noe tayle of rewarde shalbe in and by all thinges intreated in the Kinges Eschequier as thoughe the saide former Acte were and shoulde contynue in his full strengh & effecte, any thinge before spified notwithstandinge : And that the same Tayles of Rewarde and e9y of them, by force of this psent acte without anye further warraunte or warrauntf to be obteyned for the same, shalbe levyed or striken at the receipt of the Kinges Majesties Eschequier in due manner and forme withe suche lyke Ires or writings upon the same tayles and everie of them as before the makinge of the sayde former acte were and have bene accustomed to be levyed and stryken, and that the same tayles soe hereafter there to be levyed and striken, shalbe delyv’ed unto ePye of the same Sheriffes or their suffyeient attorney for them without prest or other chardge to be sett upon them for the same ; and that this acte shalbee a suffyeient warraunte and discharge unto the Treasorer of Englande and all other offyeers within the saide receipte for strikinge levyinge and delyverie of the saide tayles and everie of them.

CHAPTER XI.

An Acte for the true Tannyngc of Leather.

WHEARE before tyme divers good estatutes have bene made for the true fannynge of Leather, wherein Drceieful Practice* consisteth a greate comon wealth and comoditie to all men, for that everie sorte of people of necessitie must oTlIithnto^"ng use and have Lether for divers and sondrie purposes; for lacke of true tannynge whereof evy man y» not onlye putt

to great losse and charges, but also by the naughtynes thereof dothe take div’se and sondrie diseases to the shortenynge of thire lyves; And yet notwithstandinge the saide good estarutf in that case pvyded yt is manyfeste to all psons that ther was never worse Lether used or made within this Realme then hathe latelye bene and nowe ys used and made within the same, the chief cause whereof cometh by reason of the evill and deceiptfull tannynge of the same Lether, for albcyt the currier and also the Shomaker or other Artificer doe his or their diligence never so well yet nothinge made therwith can be good pfecte or pfytable as yt ought or shoulde be, the Lether not beinge well and sufficientlye tanned, thocca&m of the naughtie tannynge wherof groweth moche by the gredynes of the gayne of the Tanner, for that they covet to sett for the the same to sale withe more spede and shorter tyme that it can be well & pfytlye tanned and have his due tyme requisite and necessarie for the true tannynge of the same ; For whereas in tymes past the Hydes or Lether were wonte to lye in the tanne fattf by the space of one yere or fyve quarters of the yere, before it was taken out of the same fattf or put to sale, nowe for the spedye utterance and tannynge heros they have invented div’se and sondrie deceiptfull and craftie meanes to have the same Lether tanned, some tyme in thre wekes and sometyme in one monethe or sixe wekes at the moste, as by crafte of over lymynge therof in their lyme pittf, or otherwise by layinge thereof in their fattf sett in their olde tanne hills, where it shall be tanned withe the hotte ozys takinge unkynde heat in the same hill, and sometyme by puttinge of sethinge whotte lycre with their ozes into their tanne fattf where the same Hydes or Lether lye, whiche they most comonlye doe practyse in the night tyme, and by diPse and manye other suche craftye and subtyll meanes, wherby they make the Lether to seeme, to them that have not the knowledge or skill thereof, to be aswell and sufficiently tanned within the space of thre weeks or a monethe or sixe weeks at the most as yf it had beene in the fattf untill it had had the full tyme requysite for the true tannynge of the same, whiche shoulde have bene at the leaste by the space of thre quarters of a yere: For remedy whereof, and to thintente that Lether maye hereafter be sufficiendye and trulye tanned and have his full kynde and pfeccon as ys requisyte for the same, Be it enacted by the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde withe thassent of the Lordes and Comons in this p>sent parliament All exiting Act* assembled and by thauctoritie of the same, that all Acts heretofore made conceminge the true tannynge of Lether ^'*nning

not beinge yet repealed, shall stande in their full strengthe and force and be putt in due execution.

And be it further enacted by thauctoritye aforesaide, that yf anye pson doe subtracte or withdrawe any manner of tithes obvenc&ns pfyttf comodoties or other dutyes before mencioned or any parte of them, contrarie to the true meaninge of this Acte or of any other Acte heretofore made, that then the partie so subtractinge or withdrawinge the same, raaye or shalbe convented and sued in the Kings ecctiasticall Corte by the partie from whom the same shalbe substracted or withdrawal, to thintent the Kinges Judge ecctiasticall shall and maye then and there heare and determyne the same accordinge to the Kings ecctiasticall lawes: And that yt shall not be laufull unto the parsone vicar pprietorie owner or other their fermors or deputyes, contrarie to this Acte to convent or sue suche witholder of tithes obvencons or other duetyes aforesaide before any other Judge then ecctiasticall: And yf anye Archebisshopp Bisshoppe Chauncelor or other Judge ecctiasticall gyve anye sentence in the foresaide causes of Tithes obvencbns pfittf emolumentf and other dutyes aforesaide or in anye of them, and noe appeale ne phibic&n hanginge the partie condempned doe not obey the saide sentence, that then it shalbe lefull to epye suche Judge ecctiasticall to excomunycate the saide partie so as afore condempned and dysobeyinge, in the which sentence of excoicac&n, yf the sayde partie excoicate willfullye stande and endure still excoicate by the space of fourtie dayes nexte after, upon denunciation and publication thereof in the parishe Churche of the place or parishe where the partie soe excoicate is dwellinge or most abydinge, the saide Judge ecctiasticall maye then at his pleasure signifye to the Kinge into his Corte of Chauncerie of the estate and condition of the saide partie so excoicate, and thereuppon to require pcesse De excoicato capiend to be awarded agaynste everie suche pson as hathe bene so excoicate.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte againste the shootinge of Hayle shott.

WHEREAS an Acte was made in the [xxiij,h'] yere of the late Kinge of famous memorie Henrie the Eighte for some libertye to shoote in Handegonnes hakes and hacquebuytf, by whiche Acte nevertheles it was pvided that noe psone shoulde shote in anye of the abovesaide peecf but at a banke of earthe, and not to any deare or fowle, unlesse the partie might dispende one hundreth poundes by the yere: Forasmuche as the saide Acte havinge byne devised as it was then thought for necessarie excise tending to the defence of the Realme, ys growen sythen to the maynten*nce of muche ydlenes and to suche a libertye as not onelye dwellinge houses dovecotf and Churches are daylye damaged by the abuse thereof by men of light conversation, but that also there ys growen a customable manner of shotinge of hayleshott, wherby an infynite sorte of fowle ys killed and muche Game therby destroyed to the benefytt of no man, wherby also the meaninge of the saide Statute ys defrauded, for that the saide use of hayleshott utterly destroyeth the [the ’3 certentye of shotinge, whiche in Warres is much requisite ; Be it therfore enacted, that noe pson under the degree of a Lorde of the Parliament shall from hensforthe shote in anye handegonne within anye Cittie or Towne at any fowle or other marke, upon any Churche house or dovecote; neither that any pson shall shote in anye place any hayleshott or any moe Pellottf then one at one tyme, upon payne to forfayte for everie tyme that he or they shall soe offende cont*rye to this Acte, tenne poundes and emprisonement of his bodye duringe thre monethes.

Provided alwayes and be it enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide that this Acte nor anye thinge therein conteyned shall extende or be pjudicyall to any pson or psons auctorized by value of lande to shote in any handegonne or crosbowe, but that they maye so doe in suche fourme and order as they sholde do and myght have done before the makinge of this Acte (hayleshott excepted as in deede that kynde of shott in the saide Acte was not ment); And that all and everie other pson or p6ons auctorized to shote, or otherwise yf he inhabite in any Towne corporate to be psented to the Maior or other officer of the same, and inhabitinge in the Countrie be psented within one moneth after the publishinge of this Acte to the next Justice of Peace adjoyninge; in whiche cases the saide Maior Justice or other officer so takinge their names as is aforesaide, shall againe psent and recorde the same before Justice of the Peace at the next Quarter Sessions, to the intent the Clerke of the Peace of the Countye maye kepe a certeyne booke or rooll of the names of all suche psons, by the whiche the Kings Majestie maye from tyme to tyme be asserteyned howe manye mete and liable men excised in that feate be in e9ye Countye, that the same may be employed in his Gracf §vyce as nede and occacon shall requyre; upon payne that ePye pson offendinge in this Acte in psumynge to shote in any handegonne or halfe hake without the psentinge of his name as ys aforesaide, shall forfeytt for everie shott the some of twentye shillingf, thone moytie whereof to be to our Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge, and the other moytie to him or them that will sue for the same, by bill action playnte information or otherwise; the officer that shoulde take their names and psent the same as ys abovesaide, to incurre for the lacke of his dutye in this parte for everie tyme so offendinge lyke payne.

CHAPTER XVII. (•)

An Act for the confirmation of the Attayndo' of S' Wittm Sherington.

FORASMUCHE as S' Will*m Sheryngton late of London Knighte, the xiiij,h daye of Februarye in the thirde yere of the reigne of o' Soveraigne Lorde Edwarde the Sixte, by the grace of God of Englande Fr*unce and Irelande King, defendo' of the Faithe and of the Churche of Englande and allso of Irelande in Earthe the supreme Hed, was lawfullye indycted before the Mayour of the Cide of London and other the Kings Comyssioners of Oyer and Terminer in the Guylde Hall in London, for that the same S' Will*in the x,b daye of Julye in the fyrst yere of the Reigne of o' saide Souveraigne Lorde King Edwarde the Sixte, and dyvers dayes and tymes before and after, at the Cide of Brystowe in the Counde of the Cide of Brystowe, imagenynge falselye to deceyve o' saide Soveraigne Lorde the King and his people, falselye and trayterouslye did make forge and counterfayte twoo Thousande powndes of Coyne of sylver, to the similitude of a certayne coyne of o' saide Souveraine Lorde the King, comonly called Testons, of his owne auctoride withowt anny warr'unte of o' saide Souveraigne Lorde the King, and against the Kings prohibycbns to the cont*rie therof to him made and given, and against the peace of o' Soveraigne Lorde the King his Crowne and dignitie; ALBEIT the Kinges Subgectf nowe havinge a more pfytt and clere light of the Gospell and true worde of God, throughe the infynite elemeneye and mercye of Almightie God by the hands of the Kinges Majestie and his moste noble father of famous memorye pmulgate shewed declared and oponed, and therby pceyvinge that one daye or one kynde of Meate of it selfe is not more holie more pure or more cleane then an other, for that all dayes and all Meates be of their nature of one equall puritie cleanes and holynes, and that all men shoulde by them lyve to the glorie of God and at all tymes and for all Meates give thanckf unto Him, of whiche Meates none can defyle Cristien men or make them uncleane at any tyme, to whom all Meates be laufull and pure, so that they be not used in disobedience or vice;

Yet forasmuche as diPse of the Kings Subjects turnynge their knowledge therein to satisfye their sensualitye where they shoulde therby encrease in vertue, have of late tyme more then in tymes paste, broken and contempned suche abstynence whiche hathe byne used in this Realme upon the Fridayes and Satterdayes, the Ymbringe dayes and other dayes comonly called Vigillf, and in the tyme comonlye called Lent, and other accustomed tymes: The Kings Majestie consideringe that due and godlye abstynence ys a meane to vertue and to subdue mens Bodies to their Soule and Spirite, and consideringe also speciallye that Fysshers and men usinge the trade of lyvinge by fysshinge in the Sea, may therby the rather be sett or worke, and that by eatinge of Fyshe, muche Fleshe shalbe saved and encreased, and also for div’se other consideracbns and comodities of this Realme, dothe ordeyne and enacte with thassent of the Lordes spuall and temporall & Comons in this psent Parliament assembled and by the auctoritie of the same, that all manner of Statutf Lawes Constitucfins and Usages conceminge any manner of fastinge or abstynence from any kynde of Meats heretofore in this Reelme made or used, shall from the fyrste daye of Maye next ensuynge, lose their force and strenghe and be voyde and of none effecte. And also that noe pson or psones of what Estate degree or condition he or she be shall at any tyme after the saide firste daye of Maye in the yere of our Lorde God a thousand fyve hundreth fourtye and nyne, willinglie and wittinglye eate anye manner of Fleshe after what manner of kynde or sorte it shalbe ordered dressed or used, uppon anye Frydaye or Satterdaye, or the Ymbringe dayes, or in any daye in the tyme cdmonly called Lent, nor at anye suche other daye as ys or shalbe at any tyme hereafter comonly accepted and reputed as a Fyshe daye within this Realme of Englande, wherin it hath byne comonly used for to eate Fyshe and not Fleshe; upon payne that ev'ye pson eatinge any manner of Fleshe upon anye of the saide dayes or tymes phibited by this Acte, to forfeyt for the same firste offence tenne shillingf of laufull money of Englande, and also to suffer ymprisonment by the space of tenne dayes, and duringe the tyme of his or her saide ymprisonment, to abstayne from eatinge of any manner of Fleshe: And yf any pson after he shall be laufullye convicte of any offence cont'rye to this Acte doe eftsones offende cont*rye to this Acte, and be therof laufully convicte, that then everie pson so offendinge the seconde tyme, shall for his seconde offence forfett twentie shillingf of laufull money of Englande, and also suffer emprisonment by the space of twentie dayes and duringe the tyme of his or her saide ymprisonment to abstayne from eatinge any manner of Fleshe;

And soe lyke payne and emprisonment as often as he or she afterwarde shall offende.

CHAPTER XXL An Acte to take awaye all posityve Lawes againste Marriage of Priestes.

ALTHOUGHE it were not onely better for thestymaf&n of priestes and other ministers in the Churche of God to lyve chaste sole and sepate from the companye of Wymen and the bonde of Mariage, but also therby they myght the better entende to thadmynistrac&n of the Gospell, and be lesse entricated and troubled withe the Chardge of householde, beinge free and unburdened from the care and coste of fyndinge Wyef and Children, and that it were most to be wisshed that they woulde willingly and of their selfes endevor them selfe to a ppetuall chastytic and abstynence from the use of Wymen, yet forasmuche as the contrarie hathe rather byne seene, and suche undenes of lyvinge and other greate inconveniencf, not mete to be rehersed, have followed of compelled Chastytie and of suche lawes as have phibited those suche psones the godlye use of mariage, it were better and rather to be suffred in the Comon Wealthe that those whiche coulde not conteyne shoulde after the Counsell of Scripture lyve in holie mariage, then faynedlye abuse withe worse enormytie outwarde chastytie or syngle lyes: Be it therefore enacted by our Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge, withe thassent of the Lordes spuall & temporall and the Comons in this psent parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same, that all and everie lawe and lawes posityve, cannons constitucbns and ordyn*ncf heretofore made by thauctoritie of man onlye, whiche dothe phibite or forbyd marriage to any eccliasticall or spuall pson or psones, of what estate condicon or degree they be, or by what name or names soever they be called, whiche by Gods lawe maye laufully marrye, in all and everie article braunche and sentence, concerninge onlye the phibicftn for the marriage of the psones aforesaide shalbe utterlie voyde and of none effecte: And that all manner of forfeytures paynes penaltyes crymes or accbns whiche were in the saide lawes conteyned, and the same did followe, concerninge the phibicbn for the marriage of the psons aforesaid, be clerely and utterlye voyde frustrate and of none effecte, to all intentf constructions and purposes, aswell concerninge marriagf heretofore made by any of the eccliasticall or spuall psones aforesaide, as also suche whiche hereafter shalbe dulye and laufullye had celebrate and made betwixte the psons wd’ by the lawes of God may lawfullye marrye.

Provided alwayes and be it enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide. That this Acte or any thinge therin conteyned shall not extende to give any libertye to any pson to marrye without askinge in the Churche, or without any other ceremonye being appoynted by thordre pscribed and sett fourthe in the booke intituled the booke of Comon Prayer and thadmynistracbn of the Sacramentf ; any thinge above mentioned to the contrarie in anye wise notwithstandinge.

Provided also and be it enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, that this Acte or any thinge therin conteyned shall not extende to alter chaunge revoke repeall or otherwise to disanull any decree judgment sentence or devorse heretofore had or made; but that all and everie suche decree judgment sentence and devorse shall remayne and be of suche lyke force effecte strenghe and degree, to all intentf construcc&ns & purposes, as they were in before the makinge of this Acte, and as thoughe this Acte had never bene hade ne made ; this Acte or any thinge therin conteyned to the confrye in any wise notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER XXIV.

An Acte for the triall of Murders and fellonyes in sepal 1 Counties.

FORASMUCHE as the moste necessarye offyce and duetye of the Lawe, ys to p*serve and save the lyfe of Man, and condignlye to punyshe suche psons that unlaufully and wilfully murder sley or distroy men; and also that an other offyce and duetye of Lawe ys to punyshe Robbers and Theves whiche daylie endever them selfes to robbe and stele or gyve assistaunce to the same, and yet by crafte and cautele do escape from the same without punyshment; And where it often happeneth and comethe in ure in sondrye Countyes of this Realme, that a man ys felonouslye striken in one Countie and after dyeth in an other Countye, in whiche case it hathe not bene founden by the Lawes or customes of this Realme that any sufficient Indytement thereof can be taken in any of the saide two Countyes, for that, that by the custome of this Realme the Juryors of the Countye where suche Partic dyed of suche stroke can take noe knowledge of the saide stroke beinge in a forreyn Countye, althoughe the same two Counties and Placf adjoyne verie nere together, Ne the Juriors of the Countye where the stroke was gyven cannot take knowledge of the death in an other Countye, althoughe suche death most apparauntlye come of the same stroke; so that the Kings Majestie within his owne Realme cannot by any Lawes yet made or knowen punyshe suche murderers and manquellers for offences in this forme comytted and done, nor any Appeale at sometyme may lye for the same but dothe also fayle and the saide murderers and manquellers escape thereof without punyshment, aswell in cases where the Counties where suche offences be comytted and done maye joyne as otherwise where they may not joyne: And also it is a comen practise amongf erraunt Theves and Robbers in this Realme, that after they have robbed or stollen in one Countye, they will convey their spoyle or parte thereof so robbed and stollen unto some of their adherentf into some other Counrye, where the principall offence was not comytted nc done, whoe knowinge of suche felonye willingly and by false covyn receyveth the same; in whiche case althoughe the principall felon be after attaynted in the one Countye, the accessarie escapethe by reason that he was accessarie in an other Countye, and that the Juryors of the saide other Countie by any Lawe yet made can take noe knowledge of the principall Felonye ne attaynder in the first Countie, and soe suche accessaries escape thereof unpunyshed and doe often put in ure the same, knowinge they maye scape without punyshment: For redresse and punyshment of whiche offencf and savegarde of mans lyes, be it enacted by auctoritye of this j?sent Parliament, that where any pson or psons hereafter shalbe felonously stryken or poysoned in one Countie, and dye of the same stroke or poysonynge in an other Countie, that then an Indytement thereof founden by Juryors of the Countie where the Death shall happen, whether it shalbe founden before the Coroner upon the sight of such dead bodye, or before the Justicf of Peace or other Justicf or Comyssioners whiche shall have auctoritye to enquyre of suche offencf, shalbe as good and effectuall in the Lawe as yf the stroke or poysonyng had bene comytted & done in the same Countie where the Partie shall dye or where suche Indytement shalbe soe founden; any Lawe or usage to the contrarie notwithstandinge : And that the Justicf of Gaoll Delivye and Oyer and Termyner in the same Countye where suche Indytement at any tyme hereafter shalbe taken, and also the Justicf of the Kings Benche, after suche Indytement shalbe removed before them, shall and maye pceede upon the same in all poyntf as they shouldc or ought to doe in case suche felonous stroke and deathe therby ensuynge, or poysoninge and deathe thereof ensuynge, had growen all in one same Countie: And that suche Partie to whom Appeale of Murder shalbe given by the Lawe, maye c6mei.ce take and sue Appeale of Murder in the same Countie where the ptie so felonouslye striken or poysoned shall dye, as well against the principall and principalls as against evyc Accessarie to the same offencf in whatsoever Countie or Place the accessarie or accessaries shalbe gyltyc to the same; CHAPTER XXV.

An Acte for the kepinge of Countie Dayes.

WHEARE heretofore the most parte in all the Shiers and Counties within this Realme, the Countye Courte ys and hathe be usuallye kepte and holden from monethe to moneth, and so at everie monethes ende one Countye; yet albeit in some Countries though not many, the saide Countye Courts are holden from Sixe Wekes to Sixe Wekes, by force whereof the Officers awarde out pc esse aswell for the Kinge as pcesse of the Peace out of the Kings Benche, as also other comon pcesse betwixte partie and partie; and the Attornes and Solicitors wlioe sue the same (not kuowingc the private Custome of these pticuler Shires whiche have and use their Counties to be holden everie Sixe Wekes,) give their pcesse lyke retorne as in those Shires whiche have c5mon Custome to holde and kepe Countye Cortes everie monethe ; whereby the Kinges suytes be not only deferred, the playntifff and demaundantf delayed of their laufull action and demaundf, but also the saide playntifff and demaundauntf therby put to doblc coste and charge, to the greate ignomynye and Slaunder of the Lawe, encorraginge of the Offendors and Transgressors, and to the contynuall ympoverishinge of all those who have cause of Sute: In consideration whereof be it enacted by the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde, the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons of this p'sent parliament assembled and by thauctoriue of the same, That from and after the fyrste daye of October next ensuynge this psent Session of Parliament, noe Countie Corte or Cortes hereafter to be kepte within this Realme shalbe longer deferred but one monethe from Courte to Courte, and so the saide Courts from thensforthe shalbe kepte ev’ye monethe and none otherwise: Any usage custome statute or lawe heretofore had or made to the contrarie in any wise notwithstandinge.

And be it further enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, that the Sheriffe of Northumberland from thensforthe shall kepe the Countye Courte of that Shyre in the Towne or Castle of Alnewyke and in none other place; any latter use latelye begonne and brought in to the cont*rye notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER XXX. (3)

An Acte for the Townes of Rye and Wynchellsey and for casting of Balaste into the Camber.

Decay of the Road and Harbour called the Camber, near Rye and Winchelsea:

Mayor and Jurats shall appoint Places for unfading Ballast from Ships ; and none shall be unladen elsewhere; Penalty, 40s. per Ton.

FORASMOCHE as the Inhabitauntes of the Townes and Portes of Rye and Wynchelsey in the County of Sussex, have trulye enformed the Kings mooste hono'able Councell, that the Harborowe and Rode called the Camber, beinge nere to the sayde Townes of Rye and Wynchelsey (lyinge over againste the C.ostes off Dyepe in Fraunce) in tymes past hathe bene a Harboroughe able to receyve twoo hundreth or sower hundreth saylle of Shippes, aswell in tymes of Warre as in tymes of Peaxe, and beinge there, myghte not oonly yssue owte thereof at all tymes to encounter their Enemyes, but also in tymes of stormye Wyndes mighte have had rescue and good Harborowe in the same, to the greate salvegarde of the Kings Shippes and of Marchauntes passinge to and fro uppon the narrowe Seas; Yet no we of late not oonly the sayde Harborowe and Rode called the Camber, but also all the Inne Creekf nere unto Rye and Wynchelsey aforesaide, partelye by occasyon of castinge of Ballest into the same Harborowe and Creekes, and partely bycause dyvers Mershes Inned take in no Water to scower the Channell, but lett oute ther freshe Water at Guttf, so that at this present the Channell there is so choked swared and fylled uppe, that there cannot lye in the same Harborowe above thirtie or fowrtie saylle of Shippes, and yet the same Shippes cannot come into the same harborowe withowte greate daunger: Therefore yt is enacted and ordeyned by the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde the Lordes spirituall and temporall and Commons in this present Parlyament asscbled and by the aucthoritie of the same, that the Mayo's and Juratf of Rye and Wynchelsey nowe beinge, before the XXth daye of Aprill next commynge shall appoynte covenyeute placys to laye on all balast that shalbe cast owte of anye hoye shippe crayer bote or other vessell whiche after the first daye of Maye next commynge shall come into or within the sayde harborowe or rode to the entente to receyve or take into yt any freighte or ladinge in those pties; and that all maner of ballast that shalbe had or cast owte of any hoye shippe crayer bote or other vessell after the sayde first daye of Maye shall, by the parsones beinge in every hoye shippe crayer bote cr other vessell, be layde uppon suche placys as the sayde Mayo's and Jurattf or the more nombre of them shall appoynte and assigne and at no other place, uppon payne off forfayture of fortye shillingf of laufull money of England for the first parte or porcyon of ballast so cast over, and xl s. for every tonne of ballast residewe beinge cast owte off any hoye shippe crayer bote or other vessell contrary to the fourme aforesayde, the oon hallffe of every some so forfayted to be to the Kynge our Soveraigne Lorde his heires and successoures, and the Other hallffe to be to hym that will sue for the same in any Courte of Recorde in this Realme in whiche accyon or sute no essoyn proteccyon or wager of Lawe shalbe admytted or allowed.

CHAPTER XXXI. (’)

The Citie of Chester ; towching the taking of Recognisaunces of Statute Marchant or Acton Burnell.

IN theire most humble wyse shewen unto your Highnes your true faithfull and obedient subjects the Maiour Aldermen Shireff 8c Comunaltie of your Graces Citie of Chester, that where before this tyme the Maiours of the said Citie of Chester were appoynted and auctorised to take and receve before the said Mayo's Recognis'uncf according to the Statutes Marchaunt and of Acton Burnell, whereupon were delivered unto the said Maiour by the Kinges Majesties Progeny tours that then were, a speciall seall concernyng the same, by force wherof the Maiours and other Officers there appoynted tyme oute of mynde have contynually used and practised to take recognis*uncf before theym of Statutes Marchaunte and Acton Burnell and enrolled the same, whiche ever hitherto was allowed permytted and taken to be good and effectuall in the Lawe; until nowe of late that ambiguytie and doubte hath risen by the meanes of certen synyster persons, more for the defrauding of right equitie and justice, then upon any good grounde or mattier for theire private comoditie, bycause that in all poyntes it doth not fullye folowe and agree according to all the strayte wordes of the said Statutes Marchaunt and Acton Burnell; aswell to the greate hurte and sclaunder of the said Citie, as also to the decay of the Marchauntes whiche have and shall lende theire Livinges wares and money and greate boldenes of the [holdenes of the "] Creditours and dettours to detayne the same in theire handes, to the greate decay of the said Citie: wherfore for the inconvenience therof, and also for thadvoidyng of the said ambiguytie and doubte, it may please your Highnes that it may be by your Grace with thassent of the Lordes spirituall and temporall and the Comens in this present Parliament assembled ordeyned establisshed and enacted by auctoride of the same, that all and every suche Recognisaunce of Statutes Marchaunte and Acton Burnell, whiche after the first day of Maye next comyng shalbe taken knowleged enrolled had and sealed with the said Seale appoynted to the said Cide of Chester before the Maiour of the same Cide for the tyme being, in like manner as heretofore the Predecessours Maiours and other Officers in the said Cide have accustomed to take and enrolle and seale, shalbe as goode effectuall and of force in the Lawe to all ententf constructions and purposes as if the taking of suche recognisaunce did fully agree and accorde to all ententes and purposes with the straite wordes of the said Statutes of Acton Burnell and the Statute Marchaunte ; and that upon all Certificates of the said Maiours hereafter like proces & execuc&ns to be awarded and directed oute of the High Co'cf of Ch*uncery 8c Coen place to all Shirefff Maiours Bailifff or other Officers in Englonde and Wales, in as ample maner and fourme as is used elswhere within this Realme for any recognis'unce taken upon any of the Estatutf aforesaid; any Lawe statute libertie franchise or usuage had or used to the contrary notwithstondyng.

CHAPTER XXXIII.

An Acte that no Man stealinge horse or horses shall enjoye the benefitt of his Clergie.

FORASMUCHE as it is and hathe byne ambyguous and doubtfull, upon the Wordes mencioned in one Acte of Parliament made in the firste Yere of the Raigne of our Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge, whether that any pson being in due fourme of the lawes founde gyltye or otherwise attaynted or convicted for felonyous stealinge of one horse geldynge or mare ought to be admytted to have and enjoye the priviledge and benefyte of his Clergie or Sanctuarye, therefore yt is declared and enacted by the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde and the Lordes and Comons in this p*sent parliament assembled and by the auctoritye of the same parliament, that all and singuler pson and psons felonyously takinge or stealinge any horse geldynge or mare shall not be admytted to have or enjoye the pViledge or benefyte of his or their Clergy or Sanctuarie, but shall be put from the same, in lyke manner and fourme as thoughe he or they had bene indyted or appealed of felonyous stealinge of two horses two geldyngf or two mares of anye other, and thereupon founde gyltye by veredict of twelve men or confessed the same upon his or thire arraynment or stande wilfiillye or of malice muett.

CHAPTER XXXIV.

An Acte for the Shirieff of Northumberlande to be accomptable for his Office as other Shirieffes bee.

FORASMUCHE as the Shrieff of the Counde of Northumbr, whiche have bene named nowe of longe tyme passed, have not accompted to the Kings Majesde of the yssues and pfittes of their Baylywyke, in the Kinges Highnes Eschequyer nor ells where, as other Shrieff of the saide Counde in olde tyme passed have done nor as the Shrieff of other Coundes of this Realme doc at this tyme, but doe yerelye receyve and take the whole pfittf thereof to their owne uses, to the great detryment and losse of the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde bothe of his vycoundellf and other fermes answerable by thandf of the saide Shrief, and of all other Dettf yssues fynes and aniciamentf within the saide Counde, and of all alienacons and intrusions wardes manages releves and suche other: Wherefore be it enacted by the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde withe thassent of the Lordes spuall & temporall and the C5mons in this p*sent parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same, that from hensforthe all and everie suche pson and psons as shalbe hereafter named to be Shrieff of the saide Countye of Northumbr forthwithe, before he receyve his Patent and before he doe excyse any parte of the saide office, shall putt in sufficient suertyes by him selfe or by his suffycient deputye or depudes, into the Kinges Eschequer there, to entre in Recognizaunce in suche some and upon suche conditions as to the Lorde Treasourer and Barons of the saide Eschequer shall seme convenient, in manner and fourme as all other Sheriefff of other Countyes of this Realme doe; upon peyne of everie suche Shriefe makinge defalte to forfeyt to the Kings Majesde a hundred Pounds to be levyed of his goods and chattellf lands and teiites wheresoever theye maye be founde to the Kinges Highnes use: And that the saide Barons from tyme to tyme shall cause suche pcesse to be made for the Kinge for the levyinge of the saide hundred pounde so to be forfeyted, to be dyrected to suche pson and psons and in suche nature and sorte as to them shall seme best for the Kinge for the levyinge thereof; any thinge in this Acte or any other lawe statute use pvysion or custome to the contrarie notwithstandinge.

Provided always and be it enacted by the saide auctoride, that anye suche Shrief beinge so bounden as ys abovesaide shall not be accomptable but for his owne tyme and for the yere of his Shrivewyke onelye; neither shalbe charged, in or upon his accompte, by any pcesse withe anye arrearagf or dutyes due to the Kings Majesde by anye his predecessors in the saide office of Sherieff ; anye thinge in this Acte or any lawe usage or prerogaty ve to the contrarie notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER XXXVI. (■)

An Acte for a Reliefs graunted to the Kyngf Magestie by the Temporaltie.

WHILEST WE the Kyngf Ma'" faythfull lovinge and obedient Subjects, the Lordes and Comens assembled in this present Parlyament, do consider the present state of the Worlde, what great troubles be in all Places, what Enemyes bothe his Ma,ie and this his Realme hathe and is lyke to have, and that their malice and hatred is bent partelie to dymyshe his Graces Ma*" and the honour of this his Realme, partlie to spoyle the same of the just true and auncyent enheryt'unce right and title that his Highnes and his most noble progenytours Kyngf of this Realme of Englonde have alweys had to the Realme of Scotlande, beinge a member and parte of his Kyngdome and Domynyon; and cheiflie for that We of late havynge abandoned the auctoryte of the Busshope of Rome and his wycked doctryne have and do adhere to Chryst and his moste holie worde, as becomythe all Chrystyans to do that meane to be no lesse in deade then they professe in name: Whylest We also consyder that his Grace and We his faythfull and obedyent Subjects be but one bodye polytyque, his Highnes the hedde and We the membres, and that no good or felycytie canne come to the one but the other shalbe partaker therof, and that no hurte or adversyde canne happen to the one wherw* the other shall not also be greyed: Whylest also We consyder the practyses and pollycies of other Prynces and Potentates, what great preparations they make bothe of men and also of other furniture for the Warres, and what great Treasure they of late have levyed and gathered of their Subjects ; W e perceavynge that all the Kyngf Ma'" procedyngf holly tende to the advauncemente of the true glorye of God, the maynten*nce of the MaUe of the Imperyall Crowne of this Realme, and the defense and savede of us and this his Realme, fully mynded to cleave and stycke to God and his moste holie worde, utterlie determyned to meynteyne his Graces honour and all suche ryghds and titles as be annexed to his Imperyall Crowne; prest and redie to defende our selfs and this his Realme and our Countrie, and fynallie content to leave Father mother brothem system wyfes chyldren landes goodes, yea and this mortall lyfe also, rather then We wolde denye Chryst and forsake his worde, whiche is the lyvelie food of mans sowle, rather than We wolde suffer his royall Ma,k to be in any parte dymynyshed, rather then We wolde consente that the Imperyall Crowne of this Realme shoulde be depryved of any honour title ryght or interest therunto belongynge; and fynallye rather then any foiren Power shoulde do us or our Countrie any hurte or injurye; have thought it good to prepare and make not onlie our psons redie for the warres, havynge a full affyaunce and parfette confydence in God, that as he alweyes hathe sent victorye to suche as professed hym and put their hole trust in hym, albeit they were but verye fewe and that verye feble in mans sight in respecte of the multytude and force of their enemyes, so he nowe woll have specyall regarde and eie to this lytle Realme, and us his poore S'v*ntf and litle flocke, takynge to his charge and defence our title Sheparde, till yeares and strenght make hym better able to bycker withe his enemyes, and that therfore he w' us and for us woll devyse to withstonde resyste and subdue the force and puissaunce of our stoute foes, no more ours then his, at the least ours for his cause; but also to make emonge us a masse of moneye to releeve and meynteyne the great and inestymable chargf that our most gracious Sovereigne Lorde hathe and dayllie dothe susteyne, a thinge moche unable to serve any peace of his present necessities, if his Grace dyd mean to spare any parte of his owne Threasure, besichynge his Grace not to cast his eies uppon the smalnes of this our symple present, but to laye by it our good wylle whiche we make the chiefest part of our Relief, it faythfullie promysinge all the reast to be readie when perrell or enemye shall declare this not to suffice : Fyrst We his Graces said Subjects do, by thauctorytie of this present Parlyament, frelie and franckelie gyve and graunte unto his most Royall Ma1' a Relief, to contynewe by the space of thre yeares, to be rated taxed levyed and gathered of every pson, of what estate or degree he be, accordinge to the tenour of this Acte alter the rate and in manner and forme followynge, that is to saye; aswell of all and everye pson as is or hereafter shalbe his Graces naturall subjects, as of all and every Fratemyte Guylde Corporation Mysterye Brotherhod Companye and C5mynalde, corporat or not corporat, win this Realme of Englonde Walis and other the Kyngf

And be it ferther enacted, That the said Estatute made in the saide xxxiij," yere of the raigne of the saide late King Henry the eighte, and every artycle and provision beinge not alterid by this Estatute, shall be good and effectuall.
