CHAPTER I.

An Acte that the Lorde Chauncellor or Lorde Keeper of the greate Seale for the tyme being shall name and appoynte the Custos Rotulop thoroughout all Shires of Englande accordinge as in tyme paste hathe bene accustomed.

WHERE in the Parliament holden at Westni in the xxxvij"1 yere of the Reigne of the most excellent Prince of famous meniorie Kinge Henrie theight. It was enacted that noe pson or psons sholde from the makinge of the saide Acte be nolated and appoynted to the Office or Offices of the Custos Rotulof, within anye Shire of this Realme of Englande Wales or other the Kings Dnyons Marches or Territories of the same, but suche as sholde have a bill signed with the Kings hande for the same; whiche bill signed sholde be a sufficient Warraunte by auctorytie of the saide Acte, to the Lorde Chauncellor of Englande and Lorde Keeper of the great Seale for the tyme beinge to make from tyme to tyme Comyssion or C5myssions, assigninge and authorisinge therby the same pson to be Custos Rotulop, untill the Kinge had by an other bill assigned withe his owne hande appoynted and ordeyned an other pson to have occupie and exeyse the same Office of Custos Rotulop; and that the saide pson appoynted and assigned to be Custos Rotulop as ys abovesaide sholde and myght occupye excise and enjoye the saide Office of Custos Rotulop by him selfe, or by his sufficient Deputye learned in the lawes of this Realme, and mete and liable to supplye the saide Office accordinge to the tenor of the graunte or Comyssion: as by the same Acte amonge other things more at large it dothe and maye appere: Synce the makinge of whiche Statute div'se and manye psons, beinge in the saide Offices of Custos Rotulo^ in divse Shires of the Realme have depted this p>sent lyes and dyed, so that there hathe not come to thandes of the Chauncelor of Englande or Lorde Keeper of the great Seale anye bill or billes assigned withe the Kinges Majesties hande, for the namynge appoyntinge or assigninge of anye newe Custos Rotulop in the same Shires, the saide Offices have remayned voyde for a longe tyme, to the great lett of Justice; And also for that yt shalbe verie tedyous and muche to the molestinge of the Kings Majestie upon ev’ye avoydaunce of suche Custos Rotulop by deathe or otherwise, to move his Majestie for the signinge of billes for other psons to be elected named chosen and appoynted to supplye the saide Offices of Custos Rotulop beinge voyde; And for that the noiac&n and appoyntinge of the saide Office of Custos Rotulo^ longe tyme before the makinge of the saide Statute laste before rehersed did apperteyne and belonge to the Office of the Chauncellor of Englande or Lorde Keeper of the great Seale for the tyme beinge: Be it therefore enacted by the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde withe thassent of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent Parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same, That the Chauncelor of Englande or Lorde Keeper of the great Seale for the tyme beinge shall at all tymes hereafter, and from tyme to tyme, without anye bill or billes to be assigned withe the Kinges hande, name electe assigne and appoynte suche pson and psons to be Custos Rotulop within ePye Shire of this Realme of Englande Wales and other the Kings Domynions Marches and Territories of the same, or [by1] any of them, as by the discrec&n of the saide Lorde Chauncelor or Lorde Keper of the greate Seale for the tyme beinge shalbe thought liable and mete to have and excise the same: And that the saide parson and parsons soe to be appoynted elected named or assigned by the saide Lorde Chauncelor or Lorde Keper of the greate Seale for the tyme beinge, shall and maye occupye excise and enjoye the same Office of Custos Rotuloj, by him selfe or by his sufficient Deputye or Deputyes, in as ample and large manner and fourme as yf the saide Acte had never bene had ne made; The before rehersed Acte or any thinge therm contcyncd to the contrarie hereof in any wise notwithstandinge.

Provided alwaye and be it enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, that all suche as nowe have any of the saide Offices of Custos Rotulo^, by the Kinges tres patentf or Comyssion to them or anye of them made, shall and may enjoye have and excise their saide Offices by vertue of the same ires patentf or Comyssion, by himselfe or his sufficient and liable Deputye instructed in the Lawes of this Realme; Any thinge in this psent Acte had or made to the cont*rye notwithstandinge.

Provided also that it be enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, that the Archebisshopp of Yorke the Bisshopp of Durham the Bisshopp of Elye, and everie of their successors, the Chauncelor of the Dutchie of Lancastre for the tyme beinge, and all and everie pson and psons corporacions and bodyes corporated, to whom the Kinges Majestie or anye of his noble pgenitors, by his or their tres patentf or Acte of Parliament, have gyven and graunted anye libertye and auctoritie, or otherwise have auctoritie by other laufull meanes or wayes, to ordeyne make and constitute anye of the saide Officers of Custos Rotulof, within any Countie Palentyne or other Place, shall and maye have and enjoye the same libertye Sc auctoritie accordinge as they have had and enjoyed the same; Anye thinge in this psent Acte hadd or made to the contrarie notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER III.

An Acte conceminge the ymprovement of Comons and Waste Groundes.

Recital of Stat. of Merton, to H. LL c. 4. as to improving of Waster.; and Assi -e given for Common of Pasture;

WHERE in the Parliament holden at Marton in the twentith yere of the raigne of Kinge Henrie the thirde, it ys conteyned. That for because many greate men of Englande whiche had enfeoffed Knyghtf and other their free Ten'ntes of [smale1 ] tentes in their great Mannors, did complayne that they might not make their pfyttf of the residue of their Mannors, as of Waste Woods and Pastures, where the same feoffees had sufficient pasture as muche as belonged unto their teiitf ; It was pvyded and graunted that whatsoever psons soe enfeoffed, brought Assise of Novell Disseison of their Comon of Pasture, and before the Justicf it were recognized that they had asmuche pasture as did suffice unto their tethf, and that they had free ingresse and egresse into and from their tentes unto their pasture, that then they sholde therwithe be contented, and that they upon whom they had complayned shoulde departe quyte, withe that that they might make their pfytt of their lands wastf woodes and pastures; And yf it were saide that they had not sufficient pasture or suffycient ingresse and egresse, as muche as dothe belonge unto their teiitf, as ys abovesaide, that then the trueth thereof shoulde be enquired by assise, and yf it were recognized by thassise that their ingresse and egresse were in any thinge letted by the same deforciators, or that they had not sufficient pasture and sufficient ingresse and egresse as is abovesaide, that then they shoulde recover their seison by vewe of the Jurors, so that by the discrecon and

For tuppreuion of all »uch Assemblies;

Where more than Two are assembled for any auch unlawful Purpose, any Just ice of Peace, Sheriff, Mayor, he. or Persona commissioned by the King, &c. may assemble People to suppress such Assembly by force; and to apprehend and kill the Offenders.

And for so muche as suche evill disposed psons whiche of late tyme made comocions and rebellion in certeyne places within this Realtne, beinge but fewe in nombre at suche tyme as they did begynne the same comotion, were not in shorte tyme after the begynynge thereof suppressed by strenghe, for that the Kings lovinge Subjects for feare to encurre in daunger of the Lawes of this Realme durst not take upon them so to doe, a great nomber of evill disposed psones did come and joyne them selves to the saide small nombre, wherby the same evill disposed psons toke upon them suche boldnes that they wolde not be reduced to obedience without muche bloodshedinge, to the great daunger of the Kings Majesties pson, where yf the Kings lovinge Subjects durst have taken upon them to have suppressed them at the begynnynge, suche inconvenience and bloudshed sholde not have followed: Therefore yt is also ordeyned and enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, that yf anye psons above the nombre of two, that at anye tyme after the saide twelveth daye of Februarie, shalbe unlaufully and of their owne auctoritie assembled togither, to thintent withe force and armes to doe practise or put in ure any of the thinges abovemencioned, that then it shalbe laufull to everie Justice of Peace, and to everie Sheriffe in anye Countie beinge within the Kings Iknions, and to everie Mayor Bayliffe and other hedd Officer of any Cittie or Towne corporate for the tyme he shalbe in Office, or any other pson or psons havinge the Kings Comyssion or Ires from his Highnes or his Privy Counsel), as well to rayse and assemble the Kings lovinge Subjects in manner of warre to be arrayed in suche great nombre as he or they then shall thincke mete or able, to thintent by violence and strenght to suppresse appffiende and take the saide psons that so shalbe unlaufullye assembled ; And that yf the saide psons soe unlaufully assembled, after suche edmaundment or request by Pclamacon or otherwise made shall contynue togither, and not endevor them selfes to retorne towards their Habitacons houses or placf from whence they came in suche shorte tyme as they maye convenientlie, that then yt shalbe laufull to everie Justice of Peace Sheriff and also to everie Mayor Bayliff and other hed Officer of any Cittie or Towne corporate, and to everie other pson havinge auctoritie as ys aforesaide, after suche comaundment or request by •Pclamac&n made, and to suche psons as shalbe assembled withe anye Justice of Peace or Sheriff or withe any Mayor Bayliff or other hedd Officer of anye Cittie or Towne corporate, and withe everie other pson havinge auctoritie as ys aforesaide, to suppresse apphende and take those psons so unlaufully assembled, whiche after suche request made shall contynue together and not endevor them selves to retome towards their habitaf&ns or places from whence they came: And that yf the saide psons so unlaufullye assembled togither or anye of them shall fortune to be killed slavne maymed or hurte in or aboute the suppressinge or takinge of them, that then everie suche Justice of Peace Sheriff Mayor Bayliffe and other hed Officer, and everie other pson havinge auctoritie as ys aforesaide, and all and singuler psons by him or them assembled shalbe free discharged and unpunysheable, aswell againste the Kinge as againste all and everie other pson and psons, of for or conceminge the killinge slayinge maymynge and hurtinge of any pson or psons so unlaufully assembled, that shall fortune to be killed slayne maymed or hurte aboute or by occac&n of suppressinge or takinge of them.

FORASMUCHE as Leather is growen to an unreasonable price, whereby the Kings Subjects are not able at this daye to pvyde them selfes suche necessaries thereof made as Shoes and Boots and suche lyke at anye reasonable price, as they heretofore have done, to the utter ympoverishement of divW the Kinge lovinge and obedient Subjects, whiche saide unreasonable prices of Leather doth onlye growe and ryse by reason of the unsaciable desire of div’se and sondrye psons, beinge noe Tanners, whiche daylye in everie Markett and other place buy and regrate grene hydes in the heare and out of the heare to their handes, to thintent to sell the same to their owne lucre and gayne: Be it therefore enacted by the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent Parliament assembled and buy thauctoritie of the same, that noe pson or psons within this Realme, shall from and after the feast of the Anunciacon of our Ladye next comynge, buy or cause to be bought anye Calve Skynnes or Hydes, in the heare or out of the heare, to thintent to sell agayne the same untanned, except onlye suche pson and psons as will tanne or tawe the same, uppon payne to forfeyte’ for everie Skynne so bought, to the intent to sell agayne as aforesaide, sixe shillingf eight pence ; the one halfe of whiche forfeyture to be unto our Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge the other halfe to him or them that will sue for the same in anye the Kings Courts by bill playnte or other lawfull pcesse, wherein noe ptecc&n or wager of Lawe nor yet any Essoyne to the partie defendaunte shalbe allowed or admytted.

As Acte for the keping of Hollie daies and Fastinge dayes.

Purpose of Holidays and Fasting Days:

Holidays to be

observed,

enumerated.

FORASMUCHE as at all tymes Men be not so myndefull to lawde and praysc God, so readie to resorte and heare Goddf hollie worde, and to come to the hollie Comunion and other lawdable Rites w* ar to be obs'ved in every Christen Congregation, as their bownden dewtie doth require; Therfore to call Men to remembr'unce of their dewtie and to helpp their infirmytie, it hath ben holsomelye provyded That there sholde be some certaine tymes and dayes appointed, wherin the Christians shoulde cease from all other kynde of labours, and shoulde applie themselff onelye and holie unto the aforesaid hollie workes proprely perteyning unto trewe Religion, that is to heare to leame and to remembre Almightie Goddf greate benefittf, his manifolde mercies, his inestimable gracious goodnes so plenteously poured uppon all his Creatures, and that of his infinite and unspeakeable goodnes withowt anny Mans desert; And in remembr'unce hereof to rendre unto him most highe and hartie thanks, w"1 Prayers and Supplicac&ns for the relief of all o' dailye Necessities; And becawse thes be the chief and principall wourkes wherin Man is cumaunded to wo'shipp God, and doo properlie partaine unto the first Table, Therefore as thes wourkes are bothe moste comonlie and allso maye well be called Goddf service, So the tymes appointed spiallie for the same ar called hollie dayes, not for the matter and nature either of the tyme or daye, nor for anny of the Sainctf sake whose memories ar had on those dayes, for so all dayes and tymes consydered arr Goddf creatures and all of lyke holiness, but for the nature and condition of those godlie and holie wourckes wherew"1 onelye Godde is to be honoured, and the Congregac&n to be edefyed, whereunto such tymes and daies arr sanctified and hallowed, that is to saye, Seperated from all prophane uses, and dedicated and appointed not unto anny Saincte or creature, but onely unto God and his trewe wourshippe; Neither it. is to be thought that there is anny certaine tyme or definite nombre of dayes prescribed in hollie Scripture, but that the appointment bothe of the tyme, and allso of the nombre of the daies, is left by thauctoritie of Goddf worde to the libertie of Christes Churche, to be determyned and assigned ordrelye in every Countree by the discretion of the rulers and ministers therof, as they shall judge moste expedyent, to the trewe setting forth of Goddf glorie and the edification of their People: Be it therefore Enacted by the King our Soveraigne Lorde w"1 the assent of the Lordes spuall and teinporall and the Comons in this psent Parlament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same. That all the daies hereafter mentyoned shalbe kepte and comaunded to be kepte hollie daies and none other, that is to saye; All Sondaies in the yere, The dayes of the Feastf of the Circumcisyon of our Lorde Jhesus Christe, Of Thepiphanie, Of the Purificac&n of the blessed Virgin, Of S' Mathie Thapostle, Of the Anucacbn of the blessed Virgyn, Of S' Marcke Thevangelist, Of S' Philipp and Jacobe Thapostles, Of thascentyon of our Lorde Jhesus Christe, Of the Nativitye of S' shon Baptist, Of S' Peter Thapostle, Of S' James Thapostle, Of S’ Barthilmewe Thapostle, Of S' MatheweThapostle, Of S' Michaell

CHAPTER VI.

An Acte for the makinge of Wollen Clothe.

WHEARE heretofore div’se and manye goodlie Statutf have bene made for the true makinge of Clothe within this Realme, whiche nevertheles, Forasmuche as Clothiers, some for lacke of knowledge and experience and some of extreame covetousnes, doe daylie more and more studdye rather to make manye then to make good Clothes, havinge more respecte to their private comoditie and gayne then the advauncement of truthe and contynuance of the comoditie in estymacbn accordinge to the worthynes thereof, have and doe daylie instead of truthe practyse falsehode, and instead of substanciall makinge of Clothe, doe practyse sleight and slender makinge, some by myngelinge of Yemes of d$se spynnyngf in one Clothe, some by myngelinge Fell Wooll and Lambes Wooll or either of them withe Fleese Wool), some by puttinge to little Stuffe, some by takinge them out of the mill before they be full thicked, some by overstretchinge them upon the tentor and then stoppinge withe flockf suche brackf as shalbe made by meanes thereof, fynallye by usinge so manye subtill sleightf and untruthes as when the Clothes soe made be put in the water to trye them, they ryse out of the same neither in lenghe nor bredith as they ought to doe and in some place narrower then some, beside suche cockelinge bandinge and dirse other great and notable faultf as almoste cannot be thought to be true; And yet nevertheles nether fearinge the lawe in that case pvyded, nor regarding the estymaf&n of their Countrie, doe not onely peure the Alneger to set the Kinge his Seale to suche false untrue and faultie Clothe, but doe them* selfes weave into the same the lykencs and simylitude of the Kinge his Highnes most noble and ympiall Crowne, and also the firste Ire of his name, whiche shoulde be testimonye of truthe and not a defence of untruthe, to great slaunder of the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde and the shame of this lande, and to the utter dystruccon of so greate and notable comodite as the lyke ys not in anye forreyn Nation: Our saide Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge therefore myndinge to advaunce all truthe and to abandon falsehode, and also to pvyde for the contynuaunce of the saide comoditie of Cloth makinge to his honor and the comon pfytt of the Realme, hathe by thadvise of the Lordes & Comons in this p*sent Parliament assembled, caused aswell div'se honest Clothiers, as also divse Drapers Marchaunttaillors Clotheworkers Sheremen and other Artificers to whom it apperteyneth, to be examyned by certen wise discreate and sage Knyghtf and Burgeses in this p'sent Parliament, of suche matters as towche aswell the false as the true makinge of Clothes, by whose declaration consent agreament and advyse after div*se and sondrie meatingf and greate deliberate advyse taken in the jPmysses by thauctoritie of this p>sent Parliament, It ys enacted as hereafter followeth, to retnayne fyrme and pfecte, notwithstandinge any suggestions hereafter to be made by anye Clothier or Clothmaker to the contrarie as they have in like cases heretofore done, that is to saye, That epye Clothe Karsey pece of Frice and Cottonne 6halbe made in suche sorte and fourme, and shall conteyne in lenghe bredith And to thintent that yt maye be pfectlye knowen whiche Clothes are pfectly dressed dyed and pressed with the colde presse without firaude coven and deceyte, as well within the Cittie of London as elswhere, and have sufficient Workemanshipp ; Be it further enacted, that aswell the Maior of the Cittie of London and Aldermen for the most parte of them for the tyme beinge, as all and everie other Maior Baylifff and other hed Officer or Officers of everie Cittie Boroughe or Towne Corporate within this Realme, shall have full power and aucthoritie by virtue of this Acte to noiate depute and appoynte from tyme to tyme as occac&n shall serve, and shall so from tyme to tyme noyate depute and appoynt two or mo honest discrete and experte psons, whiche shall from tyme to tyme upon their othes viewe and searche all and everie Clothe and Clothes that shall be dressed dried or pissed with the colde presse within everie suche Cittie Boroughe Towne corporate or Porte Towne, and viewe and searche whether the same Clothe or Clothes be well and sufficientlye dressed and pressed withe the colde presse, without puttinge therto flox solace chalke flower or any other deceiptfull thinge ; and also whether the same shalbe well and substanciallye died withe good and pfecte Collors without any deceyvable thinge; or whether it shalbe stretched or streyned any more then is above spiffed; and shall have full power and aucthoritie by vertue of this Acte to enter into all and everie psons house or houses where they shall thincke mete to searche and to sease all and everie suche Clothe and Clothes as they shall fynde defectyve in the fPmisses as forfeited in whose handes soever they shalbe founden, The moytie of whiche forfeyture shalbe to the use of our Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge and thother moytie to thuse of the Maior and Coialtie of the Cittie of London or to the use of e$y Cittie Boroughe Towne Corporate Porte Towne or Markett Towne where the same shalbe seased.

CHAPTER VII.

An Acte lymittinge the tymes of buyinge and sellinge of Woolles.

FORASMUCHE as the greate plentye of Woolles within this Realme ought by all reason to cause the same to be of convenient and reasonable pries, yet by the gredye and covetous myndes aswell of suche as have the great plentye and habundaunce of Sheepe and Woolles, as also by the corrupt practises of dipse Broggars Ingrocers Woolgatherers and Regrators and sondrie other psons, by the havinge to muche libtye of buyinge kepinge usinge and occupyinge of the same Woolles, it manifestlye appeareth that the prices thereof be wonderfullye and excedinglie enhaunsed and raysed, to the greate hurte detryment and decaye of the Realme: Be it therefore ordeyned established and enacted by thauctoritie of this psent Parliament, That noe manner of pson or psons beinge borne within the Kings obeysaunce shall after the last daye of Maie next, buy bargayne take or make anye pmyse or bargayne of Woolles, but onelye suche pson or psons, his wief or his or their apprentice or apprentices inhabitinge in his or their Mansion house or houses, as shall of the saide Woolles make Yarne any kynde of Clothe Chamlettf Wolstede Sayes Stamyn Knythose Knytpetycotes Knytgloves Knytsleves Hattf Coyves Cappes Arrace Tapesserie Coverlettf Gurdellf, or any other thing used to be made of Wooll or myxed withe Wooll within the Realme, Or els a Marchaunte or Marchauntf of the Staple at Callice or his or their apprentice or apprentices dwellinge in his or their Mansion house or houses to be shipped onlye to the Staple at Callice, upon payne of forfeiture of the double value of the saide Woolles so to be bought or bargayned or taken by pmyse of bargayne contrarie to this psent Acte.

And be it further enacted by thauctoritye aforesaide, That noe Marchaunte Straunger, after the twentith daye of Aprill next comynge, by him selfe or by any other pson or psons for hym in his name or to his use in any yere after the saide twentith daye of Aprill then to come, shall bargayne or buy any Woolles before the Feast of the Purificacbn of our Ladye next after the clippinge or sheringe of the same Woolles, upon payne of forfeyture of the doble value of the same Woolles.

And be it further enacted by thaucthoritie aforesaide, That noe manner of pson or psons havinge any Wooll or Woollf of his or their owne grothe, shall at any tyme after the Feast of the Natyvitie of Saincte John Baptiste next edmynge, kepe the same Woolles, to thentent to sell the same in Woolle unwrought, over and above one hole yere next and ymediatlie after the sheringe of the same Woolles; So as there be offered without fraude or covyn to the owner or owners thereof within the same tyme, suche price as then shalbe most comenlye given in the same Shire for Wooll of like goodnes and packinge ; upon payne of forfeyture for ev*y Todde, or Todde weight thereof so kepte above one yere unsolde as is aforesaide the some of tenne shillingf; the moytie of all and everie suche forfeiture and forfeitures penaltye or penaltyes before rehersed to be to thuse of our Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge his heires and successors, and thother halfe to thuse of him that will sue for the same in anye of the Kings Courts of Recorde by accon of dett bill playnt informac&n or otherwise, wherin noe wager of lawe pteccon or essoyne shalbe allowed for the Defendaunte.

Provided always that the Marchauntf of Newcastle and other psons, maye buye Woolles of the groeth of the Counties of Northumberland Cumberland Westifiland Richemonde and Allerton Shire or the Bisshoppriche of Duresme, to the intent to shippe or t'nsporte the same into the Parts beyonde the Sea as they have bene accustomed; Any thing in this Estatute to the contrarie in anye wise notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte that noe Man robbinge any House Boothe or Tent shall not be admytted to the benefyt of his Clergie.

Recital of Statute 23 H.VIII. c. i. taking away Clergy from certain Offencei

Stilt utcs against Forestalled Regraters and Ingrossers. deficient

Forestalled defined, via. Persons buying Goods or Victuals on their way to a Market or Port; or contracting to buy the same before actually brought for Sale; or endeavouring to enhance the Price or prevent the Supply.

II.

Regratora defined; viz. Persons buying Corn, Victuals, Ike. and re-selling them in the tame Market Place, or within Miles thereof.

III.

Ingrossers defined ; viz. Persons buying Com growing, or buying Corn or Victuals to tell again.

Penalties on all such Offenders; tst Offence, Two Months Impriton-ment.and Forfeiture of the Value of the Goods;

CHAPTER XV.

An Acte againste Regratours of tanned Lether.

WHERE by the covetousnes of div’se gredie psons Regratinge and Ingrossinge all kynde of tanned Leather into their hands, and sellinge agayne the same at excessive pries to Sadlers Girdlers Cordwayners and suche other Artificers and Handy Crafts men as make Wares of tanned Leather, the Kings lovinge Subjects are enforced to buy the saide Wares at unreasonable pries: For Remedye and reformaeftn whereof. CHAPTER I.

An Acte for the true aunsweringe of the Kinges Majesties Revenues.

FORASMUCHE as the Kinges Majesties Treasourers and Generali and perticuler Receyvoure and Bailiefes of his Honoures Castelles Lordeshippes Manours Landes and Tenementes Reverc&ns Possessions and other his Hereditam" in Englande Wales and Calice and the Marches of the same or els wher within the Kings Dominions, have not so justlye spedely neither dulye made yerely paimentes of suche some and somes of Money as hathe been by them and every of them received of the Kings Majesties Revenues Possessions and Profites into the Kinges Matta Treasourie according to their duties, but doo yerely deteine and kepe the same to their own gaine profiecte and lucre, contrarie to all right truthe and equitie, and to the manifest injurie wrong and hinderance of and to the King our Soveraine Lorde: Be yt therfore enacted by the King oure Sovereyn Lorde the Lordes spiritual! and temporal! and the C5mens of this pnte Parlament assembled and by the aucthorite of the same, That every Treasourer and Generali and particuler Receivour Collectour and Bailiefe and other Minister accomptant, whiche now ys chardged or changeable with or for the receipte of any of the Kings Majesties Moneye Rentes or Revenues whatsoever, not being bownde withe suretie or sureties by oblygac&n recognisance or otherwise to our late Soverayn Lorde the King, or to our Soverein Lorde the King that nowe is, for or concerning their Office or Offices, before the xx'h day of Decembre next coming, or at any time or tymes before the same xx*1 daye of Decembre, yf they or any of them be reasonably required, shall upon payn of forfeiture of his Office bee bownde to the Kinges Ma,ie by sufficient writyng oblygatorye in reasonable som or somes of money j The same writing oblagatorie to be made withe or upon condition that the parson whiche so shalbee bownden his heires executours administratoures deputie or deputies, or one of them, from tyme to tyme, shall yelde a perfeict and true accompte of all somes of moneye and other thinges, that the same Treasourer and Generali and particuler Receivour Collectour Bailief or other Ministre accomptaunt shall may or reasonably might be chardged with concerning or by reason of his or their Office or Offices, and also shall make paymentes of the same somes of money at suche dayes and tymes and in suche maner and forme as hereafter in this Acte is expressed and declared.

And be yt ferther enacted, That all and every pson and parsones hereafter to be named assigned or appointed to be Treasourer or Generali or particular Receyvour Collectour or Bayliefe or Minister accoumptaunt of oure said Sovereyn Lorde the King, shall before any their entrye executing using or exersising of his or their Office or Offices wherunto he or thei shalbee so nominated or appoincted, together with suretie or sureties, acknowledge and make sufficient and lawfull bonde and bondes to the Kings Ma,le, in suche Courte of Recorde wher the same Officer or Officers is or shalbee accoumptable and chargeable, that they their heires executours administratoures assignes or deputies shall truly accoumpte and pay all suche somes of money as shall come to their handes, or shall may or reasonably might be charged withe, conceminge his or their office or offices to the Kings use within the circuitf of their severall Receiptes and Collections, at suche or lyke days and tymes and in suche maner and fourme as ys abovesayd, to be conteyned in the conditions of every of the sayd bondes ; upon paine of losse and forfayture of his or their Office or Offices and of his and their lettres patentes of the same Office or Offices.

Be yt ferther enacted by thauctoritee aforesaid, That every Receivour of the Kings Majesties Honours Manours landes possessions rentes and revenues for the tyme beinge, or his Deputie or Deputies, shall yerely make his severall Preceptes to all and singuler the Collectours Ministeres and Bailiefes accoumptaunte within the circuite of his Office, charging and comaunding them on the Kinges Majesties behalf by the same Preceipte [tappeare' ] before them, personallye or by their sufficient Deputie or Deputies for whom thei will aunswer, within the Countie where the same Offices Bayliewikes Receiptes or Collections doo lye, at a certaine day and place in the same Precepte to be lymited, and to paye to the Kinges Majesties use, suche sdmes of money as thei ought to doo by reason of any of their said Offices, being due to oure said Sovereine Lorde the King at or before the feast of Easter, whiche thei have or may by any lawfull or due meane levie or receive within or by reason of their said Offices or Collections; and that the same Preceptes shalbe severally delyvered to every of the said Officers Ministers and Bailiefes accoumptaunt, or to their Deputie or Deputies, or elles be lefte at their Dwelling howses or at the Manour Lordeshippe or Place wher their Receipte or Collection ys or ought to bee, twelve dayes at the least before the dave of apparaunce to them geven and prefixed in the same Precepte or Preceptes. And if any of the sayd Mynystres Collectoures or Baliefes accowmptaunt, uppon or after any suche Precepte or Preceptes at any tyme hereafter made by any suche Receivour and being delivered or lefte in fourme aforesaid, doo make defaulte at the same day and place assigned and appoincted in and by the sayd Precepte or Preceptes, that then the same Collectour Minister or Bailief accowmptaunte so making defaute and not appearing as ys aforesayd, and being therof dulie and lawfullie convicted, in the Courte where the Revenue ys or shalbe aunswered, shall for the first offence lose and forfayte to the King our Sovereine Lorde his whole fee for that yere wherin he shall so make defaulte, or the value therof; And for nonpayment of the said money due and paiable at or before the sayd feast of Easter unto oure sayd Sovereine Lorde the Kinge, within or by reason of his sayd Office Collecc&n or Bailiewyke, shall lose and forfaict for the first offence of none payment syxe pens of the pownd, in the name of a peyne, for every monethe after the sayd day of apparaunce untill the same money shalbee by him or his Deputie payde to thandes of the said Receivour to the Kings Majesties use: And after the first default of apparaunce made by any of the said Officers, and an other Precepte by the said Receyvour be made and delyvered or lefte in fourme aforesaid, then the sayd Officer or Officers making agayn defaulte and being therof lawfully convicte as ys aforesayd, for the seconde defaulte and offence for none apparaunce shall lose and forfeite to the King our Soverein Lorde his office and fee; And for the sayd second offence in the non paiement of the sayd money due and

And Ferther Be yt enacted by aucthorite aforesayd, That all and every Receivo" Collectoures and Bailafes of any the Kinges Honnoures Manoures Landes Tenementes Rentes or Revenues, for lack of paiment and levieng of their said Rentes Issues and Revenues within their Offices and Charges, shall and may have power and aucthorite from hensforthe by vertue of this Acte to distreine for the same, and to use and order the same distres in suche sorte and fourme as any Officer or Officers of the Kings Courte of Thexchequer for levieng and lack of payment of the Kinges Rentes and Revenues answerable in the same Courte heretofore have lawfully doon and may lawfully use to doo; delyvering to the ptie distreigned the surplusage and overplus of the valew of (1) such distres yf any shalbe, the Kings dettes and duties being first paid and the distreny'unt aunswered of reasonable costes: And that the heade and chafe Officer or Officers of every of the Kings Courtes of Revenue, being of Record or that shalbee of Recorde, shall have full powre and aucthorite by vertue of this Acte, to sett and assesse reasonable fines and amerciamentes upon any Shirief or Shiriefes for not returning or misreturning of any Write to them directed or delivered out of any of the same Courtes, touching or concerning the levieng or aunswering of any of the said Issues Rentes or Revenues, or of any dett due to our said Sovereyne Lorde the Kinge, in suche sorte and after suche maner and fourme as now ys or heretofore hathe been lawfully used in the lyke and suche other cases in the Kinges Highnes Courte of Thexchequer.

Be yt also ferther enacted by thauctoritee aforesaid, That all Treasourers and Chamberlaines and generall Receivours of any of the Kinges Graces Courtes of Revenue for the tyme being, and all Customers and Collectoures of Customes or certeyne and stalled Subsidies within any Porte Haven or Creeke of thys the Kinges Realme of Englande, that nowe bee or hereafter shalbee, within tenne dayes next after notice to him or them gyven from the King or syxe of his most Honourable Pryvye Councell in Writing signed withe their handes, shall by them selfes or theyre sufficyent Deputye or Deputyes for whom they wyll aunswere declare in Wryting what somes of Moneye then being due unto our sayd Sovereyne Lorde the Kyng bee at that tyme in his or their handes or custodye, and shall make readye and foil payment of all the sayd somes of moneye as then shall remayne in his or their handes or custodye over and above thordinarye paymentes and somes of money conteined and expressed in sufficyent Warraunte or Warrauntes resting and remayning in his or their Office or Offices, and being in their full force strengthe and effecte and not lawfollye countremaunded nor revoked to theyr Knowledge, to thuse of our Sovereine Lorde the Kyng, at suche tyme and in suche sorte as he or they shalbee comaunded and appointed by sufficyent Warraunte, upon payne of forfeyture of his or their Office or Offices.

And Be it ferther enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That the same Threasourers Chamberlaynes and Generall Receyvoures by them selfes or their Deputye or Deputyes for whom they will aunswcr, shall yerelye before the twentye daye of June make a perfecte accompte of all suche Money or Treasure as hathe comen to theyr handes to the Kynges use yerelye at or before the twentye daye of Marche then next before the sayd twentye daye of June ; and shall make a pfecte and whole declaration in writing of the money remayning in every of their handes to the Kings Majestie or to his Pryvye Councell yerelye before the last daye of June then next following, and make payment of the same, at suche tyme and in suche sorte as he or they shalbe comaunded or appointed by sufficient Warraunt, upon payne of forfeiture of his or their Office or Offices.

CHAPTER U.

An Acte for the dissolving uniting or annexing of certayne Courtes latelie erected by the King that deade ys.

WHERE in the xxvij yere of the late King of famous memorie King Henry theight father to the Kings Majestie that nowe ys, ther was ordeined made established and enacted by thaucthorite of Pliament a certeine Courte comunely called the Courte of Thaugmentacons of the Revenues of the Kings Crowne; And wher also in the xxxij yere of the said late King, ther was made and erected by aucthorite of Pleament Two severall Courtes, thone comunely called the Courte of the First Fruictes and [and' ] Tenthes, and thother the Courte of the Kinges Wardes; And where also in the xxxiij yere of the said late King, ther was made established and erected by aucthoritee of Pleament, one Courte comunely called The Courte of the Generali Surveighours of the Kings Landes; And wher ther ys one other Courte comunely called the Courte of the Duchie of Lancaster; After whiche said severall Courtes so erected as ys aforesayd, the said late King did repeale and dissolve, extinguishe and determyne, aswell the said Courte of Augmentac&n of the Revenues of the Kings Crowne, as also the said Courte of Generali Surveiours of the Kinges Landes, and Thofficers of the said late Courtes of Thaugmentacons of the Kings Crowne and Generali Surveighours of the Kings Landes did surrendre their Patentes and Offices into the sayd late Kings handes; and after, the sayd late Kyng dyd by his ires patentes erect one other Courte called The Court of Augmentac&n and Revenues of the Kings Croune, and dyd by the same his tres patentes constitute and appoint divers Officers and Mynisters for the suplyenge therof, as by the same tres patentes more playnely and at large it maye and doethe appeare: And Forasmuche as sens therecc&n of the sayd Courte of Augmentacbn and Revenues of the Kings Croune, stablyshedd and erected by tres patentf as is aforesayd, divers ambiguities and doubtes have risen and growen emong suche as be learned in the lawes of the Realme, whether [the dissolving or extinguishing and repealing of*] the sayd late Courtes erected by aucthoritee of Pleament as ys aforesayd, might by thorder of the lawe bee dissolved extinguished and repealed by tres patentes, considering that the commencement of them were first hadd and made by aucthorite of Pliament, yea or no, Wheruppon great inconveniences might ensue aswell to the Kings Majestie as to divers of his Graces most loving and obedient Subjectes who have hadd, by exchaung purchace gyfte or otherwise, divers Manours landes tenementes and other hereditamentes: For Remedy and declarac&n wherof, Bee It enacted by the King our Soverein Lorde and the Lordes and Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by thauctoritee of the same, That the said tres patentes so made by the sayd late King, and all and every thing and article therin conteyned, shalbe as good available and effectuall in the Lawe to all ententes construccons and purposes, as thoughe the same hadd been made and doon by aucthoritee of Pliament.

And where also the late King of famouse memorie Henrie theight, and also our Soverein Lorde the King Mau< that now ys, aswell by divers bargaines and sales for dyvers great somes of Money, as by giftf exchanges or otherwise, have given and granted by their severall tres patentes under the Great Seale of Englande, or under the Greate Seale of the Duchie of Lancastre, divers Manours landes tenementes and other hereditamentes withe the appurtenaunces to divers and sundry their loving Subjectes of any Estate of enheritiince, to holde in Socage onely and not in Capite for all maner of services, and without reservation of any tenthes or rentes in the same ires patentes, as by the same severall ires patentes may appeare: And Forasmuche as by certayn Statutes heretofore made, doubles and ambiguites may aryse upon suche ires patentf for lack of Tenures in Capite or reservation of Tenthes or Rentes, whiche might be hereafter to the unquietnes of suche Patentees their heires assignes or successours, contrary to thententes and inindes of the said late King and of our sayd Soverein Lorde the Kinges [Ma* ’] Majestie that now ys: For thadvoyding of all doubtes and ambyguites and for the quietnes of the Kings loving subjectes. CHAPTER VIII.

An Acte for the true fulling and thicking of Cappes.

XX THER AS in the Parliament holden at Westminster in the xxij Yere of the reigne of King Edward the iiij, great V V Grande father to the King our Sovereine Lorde that nowe ys, yt was establyshed and enacted by thaucthoride of the same Parlament, That no maner of person or persons after the feast of Easter then next following should full or thicke or cause to be fulled or thicked any Bonettes or Cappes doble or single in any sullying Mylle, or by the meane of any fulling Mill, upon payne to forfeicte and lose xl s. for every Cappe so thicked contrarye to the same Acte; And also that no Person Hatmaker Capper or other whatsoever he were after the sayd feast of Easter shoulde sett or cause to be sett any Bonettes or Cappes doble or syngle to be fulled or thicked to any suche Mill or by the mean of anye suche Mill, or setto Sale any suche Hattes Bonettes or Cappes double or single whiche after the sayd feast should bee so made fulled or thicked, upon peine to forfeict and lose the Bonettes and Cappes, so sett as ys aforesayd to any suche Mylle to bee fulled or thicked or otherweys putto Sale contrarye to the sayd Acte, and also to forfeict and lose xl s. as often as any suche person shall setto fullyng or thicking or to sale anye suche Hattes Bonettes or Cappes so thicked or putto sale contrary to the same Acte; thone half of the sayd forfeitures and penalties and every of them to the sayd late King and thother half to him or them of the Kinges Subjectes whiche shoulde sease the same or sue for the same in any of the Kinges Courtes of Recorde by informac&n, or els in any other Courte by Action of Dette by Writ at the Comune Lawe or by Bill or Plainte after the custome of the Cittye or Toune wher any suche forfeictures shall happen to fall or bee; And the Defendant in any suche Action not to bee admitted to wage his lawe nor protection nor essoine for any suche defendant shalbee allowed; whiche sayd Acte was made tendure from the sayd feaste of Easter untill thende of twoo yeres then next following and no lenger; as by the same Acte more playnely may appeare: Wheras sens the time of thexpirac&n of the sayd good & laudeable Statute, certeyn of the Subjectes of this Realme for their singuler Lucre and avayle have caused the most parte of Bonettes and Cappes made within this Realme to be fulled and thicked in fulling Mylles, by reason wherof not onely the sayd Cappes and Bonettes so thicked and fulled in fullyd Mylles, bee for the most parte broken and deceiptfiillye wrought, for that they cane not in any waise by any suche meanes of fullyng and thicking in suche Milles bee well and trewly wrought, to the greate losse of the Kings most loving Subjectes; but also a great nomber of the Kings Majesties most loving Subjectes, by whom suche Cappes and Bonettes in time paste were faithfully and truly made wrought fulled and thicked by mfnes strengthe, that ys to saye withe handes and feete, have honestly before this time gained their lyving and kepte many apprentisies and servantes in woorcke of that onely occupac&n, to the great comoditie of this Realme and the Subjectes of the same whiche nowe bee utterly decayed. And forasmuche as the said Statute ys good and profitable for the Comune wealthe of this Realme ; Owre Sovereyne Lorde the King by thassent of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporal! and the Comons in this pnte Parliament assembled and by aucthoritee of the same, hathe ordeined provided and enacted that the said Acte made in the said xxij yere of the said late King, from the Feast of Pentecoste next ensueing, shalbe revived stande and remayn in full force strengthe and effecte in all and every clause sentence penaltie and thing conteined in the same according to the tenure and effecte of the same Acte; This Acte tendure for fyve yeres next following the said feast of Pentecoste.

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte for the true making of White playne Streightes and pynned White Streightes in Devon and

Comewall.

Recital of Statute 5 k 6 E.VI. c.6.

I 5. against putting Hair, Flocks, or Lamb’s Wool into Cloths.

Certain Cloths made in Devon and Cornwall of coarse Wools, See.

WHER in the Parlament upon prorogac&n holden at Westminster the xxiij daye of Januarye in the fifthe yere of the Reigne of our Sovereyn Lorde the King that nowe ys, and ther continued unto the xv"* daye of Aprill in the vjlh yere of the Reigne of our sayd Sovereyn Lorde and then dissolved, One Acte Ordinance or Lawe was then and ther made touching and concerning the true making of Woollen Clothes, by the whiche sayd Acte emongst other Branches and Ordinaunces therin conteyned it was enacted, that from and after the feast of S' Michael! Tharchangell next ensuing the making of the sayd Acte, no persone or persons shoulde put any heire Flockes or any Yarne made withe Lambes Wooll into any Clothe Carsie Friese or Cotton so made and solde or offredd to bee solde, upon payne to forfaite every suche Clothe Carsie Frise or Cotton wherin any suche Yarne Heire or Flockes shalbe put, or the value of suche Clothe Carsie Friese or Cotton ; as by the sayd Statute it dothe and maye appear : And wher in the Cownties of Devon and Comewall in divers partes thereof ther be certeyn kindes of Clothes made of the nature of Tavestock Clothes, thone called White playn Strayghtes, and thother called pynned White Straightes, whiche sorte of Clothes be made withe the refuse and course Woolles Flockes Lambes Wool and Heire Woolles ; whiche kinde of Clothes called White playne Straightes and pynned white Streightes are transported and caryed into the partes of Brytayne beyonde the Sea, and ther uttred by the Marchauntes ther of byexchaunge and bartyre for Lynen Clothe called Doulasse Lockeram and Canvase, whiche the same Marchauntes doo afterwardes bring into this Realme to serve the Kings Majesties Subjectes therwithe, aswell duelling in the sayd Counties of Devon and Comewall as in divers other partes of the Realme:

And for asmuche as in the foresayd Acte ther ys no Remedye provided for the true making of the sayd Clothes, nor any mentyon made of the same kindes of Clothes in the sayd Acte, and therfore doubted whether they of the sayd Counties of Devon and Comewall may make the sayd kindes of Clothes or not, without Daunger of the foresaid Lawe, for that yt ys restreigned and prohibited by the sayd Acte that no persone or persones shoulde put any Heire Flockes or any Yame made of Lambes Woolle into any Clothe Fryese or Cotton so made and solde or offred to bee solde, uppon paine afore specified; And for that the said kynde of Clothes called whyte playne Streightes and pynned whyte Streyghtes ar made withe Comishe Woolle, which ys for the most part therof all Heirie Woollcs, And to thintent that from hensforthe the sayd Clothes called white Streightes and pynned white Streightes maye bee trulye made and to conteine a certeintie in Lengthe Bredthe and Weight: Be yt therefore enacted by the King our Sovereine Lorde, the Lordes Spyrytuall and Temporal! and the Comons in this pnte parliament assembled and by thaucthorytee of the same, That from and after the first Day of Maye next comyng every peice of the sayd Clothes called white playne Streightes, made after the said first Day of Maye, shall conteine in Lengthe being readye dressed to putto Sale, twelve Yardes at the least, and in Breadthe one Yarde at the least, in Weight xj " at the least, upon peine of forfayture of the same or the Value therof: And that every piece of the sayd Clothes called whyte pynned Streightes, made after the sayd first daye of Maye, being readye dressed to putto sale shall conteine in Lengthe xj Yardes at the least, and in Breadthe three quarters of a Yarde at the least, and in Weight eight powndes at the least, upon peine of forfayture of the sayd Clothes or the true Value thereof; thone Moietie of all whiche forfaytures to bee to the King our Sovereyn Lorde, and thother Moietie to him or them that will sue for the same, by Action of Dett Detinue Byll Playnte or Informac&n in any of the Kinges Courtes wherin no essoine protecfSn or wager of lawe shalbee admitted or allowed for the Defendaunte.

And ferther be yt enacted by thaucthoride aforesayd, That it shall and maye be lawfull to and for any persone or persones whatsoever, inhabiting or dwelling whithin the said Counties of Devon and Comewall or either of them, to make the foresayd sortes of Clothes withe Heire Flockes or Yarne made of Lambes Woolle or otherwise without any penaltie or forfeiture therof; The forsaid Acte made in the sayd last Parliament or any other Lawe or Statute afore this Parliament hadd or made to the contrary notwithstanding.

Be yt ferther enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That thowners or Owner of every suche Clothe and Clothes so wrought and made shall bring or cause to bee brought the same Clothe or Clothes to the next Cytye Bourghe or Towne Corporate wher the same shalbe fulled dressed and made, ther to be measured weighed and sealed withe a Seale of Leade fyxed to every of the sayd pieces of Clothe, in whiche Seale tharmes or name of every suche Cytye Bourghe or Toune Corporate shalbee graven, and that the Maior of every Cytye Bourghe or Toune corporate wher the same Clothe or Clothes shalbee brought shall appoincte and swere twoo Officers for the true weighing measuring and sealing therof, and that the same Officers shall have for their weighing measuring and sealing of everye peice of the sayd Clothes one half penny and no more.

Be yt ferther enacted by thaucthorytee aforesayd, That every Clothier or Clothyers whiche shall put any of the Clothes aforesayd to sale or offer the same to be solde, before the same bee weighed measured and sealed as ys aforesaid, shall forfaite for every suche Defaulte the Clothe or Clothes so by him or them solde or offered to be sold; Thone moitie wherof to bee to the King our Soverayne [L.‘ ] and thother moietie to him or them that will sue for the same by Action of Debte Detinue Byll Playnt or Informac&n in any of the Kinges Courtes wherin no Essoine Protection or wager of Lawe shall bee admitted or allowed for the Defendaunt.

CHAPTER XL An Acte for the continuaunce of certayne Statutes.

WHERE in the Parliament begune and holden at London the thirdd day of November in the xxj yere of the Reigne of our most dreade Sovereyn Lorde of most famous inemorye King Henry the Eight, and from thens adjourned to Westmynster, and ther holden and continued by divers prorogacbns unto the dissoluc&n therof, One Acte was made and establyshed for the restreinte of carriage and conveigheing of Horses and Mares out of this Realme: And also one other Acte was ther made in the sayd Pliament for the true making of Cables Halsers and Ropes: And also one other Acte was ther made for the true wynding of Woolles: And one other Acte was ther made to restrayne killyng of Wainlynges Bullocks Stieres and Heiefers being under thage of twoo yeres: whiche said severall Actes were then made tendure and contynue to the next Plament, as by the same [three1] severall Actes more playnlye appearethe: And wher also in the same Plament one other Acte was made and establyshed for Atteintes to be sued for the punishement of Perjurye upon untrue Veredictes; whiche [Actes*] last before rehearsed were then made and ordeyned to contynue and endure to the last day of of the nexte Plament, as by the same [severall Actes’] more playnely at large ys shewed and may appeare : And Wher also in the Plament begune and holden at Westminster theight day of June in the xxviij yere of the Reigne of our sayd most dread Soverein Lorde King Henrye theight, and ther contynued and kepte unto the dyssolution therof, yt was ordeyned and enacted, that all and singler the sayd Actes above remembred and every of them shoulde contynue and endure in their force and strengthe and also bee observed and kept untill the last day of the next Plament; That is to saie; that everie Archebusshopp Busshopp Deane Archedeacon Prebendarye Provouste Master of Colleges M' of Hospitallf Parsone Vycar, and everie other Parsone and Parsons of what so ever Name or Degree he or they be enjoying anny Spuall Promocbn or other Temporal I Possessions to the same Spuall Promocbn annexed, now not devided nor seperate by Acte of Parlyament or otherwise from the possessyon of the Clergye, shall paye to the Kings Highnes for everye pownde that he maye yerelye dispende by reasone of the saide Spuall Promocbn, the some of Sixe shillingf: And for the trewe and certaine knowledge of the yerelie vallewe of the saide Promoc&ns and everye of them wherof the payment shalbe made, the rate taxation and valuacbn and estimac&n remayning of Recorde in the Kings Ma1" Courteof the First Fruitf and Tenthe, for the payment of the perpetuall Disme, concerninge all suche Promocbns as be in possessyon of the Clergye or anny other not devided by Acte of Parlyament or otherwise as is aforesaide, shalbe followed and obs'ved withowt anny makinge anny valuacbn rate taxacon or estimacbn, other then in the saide Recorde is comprised ; CHAPTER XIV. (■)

The Kings Ma*" moste free and generall Pardone.

THE Kings moste Excellent Ma" considering his highe Power to be given unto him from Allmightie God to goveme and rule his people by distribution of Judgement and Mercie as cawses doo require, and remembring this pnt tyme into how manye penalties and daungers of Lawes sondrie his lovinge Subgectf be fallen, owt of the wrt (allthoughe they shewe them selfs mannye waies sorrie therfore) they can not be delyvered yf his Ma" shall suffer the weight and burden of Justice to remayne uppon their shoulders, is mercifullie moved by Allmightie God (in whose hands the hartes of Kings be) of reasonable pitie and Princelye bountefulnes, having on the one pte great hope of an universall amendement (by Goddes grace) of suche as have erred, and on thother parte a manifest dedarac&n in this Parlyament of the feithfull lovinge hartes of his saide Subgectf, to gr*unte and give, withowt respecte of a great increase of Treasure which might arryse by execuc&n of the penall Lawes, A generall free bountefull and beneficiall Pardone as followeth, that is to saie; That all and everie of his seid Subjects aswell Spuall as Temporall of this his Realme of Englande Wales and the Isles of Jemesey and Gernseye Barwycke and Callaice and the Marches of the same, their heires successo" executo" and administrate" of them and everie of them, and all and singuler Bodyes in anny manner of wise Corporate Cities Boroughes Shires Ridingf Hundreds Lathes Rapes Wapentakes Townes Villages and Tythingf and everie of them, and the Successo' and Successo" of everie of them, shall be by aucthoride of this pnt Parlyament acquired pardoned released and discharged against the Kings Highnes his heires successo" executo" and everie of them, of all manner Treasone Felonies Robberyes Offencf Contemptf Trespases Wronges Disceitf Misdemeano" Forfeitures Penalties and Proffittf, Somes of money, paynes of deathe, paynes corporall and pecuniarye, and generallie of all other things causes quarrellf suits judgementes and execucions, in this pnt Acte hereafter not excepted nor forprised, which may be or can be by his Highnes in anny wise or by anny meane pardoned before and unto the first daye of Februarye last past, and next before the Session of this pnt parlyament, to everie or anny of his saide Subgectf Bodies Corporate Cides Boroughes Shires Rydingf Hundredes Lathes Rapes Wapentakes Townes Villages and Tythingf or anny of them.

Provided allwaie that this Acte of generall and free Pardone or anny thing therin conteyned, shall not extende to Cardynall Poole Jeffereys Poole Doctor Hillyard Michaell Throkmerton Richard Pate Goldwell John Clement Docto' of Phisycke John Storye Docto' of the Lawe Willm11 Rastall Anthonye Bouvyce Balthaser Guarsy Surgen Benedict Bouvyce Germayne Seo, ne to Edwarde Crayforde alias Crafforthe Thomas Crayforde alias Crayfforthe Thomas Fynche Thomas Raynoldes of Whitstable in the Counrie of Kent Yeoman ne to Will*m Bedell ne to Thomas Raynoldes nor to anny of them, for anny kynde of Treasone nor for anny Fellonye Robberye wilfull murder or burglarye by them or anny of them comitted or done before the saide XXth daye of Marche in the yere of or Lorde God a thousande fyve hundred fiftie and twoo: ne to dischardge or acquite anny parsone or parsons which have procured ayded assisted or cownceled them or anny of them to breake anny Prisone or to go or flye over the Sea without the Kings Lycence ; Anny thing in this Acte of Fre Pardone to the contrarie in anny wise notwithstanding.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte repealing certayne Treasons Felonies and Premunire.

The State of a King more aisured by the Love of hit Subjects than in the fear of rigorous Laws;

Unusual Punishments under former Laws;

No Act or Offence shall be Treason, Petty Treason,

nr Misprision of Treason, but such as be so declared by Stat. 2$ E.I1I. st. 5. c.2.

II.

Exception of Persons imprisoned, Arc. for Treason before a certain Day.

III.

All Offences made Felony, or within the Case of Premunire, since beginning of K. Henry VIII s Reign, repealed.

FORASMUCHE as the State of every King Ruler and Govemour of any Realme Domynyon or Comynaltie standith and consistethe more assured by the love and favor of the Subjecte towarde their Sovereine Ruler and Governour, then in the dreade and feare of Lawes made withe rygorous paynes and extreame punishement for not obeyeng of their Sovereine Ruler and Govemour; And Lawes also justly made for the preservac&n of the Cdmune Weale, without extreame punishment or greate penaltie, arre more often for the most parte obeied and kepte, then Lawes and Statutes made with greate and extreame punishementes, and in especiall suche Lawes and Statutes so made, wherby not onelye the ignoraunte and rude unlearned people, but also learned and expert people myndyng honestye, are often and many tymes trapped and snared, yea many times for woordes onelye without other facte or dede doone or perpetrated: The Quenes most Excellent Majestye calling to remembraunce that many, aswell honorable and noble persones as other of good reputacbn within this her Graces Realme of England, have of late, for Woordes onelye without other [opinion1 ] facte or dede, suffredd shamefull Deathe not accustomed to Nobles j Her Highnes therfore of her accustomed elemeneye and mercyc, myndinge to avoyde and put awaye thoccasion and cause of lyke chaunces hereafter to ensue, trusting her loving Subjectes will for her elemeneye to them shewed, love serve and obeye her Grace the more hartely and faithefully then for dread or feare of paynes of bodye, ys contented and pleased that the severetye of suche lyke extreame daungerous and paynfull Lawes shalbe abolished adnulled and made frustrate and voide: Be it therfore ordeined and enacted by the Quene our Sovereine Ladye with the assent of the Lordes Spiritaal 1 and Temporall and of the Comons in this pnte Parliamente assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same. That from hensforthe none Acte Dede or Offence, being by Acte of Plyament or Statute made Treasone petite Treasone or Misprision of Treason, by woordes writing ciphering dedes or otherwise whatsoever, shalbee taken hadd demed or adjudged to be Highe Treason petite Treason or Misprision of Treason, but onely suche as bee declared and expressed to bee Treason petite Treason or Mysprision of Treason in or by thacte of Plyament or Statute made in the fyve and twentye yere of the Reigne of the most noble King of famous memorye King Edwarde (1 ) Thirde, touching or concerning Treason or the declarac&ns of Treasons, and none other; Nor that any peines of Deathe Penaltye or Forfeyture in eny wise ensue or bee to any Offendour or Offendoures for the doing or comitting any Treason petite Treason or misprision of Treasone, other then suche as be in the said Estatute, made in the said XXVth yere of the Reigne of the sayd King Edwarde the Third, ordeyned and provided; Any Acte or Actes of Plyament Statute or Statutes hadd or made at any tyme heretofore, or after the said XXVth yere of the Reigne of the sayd late King Edwarde the Thirde, or any other declarac&n or matter to the contrarye in any wise notwithestanding.

Provided alwaies and be yt ordeined and enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That this Acte of Plament, or any thing therin mentioned, shall not in any wise extende to give any maner of benefite advauntage or comoditie to any persone or persones being, the last daye of September last, past arrested or imprisoned for Treason petite Treasone or Misprision of Treason, or to any persone or persones heretofore being indicted of Treason petite Treason or Misprision of Treason, or being outlawed or attainted of Treason petite Treason or Misprision of Treason, before the said last daye of September last past, or being comaunded to kepe his or their howse or houses or other mens howses, or otherwise excepted out of the Quenes Highnes most gracyous Pardon geven the daye of her Coronacon; But that they and every of them for any thoffences before mentioned, perpetrated comitted or doon by them or any of them before the sayd last daye of September, shall suffer suche paynes of Deathe Losses and Forfeitures of Landes and Gooddes, as in cases of Treason, as thoughe this Acte hadd never been hadd ne made; Any thing in this Acte to the contrarye in any wise notwithestanding.

And Be yt further ordeined and enacted by thauctoritee aforesayd, That all Offences made Felonye, or lymited or appointed to be within the cace of Premunire, by any Acte or Actes of Pleament, Statute or Statutes made sithens the first daye of the first yere of the Reigne of the late King of famous memorye King Henrye theight, not being Felony before, nor within the cace of Premunire, and also all and every Braunche Article and Clause mentioned or in any wise declared in any of the same Estatutes concerning the making of any Offence or Offences to be Felonye, or within the cace of Premunire, not being Felonye nor within the cace of Premunire before, and all peines and forfeitures concerning the same or any of them, shall from hensforthe bee repealed and utterlye voide and of none effect.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte declaring the Quenes Hyghnes to have bene borne in a most just and lawfull Matrimonie, and also repealing all Actes of Pliament and Sentences of Divorce hadd and made to the contrarie.

FORASMUCHE as Truthe, being of her own Nature of a most excellent vertue efficacie force and worcking, can not but by processe of tyme break out and shewe her self, howesoever for awhile she maye by thiniquitie and frailetie of Man be suppressed and kepte close; And being revealed and manifested, ought to be embraced acknowledged confessed and professed in all cases and matters whatsoever and whomsoever they touche or conceme without respecte of persons, But in suche cases and matters speciallye, as wherby the glorye and honour of God in Heven (who ys thaucthour of truthe and truthe it self) is to be speciallye setfurthe, and wherby also the Honour Dignitie Suertie and preservation of the Prince and Ruler (under God) in Earthe dependethe, and the welfare profitt and specyall benefiteof the Universall People and Bodye of a Realme is to be continued and maynteyned: We Youre Highnes most loving faithfull and obedient Subjectes understanding the verye truthe of the State of Matriinonye betwen the Twoo most Excellent Princes of most worthye memorye King Henrye the Eight and Quene Katheryne, his loving godlye and lawful Wief, your Highnes lawfull Father and Mother, can not but thinck Our selfe most bownden bothe by our Dutie of Allegeance to yor Majestie and of Conscience towarde God, to shewe unto yo' Highnes, first howe that the same Matrimonie being contracted solempnised and consumated by thagreament and assent of bothe their moste noble Parentes, by the councell and advice of the most wise and g'avest men of bothe their Realmes, by the deliberate and mature considerac&n and consent of the beste and most notable Men in learning in those days of Christendome, dyd even so continewe by the space of twentye yeres and more betwen them, to the pleasure of Almightye God the Satisfaction of the Worlde the Joye and Comforte of all the Subjectes of this Realme, and to their owne Repose and goodd Contentement, God gyving for a sewer token and testimonie of his goodd acceptac&n of the same not onelye godlye fruite (yor Highnes moste noble Person) whom wee beseche Thalmightye and ever lyving God long to prosper and preserve here amongest Us, and other yssue also, whom it hathe pleased God to take out of this transitorie lief unto his Etemall Glorie, but also sending us a happie florishing and most prosperous Comon Wealthe in all thinges; And then afterwardes howe that the malicious and perverse affections of somrne a verye fewe persones, envyeng the greate Felicitee wherin, by the goodnes of God, yo' said most noble Father and Mother and all their goodd Subjectes lyved and continued in manye yeres, dyd for their own singuler Glorye and vayn Reputac&n, conceyve sundrye subtile and disloyall practises for the interruption and breache of the sayd most lawfull and godly Concorde, and travelling to putt the same in Ure, devised first to insinuate a Scruple into the King yo' Fathers Conscience of an unlawfull Marriage betwen him and his most lawfull Wyef the Quene yo’ Highnes Mother, pretending for the grownde therof that the same was against the woorde of God; And theruppon ceased not to persuade continually unto the said King yo' Father, that he coulde not without daunger of the losse of his Soule, continue withe his sayd most lawfull Wyef but must bee seperated and dyvorsed from her; And to this Entent cawsed the Seales as well of certayne Universitees in Italie and France to be gotte as it were for a testimonie, by the corruption withe moneye of a fewe light persons, Scolers of the same Universities, As also the Seales of the Universitees of this Realme to be obteyned by greate travaile synister worckingf secrett threatningf and entreatinges of some Men of aucthoritee speciallye sent thither at that time for the same purposes; And howe that finallye Thomas Cranmer then newlie made Archebishoppe of Cantorburie, most ungodly and against all Lawes Equitie and Conscience prosecuting the said wicked devise of Devorse and Seperation of the said King yo' Father and Quene yo' Mother, called before him Ex Officio the hearing of the sayd matter of Marriage, and taking his foundac&n partely upon his owne unadvised Judgment

CHAPTER II.

An Acte for the Repeale of certayne Statutes made in the time of the Raigne of Kinge Edwarde the Syxthe.

FORASMUCHE as by dyvers and severall Actes hereafter mentioned, aswell the Dyvine service and goodde administracbn of the Sacramentes, as dyvers other matters of Religion whiche We and our Forefathers founde in this Churche of Englande to us lefte by thaucthoritee of the Catholyke Churche, bee partely altered and in some parte taken from Us, and in place therof newe thinges imagined and set for the by the sayd Actes, suche as a fewe of singularitie have of themselves devised, wherof hathe ensewed amongest Us in verie shorte time numbers of divers and straung Opinions and diversitees of Sectes, and therby growen greate unquietnes and muche discorde, to the greate disturbance of the C.omon wealthe of this Realme, and in very shorte time lyke to growe to extreame perill and utter confusion of the same, onles some Remedye bee in that behalf provided, whiche thing all true loving [Subjectes'] and obedient Subjectes ought and are bounden to foresee and provide to thutttermost of their power: In Consideration wherof Be it enacted and establishedd by the Quenes Highnes the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the C.omons in this same pnt Pliament assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same. That an Acte made in the Pliament begonne at Westminster the fourthe daye of November in the first yere of the raigne of the late King Edwarde the Syxthe, and from thens continued to the xxiiij day of December then next ensuing, that is to saye, in the first Session of the same Pliament, intituled, An Acte against suche parsons as shoulde unreverentlye speake against the Sacrament of the Bodye and Bloude of Christ, comonlye called the Sacrament of the Alter, and for the receyving therof in bothe kindes; And also One other Acte in the same Session, whiche is intituled, An Acte for thelecc&n of Bishoppes, and what seales and stiles they and other spuall parsons exercising jurisdiccon Ecclesiastical 1 shoulde use; And also one other Acte made in one other Session of the said Pliament holden upon prorogation at Westminster the fourthe daye of November in the seconde yere of the raigne of the said late Kinge Edwarde the Sixthe and ther continued and kepte to the xiiij daye of Marche in the thirde yere of the said late Kings reigne, intituled, An Acte for the Uniformitie of Service and administration of the Sacramentes throughout the Realme; And also one other Acte made in the Session last before [named 1 ] whiche is intituled, An Acte to take awaye all positive Lawes made against the mariage of Priestes; And also one other Acte made in one other Session of the said Pliament holden upon prorogacbn at Westminster the fourthe daye of November in the thirde yere of the raigne of the sayd late King Edwarde the Sixte and ther continued and kepte to the first daye of Februarie in the fourthe yere of his raigne, intituled, An Acte for thabolishing and putting awaye of divers Bookes and Images; And also one other Acte made in the same Session last before mentioned, intituled, An Acte made for thordering of the Ecclesiasticall Ministers; And also one other Acte made in one other Session of the said Pliament holden upon prorogation at Westminster the xxiij day of Januarie in the fifthe yere of the Reigne of the sayd late King Edwarde the Syxte, and ther continued and kepte till the xvlh daye of Aprill in the syxte yere of the Reigne of the sayd late King, intituled, An Acte for the Uniformitie of Comon Prayour and thadministracon of the Sacramentes ; And one other Acte made in the same last Session, intituled, An Acte for the keping of Holye dayes and Fasting daies; And one other Acte made in the Session last recited, intituled, An Acte made for the Declaration of a Statute made for the Mariage of Preistes and for the legittimacbn of their children; And everye Clause Sentence Braunche Article and Articles mentioned expressed or conteined in the said Estatutes and in everye of them, shalbee from hensforthe utterly repelled voide adnichillate and of none effecte, to all purposes construccftns and internes; Any thing or thinges conteined or specifiedd in the sayd Estatutes or any of them to the contrarie in any wise notwithestanding.

And Be it furthere enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, that all suche Divine Service and Administration of Sacramentes, as were most comonly used in the Realme of Englande, in the last yere of the reigne of our late Sovereine Lorde King Henrie theight, shall bee from and after the xx"1 daye of December, in this pnte yere of our Lorde God One thowsande five hundrethe fiftie and three, used and frequented throughe the hole Realme of Englande, and all other the Quenes Majesties Dominions; And that no other kinde nor order of Divine Service nor Administratyon of Sacrates be after the said XXth daye of December used or ministredd, in any other maner fourme or degree within the said Realme of Englande or other the Quenes Dominions, then was most comonly used ministred and frequented in the said last yere of the Raigne of the said late King Henrye the Eight.

And Be it further enacted by the aucthoritee aforesaid, That no person shall be empeached or molested in body or gooddes, for using, heretofore or untill the said xx* day of December, the Divine Service mentioned in the said Actes or any of them, nor for the using of the olde Dyvine Service and Administration of Sacramentes, in suche manner and fourme as was used in the Churche of Englande before the making of any of the said Actes.
