CHAPTER III.

An Acte against Offenders of Preachers and other Ministers in the Churche.

FORASMUCHE as it is most necessary in every Christian Comonwelthe, to provide that Tranquilite and Peace maye bee preserved and continued amonges the People, and specially in Holye Churche in the tyme of Divine Service and Administration of Sacramentes and Sacramentalles, as before this time it hathe been accustomed in Holy Churche within this Realme, and that all things being contrarye theronto, or that are or maye bee in disturbance therof, maye by foresight be eschewed and avoided, and Remedie therfore in due tyme provided, aswell for the preservac&n of the Quenes Highnes peace, as for an universall Quietnes and Order to be used within this Realme: Be it therfore enacted by the Quene our Soveraigne Ladye the Lordf Spuall and Temporall and Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by the aucthoritee of the same. That yf any pson or psons of their own power and aucthorite, at any time or times after the xx'h daye of December nexte coming, doo or shall willinglye and of purpose by open and overt woorde facte acte or dede, maliciouslye or contemptuouslye molest let disturbe vexe or troble, or by any other unlawfull waies or meanes disquiet or misuse, any Preachour or Preachours that nowe ys or that at any rime or times hereafter shall be lycensed allowed or aucthorised to preache, by the Quenes Highnes, or by any Archebishoppe or Bishoppe of this Realme, or by any other lawfull Ordinarie, or by any of the Universities of Oxforde and Cambridge, or otherwise lawfully aucthorised or chardged by reason of his or their Cure Benefice or other spuall Promotion or Charge, in any of his or their open Sermon Preaching or Collation that he or they shall make declare preache or pronounce in any Churche Chapell Churchyarde or in any other place or places used frequented or appointed, or that hereafter shalbee used or appointed to be preached in ; Or if anie person or persons after the sayd xx,h day of December next coming, shall maliciouslye willinglie or of purpose molest lett disturbe vexe disquiete or otherwise troble any Person Vicar Parishe Preist or Curate, or any lawfull Preist, preparing saieng doing singing ministring or celebrating the Masse or other such Divine Service Sacramentes or Sacramentalles as was most comonly frequented and used in the last yere of the Raigne of the late Sovereine Lorde King Henrye theigKt, or that at anye rime hereafter shalbe allowedd sett for the or aucthorised by the Quenes Majestie ; Or if anye person or persones, at any rime or times after the said xx" daye of December, shall contemptuouslye unlawfullye or maliciouslie of their owne power or aucthoritie, pull downe deface spoile abuse breake or otherwise unreverentlye handle or order the most Blessed Comfortable and Holy Sacrament of the Body and Bloude of our Saviour Jesus Christ, comonly called the Sacrament of the Aulter, being or that shall bee in anye Churche or Chappell or in any other decent place, or the Pixe or Canapie wherin the same Sacrament is or shalbee; Or unlawfully contemptuously or maliciouslye of their own power and aucthoritie pull down deface spoile or otherwise breake any Aulter or Aulters or any Crucifixe or Crosse that nowe or hereafter shalbee in any Churche Chappell or Churchyarde} That then every suche Offendour and Offenders in any the Premisses, his or their aydour procurour or abettour, aidours procurours or abettours, immediatelye and forthwithe after any of the said Acte or Actes or other the said misdemeanours so comitted doone or made or (1 ) any time or times after, shalbe apprehended arrested and taken by anye Constable or Constables Churchwardein or Churchwardeines of the sayd Parishe Towne or Place where the said Offence or Offences shalbe so comitted made or doone, or by any other Officer or Officers, or by any other person or persons then being present at the time of the said Offence or Offences so unlaufully comitted made or doone; Whiche person or persons so apprehended taken or arrestedd, withe convenient spede shall bee brought and caried to any Justice of Peace within the sayd Shire, or within any Citie Borowe Libertie or Towne Corporate wherin Justices of Peace bee, wher the said Offence or Offences shall bee so comitted done and made; and that the sayd Justice of Peace, upon due accusation therupon hadd and made, by the apprehendour or apprehendours or other person or persons, of any of the said person or persons so offending, forthwithe shall comitt the said person or persons so apprehended arrested and taken, to safe keping and custodie, as by the discretion of the said Justice shall be thought most meete and convenient; And that within sixe dayes nexte and immediatelye after the said accusation so hadd and made to the said Justice, the said Justice withe one other Justice of Peace in the said Shire Citie Burghe Libertie or Towne Corporate, shall diligentlye examine the Acte or Actes Offence or Offences aforesaid; And if they the said twoo Jusricesof Peace shall upon their said examination, finde or perceyve the said person or persons so accused, giltie of any of the said Offence or Offences wherof he or thei shall be so accused, and that by twoo sufficient Witnesses, or by his or their owne confession or confessions, that then and immediatlye withe convenient spede, the said twoo Justices shall comit and award the said person or persons so accused as is aforesaid, to the Gayle of or for the said Shire Citie Borowe Libertie or Towne Corporate wher the said Offence or Offences was so comitted made or doon, there to remaine without baile or maineprise by the space of three Monethes then next ensueng, and further to the next Quarter Sessions to be holden within the said Shire Citie Bourghe Libertye or Towne Corporate nexte after the ende of the said three Monethes; At whiche said Quarter Sessions the said pson or persones so comitted to the Gaile as is aforesayd, upon his or their reconsilyacon and repentance in that behalfe, before the sayd Justices of Peace at the said Sessions, shalbe delyvered and dischardged out of Prison and Gayle, uppon sufficient suertie of his good abearing and behavour, to be then and ther taken by the said Justices for one hole yere then next ensuing, as by the discretion or discretions of the sayd Justices then and ther being, or of the more parte of them, shalbe thought mete and convenient; And if the sayd person or persons so in Gaile as ys aforesaid, will not be reconciled and repent at the said Quarter Sessions, that then the said person or persons immediatly in time convenient, shalbe further awarded and comitted to the said Gaile by the said Justices or by the more part of them, there to remayne without baile or maineprise, untill he or thei so comitted and awarded to Gaile as is aforesaid, shalbe reconciled and be penitent for his or their sayd Offence or Offences.

(') Provided Alwaies and be yt enacted, That whatsoever person offending in the premisses shall for any of the Offences afore recited receive punishement of the Ordinarie, having a testimoniall therof under the said Ordinaries Seale, shall not for the same Offence eftesones be convicted before the Justice; and in lykewise receiving for the said Offences punishement by the Justice, he shall not for the same Offence eftesones receive punishement of thordinarie: Any thing in this Acte to the contrary notwithestanding.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte touching Writinges made from the syxthe daye of Julye last paste, and before the first daye of August

then nexte ensuenge.

TTY THERE it hathe pleased Almightie God, the syxte daye of Julye last paste, to call out of this transitorie lyes V ▼ unto his Mercie, Our late Sovereine Lorde King Edwarde the Syxte; By and immediatelye after whose deathe the Imperiall Crowne of this Realme, with all Dignifies Dominions Honours Preheminences Prerogatives Stiles Authorities and Jurisdice&ns to the same united annexed or belonging, dyd not onelye discende remayne and come unto our most dreade Soverein Ladye the Quenes Majestie, But also the same was then immediatelye and lawfully invested demed and judged in her Highnes most Roiall person, by the due course of Inheritance and by the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme; Nevertheles the same her Highnes most lawfull possession was for a time disturbed and disquieted by the Trayterous Rebellion and Usurpac&n of the Lady Jane Dudley, wief unto Guildeford Dudley, Esquire, otherwise called the Ladye Jane Greye, and other her complices, during the time of the whiche sayde Rebellyon and Usurpation, dyvers Estatutes Recognisaunces Indentures Obligac&ns Acquitances Grauntes Patentes Evidences and other Writinges were made and devised betwen and to sundrye of the Subjects of this Realme, Whereupon divers questions suites & doughtes may hereafter arise growe and ensue to many of the Quenes Highnes true loving Subjectes: For the avoiding of all whiche ambiguities and doubtes whiche by reason therof may be stirred or moved; Be It enacted and ordeyned. That all Estatutes Recognisaunces Indentures and other Writinges whatsoever knowleddged or made by or to any Person or Persons Bodies Politique or Corporate being the Quenes Subjectes, since the sixte daye of Julye last paste, and before the firste day of Auguste then next following, under the name of the Reigne of any other person then under the name of our Sovereigne Ladye the Quene, shalbe as good and effectuall in the Law to all intentes purposes constructions and meaninges, as if uppon the making thereof the name of our Sovereigne Ladye the Quenes Majestie, withe her Stile appropriate and united unto her Majesties Imperiall Crowne, hadd bene fully and playnlye expressed and conteined in the same Obligac6ns Recognisances Indentures Estatutes and other Writinges; And that the

CHAPTER VI.

An Acte against counterfeiting of straunge Coignes being currant within this Realme, or of the Quenes Highnes Signe Manuell Sygnet or Privie Seale.

FORASMUCHE as by the Lawes of this Realme, small and no due condigne punishement is at this pnte time provided for suche evill disposed persons as shall counterfeite or fordge such kinde of Gold or Silver of other Realmes as is not the proper Coigne of this Realme, and yet permitted and suffered by the Quene our Soveraigne Ladyes consent, and heretofore hathe bene permitted and suffered by the consent of her most noble Progenitours, to be currant in payment within this her Realme, nor for suche persons as shall counterfeite the Quenes Highnes Signe Manuell her Privie Signet or Privie Seale; By Reason wherof divers evell disposed persons ar encouraged and boldened daylye to perpetrate and committ the sayd severall Offences : For Remedie wherof Be it enacted by our said Soveraigne Ladie the Quene the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same, That if any person or persons hereafter falselye forge and counterfeite any such kinde of Coine of Golde or Sylver as is not the proper Come of this Realme, and is or shalbe current within this Realme by the consent of the Quene her heires or successoures, Or if any person or persons at any tyme hereafter doo falslye forge or counterfeite the Quenes Signe Manuell Privie Signet or Privie Seale, That then every such Offence shall be deemed and judged Highe Treason; and thoffendours therin, their counseylours procurers ayders and abettors, beinge convicte according to the Lawes of this Realme of any of the saide Offences, shalbe lykewise demed and adjudged Traytours agenst the Quene her heires and successoures and the Realme, and shall suffer and have suche paynes of Deathe forfeiture of landes goodes and cattelles, and also lose the privilege of all Sanctuarie, as in cace of Highe Treason it is used and ordeined.

CHAPTER VB.

An Acte touching Proclamations upon Fines.

"TXTHERAS upon Fines levied withe Proclamations, doubtes have of late risen, by occasion of adjournement of V V Termes in whiche Proclamac&ns shoulde have been made, according to the fourme limitted for Proclamac&ns upon Fines by the Statute made in the fourthe yere of King Henry the Seventhe, and were not by reason of suche adjoumementes hadd ne made, according to the purvey of the same Estatute : Be it therfore enacted, That all Fines, aswell heretofore levied as hereafter to bee levied before the Justices of the Comon Place, of any Manours landes tenementes or other hereditamentes, whereupon the Proclamations hathe not or shall not by reason of adjournement of any Terme by Writte bee dulye made, shalbe of as good force effecte and strengthe to all internes constructions and purposes, as yf any Terme heretofore so adjourned, or that at any time hereafter shall bee so adjourned, hadd been holden and kepte from the begginning to the ende therof not adjourned, and Proclamations therin made according to the fourme and effecte of the sayd Estatute.

Provided alwaies that this Acte shall not in any wise extende to any Fine heretofore levied of any Manours landes tenementes or hereditamentes, now in suite demande or variance in any of the Quenes Courtes, or wherof any Charters Evidences or Munimentes concerning the same bee now in demaunde in the Quenes Highe Court of Chancerye, Nor to any Fine or Fines heretofore levied of any Manours landes tenementes or hereditamentes whiche, before the first daye of this presente Pliament, have beene recovered gotten or obteined by reason of any Judgement Entre Decree Arbitrement or other lawfull meanes, contrary to the purporte entent or effecte of any such Fine or Fines therof heretofore levied.

CHAPTER Vin.

An Acts that Shiriffes shall not be Justices of Peace during that Office.

WHERE in one Acte of Pliament, intituled, An Acte for the continuance of Actions after the deathe of any King, made in the first yere of our late Sovereigne Lorde King Edwarde the Syxthe, amongest other things it is ordeined and enacted, that albeit any persone or persons being Justice of Assise Justice of Gaole Delyverye or Justice of Peace within any of the Kings Dominions, or being in any other of the Kings Comissions whatsoever, shall fortune to be made Duke Archebyshoppe Marques Erie Viscounte Baron Bishoppe Knight Justice of thone Benche or of the other, or Sargeaunte at the Lawe or Shreiff, yet that notwithstanding, he and they shoulde remayne Justice and Comissioner, and have full power and aucthorite texecute the same, in like maner and fourme as he or they might or ought to have doone before the same; as in the saide Acte more playnly appearethe: Sythens the making of the whiche Acte divers persons being in the Comission of the Peace in one Countie have beene made Sheriffes of the same Countie, and have exercised either of the sayd Offices whiche semethe not to bee convenient: Wherfore Be it enacted by thaucthorite of this pnte Pliament, That no maner of jeon or psons, having using or exercising the Office of the Sheriffe of any Cowntye or Counties, shall use or exercise the Office of the Justice of the Peace by force of any Comission or otherwise, in any Countie or Counties where he or they shalbe Sheriffe, during the time onely that he or they shall use or exercise the sayd Office [or1] Sheriffwike; Any thing in the said former Acte to the contrarie in any wise notwithstanding: And that all and every Acte and Actes to be doon by any suche Sheriff or Sheriffes by aucthorite of any Comission of the Peace during the time abovesaid, shall be voide and of none effecte; The said former Acte notwithstanding.

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte touching thincorporations of the Phisitions in London.

WHERE in the Pliament holden at London the xv daye of Aprill in the xiiij yere of the Raigne of our late Soveraygne Lorde King Henrie theight, and from thens adjourned to Westminster the last daye of Julye in the xvlh yere of the Raigne of the same King, and ther holden; It was Enacted, that a certeyne graunte by Letters Patentes of IncorporacSn, made and graunted by our said late King to the Phisitions of London, and all Clauses and Articles conteined in the same Graunte shoulde be approved graunted ratified and confirmed by the same Parliament: For. the Consideration therof be it enacted by aucthorite of this pnte Pliament, That the sayd Statute or Acte of Pliament, withe every Article and Clause therin conteined, shall from hensforthe stande and continue still in full strengthe force and effecte; Any Acte Statute Lawe Custome or any other thing made hadd or used to the contrarye in any wise notwithstanding.

And for the better Reformation of divers Enormities happening to the Comonwelthe by the evill using and undue administration of Phisick, and for the enlarging of further Articles for the better execuc&n of the things conteined in the said graunt Enacted; Be it therfore nowe enacted, That whensoever the Presidente of the Colledge or Comonaltie of the Facultie of Physicke of London for the time being, or such as the said President and Colledge shall yerely according to the tenor and meaning of the said Acte aucthorise to searche examine correcte and punishe all Offendours and Transgressours in the said Facultie within the same Citie and Precincte in the said Acte expressed, shall sende or comit any suche Offendour or Offendours, for his or their offences or disobedience contrarye to any Article or Clause conteyned in the said Graunte or Acte, to any Warde Gayle or Pryson within the same Citie and Precincte, (the Towre of London except,) that then from time to tyme the Warden Gaolour or Keper, Wardeines Geylours or Kepers of the Wardes Gayles or Prisons within the Citie or Precincte aforesayd (excepte before excepted) shall receyve into his or their Prisons all and every suche persone and persons so offending, as shalbe so sent or comitted to him or them as is aforesayd, and ther shall safely kepe the person or persons so comitted in any of their Prisons, at the proper costes and chardges of the said person or persons so comitted, without Bayle or Mayneprise, untill suche time as such Offendour or Offendors or disobedientes be dischardged of the said Imprisonement by the said President, and suche persons as by the said Colledge shalbe therunto aucthorised; upon payn that all and every suche Wardeyn Gaylo' or Keper doing the contrary shall lose and forfeite the double of suche Fine and Amerciament, as suche Offender and Offenders or disobedientes shalbe assessed to paye, by suche as the said President and Colledge shall aucthorise as aforesaid. So that the same Fyne and Amerciament bee not at any one tyme above the some of Twentye powndes; The moitie therof to be employed to thuse of our Soveraygne Ladye the Quene her heires and successoures, thother moitie unto the said President and Colledge: All whiche Forfeitures to be recovered by accon of Dett Bill Plainte or Information in any of the Queues her heires and successoures Courtes of Recorde, against any suche Wardeyn Gaylour or Keper so offending; In whiche suite no Essoigne wager of Lawe nor Proteccion shall be allowed ne admitted for the Defendant.

CHAPTER X.

An Acte for the uniting dissolving or newe erecting of Courtes.

WHERE in the Session of the Parliament holden & begune at Westminster the firste daye of Marche, in the seventhe yere of the Reigne of our late Sovereigne Lorde of most famouse and worthye memorie King Edwarde the Sixte, and ther continued to the dissolution of the same being the last daye of the said monethe of Marche, amongest other Actes it was enacted by thauctoritye of the said Pliament, That the Kinges Majestie shoulde or might at any time during his naturall lyes, by his Graces Letters Patentes under his Greate Seale of Englande, at his most gratious will and pleasure, alter change unite transpose dissolve or determine all or any of the Courtes comonly called the Courte of thaugmentaeftns of the Revenues of the Kinges Crowne, the Courte of the First Fruites and Tenthes, the Courte of the Kinges Wardes, the Court of the Generali Surveiours of the Kinges Landes, and the Courte of the Duchie of Lancastree; and to reduce the same Courtes or any of them into one twoo or more Courte or Courtes, or to unite and annexe the said Courtes or any twoo or more of them together, or to any other his Majesties Courtes of Recorde, or to erecte any other newe Courte or Courtes, as to his Highnes shoulde have bene thought most convenient and best for the better surer and more spedye aunswering of his yerely Revenues Casualties or Profites aunswerable in the said Courtes or in any of them; And that all and singter such alterations chaunginges unitinges annexinges transposinges dissolvinges or determinacons of the said Courtes or of any of them, so by his Highnes to be altered chaunged united annexed transposed dissolved or determined or otherwise, so to have bene erected by the said King concerning order for the true payment of his Revenues Rents Issues Casualties and Proffites, as shoulde bee set for the and declared in any suche his Letters Patentes or Writinges under his Greate Seale of Englande, by his Highnes to be made set for the and declared, shoulde have bene of suche lyke and of the same force and strength to all internes construcc&ns and purposes, as thoughe the same were or shoulde have bene set for the or declared by thaucthoritee of Pliament; Therection of the said severall Courtes, or any other thing hadd or made before the making of the said Acte to the contrarye in any wise notwithestanding: As by the sayd Acte more playnely it dothe and maye appeare: Sithens the making of whiche Acte it hath pleased Almightye God to take unto his Mercye our said late Sovereigne Lorde King Edwarde the Syxthe, before any alteration unityng transposyng dissolving or determining of any of the sayd Courtes by his Letters Patentes, according to the tenour of the saide Acte: In consideration wherof, and to thintent that the Quenes Highnes maye at all times herafter during her Highnes lyes, (which Almighty God long preserve,) alter chaunge unite transpose dissolve determine or reduce the same Courtes or any of them into one twoo or more Courtes, at her Highnes free will and pleasure, Be it therfore enacted by thaucthorite of this pnte Pliament, That the Quenes Highnes shall or may at any tyme hereafter during her naturall lyes, by her Graces Ires patentes under her Greate Seale of Englande, at her most gracious will and pleasure, alter chaunge unite transpose dissolve or determine all or any of the said Courte or Courtes, and to reduce the same Courtes or any of them into one two or more Courte or Courtes; or to unite and annexe the said Courtes or any twoo or more of them together, or to any other of her Majesties Courtes of Recorde, or to erecte of the same any other newe Courte or Courtes, as to her Highnes shalbee thought most convenient and best for the better surer and more spedye aunswering of her yerely Revenues Casualties or Profites now aunswerable in the said Courtes or in any of them: And that all and singler suche alterafons chaunginges unitinges transposinges dissolvinges or determinacons of the said Courtes, or any of them, so to be altered chaunged united annexed transposed dissolved or determined, or otherwise newly to be erected as is aforesayd, and concerning all and every order for the true paiment of the Revenues Rentes Yssues Casualties and Profites of our said Soveraygne Ladye the Quene, nowe aunswerable in the said Courtes or in any of them, as shalbe set for the and declared in any such Ires patentes or writings, under her Highnes Greate Seale of Englande hereafter to be made set for the and declared, shall bee of suche lyke and of the same force

CHAPTER XI.

An Acte for the sale of Hattes and Cappes made beyonde the Sea.

WHERE in the Parliament holden at Westminster in the xxj* yere of the reigne of our late Sovereine Lorde King Henry theight, Father onto our Soveraygne Ladye the Quene: It was amongest other thinges ordeined established and enacted, That no maner of person or persons whatsoever he or they were, shoulde from the Feast of the Purificac&n of our Ladye then next following after the making of the said Acte, sell or cause to be solde within this Realme of Englande, to any person or persons, any Wollen Hattes or Bonettes or Wollen Hatt or Cappe made or to be made in any place or places out of this Realme of Englande in anie of the parties beyonde the See, over and above the prices limited in the said Acte; that is to saye, that no suche Cappe or Bonett shoulde bee solde above the some of twoo Shillinges sterling, and that no suche Hatt shoulde be solde above the some of tenne pens, and that no suche single crowned Cappe nor single Night Cappe shoulde be solde above the some of syxe pens, upon payne to forfeite for every suche Bonet Cappe or Hatt that at any time after the sayd Feast shoulde bee solde over the price abovesayd, contrarye to the tenour of the said Acte xl s. sterling: as by the said Acte more at large dothe appeare: Since the making of whiche Acte, for lacke and wante of the due execution of the same, great nomber and plentye of the sayd Bonettes Hattes and Cappes have been and yet bee solde within this Realme at greate and unreasonable prices, muche over and above the prices lymited and appointed by the said Acte, Not onely to the greate and manifest deceipte of the Commons of this Realme, but also to the greate impoverishement of the Subjectes of the same ; Wherfore be it enacted and established by the Quenes Highnes, by thassent of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this present Filament assembled and by thaucthoride of the same. That the sayd Acte made in the sayd one and twentythe yere, and every thing article clause braunche and proviso therin mentioned, shall stande in full strengthe force and effecte.

And for the better and more perfecte due and just execution of the sayd Acte hereafter to be had according to the true meaning and intent of the Makers therof; Be it nowe further by thaucthoritie aforesaid provided established and enacted, that yf any such Bonettes Cappes or Hattes, fortune hereafter to be brought from any the pties beyond the See, into any place or places within this Realme or any the Quenes Dominions, after the last daye of Maye next comming, that then all such Bonettes Cappes and Hattes shalbee brought by the Owner of them or his Servante, to the Customer or Customers of every Citie Boroughe Towne Place or Porte within this Realme, wher such Hattes or Bonettes shalbe layde on Lande or dischardged, ther to enter into the Customer or Customers bookes the Custome for them, and to pay such Custome for them as by the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme they or any of them have used, or ought heretofore to doo. Upon payne of forfeiture of all suche Cappes and Hattes as shall so be brought in and not presented to the Customer as is aforesayd, or the value of them.

And Be it further enacted, That no person so bringing into this Realme or other the Quenes Highnes Dominions any suche Hattes or Cappes, shall in any wise remove carie or conveye suche Hattes or Cappes, or any of them, from the place wher they shall so bee layde on lande tyll suche tyme as they shalbee solde in maner and fourme as is hereafter expressed, upon paine of forfeiture for every Hatte or Cappe removed or solde contrary to the meaning of this Acte, Fowrtye shillinges.

And Be it enacted, That the Customer or Customers, his or their Deputie or Deputies of every Citye Boroughe Towne Porte Haven or Creek where such Bonettes Hattes or Cappes shalbe so brought into this Realme or other the Quenes Dominions, shall within twoo Days after the Entrye of the same Cappes or Hattes in the Customers Bookes, give notice and make relation of the said Hattes Bonettes or Cappes to the Mayours Sherieffes Bailiefes C unstables Reves or other the Cheife Officers of the said Cities Boroughes Townes or Portes, and that upon payne of forfeyture of their Offices.

And Be it further enacted, That the said Customer or Customers, or their Deputie or Deputies, together with the Maior or suche other person as the Maior shall assigne or apointe, or withe the Shrieffes Bailiefes Cunstables Reves or other the Cheife Officer or Officers of any suche place, or any of them, where suche Hattes or Cappes shall so be layde on Lande, in the presence of the Owners of them (yf they wilbee present, or in their absence yf they will not) shall sell the said Bonettes Cappes and Hattes and every of them, to suche person or persons as will bye them at such price and prices as is lymited and appointed by the said Acte made in the sayd xxj yere, and not above, and shall paye and delyver the money that the said Bonettes Cappes and Hattes shalbe solde for, to the owners of suche Bonettes Hattes and Cappes in suche convenient time as the Owners will receive the same, upon payne and forfeiture of Twentye powndes for everye tyme that such Customer or Customers Maiors Shrieffes Baylieffes or other head Officers as is aforesayd shall be remisse or negligente to make sale as is aforesayd.

And Be it further enacted by aucthorite aforesayd, That no one person, by any fraude covyn collour or collusion, shall buye or bargayne for any more Hattes or Cappes, being made out of the Realme, at one time or of one man, then one dozen; upon payne for every Cappe or Hatte bought contrary to the mening of this Acte, Fourtye shillingf, thone halfe of all suche forfeitures or somes of money to be to suche as will sue for the same by Byll Playnt or Information in any of the Quenes Courtes of Recordes, wherin ther shall lye no Essoigne wager of law or protection, and thother half therof to bee to the Quene her Highnes her heires or successoures. Provided that the sayde Customer and Customers Maiors Sheriffes Bailiefes Cunstables Reves or other heade and cheife Officers, shall not sell nor otherwise utter above one Dozen of the sayd Bonettes Cappes or Hattes to any one persone or persons.

CHAPTER XII.

An Acte againste unlawfull and rebellyous Assembles.

FORASMUCHE as it ys most necessarye in a Common Wealthe to provyde that Tranquilitie and Peace may be continued in the Realme, and that all thinges being contrary therunto maye by foresight be eschewed : Therefore it ys Ordeined and Enacted by the Quene our Soveraigne Ladye, withe thassent of the Lordes and Comons of this present Parliament assembled and by thaucthorite of the same, That yf any persons, to the number of twelve or above, being assembled together at any tyme after the twentithe daye of December nexte comming, shall ‘intende goe aboute practise or put in ure with force of VI.

For suppressing all such Meetings;

Where Ttvo or more an- assembled for any of the said Purposes, any Justice, Sheriff, &c. or other Person authorized by Commission may by force of Arms, \-c. disperse such Meetings, and shall be indemnified in case any Persons are killed, 8tc.

VII. Copyholders refusing to assist in dispersing such Meetings, shall forfeit their Copyholds to the Lord for Life.

And Furthermore it is ordeyned and enacted by thaucthoritee abovesayd, That yf any persons above the number of two and under the number of twelve, being assembled together, at any tyme after the sayd xx’h daye of December, shall intende go aboute practise or put in Ure with force of Armes unlawfully and of their owne aucthorite to murther kill or slea any of the Quenes Majesties subject? or to overthrowe cut breake or cast down or dygge up the Pales Hedges Dyches Wall or other Closure of any Parkes Parke or other ground enclosed, or the bancke of any Fishe Ponde or Poole, to thintente that the same or any of them from thensforthe shoulde remayn open or not enclosed or voide, or to have comon or waye in the same Parkes or Parke or other grounde or groundes enclosed or in any of them or to destroye any maner of Parkes or Parke or fisheponde or poole or any warrens or warren of Coneis or any Dovehouses, or to pull or cutt downe any house barne myll, or to burne any stackes of Corne or Grayne, or alter defalke or abate the rentes or yearly valewe of any Manours landes or tenementes of any the Quenes subjectes, or the price of any victuall corne or grayne, or any thing usual) for the sustenance or apparell of Men, and being required or comanded by any Justice of the Peace or the Shiriffe of the Countye, or by any Maiors Bailief or Bailiefes or other head Officer of any Citie or Towne corporate where such assemble shalbee had, by proclamac&n to be made in the Quenes name, to retire or returne to their habitations places or howses, and they so required by suche proclamation shall not so doo, but after that shall in forceable maner in forme aforesaid attempt to doo or put in Ure any of the thinges last above mentioned ; That then every of the same persons, being above the number of twoo and under the number of twelve, shall suffer imprisonement of his or their bodies by the space of one yeere without baile or mainprise : And also that yf any person or persons at any time after the said xx,h day of December, shall bee dampnified or hurted by the doing comitting or putting in Ure of any unlawfull Acte or thing above mentioned, that then all and singler persons so dampnified and hurte, shall recover and have domages with the costes of their suyte susteyned in that behalf trebled, against thoffendours therin.

And Forasmuche as suche evell disposed persones whiche of late tyme made comotions and rebellion in certayne places within this Realme, being but fewe in number, at suche time as they dyd begin the same edmotion, were not in shone tyme after the beginning therof suppressed by strengthe, for that the loving subjectes at that tyme for feare to incurre in daunger of the Lawes of this Realme, durst not take upon them so to doo, a greate number of evill disposed persons did come and joyne themselfes to the said smal number, Wherby the said evill disposed persons tooke upon them suche boldnes that they woulde not be reduced to obedience without much bloudshedding, to the great daunger of the persone of the Prince, where yf the saide subjectes durst have taken upon them to have suppressed at the beginning, suche inconvenience and bloudshed should not have folowed ; Therefore it is also ordeined and enacted by the aucthoritie aforesayd, That yf any persons above the number of twoo, that at any tyme after the said xx,h daye of December shalbee unlawfullye and of their owne aucthoritie assembled together, to thintent withe force and armes to doo practice or put in Ure any of the thinges above mentioned; that then it shall bee lawfull to every Justice of Peace and to every Shiriffe in any Countie being within the Quenes Dominyons, and to every Mayor Bailyf and other Heade Officer of any Citie or Towne corporate for the time he shalbe in office, or any other person or persons having the Quenes Comission or Ires from her Highnes, as well to reise and assemble the Quenes loving subjectes in maner of warre to be arraied in suche greate number as he or they then shall thinck mete or liable, to thintent by violence and strengthe to suppresse apprehende and take the sayd persons that so shalbe unlaufully assembled ; And that yf the sayd persons so unlawfully assembled, after suche comaundement or request by proclamation made, shall continue together and not endevour themselfes to returne towardes their habitaebns houses or places from whens they came, in suche shorte tyme as they may convenientlye, that then it shalbe lefull to every Justice of Peace Shiriff and also everye Maior Bailief and other heade Officer of any Citie or Towne corporate, and to every other person having aucthoritie as is aforesaid, after suche comaundement or request by proclamation made, and to suche persones as shalbe assembled withe any Justice of Peace or Shiriffe, or withe any Maior Baileif and other head Officer of any Citie or Towne corporate, and withe every other person having aucthoritie as is aforesaid, to suppresse apprehende and take those persons so unlawfully assembled, whiche after suche proclamation made shall continue together, and not endevour themselfes to returne towarde their habitations or places from whens they came, and that yf the said persons so unlaufully assembled together, or any of them shall fortune to be killed slayne maymed or hurte in or aboute the suppressing or taking of them, that then every suche Justice of Peace Shirif Maior Bailief and other head Officer, and every other person having aucthoritie as is aforesaid, and all and singler persons by him or them assembled, shalbe free dischardged and unpunishable as well agenst the Quene, as agenst all and everye other person or persons of for or concerning the killing sleing mayming or hurting of any person or persons so unlawfully assembled, that shall fortune to be killed slayne maimed or hurte aboute or by occasion of suppressing or taking of them.

And be it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That the order and forme of the Proclamations that shalbe made by thaucthorite of this Acte shalbe as hereafter followethe, or with the lyke order and woordes in effect, That is to saye; The Justice or other person aucthorised by this Acte to make the said Proclamation shall make or cause to be made an Oyes, and after that shall openly pronounce or cause to be pronounced theis words or lyke in effecte: The Quene our Sovereigne Ladye chardgethe and comaundethe all persons being assembled immediatlie to disperse themselfes and peaceablie to departe to their habitations or to their lawfull busines, uppon payne conteyned in the Acte lately made ageinst Unlaufull and Rebellyous Assembles. And God save the Quene.

And that if any persons to the number of fourtye or moo, after the said xx*b daye of December, shall assemble together in forceable maner unlawfully and of their own aucthorite, to thintent to doo exercise or put in Ure any of the thinges above specified, or to doo other felonous or rebellious Acte or Actes, and so shall continue together by the space of three houres after Proclamation shalbe made, at or nigh the place where they so shall be assembled, or in some Market Towne theronto next adjoyning, and after Notice therof to them geven, that then every person so willingly assembled in forceable maner, and so continuing together by the space of three houres after suche Proclamation shall be made and Notice therof geven, shall be adjudged a felon, and shall suffer deathe as in case of felonye.

And Be it further enacted by the said aucthoritie, That no Lieutenant or Lieutenants that shall be appointed or made by aucthoritie or colour of this Acte, or for texecute this Acte, shall in any wise make put or constitute under him or them, or in his or their place, any Deputie or Deputies, nor shall call convent or appoint to appeare before him or them by thonelye aucthoritie of Lieutenauncye or of Comission of Lieutenauncye, any person or persons for any cause or matter whatsoever, save onelye for the causes and matters expressed in this present Acte and for none other.

And that no person or persones shall be put to any losse forfeitur payne or punishement of lyes lande or gooddes as Accessarie to any person or persons that shall edmitt any of the Offences conteined in this pnte Acte for receyaving comforting or ayding of any suche offendour after such Acte comitted or doon; And that no attayndour or conviction of any person or persons for any offence or offences herein conteined, shall be any maner of corruption of bloudd betwene the Offendour and any of his Auncesters, or suche person and persones as should have bene heire to suche Offender, yf no suche attaynder or conviction hadd bene hadd: Saving to all and every person and persons bodye and bodies politike and corporate and their successours their lyberties and franchesies, in such maner and fourme as if this Acte had never bene hadd ne made.

And Be it further enacted by the sayd aucthorite, That one Acte of Pliament made in the Session of the Parliament holden upon prorogation at Westminster, the fourthe daye of November in the thirdde yere of the raigne of King Edwarde the Sixte, and ther continued and kepte to the first daye of Februarie in the fourthe yere of the raigne of the sayd King, intituled by the name of An Acte for the punishement of Unlawfull Assemblyes and rising of the Kinges subjectes, and all and every braunche clause sentence and article therin conteined, shalbe from the twentithe daye of December next coming, utterly voide and of no force to all intentes constructions and purposes, and this Acte onely to be put in execution for and concerning thoffences mentioned in the said former Acte: This Acte to continue unto thende of the next Pliament.

CHAPTER XV.

An Acte for the reedifieng of the Parishe Churche of Saynte Elens in Stanegate, within the Citie of Yorcke.

WHERE in the Parliament begune at Westminster the fourthe daye of November in the first yeere of the Raigne of the late King of famouse Memorie Edwarde the Syxt, An Acte was made for Uniting of certayne Churches within the Citie ofYorke, and the Suburbes of the same; In whiche Acte amonges other thinges it was enacted, that from thenceforthe it shoulde be lawfull to the Maiour and Recorder of the same Citie, and to the Ordinarie or his Deputie, and syxe Justices of Peace within the said Citie, to Unite and knit together certayne Parishe Churches within the said Citie and Suburbes into a fewer nomber, as by the same Acte more plainly it appearethe: Sithens the making of whiche Acte, One Parishe Churche called S' Elens in Stanegate within the said Citie, was by thaucthoritee of the same Acte suppressed defaced and the Parishe united and knitt to another; and because the said Parishe Churche of S' Elens in Stanegate, did stande in a principall place of the said Citie, the Suppression therof hathe muche defaced and deformed the said Citie, and is a greate decaye to sundrye stretes of the said Citie, meting and joyning at the said Churche: In consideration wherof. Be it enacted by the Quenes Ma'", the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Commons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by thaucthoritie of the same, That it shalbe lawfull to the Parishoners of the said late Parishe of S' Elens in Stanegate, and the Inhabitantes resident and dwelling within the bowndes and limites of the said late Parishe, that nowe bee and that hereafter shalbe, to repayre reedyfie and builde ageyne the same Parishe Churche of S' Elens in Stanegate. and the Churcheyarde of the same, and therin to have use and [to '] perceive all Dyvine Services Sacramentes and Sacramentalles, as shall be lawfull for any Parishoners to have in or at their Parishe Churches, and to be Parishoners of the same, in as ample and as lardge maner as they were at any tyme before the suppression of the same; Any thing in the former Acte or any thinge by the aucthoritie therof doon, or any Uniting Ordinaunce or Decree doone or made by the Ordinarie, or by the aucthoritie of the said Acte, in anye wise notwithestanding.

CHAPTER XVII.

An Acte for the Release of the last Subsidie of the Temporaltie.

WHERE (’) the Quenes Highnes our Sovereigne Ladye by her Graces Ires patentes, sealed withe the Greate Seale, bearing date the firste daye of September last past, Reciting, Wheras in the Pliament holden in the seventhe yere of the Raigne of the Excellent Prince our late Sovereigne Lorde King Edwarde the Syxthe her Highnes Brother, ther was graunted by Acte of Pliament unto the same late Kinge, twoo Dismes and twoFiftenes, and one Subsidie of sour shillinges of the Pownde, to be raised and levied of the Manois Landes and Tenementes, and twoo shillinges eight pens of the Gooddes and Cattelles, of his late Subjectes; whiche Grauntes were then due unto Her Highnes by the said Acte; Her Majestie for the Considerations expressed in the said Ires patentes, of her mere Grace and greate Clemencie, for the relief and succour of her sayd Subjectes, dyd freely for her her heires and successoures, perdon and remit unto her said Subjectes and their heires and executoures, the saide Subsidie of sour shillinges the pownde, and twoo shillinges viij d. the pownde, graunted in the said Pliament; as by the said Ires patentes more at lardge it dothe and maye appeare j Whiche Ires patentes were by Her Highnes Comaundement published and proclaymed throughout this Realme : Oure said Sovereigne Ladye the Queue, upon her further gracious respecte and especiall love towardes her said Subjectes, and for thavoiding of all doubles and questions whiche might rise or be moved of the validitee and force of the said Ires patentes set for the by Proclamation as is aforesayd, is pleased and contented that her said gratious Remission of the said Subsidies be ratified and confirmed by aucthoritie of Pliament: Therfore be it enacted by thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporal), and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by thautborite of the same. That all and every person and persons, Bodyes Politick and Corporate, their heires successoures executoures and administratours, being Laye Subjectes, whiche shoulde or ought to have payde any sdme or somes of moneye for the said Subsidye of iiij s. the pownde, and ij s. viij d. the pownde, graunted in the said late Pliament, Or of or for anye other Rate or Rates of Landes Gooddes Cattelles, or otherwise towching or concerning the payment of any some or somes of money for or by reason of the Graunte of the said Subsidie, shalbe therof clerelye acquired and discharged against the Quenes Highnes, her heires and successoures executoures and administratoures, to all respectes and purposes as thoughe the said Acte of Graunte of the said Subsidie had never bene hadd ne made.

Provided alwaies that (’) pnte Acte shall not extende to dischardge any person or persons bodies politique and corporate of or for the payment of any some or somes of moneye whiche is ought or shalbe due unto her Highnes her heires or successours for the twoo Fiftenes and Dismes graunted to the saide late Kinge by the said Acte; Any thinge in this Acte conteined notwithstanding.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte declaring that the Regall Power of this Realme is in the Quenes MaUe as fully and absolutely as ever it was in any of her moste noble Progenitours Kings of this Realme.

By Descent of the Crown to the Queen all Regal Power vested in her;

The Name of King only used in the ancient Statutes of the Realm

The Kingly Office and Prerogative declared to beequal, whether vested in Male or Female ; and a Queen Regent to have all the Powers of a King.

FORASMUCHE as the Imperiall Crowne of this Realme, withe all Dignities Honours Prerogatives Aucthorities Jurisdictions and Preheminences therunto annexed united and belonging, by the Dyvine Providence of Almighty God, ys most lawfully justly and rightfully discended and come unto the Quenes Highnes that now ys, being the

verye true and undoubted heire and inheritrixe therof, and invested in her most Royall Person, according unto the

Lawes of this Realme ; And by force and vertue of the same, all Regall Power Dignitie Honour Aucthoritie Prerogative Preheminence and Jurisdictions dothe apperteine, and of right ought to apperteine and belong unto her Highnes, as to the Sovereine supreme Govemour and Quene of this Realme and the Dominions therof, in as full large and ample maner as it hathe done heretofore to any other her most noble Progenitours Kinges of this Realme: Nevertheles the most auncient Statutes of this Realme being made by Kinges then reigning, doo not onely attribute and referre all Prerogative Preheminence Power and Jurisdiction Roiall unto the name of King, but also doo gyve assigne and appointe the Correcc&n and Punishment of all Offendours against the Regaltie and Dignitie of the Crowne and the Lawes of this Realme unto the Kinge; By occasion wherof the malitious and ignorant persones may bee hereafter induced and perswaded unto this errour and folly, to thinck that her Highnes coulde ne shoulde have enjoye and use suche lyke Royall Aucthoritie Power Preheminence Prerogative and Jurisdice&n, nor doo ne execute and use all thinges concerning the sayd Statutes, and take the benefit! and privilege of the same, nor correcte and punislie Offendours

against her most Royall Person and the Regaltie and Dignitie of the Crowne of this Realme and the Dominions

thereof, as the Kinges of this Realme her most noble Progenitours have heretofore doon enjoied used and exersised: For thadvoiding and clere extinguishement of whiche sayd errour or doubte, and for a playn declaracon of the Lawes of this Realme in that behalf; Be it declared and enacted by thauctorite of this pnte Pliament, that the

Lawe of this Realme is and ever hathe been and ought to bee understande, that the Kinglye or Regall Office of the

Realme, and all Dignities Prerogative Royall Power Preheminences Privilegies Aucthorities and Jurisdictions therunto annexed united or belonging, being invested either in Male or Female, are and bee and ought to bee as fully wholly absolutely and [enteerly '] demed judged accepted invested and taken in thone as in thother ; so that what or whansoever Statute or Law doothe lymitte and appointe that the King of this Realme may or shall have execute and doo any thing as King, or dothe geve any profitt or comodite to the King, or dothe lymitte or appointe any paines or punishement for the Correction of Offendours or Transgressoures against the Regaltie and Dignitie of the King or of the Crowne, The same the Quene, (being supreme Governesse possessour and enheritour to the Imperiall Crowne of this Realme as our sayd Sovereigne Ladye the Quene most justly presentlye is,) may by the same aucthoritie and power likewise have exersice execute punishe correcte and doo, to all intentes constructions and purposes without

Doubte Ambiguitie Scruple or Question: Any Custome Use or Scruple or any other thing whatsoever to be made

to the contrary notwithstanding.

CHAPTER II.

An Acte touching the Articles of the Quenes Highnes most noble Marriage.

Intended Marriage of the Queen with Prince Philip of Spain 5

Stipulation! of one of the Treaties as to the said Marriage

The Kingly Title given to Philip in the Queen's Dominions, the Laws thereof, &c. being maintained

WHEREAS most Instant Sute hathe been made to yor Most Excellent Majestie, on the behalf of the most noble and most Victorious Prince Charles, Emperour of Rome, &c. for Marriage to be had betwen your Highnes, and his onelye Sonne and Heyre the noble Prince Philippe of Spayne, &c.: Wherupon to the Pleasure of Almightye God, to the Comfort of yo' most noble Persone, and to the great and singuler Honour Wealthe Benefite and Comoditec of this yor Realme of Englande, and of all Us yo’ most humble and obedient Subjectes of the same, ther hathe passed and been concluded in twoo sundrye [Treatyse,1] certeyne Pactes and Covenauntes towching the sayd Marryage, withe dependances and circumstaunces of the same, and in thone Treatie theis Articles: First, It is covenaunted and agreed that as soone as convenientlye may bee, trewe and perfite Maryage by woordes of the tyme present, shalbee contracted solemnised and consumate in Englande, betwen the sayd most noble Prince, and the sayd most vertuous Ladye the Quene ; By force of whiche Marryage so celebrated and consumate, the sayd most noble Prynce Phillyppe, shall during the sayd Marryage have and enjoye joyntlye together withe the sayd most gratyous Quene his Wyef, the Stile Honoure and

Kinglye Name of the Realmes and Domynyons unto the said most noble Quene apperteyning, and shall ayde her

Highnes being his Wyef, in the happye administrac&n of her Graces Realmes and Dominions; The Rightes Lawes Privileges and Customes of the same Realmes and Dominions being nevertheles preserved and maynteyned: And speciallye yt ys provided and covenaunted, that the sayd most noble Prince shall permitt and suffer the said

most gracyous Quene his Wyef, to have the whole disposicon of all the Benefices and Offices Landes Revenues and

Fruites of the sayd Realmes and Dominions, and that they shalbe bestowed uppon suche as bee naturallye borne in the same; And that all the matters of the sayd Realmes and Dominions shall bee treated and mayntayned in the same Tongues wherin of olde they have been wont to bee treated, and by the naturall borne of the same Realmes:

First, That as touching the right of the Mothers Inheritaunce in the Realme of Englande, and the other Realmes and Dominions depending of the same, the Children as well Males as Females that shalbee borne of this Matriinonye shall succede in them, according to the Lawes Statutes and Customes of the same: And as touching the Landes that the sayd most noble Prince shall leave behinde him; First, ther shalbe reserved unto his eldest sonne the Lorde Charles of Austriche, Infante of Spayne, and to the Children and Heires of him discending, as well Females as Males, all and singuler their Rightes whiche to the sayd Prynce doo either nowe or hereafter shall belong, and shall at any tyme by the deathe either of the noble Quene his Graundame, or the most Victorious Emprour Charles the Fifthe his Father,

But yf yt fortune the same Lord Charles to dye, and thissue of his bodye to faile, then and in that cace theldest Sonne of this Matrimonye shalbee admitted unto the sayd Right, and according to the Nature Lawes and Customes of the sayd Realmes and Dominions shall succede: The same eldest Sonne shall also succede in all the Dukedomes Earledomes Dominions and primoniall Landes belonging unto the sayd Lorde Themprour, aswell in Burgundie as in the Lower Germanye; that ys to saye, In the Dukedomes of Brabant, Luxenborghe, Gheldres, Zutphane, Burgondye,

Moreover if it fortune no Male Childe to be borne of this Matrimonie but one/ye Females, in that cace theldest Female shall withe full right succede in the sayd Landes and Dominions of the Lower Germanye; so as nevertheles she being mynded to choose to husbande any man not borne in Englande or in the Lower Germanye, she doe contract the same Matrymonye by the counsel! and consent of the said Lord Charles thinfant her brother, Or elles yf she take any Man to husbande that ys not borne in Englande or in the Lower Germanye, neglecting the counsell and consent of the sayd Lorde Charles, in that cace the Right of the Succession shalbee and remayne to the sayd Lorde Charles thinfant in the sayd Dominions of Lower Germanye Burgundye and theyr appertenaunces, whiche in the cace aforesaid shall revert unto him or his Issue aswell Males as Females; And yet nevertheles in that cace both she and thother Doughters also discending of this Matrimonye, no Male Children remaining, shalbee endowed of their Fatheres Landes and Possessions aswell of Spayne as of Lower Germanye, competentlye and according to the Customes of the said Realmes and Dominions; And for want also of the said Lorde Charles and thissue of him, and none other Children remayning of this Matrymonye but Women, in that cace theldest Doughter to be borne of this Matrimonye shall succede not onelye in the sayd Dominions of Lower Germanye and Burgundye but also in thother Realmes of Spayne Englande and the rest, after the Nature Lawes and Customer of the same: Provided nevertheles and expresselye

And in one other [Treatise'] these Articles following: First, That the sayd most noble Prince shall not promote admitt or receyve to any Office Administrac&n or [ Benefitt1 ] in the sayd Realme of Englande, and the Dominions therunto belonging, anye Straunger or [personnesJ] not borne under the Domynion and Subjection of the sayd most noble Quene of Englande: That the sayd most noble Prince shall receive and admit into the Service of his Housholde and Courte Gentlemen and Yeomen of the same Realme of Englande in a convenient numbre, and shall esteme enterteyne and nourishe them as his proper Subjectes, and shall bring none in his Retinue, nor have none withe him that will doo anye displeasure or wrong to the Subjectes of the sayd Realme; and yf they doo, he shall take Order to correcte them withe condigne punishem1 and see them expelled his Courte: That the sayd most noble Prynce shall doo nothing wherby any thing bee innovated in the State and Right, eyther publike or private, or in the Lawes and Customes of the sayd Realme of Englande or the Dominions therunto belonging; but shal contrarye wise, confirme and kepe to all Estates and Ordres their Rightes and Privileges: That the sayd Lorde Prince shall not leade awaye thforesayd most noble Ladye the Quene out of the borders of her Highnes Realme, oneles she her selfe desyre yt, nor carye the Children that shalbe borne of this Matrimonye out of the same Realme of Englande, but to the hope of Succession to come, shall ther suffer them to be nourished and brought uppe, oneles it shalbe otherwise thought good by the consent and agreament of the Nobilytee of Englande; and in cace that no Children being lefte, the said most noble Quene doo dye before him, the sayd Lorde Prynce shall not chalendge any Right at all in the sayd Kingdome, but without any impediment shall permytte the Succession therof to come unto them to whom yt shall belong and apperteine by the Right and Lawes of the sayd Realme: Item, That the sayd most noble Prynce shall not beare or carye over out of the foresayd Realme, the Juelles and precyous thynges of estimacon, neyther shall he alienate or doo awaye any whitt of thappertenaunces of the sayd Realme of Englande, or suffer any part of them to be usurped by his Subjectes or any other; but shall see that all and singuler places of the Realme, and specyallye the Fortes and Frontyers of the same, bee faithefullye kepte and preserved to the use and profitt of the sayd Realme and by the naturall borne of the same; He shall not suffer any Shippe Gonnes Ordin*nces whatsoever of Warre or Defence to bee removed or conveyed out of the sayd Realme, but shall contrarye wyse cause them dylygentlye to bee kepte and renued when nede requyrethe, and shall so provide that the same may allwayes bee readye in their strengthe and force for the defence of the Realme : Item, That the Realme of Englande by occasyon of this Matrymonye, shall not directlye or indirectlye bee entangledd withe the Warre that is betwen the most Victorious Lorde Themprour, Father unto the said Lorde Prynce, and Henrye the Freche King, but he the said Lorde Philippe, as muche as shall lye in him on the behalfe of the sayd Realme of Englande, shall see the Peace betwen the sayd Realmes of Fraunce and Englande observed, and shall gyve no cause of any breache; By whiche Covenaunt the latter Treatyce of a straighter Amytee, shall not bee in any poynte derogated, but the same shall still remayne in his vygour and force: Saving also that on the behalf of his Fatheres other Realmes and Dominions, the sayd Prynce shall have free power to ayde and assyste his most noble Father as he shall thincke best in the Defence of his Landes, and Revendge of the Injuries he hathe receyved : Forasmuche as We yo' most humble and obedient Subjectes the Lordes Spyrytuall and Temporall, and the Comons in this present Parliament assembled, have maturelye sincerelye and delyberatelye considered and weyed all and singuler the sayd Covenauntes Grauntes Pacts Treatises and Agreamentes, concerning the sayd most honourable and fortunate Mariage betwen yo' Highnes and the sayd most noble Prince of Spayne, and the Dependances therof, and doe therupon thincke deme and judge the same to be bothe honorable unto yo' Highnes, and comodious unto the C5mon Welthe of this yo' Realme : Therefore Wee Yo' said humble and obedyent Subjectes most humblye pray and beseche your Majestie that lyke as it hath pleased yo' Highnes upon yo' free and naturall zeale and good will that yo have and beare unto this yo' Realme, and to yo' loving Subjectes of the same, to condiscende and agree that all and singler the sayd Grauntes Articles Pactes and Agreamentes concerning the sayd Marryage, should bee revealed opened and declared unto Us yo' sayd loving Subjectes in this yo' Highe Courte of Parlyament; So yt maye also please yo' Majestie for, the more perfitte coroborac&n and strengthe of the said Artycles Grauntes Pactes and Agreamentes, and to thintent that the same maye bee the more inviolablye observed and kepte, That it maye bee enacted by thauthoritee of this pnte Parlyament, That all and singler the sayd Articles Covenauntes Grantes Pactes Treatises and Agreamentes, hadd made and concluded for and concerning the said Marryage betwen yo' Highnes and the sayd Prynce of Spayne, and all and singuler the Dependaunces therof before rehearsed, shall immediatelye after the sayd Marryage hadd and solemnised, stande remayne and abyde in perfect force and efficacye, according to the effecte sence and true meaning of the sayd Treatyse.

CHAPTER HI.

An Actk for the Repeale of two severall Actes made in the seventhe yere of King Edward the Syxte, touching the dissoluc&n of the Bishoprick of Durham.

WHERE there hathe beene tyme out of mynde of any Man to the contrary, A See of a Bisshoppe of Durham within the Northe Partes of this Realme of Englande, comonlye called the Byshoprick of Durham, whiche hathe beene one of the most auncyentest and worthiest Bishoprickes Dignities and Promocon Spirituall within the sayd Realme, and the same Place Rowme and Dignitie alwayes supplyed and furnished withe a Man of greate Learning and Vertue, the whiche was bothe to the Honour of God, and the increase of his trewe Relygion, and a great suretie to that [Place '] of this Realme ; Nevertheles the sayd Bishoprick, in the Pliament begonne at Westminster the first daye of Marche in the seventhe yere of the Reigne of our late Sovereine Lorde of famous memorye King Edwarde the Syxte, nowe deceassed, and ther holden and continued unto the dissolution of the same. Was without any just cause or consideration, by aucthorite of the sayd Pliament, dissolved extinguished and determined; And further by thaucthorite of the said Pliament, It was ordeined and enacted that the sayd Bishoprick, together with all the ordinarie Jurisdictions therunto apperteining, shoulde be adjudged from the said first daye of the said Pliament, clerelye dissolved extinguished and determined ; And that our said (‘) Sovereine Lorde the King, shoulde from thensfoorthe have holde possede and enjoy to him his heirs and successoures for ever, all and singler Honoures Castelles Manoures Lordeshipes Graunges Meases Landes Tenementes Medowes Pastures Rentes RevercOns Services Wooddes Tithes Pencons PorcOns Personages appropriated Vicaredgges Churches Chappelles Advousons NominacOns Patronages Anuities Rightes Interestes Entrees Conditions Comons Leetes Courtes Lyberties Priveleges Franchisees and other Hereditamentes whatsoever, whiche dyd apperteine or belong to the said Bishopricke of Durham, in as large and ample manner and forme as the late Bishoppe of the said Bishoprick, meaning to be the said late Bishoppe the Reverende Father in God Cutheberte Tunstall nowe Bishoppe of the said Bishoprick who was then supposed to be deprived thereof, or any of his Predecessoures Bishoppes ther held or occupied, or of right ought to have holden or occupied in the right of the sayd Bishoprick, together with all thissues and profites rising coming and growing of the premisses, and of every percell of the same from the tyme of the supposed avoydaunce of the CHAPTER IV.

An Acte for thestablishing of thoffice of the L. Steward of the Quenes Majesties most Honourable Housholde.

WHERE in the Session of Pliament holden at Westminster the [thoo and thertye *] yere of the raigne of the late King of most famous Memory King Henry the Eight, It was amongest other thinges, withe thassent of the Lordes Spiritual! and Temporall and the C5mons in the said Pliament assembled, enacted and established, that Charles late Duke of Suffolk then having thoffice of Create Maister of the Kings Housholde or Grande Maister D'Hostell du Roye, and all other who after that time should have the sayd Office, by those Names or any of them should have use and enjoye all suche and singuler Preeminence Aucthoritees Privileges and Jurisdictions, in as large and ample maner fashion fourme and condic&n as the Lorde Stuarde of the Kings Housholde by vertue of thoffice, and in name of Lorde Stuarde hadd used or ought to have used or hadd, by reason of any Custome Usages Statutes or Comon Lawes of this Realme, and as yf the sayd Duke and suche other as should have the sayd Office had been called and named Lorde Stewarde of the Kings Housholde, as more plainlye at large may appeare by the sayd Statute: Forasmuche as it hathe now pleased the Quenes Majestie to reduce alter and chaunge the name of the Create Maister of her Highnes most honourable Housholde or Grand Maister D'Hostell du Roy, into the name of the sayd Lorde Stuarde of her most honourable Housholde, and therupon hathe granted and gyven the sayd Office of Lord Stewarde of her sayd most honourable Householde unto her right trustye and entierly beloved Cosyn and Councellour Henry Earle of Arundell, and hathe ordeined named and appointed him to be called Lorde Stewarde of her honourable Housholde: That it may please her Highnes it be enacted ordeined and established by thassent of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same, That the sayd Statute made in the sayd xxxij"* yere concerning the Jurisdiction of the Greate M' of the Kings Housholde, and every Branche Clause Article and Sentence in the same conteyned shall bee from hensforthe frustrate voide and of none effecte.

CHAPTER V.

An Acte for the continuac&n of a Statute made for the repairing of Shirbourne Causeye.

WHERE in the Parliament begunne and holden at Westminster the fifthe daye of October in the first yere of the Raigne of our Sovereyne Ladye Quene Marye, in the seconde and last Session of the same Pliament ther holden upon prorogacon the xxiiij of October then next following, and ther continued and kept untill the dissoluC&n of the same Pliament, being the syxthe daye of December then next ensuing; amongest other things One Acte was made and provided, for and concerning the making repairing and amending of the Comon Highewaye and Cawsey in the Counties of Dorsett and Somersett, betwen the Townes of Shaftesburye and Shirebourne, in the same Countye of Dorsett; The tenor of whiche Acte here followen in theis woordes ensuing

" Whehe it is evident that the Comon Highewaye called the Cawsey, paved withe Stone in the Counties of Dorsett and Somersett, betwen the Townes of Shaftesburye and Shirebourne in the same Countye of Dorsett, ys nowe in greate decaye, to the greate hurte and daunger of all people whiche of necessite must dayly passe that waye in joumeis and withe their Cariages: For Remedy wherof, because it ys thought meete that the chardges of the making repairing and amending of the same Highewaye and Causeye, being in length twelf miles, shoulde bee borne by the Owners Tenantes Fermours and Inhabitauntes of the Manoures Landes Tenementes and Parishes heng nighe to the sayd Cawseye and Highewaye on either syde of the same, by the Owners Tenauntes Fermours and Inhabitauntes of the Townes of Shaftisburye and Shirbourne; Be it therefore enacted by aucthoritee of this pnt Pliament, That the sayd Highewaye and Cawsey shall from hensforthe from time to time be made repaired and amended by the Owners Tenauntes and Fermoures of the Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes heng nighe to the sayd Cawseye and Highewaye on either side of the same, and by thinhabitantes of and within the sayd Townes of Shaftesburye ande Shirbourne, and by the Owners Tenantes and Fermoures of the Manours Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes, and by thinhabitantes of and within the Forest of Gillingham, and Lyberties of Gillingham and Alcetter, and the Hundredes of Redlane and Shirbourne in the sayd Countie of Dorsett, and of the Hundredd of Horethorne in the sayd Countie of Somersett.

" And Be it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesayd, That the Justices of the Peace aswell of the said Counde of Dorsett as of the said Countie of Somersett for the time being, from time to time, aswell in their Quarter Sessions as otherwyse, shall have full powre and aucthoritee to call before them, or before foure of them at the least, wherof twoo to bee of the Quorum, the said Owners Tenantes Fermours and Inhabitantes, and all other suche persone and persones as by this Acte as ys aforesayd shalbe bounde to repayre and amende the said Cawseye and Highewaye, or such or so many of them as to the same Justices of the Peace or foure of them at the least, wherof twoo to bee of the Quorum, shall bee thought most meete and convenient; and therupon to take suche reasonable orders and directions from time to tyme for and concerning the making repayring and amendeinent of the said Highewaye and Cawseye, and for the charges therof to make from time to tyme suche assessementes and taxations of money or otherwise upon the sayd Owners Tenantes Fermoures and Inhabitantes, and all other such persone and persons as by this Acte as is aforesayd shalbe bounde to repayre and amende the said Cawseye and Highewaye, having goodd and indifferent respecte to the severall habilitees of them and every of them, as to the said Justices of the Peace or foure of them at the least, wherof twoo to bee of the Quorum, shalbe thought most meete expedient and convenient; and that it shalbe lawfull to the same Justices of the Peace or to foure of them at the least, wherof twoo to be of the Quorum, to put and sett paines aswell for the observacon and perfourmance of the said Ordinance and Directions, as also for the payment and levieng of suche money and other things as shall be taxed or assessed, or wherof any order shalbe made in fourme aforesayd, and to sett order for accompte to be made yerely of suche somes of money and other things as shalbee levied and gathered for and to the reparac&n and amendement of the said Highewaye and Cawseye, and before whom and to whom the said accompte shalbe made; and that the same Orders and Directions shalbe entred and enrolled of Recorde by the Clercke of the Peace for the tyme being, aswell of the sayd Countie of Dorsett as of the sayd Countie of Somersett, in the Rolles of Sessions of the same Counties, to thintent that processe maye be made against suche persone and persones as shall withstande breake or disobeye any of the Orders Decrees Ordinances Taxaetms or Assessementes to be made concerning the Premisses in fourme aforesaid, the forfeitures of whiche paynes and penalties to goo to the making repairing and amendement of the sayd Highewaye and Cawseye.

" And Be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid. That for not perfourming of the said Orders Directions and Ordinances, and for the levieng of the sayd Taxations and Assessementes, yt shalbe lawfull to distrayne and take Distresses, and to use the same Distresses in suche wise as, in other cases where Distresses doo lye by the Lawes of this Realme, hathe and may bee doone and used.

CHAPTER VI.

An Acte for the repairing of a Cawseie betwext Bristowe and Gloucestre.

WHEREAS the Quenes Highe waye leading betwen the Cities of Bristowe and Gloucester having been heretofore well repayred by the devoc&n of dyvers good people, ys now fallen into suche decaye withe slowghes waters and holes in most places, as neither people horse nor cariage without greate daunger can now passe ther: By reason wherof many people withe their waynes cartes horses and cariage have been and bee marredd perished maimed and killed dyvers tymes, forasmuche as the people labouring betwen the sayd twoo Cityes have none other so convenient a waye as that, yf yt were repayred : It maie therfore bee enacted by thaucthoritee of this Pliament, that thinhabirantes of the Countie of the Citie of Glocestre and of the C.ountie of the Citie of Bristowe, within their severall lyberties, and thinhabitantes of the Hundredes of Barton next Bristowe Gromboll Ashe Barckeleye Whitestone Thomeburye and Hendburye within the Countie of Glocestre, for their severall lymites and Hundredes, shall be chardged withe the amending and reparac&n of the said waye or Causeye from tyme to tyme hereafter: And that the Justices of Peace of the said Countie or three of them at the least, dwelling within the severall Cities aforesayd, for their Liberties, and three other Justices of Peace of the sayd Countie of Glocestre, dwelling within every of the sayd severall Hundredes, or nigheste to the same, and Highe Constables of the said Hundredes, for their severall Hundredes, maye and shall by vertue of this Acte, at every Session of Peace to be holden in the said Countie next after the feast of Christmas yerelv during theis syxe yeres, rate and sesse every of the sayd Hundredes at suche a convenient portion or some of moneye as shallbee by them thought sufficient for the due reparac&n of the sayd Cawseye, and for. the charges of the Overseers of the same. And that the sayd Justices and Highe Constables by vertue of this pnte Acte shall from time to tyme yerely, during the said terme of syxe yeeres, appointe rate and sesse the inhabitantes of the same, and also appoint Collectoures and Overseers for the due levieng of the money and making of the sayd waye, and that all and every of the sayd inhabitantes shall beare pay and contrybute their severall rates and porc&ns as the said Justices and Highe Constables shall severally appointe and determyne: And that the sayd Collectoures and Overseers shall at the feast of S' Mighell tharchaungell yerely yelde and make a true and perfectte accompte in writing before the said Justices and Highe Constables or such other as they shall appointe ther, for the tyme wherin reasonable wages for all necessarye Ministers shalbe allowed by the sayd Justices, upon the payne that he that shall neglecte or refuse to doo any thing to him apperteyning that ys before lymited, shall forfeite for every time Fyve poundes, thone halfe to the Queenes Highnes use her heires and successoures, the other moytie to him that will sue for the same, by Action Bill Plaint or otherwise, wherin no essoigne wager of lawe or protection shall bee allowed.

And further that it may bee enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That the sayd Highe waye may be made new as good and substancyall on thisside the feast of the Nativitee of our Lorde God whiche shalbee in the yere of our Lorde One Thousande fyve hundrethe fyftye and seven, at the costes and chardges of thinhabitantes aforesaid, and to be well syded pitched and bottomed withe stones and other worckmanshippe and guttered for [avoiding *J of Waters.

And be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That as well thinhabitantes of the sayd Cities of Bristowe and Gloucestre and of the Counties of the same Cyties within their severall Lyberties, as thinhabitantes of the sayd Hundredes above named within the sayd Countye of Gloucester, shall yerely from tyme to tyme during the sayd terme of syxe yeeres paye unto the sayd Collectoures upon reasonable warning. All such somes of money as shalbe rated and taxed by the said Justices and Highe Constables within their sayd severall lymites, in payn of forfeiture of everye suche persone as refuse this to doo, Fourtye shillinges, to be levied to thuse aforesayd, in maner and fourme above recited: This Acte tendure but for Syxe yeres nexte ensewing.

CHAPTER VII.

An Acte touching Cloth making in Corporate Townes and Market Townes.

XT THERE the Citye of Worcester and divers other Cities Borowghes and Townes Corporate within the Realme of V V Engfande, of long time have bene upholden repay red and onely maintayned by making of Broade Clothes called Long Clothes Short Clothes and Couloured Clothes, and the Citizens Freemen and thinhabitantes of the same Cities Townes and Borowes Corporate, have therby bene greatly enriched, and the poore people and handyecraftes men of the same and the Contreis adjoyning dayly sett a woorcke, as Weavers Walkers Fullers Fulling Mill-men Sheremen and Dyers Forcers of Wolles Casters of Wolles and Sorters of Wolles Spinners Carders and Spullars of Yarne, and have had their onely lyving therby; tyll nowe of late in the fifthe yere of the Rayne of our late Sovereyne Lorde King Edwarde the Syxthe, that an Estatute was made, that no Man shoulde occupye Clothe making, ne put any brode Clothe or Clothes to weaving or making, except he hath bene Aprentice to Clothe making by the space of seven yeres, or elles have occupyed and practised Clothe making by the space of seven yeres or more, under payne of*forfeyture of great penaltyes in the same Estatute limited; By reason wherof dyvers and many good Clothiers dwelling in the said Cities and Townes Corporate, whiche hadd occupied and made Clothe by the space of fyve or syxe yeres, and some which have maried Clothiers Wyves whiche hadd occupied Clothe making by the space of twentye yeres before, by reason of the same Estatute have been enforced to leave off and clearly discontynewe their Clothe making, to their great Impoverishment and to the utter undoing of a great nomber of poore people and handycraftesmen whiche dayly hadd their lyving by the said Clothiers: And Forasmuche as the perfect and principall grounde of Clothmaking ys the true sorting of Wolles, and thexperience therof consistethe onely in Women, as Clothiers Wives and their Women Servantes and not in Apprentices, they be therby verye lyke to bee utterlye undone for ever, oneles spedye remedy be therin provided : In consideration wherof, be it enacted established and ordeined by the Quenes most Excellent Ma1', withe thassent of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the C5mons in this pnte Pliament assembled, and by thaucthorite of the same Pliament, That every persone or persones inhabiting in any of the sayd Cities Borowes or Townes Corporate, or in Market Townes within the Realme of Englande, where Clothe making at any tyme before the making of the sayd Acte hathe been used, shall or may from hensforthe lawfully make all maner of Brode Clothes aforesayd, and put them to weaving walking fulling dyeng and shearinge, without any Impediment, so that the same Clothes be substantially made, bearing lawful lengthe breadthe and waight, according to the Statute for goodd and trewe Clothe making made in the fifthe yere of the Raigne of our sayd late Soverayn Lorde King Edwarde the Sixthe; Any Article or Clause in the sayd former Estatute, or any other Estatute for Clothe making made to the contrarye in any wise notwithestanding.
