CHAPTER VIII.

An Acte touching the buieng and corrieng of Leather.

WHERE at the Parliament holden at Westminster upon Prorogation the fyftethe daye of Aprill, in the sixte yere of the Raigne of our late Sovereine Lorde King Edwarde the Sixthe, it was amongest other thinges enacted, that no persone or persones of what estate degree or condition soever he or they bee, should buy engrosse or cause to to be bought or engrossed any kinde of tanned Leather to sell the same agayn, saving onelye Sadlers Gyrdelers Cordeweiners and certayn other Artificers, as by the same Acte more playnelye maye appeare: Sithens the making wherof, forasmuche as many poore Artificers as Shoomakers and Coblers, who afore that might buy from tyme to tyme their Stuffe of the Corrier, ready provided and wrought sufficientlye, and to buy the same at a price reasonable, and nowe being very poore Men and not able to buye twoo or three Hides or Backes of Leather at one tyme, nor to paye readye moneye for the same, arre enforced to gyve upp their Occupations in greate nomber, to their utter empoverishement and undooing: And forasmuche also as sythens the making of the sayd Estatute, All kinde of Stuffe made of Leather ys more slenderlye and deceiptfullye wrought and made then ever it was, and neverthelesse as deare or dearer, wherby it maye appeare that the sayd former Acte was procured for the synguler comodite of a fewe riche Shoomakers and other Artificers that arre nowe comon Regratoures and Engrossers of Leather, who without respecte of perfecte woorckmanshippe, either of the Comonwealthe, whiche is well perceyved bothe in meiies purses and also in their shoes, thexperience is well proved, they having thonelye trade of buieng of Leather Stuffe and Talowe in their handes, and notwithestanding, doo delyver to the Corrier so little Stuffe and Talowe, wherby the Leather cannot bee sufficientlye wrought. And forasmuche as the Corners arre by divers lawes bounden to the sufficient woorckemanshippe and corrieng of Leather upon divers paynes wher they maye buye no Leather nor the Shoomaker will not allowe them sufficientlye to doo the same: Be it therefore enacted, that from hensforthe yt shall bee lawfull aswell for the Corryer Shoomaker Gyrdler Sadler Bugetmaker and all other Artificers occupieng the Crafte or Misterie of Leather, buieng, lawfully to buy all kindes of tanned Leather in Fayres and Markettcs within all places of this Realme accustomed to be solde, yt being lawfully tanned and dressed, so that the sayd Corriers Shoomakers and Girdelers, nor any persone for them or for their use, shall buye any kynde of tanned Leather to sell agayn to any Marchant or other Stranger to bee conveyed over the Sea, ne shall sende ne conveye any Leather beyonde the Sea, upon the forfeiting of all suche Leather so bought, thone half of the same to the Quenes Highnes, and thother half to him that presentethe the same: And further, the foresaid Acte from hensforthe to be repealed made voide and of none effecte concerning the Corryers Shoomakers Sadlers Bugetmakers Girdelers and all other Artificers, occupieng the Mistery of Leather buieng corried and dressed.

And be it further enacted, That from hensforthe no persone or persones occupieng the Feate or Misterye of corrieng of tanned Leather within the Citie of London or Suburbes of the same, shall occupie about the corrieng of the same Leather any other Stuffe or Tallowe brought unto him by any other persone or persones but such as shalbee his owne, uppon payne of forfeyture of all suche Leather so corried contrarye to the true meaning therof: And furthermore, that no Corner shall corrye any Hides for any Shoomaker to make Shoos or Bootes of, from the feast of S' James Thapostle unto the xxv14 day of Marche, but suche as shalbee dipped sufficientlye twise in the panne for the true and just worckmanshippe therof, upon payne of forfeiture of all suche Leather as shalbe wrought to the contrary, thone halfe of the same to the Quenes Highnes, and the other moitie to him that shall finde and present the same: all the same penalties to be recovered in fourme aforesaid, by him or them that will sue for the same by Action of Dett Byll Plainte or Informacon in any Courte of Recorde, wherin no Essoigne Proteccion ne Wager of Lawe shalbee admitted ne allowed for the Defendaunte.

Provided alwaies and be it enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd. That when and as often as any Shoemaker or his Deputie dothe bring any Leather sufficientlye tanned to any Corner to be coried, delivering sufficient Liquor for well dressing of the same; the same shalbe by every suche Corrier well and sufficiently corried and made readie for the Shoemaker within the space of fyve dayes in Sommer, that is to saye, from the first daye of Marche to the last daye of September ; and also in lyke maner within the space of tenne days in Winter, that is to saye, from the first daye of October unto the last daye of Februarie; uppon payn to forfet to the ptie greyed, for every Hide not corried and dressed in maner and fourme aforsaid the some of Tenne shillinges. Piiovided further, that this Proviso shall not extende to binde any Corrier to dresse any Leather whiche he, doing his best, is not liable to dresse within everie of the times aforesayd, but shall extende to all suche Leather as he convenientlye inaye dresse after the comon rate of dressing.

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte touching Ordin"nces and Rules in Cathedrall Churches and Scooles.

WHERAS the late noble Prynce of famous memorye King Henrye the Eight Father unto our most gracious Sovereine Ladye the Quene, amonges other his godly Actes and doinges, did erefte make and establishe divers and sundrye Churches aswell Cathedrall as Collegiate, and endowed every of the same withe divers Manours Landes Tenementes and Possessions for the maintenaunce of the Deanes Prebendaries and Ministers within the same, and for other charitable Actes to be doone and executed by the same Deanes Prebendaries and Ministers; and also dyd encorporate the same [ Deane1 ] Prebendaries and Ministers, and made them Bodyes Politike in perpetuall succession, according to the Lawes of this Realme of Englande ; And Where also as the sayd late King for the better maintenaunce and preservac&n of the sayd Churches in a Godly Unitie and good order and governaunce, graunted unto the severall Corporations and Bodies Corporate of every of the sayd Churches, that they shoulde be ruled and governed for ever according unto certaine Ordinaunces Rules and Statutes to be specified in certayne Indentures then after to be made by his Highnes, and to be delivered and declared to every of the Bodies Corporate of the sayd severall Churches; As by the severall ereccons and foundaeftns of the said Churches more plainlye it dothe and maye appeare: Since whiche sayd Ereccbns and Foundacbns the sayd late King dyd cause to be delyvered to every of the sayd Churches so as ys aforesayd erected and incorporated by certaine Commissioners by his Highnes appointed, dyvers and sundry Estatutes and Ordinaunces made and declared by the same Commissioners, for the Order Rule and Governance of the sayd severall Churches and of the Deanes Prebendaries and Ministers of the same; Whiche sayd Statutes and Ordynaunces were made by the sayd Commissioners and delyvered unto every of the CorporacSns of the sayd severall Churches in writing, but not Indented according to the fourme of the said Foundations and Erections, By reason wherof the said Churches and the severall Deanes Prebendaries and Ministers of the same, have no Statutes or Ordinaunces of any force or aucthoritye wherby they should be ruled and governed, and therfore remayne as yet not fully established in suche sorte as the godly intent of the said late King Henry theight was, to the great Imperfecc&n of the same Churches and the hinderaunce of Goddes Service and good Order and Regiment to be hadd and continued amonges the Ministers of the same: And Forasmuche as thaucthoritie of the making of the said Estatutes Ordinaunces and Orders was reserved onely unto the sayde late King, and no mention made of anye lyke aucthoritie to be reserved unto his heires and successoures, the same Orders and Statutes cannot nowe bee made and provided without aucthoritie of Pliament: Maye it therfore please the Quenes Highnes that it maye be established and enacted by her Highnes by the assent of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Comons of this pnte Pliament assembled and by the aucthoritee of the same. That our saide Sovereine Ladye the Quene from hensforthe during her naturell lyes (whiche our Lorde long preserve) shall have by vertue of this Acte full power and aucthoritee to make and prescribe unto every of the sayd Churches, and the Deanes Prebendaries and Ministers of the same, and to their successoures, suche Statutes Ordinaunces and Orders for the good Governance Rule and Ordre of every of the same Churches Deanes Prebendaries and Ministers of the same, and of the Landes Manoures Tenementes and Possessions of everie of the same Churches as shall seme good to her Highnes, the same Statutes and Ordinaunces to be made by her Highnes by writing sealed withe the Greate Seale of Englande, and to bee delivered to the Deanes Prebendaries and Ministers of every of the sayd Churches for the tyme being.

And that it may bee further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd. That our sayd Sovereigne Ladye the Quene during the tyme aforesaid, by writing sealed withe the Greate Seale of Englande shall and may alter transpose chaunge augment or diminishe the sayd Orders Statutes and Ordinaunces of every of the sayd Churches from time to time as occasion

CHAPTER X.

An Acte for the Repeale of a Statute made for the uniting of the Parishe Churches of Onger and Grenestede in the

Countie of Essexe.

C)

LAMENTABLIE complayning shewen unto yor (*) Highnes yo' obedient and faithefull Subjectes thinhabitauntes and Parishioners of the Townes and Villages of Chipping Onger otherwise called Castell Onger and Grenestede within yor Graces Cowntye of Essexe ; That where by the sinister Labour and Procurement of one Willyam Morys Esquyer yor Graces late Servaunt deceased, sometime Patrone of the Parishe Churche of Onger aforesayd, and one of the Burgesses of the Parliament holden at Westminster in the seconde yere of the Reigne of the late King of worthye memorye Edwarde the Sixte your Highnes Brother, inordinately seking his private lucre and profitt, An Acte was made and ordeined, by aucthoritee of Pliament in the same seconde yere, for a Consolidation and Union to bee hadd and made of the Parishe Churches of the sayd Townes or Villages of Onger and Grenestede, and that thinhabitauntes and Parishioners of Onger aforesayd shoulde resorte and repaire for Dyvyne Service [ into3 ] the Churche of Grenestede aforesayd, as to their Parishe Churche; whiche Acte was devised and pursewed onely by the sayd Willyam Moris without the consent or knowledge of yo' said humble Suppliauntes, and dothe conteine in yt false suggestions and untrewe surmises, aswell concerning the distaunce and value of the said [Churche4 ] and Benefices as other thinges therin mentioned : By colour of whiche Acte the sayd William Moris in his lief tyme didd not onely enter in and to the sayd Churche and Churchyarde of Onger aforesayd and the Mansion House and Glebe Lande of the Parsonage therof, but also in and to divers other peces of Lande to the sayde Churche apperteining, throughe the whiche yo' saide Subjectes of Onger aforesayd and all other yo' Highnes liege People heretofore have hadd their highe waies and pathes from time to tyme accustomablye used tyme out of mynde, and didd also take awaye all the Ornamentes Belles [Vestimentes5 ] Chalices and Leade of the (6) Churche to his owne use, and hath covered the said Churche agayn with Tyle, wherby yo' said Subjectes ever sence the time of the said Acte have wandred as She|>e without their Shepeherde to straung Parishes for Dyvine Service and Administration of Sacramentes, by reason that the said Churche of Grenestede ys not able to conteine thone halfe of the said Parishioners, neither the Curate of Grenestede able in the Winter Season to passe the Brookes running and overflowing betwen the Townes of the same Parishes, whos Churches ar distant three quarters of a mile and more, so that divers of the said Towne of Onger in the said time have dyed not onelye without Confession and Counsail of their Curate, but also withoute thadministration of the Holye Sacramentes and other Rites of the Holie Churche, to the greate perill and daunger of their Soules, to the greate [ greves7] and sorrowe of yo' said humble Subjectes, and to the greate disease and discomodite of them and their successoures inhabitauntes and Parishioners there in tyme to come, onles by yo' Grace and this Highe Courte of Pliament, Remedye maye bee provided in that behalf: The Premisses therfore considered, and forasmuche as the Parsonage of Onger, wherof the sayd Willyam Moris was Parishioner, was before the said Union worthe tenne powndes yerely so long as the sayd William did trulye and fullye paye hisTythes, and that thinhabitauntes onely of That from hensforthe every Parson and his successoures Parsones of the Churche of Onger, and the Parishioners of the same, shall have by this Acte from hensforthe the Scite of the sayd Churche of Onger and other Howses belonging to the same, and all the Parsonage Glebe Landes and Groundes called the Cimitorie, and other Howses I^andes Tenementes and Profites belonging or occupied with the same or any parcell therof withe thappurtenaunces, in lyke maner as the said Parsones and Parishioneres or any of them late helde occupyed or enjoied the same : Any Graunt Clause or Article conteined in the said late Acte or Statute to the contrarye in any wise notwithstanding.

(*) Provided alwaies and Be it enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That the said Parsonage of Grenestede and the Incombentes of the same for the time being, shall be dischardged and exonerated of and for all Tenthes, wherwth the said Parsonage of Chipping Onger is in any wise charged or due out of the same in any of the Quenes Majesties Courtes, by reason or for any Tenthes growing going or arising out of the said Parsonage of Chipping Onger, or by reason of thunidng of the same.

CHAPTER XI.

An Acte touching the Sea Sandes in Glamorganshire.

WHERE in the xxiij yere of the Reigne of the Excellent Prince of famouse memorie King Henry theight, It was enacted and established, That Comissions of Sewers from tyme to time when nede should require, should bee directed to suche substancyal| and indifferent persones as should bee named by the Lorde Chauncello' of Englande, the Lorde Treasurer, the Lorde Pryvie Seale, and the twoo Cheife Justices or thre of them, wherof the Lorde Chauncellour to be one, authorising them or syxe of them to surveye Walles Streames Dyches Bankes Gutters Sewers Guttes Cawseies Bridges Trenches Milles Mylledames Fludgates Powndes Cockes Ebbing Weires and other Lettes and Nuysaunces, by reason of the outrageous course and rage of the Sea in and uppon Marshes and other lowe Places; Which good Lawe dothe not extende nor is not taken to give aucthoritee and power unto the sayd Comissioners of Sewers to refourme the greate hurte nuysaunce and losses that cdmethe and chaunceth to the Quenes Highnes and her Subjectes, by reason of Sande rising out of the Sea and dryven to Lande by Stormes and Windes, wherby muche good Grounde lyeng on the Seacoastes in sundrye Places of this Realme and especially in the Countye of Glamorgan, bee covered with suche Sande rising out of the Sea that ther cdmethe no Profitte of the same, to the greate losse of the Quenes Highnes and her loving Subjectes, and more ys lyke to ensue yf spedye Remedie be not therin provided: Maie it therefore please the Quenes Highnes withe the assent of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Parliament assembled, and by thaucthoritee of the same, Be It Enacted, That aswell the sayd Acte of Sewers made in the sayd xxiij,h yere, as all Comissions of Sewers hereafter to bee directed according to the tenour of the said Acte, maye extende and gyve aucthorite that the Comissioners therin named for the Countie of Glamorgan, or syxe of them, wherof three to bee of the Quorum, shall by this Acte and the sayd former Acte and Commission to them directed, have full power and aucthoritee from time to tyme to make suche Lawes Provisions Ordinaunces Judgementes and Decrees within the said Countye of Glamorgan, for the redresse and saving the sayd Groundes from hurt or destruction by reason of the said Sandes, as they might or may doo by the said former Acte and Comission, for the withstanding and avoiding of the outragious course and rage of the Sea, or other Waters; Any Usage or Custome to the contrary notwithestanding.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte touchinge tres patentes and other writinges to be signed by the Quenes Majestie.

WHERE in the Pliament begone and holden at Westminster the seconde daye of Aprill in the first yere of the Reigne of our most dreade and gracious Sovereigne Ladye the Quenes Ma,le, and ther contynued and kepte till the dissoluc&n of the same, being the fifthe daye of Maye then next folowing, One Acte was made touching tharticles of her Highnes most noble Mariage; in the whiche Acte amongest other thinges. It was enacted ordred and establyshedd by thaucthoritee of the said Pliament, That all and singler Gyftes Grantes tres Patentes Exchanges Confirmac&ns Leases and other Writinges, which after the sayd Maryage and during the same shoulde passe and bee made, of anye Benefices Offices Landes Revenues and Fruites or of anny of them, shoulde be Intituled and made in the Names of our Sovereigne Lorde the King and of her most Excellent Highnes, whether his Malic shoulde bee present within the Realmes and Dominions of her Highnes, or within any of them, or absent; And that the same Gyftes Grantes Letters Patentes Exchanges ConfirmacSns Leases and other Writinges, so sett for the and made, shoulde bee sealed and signed withe the Signe Manuell of her Highnes; and the same so signed and sealed withe Greate Seale of this Realme, or withe suche Seale as hathe beene accustomed, should be by thaucthoritee of the sayd Pliament demed adjuged declared and pronounced to bee as good perfecte and of lyke force strengthe and effecte in the Lawe, to all internes construccons and purposes against our said Sovereigne Lorde and Ladye the King and the Quenes Ma*" and her Highnes heircs and successoures, as if her Ma" had bene at the tyme of making therof sole and unmaried; and that all Gyftes Grantes tres patentes Exchanges Confirmac&ns Leases and other Writinges, whiche after the said Mariage, and during the tyme of the same, should passe and bee made of the said Benefices Offices Landes Revenues and Fruites or of any of them, whereunto the Signe Manuell of her Highnes shoulde not bee sett made or put, shalbee by thaucthoritee of the said Pliament from tyme to tyme demed adjudged accepted taken and decreed to bee of no force ne effecte but utterly frustrate and voide in the Lawe to all internes construcc&ns and purposes; the sayd Mariage or anny Lawe Usage or Custome to the contrarye in annye wise notwithestanding: as by the said Acte more at lardge doethe appeare: Sithence the making of whiche Statute and the Solempnisac&n of the said Maryage, the Quenes most Excellent Majestie hathe bene greatly molested greyed and troubled, withe often signing of Letters Patentes Giftes Grauntes Exchaunges Leases and other Writinges concerning and touching Benefices Offices Landes Revenues and Fruites, made and graunted by and from our said Soveraigne Lorde the King and her Highnes, to sundrye of their most loving Subjectes; to whom also it hathe bene and ys no small charge to attend untill suche tyme as they maye procure and obteine the Signe Manuell of her Highnes unto their said Letters Patentes Giftes Grauntes Exchaunges Confirmac&ns and Leases, without which Signe the same are utterly voide by force of the said Statute, to the greate daunger losse and utter undoing of dyvers persons that have lately bought purchased or obteyned of our said Sovereigne Lorde and Ladye the King and Quenes Majesties dyvers Landes Tenementes and other Hereditamentes to their greate Costes and Chardges: For Remedie wherof, Be it enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnt Pham', That the said Braunche or Article touching or concerning onelye the signing of Letters Patentes Gyftes Grauntes Exchaunges Confirmaf&ns Leases, or of other Writinges for any Landes Benefices Offices Revenues Fruites or other Hereditamentes, shall bee from hensforthe derely repelled and made frustrate and voide to all intentes and purposes.

And Be it further enacted by aucthoritee of this pnt Pliament, That all and singler Letters Patentes touching or concerning any Gifte Graunt Exchaunge Confirmac&n Lease or other Writinge, the whiche sithens the said Mariage hathe passed and bee made of any Benefices Offices Manours Landes Tenementes Revenues Fruites Liberties or other Hereditamentes or of any of them, in the Names of our most dread Sovereygne Lorde and Ladye the King and the Quenes Majesties (the Warrante or Writinge or Warrauntes or Writinges wherof being signed withe her Highnes Signe Manuell, in suche fourme order and degree as the same heretofore have bene accustomed to be signed when her Highnes was sole and unmaried) shalbee by aucthoritee of this pnt Pliament, of the same lyke force strengthe and effect in the Lawe to all internes construccons and purposes as if the same were or hadd bene signed by her Highnes Signe Manuell, and as if her Majestie hadd bene at the tyme of the making therof sole and unmaried, and as they were before the making of the said Acte: the said Estatute or any Branche or Article therin conteyned to the contrarye in any wise notwithestanding.

CHAPTER n.

An Acte for the ReformaPon of Excesse in Apparaile.

BE it enacted by thaucthoritie of this pnt Pliament, That no pson borne within this Realine or the Dominions of the same, other then the sonne and heire apparant of a Knight, or other then suche as maye dispende twentie powndes by the yere in Landes Offices Fees or other yerely Revenues for terme of lyes, or bee woorthe in gooddes twoo hundrethe powndes, shall after the first day of Aprill next coming, weare any maner of Sylke in or upon his Hatt Bonett Nightcappe Gyrdell Hose Shooes Scabberd or Spurre Leathers, upon payne of three monethes imprysonement, and [forfeitures1 ] of Tenne Powndes for every dayes wearing contrary to the tenour of this Acte.

And Be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That Justices of Assises in their [Circuities1 ] Justices of Peace in their Sessions Sheriffes in their Turnes Stewardes in Leetes and Lawe Days Mayours Sheriffes and Baylyffes of Cytyes Boroughes and l'ownes Corporate in their Courtes, shall and maye enquyre here and deteimyne from tyme to tyme all and every the sayd Offences doone or comitted within the lymites of their severall jurisdiccftns and aucthorities: And where any suche forfeytures shall happen to be fownde within the precincte of any Cytye Boroughe Towne Corporate Leete or Lawe Daye, then the Maiour Sheriffe and Baylyffes of the said Cytyes Boroughes and Townes, and Owner of the sayd Leete or Lawedays, to have thone Moytee of the sayd Forfeytures, and thother Moitie to bee to any subjecte of this Realme that will sue for the same in any Courte of Recorde by Acc&n Information Byll or otherwise, in whiche no Wager of Lawe Protecc&n or Essoigne shalbee allowed : And wher suche Forfeiture shalbe fownde out of any Cytye Boroughe Towne Leete or Lawedaye, that the Moitie of all suche Forfeitures shalbe to the King and Quenes Majesties and theires of the Quene, and thother Moitie therof to any of their Subjectes that will sue for the same by Byll Playnte Acc&n Informac&n or otherwise in any Courte of Recorde as is aforesaid, in whiche no Wager of Lawe Proteccon or Essoigne shalbee admitted or allowed : And that all and every suche persone and persons as have aucthoritee by vertue of this Acte to heare and determyne the premisses, may upon the convicf&n of every such Offendo' award Proces unto the Sherefe of any Shire within this Realme for the apprehencion of the said Offendo', whiche being apprehended shall bee comitted by the Shirefe unto the Gaole of the said Shire, ther to remayne without Bayle or Mayneprise untill the sayd Offendo' hath payde the Forfeiture wherin he is so convicted.

And Be it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That yf any persone or persons of what Estate Condic&n or Degree soever he or they bee, after the sayd first day of Aprill nexte coming, knowing any Servante or Servantes of his or theirs to offende contrary to this Acte, doe not put the same out of his or their Service, but shall kepe in his or their Servise the same Offendour or Offendours by the Space of Fowrtene Days next after suche knowledge had, or ells being so put out of his or their service, shall reraine the same Offendour or Offendo" to his or their service agayn, within one yere next ensuing the tyme of comitting any suche Offence, the same person or persons so keping or reteyning againe, in or to his or their service, any suche servante or servantes offending contrary to the tenour of this Acte as is aforesaid, shall for every his or their Offence forfeite One Hundre he Powndes of lawfull Money of Englande: The Moietie wherof to be to the King and Quenes Majesties use, and the heires and successoures of the Quene, and thother Moietie to him that will sue for the same in any Courte of Recorde, by Acc&n Byll Plaint Informac&n or otherwise, wherin no Wager of Lawe Essoigne or Proteccon shalbe admitted or allowed.

(*) Provided alwaie and Be it enacted, That this Acte or any thing therin conteined shall not extende to any person being of or above the degree of a Knightes sonne or doughter, or being wief to any of them, nor to suche as have bene bee or shalbe Maiour Baylyef Alderman or Headd Officer in any Citie Boroughe or Towne Corporate, or to the wief of any of them, nor to any of the Kinges or Quenes servantes in ordinarye wages attendant, and wearing the Kinges or Quenes ordinarye lyveries. But that they and every of them may use and weare as they or any of them might lawfully use and weare before the making of this Acte.

Provided also that no person shalbe compelled by this Acte to put away his Prentice or hired Serv*nte before thende of the terme before agreed betwen them, nor that any M' shall forfeite or lose anye paine or forfeiture for the keping of his Prentice or hired Servante after his Offence contrarie to this Acte unto the ende of the terme before agreed betwen them : Any thing abovesaid to the contrary notwithestanding.

Provided also that Women maye weare in their Cappes Hattes Gyrdells and Hoodes as they or any of them might use and weare lawfully, before the making of this Acte.

An Acte against sedityous Woordes and Rumours.

WHERE it is conteyned as well in the Statute of Westm the First, as in the Statute made at Glocester the seconde yere of the Raigne of King Richarde the Seconde, That no Man shoulde bee so hardye to contryve speake or tell any false Newes lyes or other suche lyke false thinges of Prelates Dukes Earles Barons and other Noble* and Peares of the Realme, or of the Chancelour Treasurer Clerck of the Pry vie Seale Stewarde of the Kynges Householde Justices of thone Bancke or of thother, or of any of the greate Officers of this Realme : And that every suche Offendo' shoulde be taken and imprisoned untill suche tyme as he hadd brought him or them for the whiche did speake the same ; And where also at a Pliam' holden at Cambridge in the twelvethe yere of the reigne of the said King Richard, It was also enacted that where any suche Offendo' as is aforesaid shoulde be taken and imprisoned, and coulde not finde him of whom he hearde those Newes whiche he spake as is aforesayd, that then the same speaker shoulde bee punished by the Advice of the Cowncell; As by the same Actes amongest other more playnelye doo and maye appeare: Be it enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnt Pliam1, That all and every the said former Actes and Statutes shalbe and remaine in their full force strengthe and effect to all internes constructyons and purposes: And further that Justices of Peace in every Shire Cytie and Towne Corporate within the lymites of their severall C.omissions shall by aucihoritie of this pnte Acte, have full powre to examyne heare and determyne the causes abovesaid in the said two firste Actes specyfied, and to put the said twoo first Statutes and every branche in them conteyned in due execucftn, that from hensforthe condigne punishement be not deferred from suche Offendours.

And it is lykewise enacted by thaucthoritie aforesaid, That all and every pson and psons whiche after the said dave and after Proclamac&n made of this Acte, shall maliciouslye speake any false sedicious and sclanderous Newes Rumours or Tales to the sclander and reproche of o' said Sovereigne Lorde the King or of our said most naturall Sovereigne Ladye the Quene, of the speaking or reporting of any other, that then all and every suche pson or psons so speaking and reporting being therof convicte or attainted in fourtne hereafter in this Acte expressed, shall for every suche Offence in some Markett Place within the Shire Citie Boroughe or Towne, wher or nere unto the place where the said wordes were or shalbee so spoken and reported, bee set openly upon the Pylorye by the Sherif or his Ministers, yf it shall fortune to be without any Citie or Towne Corporate, And if it shall happen to be within any Citie or Towne Corporate then by the principall Officer or Officers of suche Citie or Towne Corporate or his or their Ministers, and ther to have one of his eares cut of, onles he paye One hundrethe Markes to the Kinge and Quenes Highnes use, within one monethe next after jugement gyven of his said Offence, and also shall suffer Imprisonement by the space of one monethe after his or their Execuc&n.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte for the punishement of certayne Persons calling themselves Egiptians.

WHERE in a Parliament holden at Westminster in the xxij yere of the Reigne of our late Sovereigne Lorde King Henry theight. For thavoyding and banishing out of this Realme of certaine outlandishe People calling themselves Egiptians, using no crafte nor feate of marchaundises for to lyve by, but going from place to place in greate Companies, using greate suttle and craftye meanes to deceyve the Kinges Subjectes, bearing them in hande that they by Palmestrye coulde tell Mens and Womens Fortune ; and so many tymes by crafte and subtiltie deceyve the People of their money, and comitted divers greate and heinous Felonies and Roberies, to the great hurte and deceypte of the People, It was amongest other things then enacted, That from the tyme of the making of the said Acte, no suche psons should be suffred to come within this the Kinges Realme, upon payne of forfeyture to the King all their Goodes and Cateles, and then to be comaunded tavoide the Realme within tyftene days next after the edmaundement, upon payn of Imprisonement; and suche psons calling themselfes Egiptians as then were within this Realme, shoulde depart within xvj dayes next after Proclamacbn of the said Acte, upon paine of Imprisonement and Forfeiture of all their Goodes and Catells; withe divers other Clauses and Articles conteyned in the sayd Acte, as by the said Acte more at large it appearethe : Forasmuche as dyvers of the sayd Companie and suche other lyke psons not fearing the penaltie of the said Statute, have enterprised to come over againe into this Realme using their olde accustomed develishe and noughty practises and devises, withe suche abhominable lyving as is not in any Christian Realme to be permitted named or knowen, and bee not dulie punished for the same, to the perillous and evell example of our Sovereigne Lorde and Ladye the King and the Quenes Majesties most loving Subjectes, and to thutter and extreame undoing of divers and many of them, as evidentlye dothe appeare: Fon Reformation wherof, Be it ordeined and enacted by the King and Quene our Sovereigne Lorde and Lady, the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnt Pliam' assembled and by the aucthoritee of the same. That if any pson or psons after the last day of Januarie next coming, doo willinglye transporte bring and conveye into this Realme of England or Wales any suche psons calling themselfes or comonly called Egiptians, That then he or they so transporting bringing or conveyeng in any suche psons, contrary to the true meaning of this Acte, shall forfeite and lose for every tyme so offending, fourtye powndes of lawfull moneye of Englande.

And Be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That if any of the said psons called Egiptians whiche shalbe transported or conveyed into this Realme of Englande or Wales as ys aforesayd, doo continue and remaine within the same by the space of one monethe, that then he or they so Offending, shall by vertue of this Acte bee demed and judged a Fellon and fellons and shall therfore suffer paynes of Deathe losse of Landes and Goodes as in cases of Fellony, by thorder of the Comen Lawe of this Realme, and shall upon the tryall of them or any of them therin be tried in the Countie and by thinhabitantes of the Countie or Place where they or he shall be apprehended or taken and not p medietatem lingue, and shall lose the benefite and privilege of Sainctuary and Clergie.

And Be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That yf the Egiptyans or other persones comonly calling themselfes Egyptians and every of them now being within this Realme of Englande or Wales, doo not depart out of the same within xx" days next after Proclamacon of this pnt Acte shalbee made, that then he or they whiche shall not depart within the said time according to the true meaning of this Acte, shall forfeite and lose all his and their Goodes and Cattels; and that then it shalbe lawfull to all and every the King and the Quenes Subjectes to sease the same, thone moietie therof to be to thuse of our Sovereygne Lorde and Ladye the King and the Quene, and the other moietie therof to be to thuse of him or them that shall so sease the same.

And Be it also enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid. That if the Egiptians and other psons comonly called Egiptians and every of them nowe being within this Realme of Englande or Wales, doo not departe out and from the same within xl* dais next after Proclamacbn shall be made of this Acte, that then he or they whiche shall not depart and avoide within the said time of xl. days according to the true meaning of this Acte, shalbe judged and demed according to the Lawes of this Realme of England a Fellon and Fellons, and shall suffer therfore paynes of Deathe, losse of Landes and Goodes as in other cases of Fellonye, and shall bee tryed as ys aforesaid, and without having any benefite or privilege of Sainctuarie or Clergie.

And Be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid. That if any pson after the first day of Januarie next coming, shall sue for thobteining of any Lycence Letter or Pasporte, for any of the said psons called Egiptians tabide or continue within this Realme of Englande or Wales contrary to the tenour of this Acte, that then every suche pson so suing shall forfeite and lose for the same xl ti. of lawfull money of Englande; and that every suche Lycence Letter and Pasporte shalbe by vertue of this Acte voyde to all intentes and purposes; thone moietie of all whiche somes of money to be forfeited as is beforesaid, shalbe to the King and Quene our Sovereigne Lorde and Ladye, and thother moitie therof to be to him or them that will sue for the same in any Courte of Recorde, by accbn of Dett Bill Plaint or Informacon, wherin any Essoigne Wager of Lawe nor Proteccbn shalbe admitted [and1 ] allowed.

Provided alwaies and Be it enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That this pnt Acte nor any thing therin conteined, shall not extende nor be hurtfull to any of the said psons comonly called Egiptians, whiche within the said time of XX. daies next after the said Proclamacbn to be made as is beforesaid, shall leave that noughtye idle and ungodly

CHAPTER V.

An Acte to restrayne carrieng of Come Victuals and Wood over the Sea.

'TX7'HERAS sundry good Estatutes and Lawes hathe bene made within this Realme in the time of the Quenes W Highnes most noble Progenitoures, that none shoulde transporte carrye or conveye out of this Realme into any place in the parties beyonde the Seas, any Come Butter Chese or other Victuall, (Except onely for the vitailing of the Towne of Caleis Hames and Guisnes and the Marches of the same,) upon divers greate paynes and forfeitures in the same conteyned; That notwithestanding, many and sundrye covetous and unsariable psons seking their onely lucert and gaynes, hathe and dayly dothe carye and convey innumerable quantitie aswell of Come Chese Butter and other Victuall, as of Wood, out of this Realme into the pties beyonde the Seas ; By reason wherof the sayd Come Vyctuall and Wood arre growen unto a wonderfuli dearthe and extreame pryses, to the greate detryment of the Common wealthe of this yo' Highnes Realme and yor faithefull subjectes of the same: For Remedie wherof, It may please yo' Highnes that it may be enacted and be it enacted by yo' Highnes by thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this present Pliam' assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same, That no maner of pson or psons after the xx* daye of Januarye next coming, shall carye and transporte out of this Realme, by any Shippe Craier or other Vessell whatsoever, into any place in the parties beyonde the Seas or into the Realme of Scotlande, any Wheate Rie Barley or other Come or Grayne growing within this Realme, or any Maulte made within the same, or any Bere Butter Chese [Hearing 1 ] or Wood, (Except onlye to and for the victualing and furniture of the Townes of Callys Hames and Guisnes and to the Towne of Barwick and the Marches of the same,) without sufficient and lawfull aucthoritie so to doo, upon the paines and penalties hereafter ensuing; that ys to saye, thowner and owners of the sayd Shippes and other Vessells to forfeite the said Shippes Craiers and other Vessels, with all their apparelles to them and every of them belonging, wherin the said Come Butter Cheese [Hearing' ] Victuall or Wood shall be so transported and caried ; and the Owners and Owner of the said Corne Butter Chese [ Hearing ' ] and Woodd to forfeite the doble value of the same so caryed and conveied, and the Mr and Mareners of the said Shippes Craiers and Vessells for evrcy suche Offence to forfeite all their Gooddes, and to be imprisoned by the space of one whole yeare without Baile or Maynprise.

And Be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That yf any pson or psons, after the said xx"1 day of Januarie, doo carye and conveye away by Boate Crayer or other Vessell, or otherwise, any Wheate Rie Barley Malte or other Come or Grayne, or any Beere Butter Cheese [Hearing1 ] or Wood to any Shippe or Vessell being on the Seas, or within any Haven Creeke or other place of the Border of this Realme, to be transported caried and conveyed into any place in the pties beyonde the Seas, or into the Realme of Scotlande, without sufficient aucthoritie so to doo; That then every Owner of the sayde Victuales Corne and other things abovesaid, so transported or caryed, and thowner and Owners of every such Boate or Vessell, and the Boatemen and Mareners of the same, shall lose forfeite and suffer all suche forfeitures paines and penalties as is above rehearsed ; Thone moietie of all and everye whiche forfeiture or forfeitures to be to the King and Quenes Highnes their heires and successours, and thother moietie to him or them that will sue for the same by Bill Informac&n Accon of Det or otherwise in any of the King and Quenes Highnes Courtes of Recorde, In whiche Acc&n Bill or Sute the Defendant shall not wage his Lawe nor have any Essoigne or Protecc&n to him allowed.

And Be it enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That yf any p6on or psons shall obteine of the King and Quenes Majesties, their heires or successoures, or any of them, any Lycence to cary and transporte any Come Victuall or Wood into any parties beyonde the Seas, that if he or they to whom any suche Licence shalbe granted, or any other to whom suche pson or persons having suche licence shall give grante or sell his or their said Licence unto, shall cary and conveye or cause to be caried and conveyed any more Corne Victuall or Wood then shall be conteined in his or their said Licence, shall forfeite the treble value of the said Come Victuall or Wood so caried and transported without sufficient aucthoritee, and shall suffer Imprisonement for one whole yeare in the common Gaole wher he shall bee apprehended, ther to remaine without Baile or Maineprise.

CHAPTER VIII.

An Acte repealing all Statutes Articles and Provisions made against the See Apostolick of Rome since the xx"' yere of King Henry theight, and also for thestablishment of all Spyrytuall and Ecdesiasticall Possessions and Hereditamentes conveyed to the Layetye.

WHEREAS since the xx" yere of King Henrye theight of famouse memorye. Father unto yor Majestie our most naturall Sovereigne and gracious Ladye and Quene, much false and erronious Doctrine hathe bene taught preached and written, partly by divers the naturall borne Subjectes of this Realme, and partly being brought in hither from sundry other foreine Countreis hathe bene sowen and spredd abroade within the same ; By reason wherof as well the Spiritualtie as the Temporaltie of your Highnes Realmes and Domynions have swerved from the Obedience of the See Apostolike, and declined from the unitie of Christes Churche, and so have continued, untill suche tyme as yo' Majestie beyng first raised up by God and sett in the Seate Roiall over Us, and then by his Devine and gracious Providence knitt in Mariage withe the most noble and vertuous Prince the King our Sovereigne Lorde yo' Husbonde, the Popes Holines and the Sea Apostolike sent hither unto yo' Majesties (as unto persons undefiled and by Godes goodnes preserved from the comon infecc&n aforesaid) and to the whole Realme, The most Reverende father in God the Lorde Cardinall Poole Legate de latere to call us home againe into the right waye, from whence we have all this long while wandred and strayed abroade : And We after sundry long and grevous plagues and calamities, seing by the goodnes of God our owne Errours, have [knowleged' ] the same unto the said most Reverende Father, and by him have bene and arr the reither at the contemplacon of yo' Majesties, receyved and embraced into the Unitie and Bosome of Christes Churche; and upon our humble submission and promise made, for a declarac&n of our repentance, to repeale and abrogate suche Actes and Statutes as had bene made in Pliam' since the said xx,y yere of the said King Henry theight, against the Supremacie of the Sea Apostolike, as in our submission exhibited to the said most Reverend Father in God by yor Ma" apperethe : The Tenor wherof ensuethe : We the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the C5mons assembled in this pnte Parliam’, representing the whole body of the Realme of Englande and the Dominions of the same. In the name of our selves pticulerlye, and also of the said bodye universally in this our supplication directed to yor Majesties withe most humble sute, that it may by yor Graces intercession and mean be exhibited to the most Reverende Father in God the Lorde Cardinall Poole Legate sent specially hither from our most Holy Father the Pope Julye the thirde and the See Apostolike of Rome, Doo declare ourselves very sory and repentante of the Scisme and Disobedience comitted in this Realme and Dominions aforesaid, against the said See Apostolike, either by making agreing or executing any Lawes Ordinances or Comaundementes against the Supremacie of the said Sea, or otherwise doing or speaking that might impugne the same ; offring our selves and promising by this our Suppplicacon that for a token and knowledge of our said repentance Wee be and shalbee alwayes readye, under and with thaucthorities of yo' Majesties, to thuttmost of our powers, to doo that shall lye in us for thabrogacon and repealing of the said Lawes and Ordinances in this pnte Pliam' aswell for our selves as for the whole bodye whom We represent: Whf.rupon We most humbly desire yo' Majesties, as psonages undefiled in thoffence of this body towardes the said Sea, whiche nevertheles God by his Providence hathe made subjecte to yo. To set furthe this our most humble Sute that We may obtaine from the See Apostolike by the said most Reverende Father, as well perticulerly as generally, Absolution Release and Dischardge from all daunger of suche Censures and Sentences as by the Lawes of the Churche We be fallen into: And that We may as children repentant be receyved into the Bosome and Unitie of Christes Churche, so as this noble Realme with all the Members therof may in this Unitie and perfecte Obedience to the Sea Apostolike and Popes for the tyme being, serve God and yo' Majesties to the furtherance and advancement of his Honour and Glorye, Wee arre at thintercession of yo' Ma" by thaucthoritie of our Holy Father Pope Julye the thirde and of the Sea Apostolike, assoiled discharged and delyvered from Excomunicacon Interdictions and other Censures Ecdesiasticall whiche hathe hanged over our heades for our said [defaultes * ] since the time of the said scisme mentioned in our (1) Supplicacon (4) It maie now lyke yo' Ma,K' that for thaccomplishement of our promise made in the said Supplication, that is to repeale all Lawes and Statutes made contrary to the said Supremacye and See Apostolike during the said Schisme, the whiche is to be understande since the xx" yere of the Raigne of the said late King Henrie theight, and so the said Lorde Legate doth accepte and recognise the same.

In the whiche Acte amongest other thinges ther is conteined certaine Provisions Paines Penalties and Forfeitures, for and against suche as shoulde by open preachinges expres woordes saienges writing printing overt dede or acte affirme or set furthe that the King of this Realme for the time being is not or ought not to bee supreame Heade in Earthe of the Churches of Englande and Irelande ne of any of them ; or that the Bishoppe of Rome or any other pson or psons other then the King of Englande for the tyme being is or ought to bee supreme Head of the same Churches, or any of them, as in the same Acte last before rehersed more at large is conteined and maye appeare: Be it enacted by aucthoritee of this present Pliam', that thes Clauses before rehersed, and other of the said Acte, concerning the Supremacye, and all and every Branche Article Woordes and Sentence in the same, sownding or tending to the derogacon of the Supremacie of the Popes Holines or the Sea of Rome, and all paines penalties and forfeitures made against them that should by any meanes set for the or extoll the said Supremacie, shall bee from henceforth utterly voyde and of none effecte.

And Where We yo* most humble Subjectes the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and Comons in this pnt Pliam* assembled have exhibited to yo* Majesties one other Supplicac&n in fourme following: We the Lords Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliam* assembled, representing the whole Body of this Realme, reauced and receyved by yo* Majesties intercession to the unitie of Christes Churche, and thobedience of the Sea Apostolike of Rome, and the Popes Holynes governing the same, make most humble suite unto yo* Majesties to be lykewise meanes and intercessoures that all occasions of contencbn hatred grudge suspicon and troble both outwardly and inwardly in mens Consciences, whiche might arise amongest Us, by reason of disobedience, maye by aucthoritee of the Popes Holynes and by the ministration of the same unto Us by the most Reverende Father in God the Lorde Cardinall Poole, by dispensaum tolleracon or permission respectively as the case shall require, be abolished and taken away, and by aucthoritye sufficient theis Articles following and generally all others whan occasion shall so require, may bee provided for and confirmed.

First, That all the Bishoprikes Cathedrall Churches Hospitalles Colleges Scoles and other suche Foundations nowe continuing, made by aucthorite of Parliament or otherwise established according to thorder of the Lawes of this Realme sithence this Scisme, may be confirmed and continued for ever. Item, that Mariages made Infra gradus prohibitos consanguinitatis affinitatis cognacois spualis, or w* might be made voide Propter impedimentum publice honestatis justicie, or for any other cause prohibited by the Canons oneiy, may be confirmed, and Children borne of those Mariages declared legittimate; so as those Mariages were made according to the Lawes of the Realme for the time being, and be not directly against the Lawes of God, nor in suche case as the Sea Apostolike hath not used to dispence withall. That lnstitucons of Benefices and other Promoc&ns Ecclesiasticall and Di*pensac6ns made according to the fourme of Thacte of Pliam* may be likewise confirmed. That all Judiciall Processes made before any Ordinaries of this Realme, or before any Delegates upon any Appeales according to thorder of the Lawes of the Realme, may bee likewise ratified and confirmed. And Finallie where certaine Actes and Statutes have bene made in the time of the late Scisme, concerning the Landes and Hereditamentes of Archebishoprikes and Bishoprikes, the suppression & dissolution of Monasteries Abbeis Priories Chantreis Colledges and all other the Gooddes and Cattalles of Religious Howses, Since the whiche tyme the Right and Dominion of certaine Landes and Hereditamentes Goodes and Cattelles belonging to the same be dispersed abroade, and come to thandes and possessions of dyvers and sundrye psons, who by gyfte purchace exchange and other meanes according to thorder of the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme for the tyme being, have the same: For thavoiding of all Scruples that might growe by any thoccasions aforesaid or by any other wayes or meanes whatsoever, It maie please yo* Majesties to be Intercessours and Mediatours to the said most Reverende Father Cardinall Poole, That all suche Causes and Quarrelles as by pretence of the saide Scisme or by any other occasion or meane whatsoever might be moved, by the Popes Holynes or See Apostolike or by anie other Jurisdiction Ecclesiasticall, maie be utterly removed and taken away ; so as all psons having sufficient conveiance of the said Landes and Hereditamentes Goodes and Cattelles as is aforesaid by the Comon Lawes Actes or Statutes of this Realme, may without Scruple of Conscience enjoy them, without Impeachem* or Troble by pretence of any generall Councell Canons or Ecclesiasticall Lawes, and clere from all dangers of the censures of the Churche.

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte for the punishement of Traterous Woordes against the Quenes Mall*.

Prayers for the Queen's Death in Schismatical Conventicles j

All Persons making such Prayers declared Traitors.

FORASMUCHE as nowe of late dyvers noughty sedicious malicious and hereticall psons, not having the feare of God before their Eies, but in a develishe sorte contrarye to the dutie of their Allegiance, have congregated themselfes together in Conventicles, in divers and sundry prophane places within the Citye of London, esteming themselfes to be in the true faithe, wher in dede they ar in Errours and Heresies, and out of the true trade of Christes Catholike Religion, and in the same places at several tymes using their fantasticall and scismaticall Services, lately taken awaye and abolished by aucthoritee of Pliam', have of their most malitious and cankerde Stomakes, prayed against the Quenes Ma'", that God woulde turne her Hart from Idolatrye to the true Faithe, or elles to shorten her dayes or take her quickly out of the waye: Whiche Prayer was never harde nor redde to have bene used by any good Christian Man against any Prince thoughe he were a Pagan and Infidell, and muche lesse against any Christian Prince, and especially so vertuous a Princes as our Soveraigne Ladye that now ys ys knowen to bee, whose Faithe ys and alwaies hath bene most trewe and Catholike, and consonaunte and agreing with Chyrstes Catholyke Churche thoroughout the Worlde dispersed : For Reformation whereof, Be it enacted by thaucthoritie of this pnte Pliam1, that every suche psone and psones whiche since the beginning of this pnt Pliam1, have by expres Woordes and Saienges, prayed required or desired as is aforesaid, or hereafter shall praye by expres Woordes or Saienges, that God should shorten her dayes or take her out of the waye, (whose lief Almighty God long preserve) or any suche like malitious Prayer, amownting to the same effecte, their Procuroures and Abbettours therin, shalbe taken reputed and judged Traytoures, and every suche prayeng requiring or desiring, shall be judged taken and reputed Highe Treason, and thoffendours therin, their Procuroures and Abbettoures being therof lawfully convicte according to the Lawes of this Realme, shall have suffer and forfeite as in cases of Highe Treasone.

Proviso on Repentance of Offender* already guilty.

Provided alwaie and Be it enacted, That if any pson or psons shalbe indicted for any thoffences aforesaid, done and ppetrated during this Session of this pnt Pliam1, and upon his or their arreignem1 shall shewe him or themselfes penitent for their offence, and submitt him or themselfes to the King and Quenes Mercye, and humblye desyre the same before such Justices or Comissioners before whom he or they shall be arraigned, that then no Judgem1 of ConvicfSn or Attaindo' of Treason shall be given against any suche pson or psons so being penitent, and submitting themselfes as is aforesaid; and in every suche cace the Justices or Comissioners before whom suche pson or psons shalbe arraigned, shall have aucthoritie by vertue of this Acte to prescribe adjudge and appointe suche Corporall Punishem1, other then Deathe, to suche Offendour and Offendours, as to them by their discretion shall seme convenient, and upon that penance prescribed and done to be discharged of the said Treason comprised in that Indictam1.

And albeit Wee the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliam' assembled, have firme hope and confidence in the goodnes of Almightye God, that lyke as he hathe hitherto miraculouslye preserved the Quenes Ma" from many greate and imminent pills and dangers, even so he will of his infinite goodnes gyve her Highnes strengthe the reither by our continuall prayours, to passe well the danger of delyverance of Childe, wherwithe it hathe pleased him (to all our greate comfortes) to blesse herre; Yet forasmuche as all thinges of this Worlde be uncertayne, and having before our eyes the dolourous experyence of thinconstante Govemement during the tyme of the Raigne of the late King Eduarde the Syxte, doo playnelye see the manifolde inconveniences great dangers and perils that maye ensue to this hole Realme yf foresight bee not used to prevent evill chances if they should happen: For thexchewing wherof, Wee the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnt Pliam* assembled, for and in consideratyon of a most speciall truste and confidence that Wee have and repose in the Kinges Ma'* for and concerning the good and politike Govemement Order and Administrac&n of this Realme in the time of the youge yeres of thissue or issues of her Ma" bodye to bee borne, if it should plase God to call the Quenes Highnes out of this pnte lyes during the tender yeres of such Issue or Issues, whiche God forbydde, according to such order and maner as hereafter in this pnte Acte his Heighnes most gratious pleasure ys shoulde be declared and sett for the, Have made our most humble sute by thassent of the Quenes Heighnes that his Ma"* woulde vouchesause taccepte and take upon him the Rule Order Education and Govemement of the said Issue or Issues to be borne as is aforesaid ; Upon whiche our sute being of his said Ma1* most gratiouslye accepted, it hathe pleased his Heighnes not onelye to declare, that like as for the first parte his Ma* verely trustethe that Almighty God who hath hitherto preserved the Quenes Ma* to give this Realme so good an hope of certayne Succession in the Bloodd Royall of the same Realme, will assiste her Highenes with his Graces and Benedictions to see the fruite of her bodye well brought for the lyve and able to goveme, wherof neither all this Realme nor all the Worlde besydes shoulde or coulde receive more comfort then his Ma* shoulde and woulde ; yet if such chance should happen, his Ma* at oure humble desyres is pleased and contented not allonely to accept and take upon him the cure and charge of the Education Rule Order and Govemement of suche Issues as of this most happie Mariage shalbe borne betwene the Quenes Highnes and him. But also during the tyme of such Govemement would by al waies and meanes studye travaile and employe himselfe to advance the Weale bothe publique and private of this Realme and Dominions theronto belonging, according to the said Trust in his Ma'" reposed, withe no lesse good will and affection then yf his Highnes hadd bene naturallye borne amongest Us: In consideracon wherof. Be it enacted by the King and the Quenes most Excellent Ma'"* by thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons of this pnte Pliam' assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same, That if it shall so please God to call the Quenes Ma'* out of this pnte lyes, which God forbidd, before thissue of her bodye inheritable to the Crowne of this Realme, if it be Male shall accomplishe thage of eightene yeres, or if it be Female before it shall bee of thage of fifetene yeres and not maried after the age of consent and before the said age of xv yeres. That then and immediatelye after and from the decease of our said Sovereigne Ladye the Quene, the Kinges Ma* that nowe ys shall have the Rule Order Education and Govemement of the pson of suche Issue or Issues, and the Rule Order and Govemement, under such Issue or Issues, of this Realme and the Dominions to the same belonging, untill the same Issue or Issues inheritable to thimperiall Crowne of this Realme, yf yt bee Male, shall accomplishe thage of xviij'h yeres, and if it bee Female untill such Issue Female shall accomplishe thage of xv yeres or be maried after thage of consent and before the said age of xv yeares, yf the sayd Issue or Issues and our said Sovereigne Lorde the King shall so long lyve togither; and that during and by all the tyme of suche Govemement, all and every the Pactes Covenantes Articles and Agreamentes mentioned and coprised in the Treatises and Actes of Pliament and every of them made and concluded for and concerning thonerable Mariage hadd and consumate betwene the Kinge and Quenes Ma'"*, whiche on the behalf of his Ma* bene to bee observed perfourmed and kepte, shall after the decease of the Quenes Ma"*, during the tyme of the said Govemement, remayne continue and bee in as good and full force strengthe and effecte to all internes and purposes as they were at any tyme during the said Manage or nowe bene, (') as yf they were newly by apte woordes termes and sentences inserted and rehearsed in this pnte Acte and newly made and enacted, to stande remayne continue and to bee observed and kept during the tyme of the said Govemement, and shalbe by his Ma"' during the sayd rime inviolably observed perfourmed maintayned and upholden, in suche sorte and in as full large and ample maner to all respectes as they shoulde and ought to bee during the tyme of the said Mariage or after; and his Highnes and the Quenes most excellent Ma"' arre pleased and contented that it be Enacted by this pnte Pliam*, That nothing shalbe doone pmitted or assented unto by his Ma"' to the contrarye.

And it is further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That no pson or psons shall in any wise bee impeached for any of the Offences abovesaid, comitted onely by open preaching or woordes, oneles the Offender or Offenders be [therfore4 ] indicted within syxe monethes next after the same open preaching or woordes; Any thing conteyned in this Acte to the contrarye notwithestanding.

CHAPTER XI.

An Acte for the punishement of bringing in of counterfeite Coine of forreyne Realmes, being currant within

this Realme.

WHERE divers and sundry Coines of Golde and Silver of other Realmes, not being of the proper Coine of this Realme of Englande, and yet by the suffrance and consent of the King and Quene our Sovereigne Lorde and Ladye be currant in paiment within this Realme, many ill disposed psons for their owne corrupte lucre and advantage, have nowe of late brought into this Realme from the parties of bevonde the Sea greate quantitie of forged and counterfeite money like to the sayd Coine of other foreine Realmes, and have uttered the same here by Marchandising and otherwise to diverse of the subjectes of this Realme, to their greate deceipt hurt and damage, because the sayd yll disposed psons have perceyved and understanded that ther was not nor yet is anye sufficient Lawe or Statute made or provided for the condigne punishement of thoffenders in that behalf; Wherfore Be it enacted and established by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliament, That if any pson or psons, after the twentithe day of Januarye next coming, shall bring from the parties of beyonde the Seas, (') or into any the Dominions of the same, any suche false and counterfeite Coyne or Money being curraunte within this Realme as is aforesayd, knowing the same Coine or Money to be false and couterfeite, to the intent to utter or make paiment withe the same within this Realme or any the Dominions of the same by marchaundising or otherwise, That all and every suche pson or psons so offending as is aforesaid theyre Coucellours procurours aydours and abettours in that behalf shalbe demed and judged to be offendo" in Highe Treason, and shall suffer, after lawfull convictyon or attaindor therof, such paines of deathe losse and forfeitur of landes gooddes and cattelles as other offendors shall doo in cases of Highe Treasone.

And Be it further enacted by thaucthoritie aforesayd. That all and everye persone and psons, that shall at any tyme after the said twentithe daye of Januarye be accused or impeached of any of thoffences conteined and provided for in this Estatute, or of any other offence or offences concerning thimpayring couterfeiting or forging of anye Coyne currant within this Reahne, shall and maye bee endicted arraigned tryed convicted or attaynted by suche lyke evydence and in suche maner and fourme as hathe bene used and accustomed within this Realme at any tyme before the first yere of the raigne of our late Soveraigne Lorde Kinge Eduarde the Syxte: Any Statute Custume Lawe or Usage to the contrarye therof in any wise notwithestanding.

Cattle distrained shall not be driven out of the Hundred, except to an open Pound, &c.

CHAPTER XII.

An Act touching thimpounding of Distresses.

FOR thavoiding of grevous vexations exaccons troubles and disorder in taking of Distresses and impoundyng of Cattayle : Be it enacted by thaucthorite of this pnte Pliam', That from and after the first daye of Aprill next coming. No Distres of Cattell shall bee dryven out of the Hundrede Rape Wapentake or Lathe wher suche [Distresses’] ys or shalbe taken, Excepte it bee to a Pownde overte within the said Shyre, not above three myles distante from the place where the said Distresse ys taken ; and that no Cattell or other Gooddes, distreigned or taken by way of Distresse for any maner of cause at one tyme, shalbe impounded in severall places, wherby the Owner or Owners of suche Distres shalbe constreyned to sue severall Replevis for the delyverye of the said Distresse so taken at one tyme; upon payne every persone offending contrarye to this Acte shall forfaite to the partye greyed for every suche Offence, one hundrethe shillinges and treble Damages.

And further Be it enacted by thaucthoritie aforesaid. That after the said first daye of Aprill, no pson or psons shall take for keping impownde impownding or pondage of any maner of Distres, above the some of iiij d. for any one hole Distres that shalbe so impounded, and where les hathe bene used, ther to take les, upon the payne of fyve powndes to be payd to the partie greyed, over and besides suche monye as he shall take above the some of iiij d. Any Usage or Prescripcbn to the contrary in any wise notwithestanding.

And for the more [spedye1 ] delyverye of Cattell taken by waye of Distres, It ys further enacted by the said aucthoritee, That every Shyryff of Shyres, being no Cyties or Townes made Shires, shall at his first Coutie daye or within two monethes next after he hathe receyved his Patent of his Office of Shirifwike, shall depute appointe and proclaime in the Shire Towne within his Balywike sour Deputies at the least dwelling not above twelve myles one distant from an other, whiche said Deputies so appointed and proclaymed shall have aucthorite in the Shiriffes name to make Replevies and Delyverance of suche Distresses, in suche maner and fourme as the Shirif may or ought to doo; upon payne that every Shiriff, for everye monethe that he shall lacke suche Deputie or Deputies, shall forfeite for every suche Offence fyve powndf; thone halfe of whiche forfaytures shall be to the Kinge and Quenes Highnes her heires and successoures, The other halfe to him that will sue for the same, by Bill Playnte Information or Accon of debte, in any the Kinge and Quenes Courtes of Recorde, in which no Essoigne Protecc&n nor Wager of Lawe shall bee admitted.

CHAPTER Xin.

An Act appointing an Order to Justices of Peace for the Bailement of Prisoners.

WHERE in the Pliam* holden at Westminster in the thirde yere of the reigne of the noble Prynce King Henrye the Seventhe, It was among other thinges ordeined and enacted, That no Prysoner arrested for Felony shoulde bee letton to Bayle or Mayneprise by any one Justice of Peace, but by the whole Justices or at least by twoo of them wherof One to be of the Quoru: Synce the making of whiche Estatute one Justice of Peace, in the name of himself and one other of the Justices his compagnion, not making the said Justice partie nor pryvie unto the case wherfore the Prysoner shoulde bee bayled, hathe often tymes by sinister labour and meanes sett at large the greatest and notablest Offenders, suche as be not replevisable by the Lawes of this Realme, and yet the reither to hide their affecc&ns in that behalf, have signified the cause of their apprehencftn to bee but onely for suspicion of Felonye, wherby the sayd Offendo" [ hathe' ] escaped unpunished, and doo daylye, to the highe displeasure of Almightye God, the greate perill of the King and Quenes true Subjectes, and encoragment of allTheves and evill doers: For Reformacftn wherof be it enacted and ordeined by the King and Quenes Ma"" the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliam* assembled and by aucthorite of the same, That from and after the first daye of Aprill next cfiming, no Justice or Justices of Peace shall lett to baile or maineprise any suche pson or psons, whiche for any Offence or Offences by them or anye of them comitted bee declared not to be [replevisable*] or bayled, or be forbidden to be replevied or bayled by The statute of Westminster Primer, made in the Pliant* holden in the thirde yere of the reigne of King Edwarde the firste:

And furthermore that any pson or psons, arrested for manslaughter or felonye or suspecc&n of manslaughter or felonye, being baileable by the Lawe, shall not after the sayd first daye of Aprill bee lett to Baile or Maineprise by anye [Justices5] of Peace, yf it bee not in open Sessions, Excepte yt be by twoo Justices of Peace at the least wherof One to bee of the Quoru, and the same Justices to be pnte together at the tyme of the said Bailement or Mayneprise ; whiche Bailem* or Mayneprise they shall certyfie, in writing signed or subscribed with their owne handes, at the nexte generall Gaole Delyverye to be holden within the Countie wher the said pson or psons shalbe arrested or suspected: And that the said Justices or one of them being of the Quoru, when any suche Prysoner ys brought before them for any Manslaughter or Felonye, before any Bailement or Maineprise, shall take thexaminacon of the said Prysoner and informacSn of them that bringes him, of the facte and circumstances therof, and the same, or asmuche therof as shalbee materiall to prove the felonye, shall put in writing before they make the same Bailem*, whiche said examinacSn togither withe the said Bailem', the said Justices shall certefie at the next generall Gaole Deliverye to bee holden within the lymytes of their Comission

And that every Coroner, upon anye Inquisition before him fownde, wherby any pson or psones shalbee indicted for murther or maslaughter, or as accessarye or accessaries to the same before the murther or manslaughter comitted, shall put in writing theffecte of thevidence geven to the Jurye before him being materyall; and aswell the said Justices as the said Coroner shall have aucthorite by this Acte to bynde all suche by Recognisance or Obligation, as doo declare any thing materiall to prove the said Murther or Manslaughter Offences or Felonies or to bee Accessarie or Accessaries to the same as is aforesaid, tappeare at the next generall Gaole Deliverye to be holden within the Countie Citie or Towne Corporate wher the tryall therof shalbee, then and ther to gyve Evydence against the partie so indicted at the tyme of his tryall; and shall certifie aswell the same evidence as suche bonde and bondes in writing as he shall take, together with thinquisition or indictament before him taken and fownde, at or before the tyme of his said trial 1 therof to be hadd or made : And lykewise the said Justices shall certefie all and every suche [bounde4] taken before them in lykemaner as before ys said of Bailementes and Examinacon : And in case anye Justice of Peace or Quorum or Coroner, shall after the said first daye of Aprill offende in any thing contrary to the true intente and meaning of this pnte Acte, that then the Justices of Gaole Delyverye of the Shire Citie Towne or Place where suche Offence shall happen to be comitted, upon due proofe therof by examinacon before them, shall for every suche Offence sett suche fine, on every of the 6ame Justices of Peace and Coroner, as the same Justices of Gaole Deliverie shall thinck meete, and shall estreate the same as other Fines and Amerciamentes assessed before Justices of Gaole Delyverie ought to bee.

Provided alwaies and Be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That Justices of Peace and Coroners within the Citie of London and the Countie of Middlesexe, and in other Cities Boroughes and Townes Corporate within this Realme and Wales, shall within their severall jurisdice&ns have aucthoritee to letto bayle Fellons and Prysoners, in suche maner and fourme as they have bene heretofore accustomed, This Acte or any thing therin conteyned to the contrarye notwithestanding ; And also shall take examinations and bondes as is aforesaid, upon every Bailement by them or any of them to be made, and shall Certifie every suche Bailementes Bondes and Examinac&ns by them or any of them taken or made, at the next Gaole Delyverye to be holden within the Shire Citie Borowe or Towne wher their severall Jurisdictions extendethe; upon like payne and forfeiture as is before limited in this pnte Acte.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Act for the making of Russelles Sattins Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Naples in the Citie of Norwiche.

WHERE of late yeres passed, Russels called Russelles Sattens and Sattens Reverses have bene practised to be made beyonde the Seas of the Woolles bredd in the Countye of Norfolke, and by reason therof so greate quantirie of the said Russels Sattens (') Sattens Reverses have bene brought into this Realme, solde and worne aswell in every parte of this 'Realme as in the partes beyonde the Seas, that therby the Misteries of Woorstedes making and weaving, wherby Marchantes and Inhabitantes of the Cyttye of Norwiche have heretofore bene well maintained and relieved, ys nowe at this pnte almost wholye decayed and brought out of estimac&n and very litle worne, either within this Realme or in any other forreine Realmes, to the greate hindrance and decaye of the said Citric and Citisens of the same Citie: Fok Remedie wherof, Thomas Marsham Maiour of the Cittie of Norwiche, John Corbet Esquire Austen Stewarde Robert Leche Robert Rugge John Ball and Alexander Mather Aldermen of the said Citie, Thomas Whall Thomas Peeke Raphe Marsham Robert Henrye John Sutton Richarde Tomson Citisens and Marchantes of the said Cittie, at their greate costes and chardges, aswell in bringing of certeine Strangers from the partes beyonde the Seas into the saide Citie, as also in making of Loombes and all other provision for the same, and also have called unto them Eight psons of the most discrete and worthy men of the misterye of Worstedd weaving within the sayd Citie, that ys to saye, John Cooke James Lyn John Crosse Symon Petyt John Marshall Roger Lecke Edmunde Barker and Edmunde Selers, being the number of xxj p6ons, whiche have not onely made Russels Sattens ( ') Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Naples within the said Citie of Norwiche, of Norfolke Woolles, But also have learned and taught other Citizens and Inhabitantes of the sayd Citie to make the same, in suche good and pfecte maner that muche better Russels Sattens Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Naples and suche like, and for easier prises, bee now at this pnt wrought and made within the sayd Citie then heretofore hathe been or nowe be made in any of the pties beyonde the Seas; wherby the said Citie and Inhabitantes therof maye and be like agayne to bee relieved and brought to [the* ] olde Estate, to the greate advancement of the Comodities of this Realme and enriching the same, yf some goodd and polirike Lawes and Ordinaunces were made for the good contynnuance of the true makinge of the sayd Russelles Sattens Sattyns Reverses and Fustians of Naples and suche lyke: In Considerac&n wherof Be it enacted by thassent of the King and Quenes Highnes the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons of this pnte Pliam1 assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same, That the sayd Russelles Sattens (1) Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Naples hereafter to bee made onely within the sayd Cytie may from hensforthe beare the name and be called by the name of Norwiche Sattens and Norwiche Fustians; and that the Maiour and thaforemenrioned Citizens of the same Citie, whiche before this tyme hathe been at the costes and charges of the bringing of the said Strangers into the same Citie for the making of the said Russelles Sattens Sattens Reverses and Fustians of Naples, and suche thaforemenrioned eight psons that they have called unto them, shalbe a Felowshippe of themselfes, and shall yerely the thirde daye of Februarye, choose of their felowes sower Wardens within the Guilde Hall of the said Citie, or any other comon and convenient place in the same Citie ; and the same Wardens so being chosen shall stande and be Wardens of the same Felowshippe during one whole yere next ensueng the said eleccon, and that the same Wardens after the said eleccon shall come before the Maio' of the said Citie for the time being yerely the Mundaye next after the said thirde daye of Februarye, and before the said Maior shalbe sworne diligentlye to viewe searche and see all the Russeles Sattens Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Naples then made or that shalbee made within the said Citie during the said yere ; And suche of the said Russelles Sattens Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Naples, as shall appeare and bee demed by them to be lawfully trulye and woorckemanlye wrought, shall seale with a seale of leade bearing the Armes of the Citie of Norwiche, wherby it maye bee knowen to the Merchant or Buyer of them that the same bee alowed and trulye made.

And that also it maye be enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That the said Wardens and Felowshippe shall be a

Bodye Corporate, and to be named and bee enabled by this Acte to sue and be sued and to give and to take by

the name of Wardens and Felowshippe of the Mysterye of Russell Sattens Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Norwiche making within the said Citie of Norwiche : And yf any defaulte at any time shall bee founde in any of the said Russells

Sattens Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Norwiche or in any of them by the said Wardens, that the same defaulte

shalbe refourmed, and thoffendo' or Offendo" therin to be punished, according to suche Rules and Ordinances as hereafter from tyme (1) shalbee made within the said Citie by the Maiour of the said Citie for the tyme being, and by the said foure Wardeines and the Felowshippe of the said Occupation or Misterie or the greatest nomber of the said Felowshippe for and concerning the same ; and that the same defaultcs from tyme to tyme as occasion shall serve shalbee enquired of and tryed before the Maio’ of the said Citie of Norwiche for the tyme being, by the Othes of twelfe honest Men of the foresaid Felowshippe ; And that the same sour Wardeynes so chosen and swome shall have full powre and aucthoritee to doo execute present and refourme all and singler thing and thinges, of for and concerning the said Misterie making woorcking and occupieng of the said Russelles Sattens Sattens Reverses and Fustian of Norwiche within the said Citie, in suche maner and fourme as in or by the said Ordinances shalbee expressed and declared ; and that at all tymes hereafter and from tyme to tyme, it shalbe lawfull to the Maio' of the said Citie for the tyme being, and to the beforenamed Felowshippe and Wardeines of the same Misterie and the more parte of them and to their successoures, to make and ordeine from tyme to tyme Rules Lawes and Ordinances meete and necessarye for the good Order and Governance of the said Misterye, and for the true and well making of the said Russelles Sattens Sattens Reverses and [Fustyans* ] of Norwiche ; and the same Ordinances so made to be at all tymes obeyed by all thinhabitantes of the said Citie or Suburbes of the
