CHAPTER XVL An Act for the continuance of certayne Statutes.

WHERE in the Pliament begone and holden at London the thirdd daye of November in the xxj yere of the Reigne of our most dreade Sovereine Lorde of most famouse memory King Henry theight, and from thence adjourned to Westin and ther holden and continued by dyvers prorogacfins unto the dissoluc&n therof, One Acte was made and established for the restraint of cariage and conveying of Horses and Mares out of this Realme: And also one other Acte was there made for the true winding of Woolles: And one other Acte was ther made to restreine killing of Wainlinges Bullockes Steres and Heifers being under thage of twoo yeres; whiche sayd several 1 Actes were then made to endure and continewe to the next Parliament, as by the said severall Actes more playnely appearethe: And where also in the same Pliam' One other Acte was made and established for Attaintes to bee sued for the punishement of Pjurye upon untrue Verdictes; whiche Actes last before rehearsed, were then made and ordeined to continue and endure to the last daye of the nexte Parliament, as by the same Acte more playnely at large is shewed and maye appeare : And where also in the Pliam' begune and holden at Westiri theight daye of June in the xxviijlh yere of the Reigne of our said most dreade Sovereine Lorde King Henry theight, and ther continued and kept [unto1] the dissolucbn therof, It was ordeined and enacted, that all and singler the said Actes above remembred and every of them, shoulde ‘continue and endure in their force and strengthe, and also be observed and kept until the last day of the next Plana', as by the same Acte amongf other things therin conteined more playnlye appearethe: And Where also in the Pliam' begune and holden at Westni the xxviij day of Aprill in the xxxj<k yere of the Reigne of our said late most dread Soveraigne Lorde King Henry theight, and ther continued untill the xxviij" daye of June then next following, It was ordfeined and enacted by thaucthorite of the same Parliament, that all and singler the sayd severall Actes above remembredd and every of them, and all Clauses Articles and Provisions in'them and every of them conteyned, shoulde continue and endure in their force and strengthe and also bee observed and kepte untill the last daye of the next Pliain1, As by the same Acte amonges other thinges therin conteyned more playnely appearethe : And where in the Parliament holden at Westminster in the xxxv"1 yeare of the Raigne of our sayd late Sovereigne Lorde King Henrye theight, One Acte was made for the preservac&n of Wooddes, to endure for seven yeres then next following, and from thence to the ende of the next Pliam’; Whiche sayd severall Actes were then and ther made to endure and continue to the ende of the nexte Parliament; As by the same severall Actes more at lardge it doethe and maye appeare: And where also at the Session of a Pliam' by prorogac&n holden at Westni the xxiij'h day of Januarie in the fifthe yere of the Reigne of our said Sovereigne Lorde, One other Acte was then and ther made against Regratours and Forstallers, tendure to thende of the next Pliam'; Whiche all and singler the said Actes above mentioned, togither withe the said Acte concerning the preservac&n of Wooddes, at a Pliam' holden at Westiii the first daye of Marche in the vij'k yere of the Reigne of our said Sovereine Lorde King Edoarde the Sixthe, and ther continued and dissolved the last daye of the same monethc of Marche, and all Clauses Articles and Provisions in them and everye of them conteyned, were ther revived, and continued to stande in their force and strengthe until the last day of the next Pliament: And where also at the Session of a Pliam* holden by prorogac&n at Westni the xxiiij*k day of October in the first yere of the Reigne of our most gratious Sovereine Ladye the Quene, and ther continued and kepte untill the dissoluc&n therof, One Acte was there made and established against Unlawfull and Rebellyous Assemblies, to endure to the ende of the nexte Parliament, as by the same Acte more playnely doethe and may appeare: And where also at the same Session of Pliam' last before mentioned, all and singler the Actes above mentioned, and before that time continued at sundry Pliamentes as is aforesaid, and all Clauses Articles and Provisions in them and every of them conteyned were ther revived, and continued to stande in their force and strength, unto the last daye of the next Pliam*: FonASMucHE as all and singler the said severall Actes above mentioned be good and beneficiall for the Comen Welthe of this Realme, Be it therfore enacted ordeined and established by the King and Quene our Sovereigne Lorde and Ladye, with thassent of the Lordes spuall and tempo rail and the Cdmons in this pnt Pliam' assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same. Provided alwayes and bee it enacted, That no Order or Decree to bee made by the said Comissionlz or any of them, shall bynde or conclude any right or interest of any pson or psons, nor the breache of any Decree or Order shalbee cause of forfeiture of the Right or Interest of any pson or psons. Except the same Decree & Ordinance so made by the said Comissioners & syxe of them, wherof A. B. C. shalbee three, bee ingrossed in pchement and certefied under theyr seales into the Courte of Chancerie, and that the Royall Assent of the Kyng & Quene her heyres [ & ’ ] successoures bee fyrst hadd to the same.

Provided also and bee yt enacted, That every Decree & Ordynance so had made certefied & assented unto, shall bynde all & every pson & psons that at the making of the same Decree hadd any interest in the lands teiitf or hereditamentf so decreed, in use possession revertion or remainder, their Heires & Feoffees and every of them; and not to bee in any wise refourmed Onles it be by aucthoritee of Pliament hereafter to bee sumoned & holden wlhin this Realme.

CHAPTER HI.

An Acte for the kepyng of Milche Kyne and for the breadyng and rearing of Calves.

FORASMUCH as of late yeres a greate nomber of psons w'"in this Realme have layde theyr Landes Fennes &e Pastures to feeding of Sheepe Oxen Runtes Schrubbes Steeres & Heckfers, and suche other lyke Cattell, having no regarde or care to brede & reare up yonge Beastes & Catell, wherby ys growen great scarsitee of Catell & Victuall necessarie for the sustenance of divers sortes of People w^in this Realme, and more ys lyke to bee, yf spedye Remedy bee not provided : It is therfore by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliam' enacted, That every pson wcl1 from the feast of the Purificac&n of o' Ladye next ensuing, shall kepe or fede above the nomber of syxe score shere Shepe for the most pte of the yere, upon his or their severall Pastures Landes Feedinges or Fermes apte or meete for Milche Kyne, and wherein [none other pson hathe at the making of this pnte Act Comon for any Cattell of any tyme of the yere, shall by aucthoritee of this Acte, yerely so long as hee kepe or feede the said nomber of syxe score shere Shepe, for every three score shere Shepe so kept or fedd, kepe one Milche Cowe and shall breede & reare up yerely for every sixe score shere Shepe so kepte as ys aforesaid one Calf, upon payne of forfeiture for every monethe that any suche pson shall not for every three score shere Shepe as ys aforesaid, kepe or feede one Milche Cowe, Twentye Shillinges for everye Cowe so not kept; And for lacke of rearing 8t breeding of one Calfe for every syxe score shere Shepe, to forfeite likewise xx s. for every Calf so not reared and fedd; and that ePy pson wch after the foresaid Feast of the Purificac&n of our Ladye, upon his or her severall Pastures as afore ys said, shall kepe or feede above the

CHAPTER V.

An Acte for the Reliefe of the Poore.

TO thintent that Idle and Loytering persons and valyant Beggers may bee avoyded, and thympotent feoble and lame, w1* arre the poore in verye dede, shoulde bee hereafter well provided for; Be yt enacted by the Kyng and Quene our Sovereigne Lorde & Ladye wth thassent of the Lordes Spuall & Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled, and by thaucthorite of the same. That the Statute made in the xxij111 yere of the late King of famous memorye King Henry theight, and also the Statute made in the iij° & iiij0 ye-°s of the reigne of the famous King Edoarde the Sixte, concerning Beggers Vagabondes & ydle psones, & every Article Clause Branche Sentence & other thinges conteyned in them & in either of them, other then suche things as shalbee by this pnte Acte otherwise ordeined and provided for, shall stande remayne & bee in their full force & effecte, and shalbee also from hensforthe justly & trulye putt in execuc&n, according to the true meaning of the sayd severall Statutes & either of them.

And further bee it enacted by thaucthorite aforesayd, That yerely on some one Holyday in the Christmas, in every Citie Bourghe & Towne Corporate, the Mayor Baylyefes or other Head Officers for the tyme beyng, and in every other pishe of the Countrey, the Parson Vicar or Curate, & the Churchewardens, having in a Regester or Booke aswell all the names of Thinhabitantf & Housholders as also the names of all suche impotent aged and [psons nedyp1] (1) being w^in their Citie Bourghe Towne Corporate or Pishe are not liable to live of themselves nor wth their owne labour, shall openly in the Churche & quietly after Dyvine Service call the said Housholders & Inhabitauntes together, among whom the Maior or other Head Officers & twoo of the cheif Inhabitantf in every suche Citie Burghes & Townes Corporate, suche as the Maior or other Hedd Officer shall thincke meete, & the Pson Vicar or Curate & Churchewardens in every other pishe, shall electe nominate & appoynte yerely twoo liable psons or moe to bee Gatherers & Collecto" of the charitable Almose of all the residue of the People inhabiting w«*in the Pishe wherof they bee chosen Collectors for the Relief of the Poore; w* Collectors, the Sundaye next after their Elecc6n or the Sonday following if nede require, when the People are at the Churche at Dyvine Service, shall gently aske & demaund of every Man and Woman what they of their Charide will bee contented to give wekely toward the Relief of the Poore, and the same to be writton in the said Register or Booke; and the sayd Gatherers so beyng elected & chosen shall justly gather & trulye distribute the same charitable Almose wekely by themeselves or their assignes, to the sayd poore & impotent psons of the said Cities Boroughes Townes Corporate & Pishes, w^out fraude or covyn favo' or affeccon & after suche sorte that the more impotent maye have the more helpe, and suche as can gett pte of their lyving to have the lesse, and by the discretyon of the Collectors to bee put in such labour as they bee fitt and liable to doo, but none to goe or sit openly a begging, upon payne lymited in thaforesaid Estatutes.

Bee it (3) enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That no pson or psons so elected nominated & appointed to bee Gatherer or Gatherers as is aforesayd shall refuse the said Office, but shall justly & truely execute the same by the space of one whole yere next ensuyng, upon payne to forfaite xl. s. to thalmes boxe of the Poore, to bee levied by the Churchwardens, where they or he dwellethe, of the Goods of the said Gatherer or Gathere" so refusing by distres.

And further bee yt enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That the said Gatherers or Collectors shal make their just Accompt quarterly to the Maiors or chief Officers of the said Cities Burghes & Townes Corporate, and in every pishe of y' coutrey, to the Pson Vicar or Curate & Churchewardens of the pishe, at wch accompt suche of the pishe as will may bee pnte, & when they goo out of their office they shall delyver or cause to bee delyvered foorthwlh upon thende of their Accomptf all suche Surplusage of Money as then shall remayne of their Collecton undistributed, to bee put in the Comon Cheste of the Churche or in some other safe place, to thuse of the Poore, at thoversight & discref&n of the Maiors Officers & other before mentioned : And if the said Collectors or any of them do refuse to make their said Accompt w,hin eight days, Then the Bishoppe of the Dioces or Thordinary of the Place shall have aucthorite by vertue of this Acte to compel the said pson or psons by censures of the Churche to make their said Accomptes before suche psons as the said Bishop or Ordinarie shall appoint, & to make immediat payment of the somes wherewth by determinacon of the said Accompt they shalbee chardged.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That yf any pson or psons being liable to further this charitable worck, doo obsdnatly & frowardly refuse to gyve towardes thelpe of the Poore, or doo wilfully discorage other from so charitable a dede, the Parsone Vicar or Curate & Churchwardens of the pishe wherin he dwellithe, shall then gently exhort him or them towardes the relief of the Poore, and yf hee or they will not so bee perswaded, then upon the certificate of the pson Vicar or Curate of the pishe to the Bishop of the Dyoces or Ordinarye of the Place, the same Bishop or Ordinarie shall sende for him or them, tinduce or perswade him or them by charitable meanes & wayes textende their Charitee as in this Acte is well ment & intended, & so according to discretion to take order for the charitable Reformation of every suche obstinate pson.

And for the better maynten*nce of this charitable worck, It ys ordeyned & established by aucthorite aforesaid. That whereas the late King of famous memorie King Henry theight, by his severall Erections & Foundac&ns hathe ordeyned & appoynted any some or s5mes of money to thuse of the Poore, not being taken away otherways by Acte of Pliament, whether the same bee in any Cathedrall Church Colledge or elswhere, the Bishoppe of the Dyoces for the time beyng shall from tyme to tyme examyne howe & after what maner the sayd money ys bestowed, and call taccompt the pties wdl retayne the said money, so that yt maye appeare that the same ys distributed to the Poore according to the goodd Intent & Purpose of the said noble King that graunted the same.

A.D. 1555

For remedying the Abuses of Purveyors 5

No Commissions to Purveyors shall endure longer than Six Months.

II.

Commissions shall specify the County, and the Particulars of the Cattle, &c. to be taken.

III.

Blanks shall be left for each County, and the Signature of the Constable, &c.

IV.

Purveyors shall sign a Docket of all Cattle, ire. taken; to be delivered to the High Constable, and by him to the Justices at Sessions, to be by them certified to the Lord Steward of the Household.

CHAPTER VI.

An Acte against thexcessive taking of Purveyours.

CHAPTER VII.

An Acte against the byeng of stolen Horses.

FORASMUCHE as Stolen Horses Mares & Geldinges, by Theves & their Confederates bee for the moste pte solde exchanged gyven or put awaye in Houses Stables Backsydes & other secrett & pryvie places of Marketes Sc Fayres, and the Toll also pryvily payde for the same, wherby the true owners therof, being not liable to trye the falshode & covyn betwene the Buyer & Seller of suche Horse Mare or Gelding, ys by the Comon Lawes of this Realme w^out Remedye: Bee yt therefore enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliam1, that the Owner Govemo' Ruler Fermo' Stuarde Baylyef or cheyfe Keper of every Faire & Markett overt w,hin this Realme & other the Queenes Dominions, shall before the feast of Easter next, and so yerely, appoynt & lymit out one certayn & speciall open place wthin the Towne Place Feylde or Cyrcuite where Horses Mares Geldings & Coltes hathe been & shalbee used to bee solde in any Fayre or Market overt; in wch said certayn & open place as ys aforesayd, there shalbee by the said Ruler or Keper of the said Fayre or Market, put in & appoynted one sufficient pson or more to take Toll & kepe the same place, from tenne of the Clock before None untill Sune set of every day of thaforesaid Faire & Market, upon payne to lose & forfeite for every defalte xl s. And that every Toll Gatherer his Deputie or Deputies shall, during the tyme of every the said Faires & Markets, take their due & lawfull Tolies for every suche Horst Mare Gelding or Colte at the sayd open Place to bee appoynted as ys beforesayd, And [betwen !] the Houres of tenne of the Clock in the Morning and the Sune sett of the same Day, yf yt bee tendered, & not at any other tyme or place; And shall have pntly before him or them at the taking of the same Tolle, the pties to the Bargayn Exchange Gifte Contract or putting awaye of every suche Horse Mare Gelding or Colte, and also the same Horse Mare Gelding Sc Colte so solde exchanged or put awaye, and shall then write or cause to bee writton in a Booke to bee kept for that purpose, tLe names surnames & dwelling places of all the said pries, and the colo', w,h one speciall marke at the least of every suche Horse Mare Gelding or Colte, in paine to forfeite at & for every defeulte contrary to the teno' hereof xls. And the sayd Toll Gatherer or Keper of the said Booke, shall wll,in one day next after every suche Faire or Market, bring & delyver his said Book to Thowner Govemo' Ruler Stewarde Bailief or Cheif Keper of the said Faire or Market, who shall then cause a note to bee made of the true nomber of all Horses Mares Geldingf Sc Coltes solde at the sayd Market or Faire, and shall there subscribe hys Name or set his Mark therunto, upon payne to him that shall make default therin, to lose and forfeite for every defaulte fortye shillingf, and also toaunswer the ptie greyed, by reason of the same his negligence in every behalf.

CHAPTER VIII.

An Acte for thamendyng of Highe Wayes.

For amending Highways, Surveyors shall be appointed yearly in Easter Week;

Penalty zos.

FOR amending of Highwais being nowe bothe verie noysome & tedious to travell in & dangerous to all Passengers and Cariages; Bee it enacted by thaucthorite of this pnte Pliam', That the Constables & Churchewardens of every pishe w,hin this Realme, shall yerely upon the Twesdaye or Wednesday in Easter weeke, call together a nomber of the Pochians, and shall then electe & choose twoo honest psons of the Pishe to bee Surveyo" & orderers, for one yere, of the worckes for Amendement of the Highewais in their pishe leading to any Market Towne, the wcl* psons shall have aucthoritee by vertue hereof torder and direct the psons & carriages y* shalbee appointed for those worckes by their discretions; And the sayd psons so named shall take upon them thexecucon of their said offices, upon payne ev*y of them making defaulte to forfeite xx s. And the said Cunstables

Four Days shall be appointed for repairing Highways before Midsummer, and Parishioners shall attend with Carts, Horses, and Tools, &c. according to the Land, &c. which they occupy.

& Churchewardens shall then also name & appointe foure days for thamending of the said Waies, before the feast of the Nativitee of S* John Baptiste then next following; And shall openly in the Churche the next Sondaye after Easter give knowledg of the same iiij dayes, & upon the sayd days the Pochians shall endevor themselfes to thamending of the said wais, & shalbee chargeable theronto as followethe ; that ys to saye, Every pson for every Plowlande in Tillage or Pasture, that he or she shall occupye in the same pishe, & every other pson keping there a Draught or Plowghe, shall finde & sende at every daye & place to be appointed for thamending of the Ways in that pishe as ys aforesaid, one Wayne or Carte furnished after the Costume of the Cuntrey, withe Oxen Horses or other Cattell, & all other necessaryes, meete to cary things convenient for that purpose, & also twoo liable men w,b the same, upon payne of every Draught making defaulte x s; and every other Housholder, & also every Cotagier & Labourer of that Pishe liable to labour, & being no hyred Servante by the yere, shall by themselfes or one sufficient Laborer for every of them, upon every of the said foure days, woorck and travayle in thamendement of the sayd Higheways, upon payne of every pson making Defaulte to lose for every day xij d; And yf the Cariages of the Pishe or any of them shall not be thought nedefull by the Supvisors to bee occupyed upon any of the said days, that then every [suche *] pson that shoulde have sent any suche Cariage, shall sende to the said woorck for every Cariage so spared twoo liable men there to labour for that daye, upon payne to lose for every Man not so sent to the

chapter X.

An Acte to take thexaminaeon of Prysoners suspected of Manslaughter or Felonye.

Recital of Stat. i, a P. k M. c. 13.

requiring Examination of Prisoners for Manslaughter or Felony, when bailed by Justices of Peace:

Like Examination shall take place when Prisoners are committed.

WHERE in the last Pliament holden at Westm, amongest other things it was enacted, That suche Justices of the Peace as have aucthoritee to bayle any Prysoners brought before them, for any Manslaughter or Felonye, before any Bailement or Mainprice shoulde take thexaminaeftn of the said Prisoner, & informac&n of them that bring him, of the facte & circumstances therof, and the same or asmuche therof as shalbee materiall to prove the Felony, shall put in writing before they make the same Bailement, w'h said examinacbn together w,h the said Bailement, the said Justices should certefie at the nexte generall Gaole Deliverie to bee holden w'Hn the limites of their Comission; as by the same Act more plainly is coteined & may appeare: And Forasmuche as the said Acte dothe not extende to suche Prisoners as shalbee brought before any [Justices1 ] of Peace for Manslaughter or Felonye, and by suche Justice shalbee comitted to Warde for the suspic&n of suche Manneslaughter or Felony, and not bayled, in w16 case examinacon of suche Prysoner, & of suche as shall bring him, is as necessarie or reither more, then where suche Prysoner shalbee lett to Bayle or Mayneprice: Bee yt therefore enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliament, That from hensforthe suche Justices or Justice before whom any peon shalbee brought for Manslaughter or Felony, or for suspicion therof, before hee or they shall comitt or sende suche Prisoner to Warde, shall take thexaminac&n of suche Prisoner, and informaf&n of those that bring him, of the facte and circumstance therof, and the same or asmuche therof as shalbee materiall to prove the Felonye shall put in writing, within twoo dayes after the said examynafon, and the same shall certefie in suche maner & fourme and at suche tyme as they shoulde & ought to doo yf suche Prysoner so comitted or sent to Warde had been bayled or lett to Maynprice, upon suche payne as in the said former Acte ys limited and appointed for not taking or not certefieng suche examinations as in the said former Acte ys expressed.

II.

Witnesses shall be bound to appear, &c.

And Bee yt further enacted, That the said Justices shall have aucthoritee by this Acte to bynde all suche by Recognisaunce or Obligation, as doo declare any thing materiall to prove the said Manslaughter or Felony, against suche Prisoner as shalbee so comitted to warde, tappeare at the next generall Gaole Delyverie to be holden w,hin the Countie Citie or Towne Corporate, wher the trial! of the said Manslaughter or Felony shalbee, then & there to give evidence against the ptie; And that the sayd Justices shall certefie the sayd Bondes taken before them, in lyke maner as they shoulde & ought to certefie the Bandes mentioned in the said former Acte, upon the payne as in the said former Acte ys mentyoned for not certefyeng such Bondes, as by the sayd former Acte ys lymited & appoynted to bee certefied.

CHAPTER XI.

An Acte touching Weavers.

Oppression of Weavers by Clothiers:

No Clothier out of a City shall keep mure than One Woollen Loom.

FORASMUCHE AS the Weavers of this Realme have, aswell at this pnte Pliament as at divers other tymes, complayned that the riche & welthie Clothyers doo many ways oppres them, some by setting up and keping in their houses divers Loomes, and keping & maynteyning them by Journeymen & psons unskilfull, to the decaye of a greate nomber of Artificers wch were brought up in the said Scyence of Weaving, their Families & Housholde, some by ingrossing of Loomes into theyr handes & possession, and letting them out at suche unreasonable Rentes as the poore Artificers are not liable to mayntayne themselfes, muche les their Wyefes Famulie & Children, some also by gyving muche les wages & hyer for the weaving & worckmanshipp of [Clothe * ] then in tymes past they did, wherby they are enforced utterly to forsake their Arte & Occupac&n wherin they have been brought uppe : It is therfore, for Remedye of the Premisses, and for thadvoiding of a greate nomber of inconveniences w'* may growe (yf in tyme yt bee not forseen) Ordeyned established & enacted by aucthoritee of this pnte Pliam*, That no pson using the feate or Misterie of Clothe makyng and dwellyng out of a Citie Burghe Market Towne or Corporate Towne, shall from the Feast of S' Mighell tharchaungell nowe next ensuing, kepe reteyne or have in his or their House or Possession any more or above one Wollen Loome at one tyme, nor shall by any meanes directly or indirectly receyve or take any maner Profit Gayne or Comodi tie by letting or setting any Loome, or any House wherin any Loome ys or shalbee used & occupied, w11* shalbee togethers by him set or let, upon payne of forfeiture for every week that any pson shall do contrarye to the teno' & true meaning hereof xx s.

II.

No Woollen Weaver out of Cities, &c. shall have more than Two Looms.

And Bee it further ordeined & enacted by like aucthorite, That no Wollen Weaver using or exercising the feate or Mistery of Weaving, & dwelling out of Citie Burghe Market Towne or Towne Corporate, shall after the said Feast have or kepe at any one time above the nomber of Twoo Wollen Loomes, or receyve any Profite Gayne or Cdmoditie, directly or indirectly as is aforesaid, by any more then Twoo Loomes at one tyme, upon payne to forfeite for every Week that any pson shall offende or doo to the contrary xxs.

CHAPTER XVI.

An Acte towching Watermen and Bargemen upon the Ryver of Thamys.

WHEREAS heretofore for lack of good Govemement & due order amongst Whirimen 8c Watermenne exersising using & occupyeng Rowyng upon the Ryver of Thamys, there have divers & many missfortunes & myschanses happened & chaunced of late yeres past, to a greate nomber of the King & Quenes Subjectes, aswell to the Nobilitee as to other the Comon People that have passed & repassed and been carried by Water, by reason of the rude yngnorant & unskilfull nomber of Watermen, wch for the most pte been masteries men and single men, of all kyndes of occupac&ns 8c faculties wch doo worcke at their owne handes, and many boyes beyng of small age and of lytle skyll, and beyng psons out of the rule and obedyence of any honest Master 8c Governo', and doo for the most pte of their tyme use Dycyng 8c Carding & other unlaufull Games, to the greate 8c evill example of other suche lyke, and against the Comonwelthe of this Realme; And all whiche sayd evill & ingnorant psons in the tyme of Prestyng by Comyssion for the Service of the Kynge and Quenes most Ryall Mall" upon the Sea, for that they have no knowen place of abydyng, doo for the moste pte absent & convey themselfes into the Countrye and other secrett places, practising there Robbryes k Felonies and other evill [8c’] detestable factes, to the greate annoyance of the C5monwelthe, and so after the said Comyssion of Presting ended, oftymes the said evill psons doo repayre agayne to their former trade of Rowyng, colouring their evill Deeds; And also dyvers of them being verie yngnorant, for lacke of convenyent tyme of learning & exercyse in the w* they might obteyne sufficient knowledg of their occupac&n, doo oftentymes presume & enterprise to receyve dyvers of our said Sovereigne Lorde & Ladye the King and Quenes Ma'f loving Subjectes into their Botes & Whyries, and doo carye & convey their said Subjectes from place to place by Water upon the said Ryver of Thamys, wherby dyvers psons have been robbed and spoyled of their Gooddes and also drowned; And for k by thoccasion aforesayd bee dayly put in feare and pill of their lyves, the wch ys very lamentable and not [to1] be pmitted or suffredd in any Comonwelthe; And by reason also that a greate nomber and the most pte of the Whines & Boates nowe occupied & used and of late tyme made for Rowing upon the said Ryver, been made so litle 8c small in [porcSn,4] and so [streight5] & narrowe in the bottome, varyeng muche from tholde substantyall sorte & sure makyng of Boates & Whiries w* was used before the space of twentye yeres last past, insomuche as the most pte of the Boates & Whiries used at this daye been so shallowe 8c tickle that therby greate pill & danger of drowning hathe many tymes ensued & dayly ys lyke tensue, oneles some spedye Remedye bee hereyn had and provided: For Reformation wherof, Bee yt enacted by the Kyng & Quenes Ma'", the Lordes Spuall 8c Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliam' assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same, That there shalbee yerely appointed chosen & elected by the Maio' & Courte of Aldreinen of the Citie of London for the time beinge, the nomber of eight psons. of the most wise discrete & best sorte of Watermen, being Housholders & occupieng as Watermen upon the said Ryver betwen Gravesende & Wyndsore, w* elecc&n shalbee yerely at the firste Cowrte of Aldermen to bee holden w^in the said Citie next after the first daye of Marche, and the same viij"1 psons so elected, shalbee named & called The Overseers and Rulers of all the Whirimen & Watermen that from and after the said first day of Marche shall use occupie or exercise any Rowing upon the said River of Thamys betwexte Gravesende & Wyndsore aforesaid, wrt said Overseers 8c Rulers shall kepe 8c maynteyne good order k obedience amongest the said Watermen, according to the true meanyng of this present Acte.

CHAPTER XXL An Acte for the contynuance of certayne Statutes.

WHERE in the Pliament begune & holden at London the thirde daye of November in the xxju* yere of the Reigne of our most drad Sovereigne Lorde of most famous memory King Henry theight, and from thence adjo'ned to Westm, and there holden & continued by divers prorogacSns unto the dissoluc&n therof. One Acte was made & established for the restrainte of carriage & conveyeng of Horses & Mares out of this Realme; And also one other Acte was there made for the true winding of Woolls; And one other Acte was there made to restrayne killing of Wainlingf Bullockes Steers & Heifers being under thage of twoo yeres; W* said severall Actes were then made to endure & continue unto the next Pliam', as by the said severall Actes more playnly appearethe: And wher also in the same Pliam1, One other Acte was made & established for Attaints to bee sued for the punishement of Pjurie upon untrue Verdictes; w1* Actes last before rehearsed were then made & ordeined to continue and endure to the last day of the next Pliam', as by the same Acte more plainly at large ys shewed & may appeare: And where also in the Pliament begune and holden at Westm the viij"1 daye of June, in the xxviij yere of the reigne of our said most dreade Sovereigne Lorde King Henry theight, and there continued 8c kepte untill the dissoluc&n therof, It was ordeyned & enacted that all 8c singler the sayd Actes above remebredd & every of them should continue 8c endure in their force 8c strengthe, and also bee observed 8c kept untill the laste day of the next Pliam', as by the same Acte amongst other thinges therin conteyned more plainly appearethe: And where also in the Pliament begune 8c holden at Westm the xxviij"1 daye of Aprill, in the xxxj yere of the reigne of our said late most dread Sovereigne Lorde King Henry theight, and there contynued untill the xxviij"1 daye of June then next following. It was ordeined and enacted by thaucthorite of the same Pliam1, that all & singler the said severall Actes above remembred Sc every of them, & all Clauses Articles & Provisions in them & every of them conteined, should continue 8e endure in their force 8c strengthe & also bee observed 8c kept untill the last day of the next Pliam', as by the same Act among other things therin conteined more playnly appearethe: And Where in the Pliam' holden at Westm in the xxxv"1 yere of the reigne of our said late Sovereigne Lorde King Henrye theight. One Acte was made for the preservac&n of Woodds, tendure for seven yeres then next following, & from thence to thende of the nexte Pliam', as by the same Act more playnely dothe & maye appeare: And Where also at the Pliam' holden at Westni in the xxxvij'" yere of the reigne of the said late King Henry the Eight, and there continued & kept until the dissoluc&n therof. It was ordeyned & enacted, that all 8c singler the said Actes above mentioned 8e every of them, (Except the sayd Acte made for the preservac&n of Wooddes as ys aforesayd,) shoulde continue 8t endure in their force & strength, & also to bee observed 8c kept untill the last day of the next Pliam' then next following, as by the same Acte amongst other things therin conteined more plainly appearethe: And Where also at a Session of the Pliam' ended at Westm the xiiij'1* day of Marche in the iij° yere of ye reigne of our late Sovereigne Lorde King Edoarde the Sixte, one Acte was made for the true currieng of Lether, w* Acte was made tendure to thende of the next Pliam', as by the same Acte more playnly appearethe : And Where also at the Session of a Pliam' ended at Westm the first day of Februarie in the fourthe yere of the Reygne of our said late Sovereigne Lorde King Edoarde the vju,) One Acte was then & there made concerning the buyeng of Rother Beastes; And also One other Acte was then 8c there made touching the buyeng and sellyng of Butter 8c Cheese; w"1 said severall Actes was then 8c there made tendure & continue to thende of the next Pliament, as by the same severall Actes more at large dothe and maye appeare:

CHAPTER II.

An Acte for the having of Horse Armour and Weapon.

FIR the better furniture and defence of this Realme, Be it enacted by the Kinge and Quenes Majesties, withe [thassent*] of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnt Pliament assembled, and by aucthorite of the same. That asmuche of all and every Acte and Statute, concerning onelye the keping or finding, of Horse Horses or Armoure or of any of them, heretofore made or provided, and all and everye forfeiture and penaltie concerning onelye the same, shalbe from hensfoorthe utterly voide repealed and of none effect.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte that Accessaries in Murder and divers Felonies shall not have the benefitte of Clergie.

Accessaries in Petty Treason, Murder, Robbery, or Arson, shall not hare Benefit of Clergy.

FOR the due punishement of suche as comaunde councell or hire any person or psons to comitte perpetrate or doo anye Petie Treason wilfull Murder or any of thoffences in this pnte Acte mentioned: Be it enacted by thaucthorite of this pnt Plam', That all and every pson and psons that after the firste daye of Marche nexte coming, shall maliciouslie comande hire or councell any pson or psons to comit or doo any Petie Treason wilfull Murder, or to doo any Robberie in any dwelling House or Howses, or to cdmitt or doo any Robberie in or nere any Highe Waye in the Realme of Englande or in any other the Quenes Dominions; or to comitt or doo any Robberie in any Place within the Marches of Englande against Scotelande, or willfully to bume any dwelling Howse or any parte therof, or any Bame then having Come or Grayne in the same ; that then everye suche Offender or Offenders, and every of them, being outlawed therof, or being therof arraigned and founde giltie by thorder of the Lawe, or being otherwise lawfullye attainted or convicted of the same Offence, or being arraigned therof doo stande muet of Malice or frowarde Mynde, or doo challendge peremtorie above the nomber of twentie persones, or will not aunswer directlye to suche Offence, shall not have the benefite of his or their Clergie.

II.

Peers shall be tried by Peers.

Provided alwaies and be it enacted, That every Lorde and Lordes of the Pliam', and Piere and Pieres of the Realme having Place and Voice in the Plam', upon every Inditement for any of thoffences aforesaid, shalbe tryed by their Piers as hathe bene accustomed by the Lawes of this Realme.

CHAPTER V.

An Acts towching the making of Wollen Clothes.

WHERE in the Plain' holden at Westminster in the Fifte and Sixte yeres of the Reigne of our late Sovereigne Lorde King Edwarde the Sixte, ther was by greate Deliberation and Advise one good Acte made for the true and perfect making of Wollen Clothe within this Realme; Sithens the making wherof, divers Clothiers founde themselfes agreved, alledging that it is impossible for them [tobserve' ] the same Acte in all pointes, and have in this pnt Pliam' prayed some Mitigation therof; It is therfor at their special Instance and Request ordered established enacted and provided in manner & forme following: In primis, that every White Clothe and Clothes cSmonly called Long Worcesters, and all like Clothes of like making mentioned in the said Acte, whiche by the same was limited to weigh Ixxxiiij" powndf being well skoured thicked milled and fully dryed, shall weighe Ixxv. powndf at the least. Item, every White Clothe whiche shalbec made in the Counties of Wiltsh' Glocester and Somerset, or any of them or ellswher of like making, being appointed by the said Act to weighe Ixiiij powndcs, shall weighe, being well skoured thicked mylled and fully dryed Ixj powndes at the leaste. Item, everie Broade Clothe made in the Shires of Kent and Sussexe, or at the Towne of Reding, or any of them or elswhere, of like making mentioned in the said Acte, whiche by the same was lymited to weighe fowreskore tenne poundes at the leaste, shall weighe beyng well scoured thicked milled and fully dryed, fowreskore sixe powndes at the leaste. Item, That every course shorte Clothe made in the Shires of Suff Norff and Essexe, or any of them or elswhere, of like sorte, and every course Clothe to bee made within the Shire of Kent not exceeding the price of Sixe powndes, all whiche by the said Acte ar appointed to conteine seven q'rters of a yarde at the least in Breadthe, shall conteine and be at the Water, being throughe wet, syxe quarters and a halfe within the Liste throughe and by all the whole Clothe at the leaste. Item, every yarde of Clothe comonly called Handywarpe, being well scoured thicked milled and fully dried, shall containe the Breadthe specified in the said Acte, and shall wayeghe twoo powndf and a halfe at the least.

And Forasmuche as many psones doo counterfeit the making of Cocksall Bocking and Braintree Clothes commonly called Handywarpes, adding therunto suche lyke Lystes as the makers of suche Clothes doo, to the great disceypte of the King and Quenes Majesties Subjectes: Be it therfore enacted, That no pson or p6ons from the first day of Maye next cdming, shall adde unto any Clothe or Clothes any suche like Liste or Listes excepte the Warpe therof be spune upon the Rocke or Distaff, upon paine of forfeiture of the same Clothe or Clothes, or the verie value therof. Provided alwaies that the Clothemakers within the Citie of Worcester may make suche Listes as they have doon heretofore.

Item, That no pson or psons inhabiting within the Westryding in the Countie of Yorke, shall make or cause to bee made any Broade Clothe or Clothes called Pewkes Tawneis Violets or Grenes, excepte the Wooll therof before it bee converted into Yarne, bee first dyed litted and coulered withe the coulour blue, of the value of ij d. a pownde, upon payne of forfeiture of every suche coulered Clothe, or the value therof, wherof the Woolle shall not be first dyed litted and coulered withe the coulo' Blue of ij d. a ti. as is aforesaid.

Item, That every ordinarie Karsey mentioned in the said Acte, shall conteine in lengthe in the water betwext xvj and xvij yardes, yarde and ynche, and being well scoured thicked milled dressed and fullye dryed, shall weighe ninetene powndes the peece at the least, and every Karseye called sorting Karsey mentioned in the said Acte, being well scouredd thicked milled dressed and fully dryed readye to be shewed, shall weighe twentye twoo powndes at the leaste. Item, that everye Devonshire Karsey called Dossone, the whiche is appointed by the same Statute to weighe being drie, xiiij powndes at the leaste, shall weighe being well scoured thicked milled and fully dryed after the rate of every yarde, one pownde at the least.

Item, That one Article mentioned in the said Statute concerning Welshe Cottons, towching the lengthe & weight, shalbee derely voide; and everie Gode of Welche lyning shall conteine and be three quarters of a yarde in Breadthe in the water, and shall weighe one pownde and a half quarter, and every yarde of Cotton being fully wrought and cottoned shall weighe one pownde at the leaste.

And bee it further enacted, That no pson or psons, whiche shall buy to sell agayn by way of Retaile or otherwise any of the said Welshe Lininges, shall dresse or woorcke or cause to be dressed or wrought within his or their Dwelling House or Houses, or in any other place by himself or his Serv*nt or Servauntes, any of the said Welshe Lininges, but shall put the same to some such pson or psons as shalbee of the Arte or Science of Sheremen Cottoners or Frisers, to be by them wrought and dressed, upon paine of forfeiture for every Welshe Cotton or Lining frised or cottoned to the contrary vj s. viij d.

Item, That all and every Cotton or Cottons called Manchester Lanckeshire and Cheshire Cottons, and all Clothes called Manchester Rugges or Manchester Frises, may be dyvided into Twoo halfe peeces, and shall conteine and be after the rate of suche Breadthe and Weight as in the said Acte ys lymited and appointed to bee a whole pece of every of the severall peeces of Cottons and Rugges aforesaid ; Any thing in the said former Statute to the contrary in any wise notwithestanding.

Item, The Article mentioned in the said former Acte of returning of defective Clothes Karseis Frises or Cottons being transported over the Seas by the Marchauntes shall bee utterly voide; But nevertheles be it enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That if it shall fortune hereafter any Marchaunt or Marchauntes, to transporte any Clothe or Clothes Karseis Frises or Cottons whereunto the Seale withe this Woorde (Faultie) was not annexed at the tyme of the Sale therof by the Clothier, and the same Clothes Karseis Frises of Cottons so transported, or any of them to be founde faultie or defective, and the same Marchaunte or Marchauntes therof, withein twoo yeares after suche Sale, to bring a Certificate sealed withe the Seale of any Towne or Companye in the pties beyonde the Seas, or signed by a Notarye ther, after thaccustomed manner, testifieng and declaring therby the losse and damage whiche the Marchantes shall have susteyned by suche defective and faultie Clothe or Clothes so transported, that then the Clothier or Clothiers or other person of whom the Clothe or Clothes was bought, their executoures or administratours, shall within Sixe Weekes next after request made by the said Marchaunt his executoures administratours or assignes, well and truly satisfie content and paye to suche Marchaunt his executoures administratours or assignes, all and every suche some and s5mes of Moneye as shall so bee mentioned expressed and declared in the sayd Certificate, upon payne of forfeiture to the partie greyed for everye none payment upon suche Request, double the value of suche some or somes mentioned in the sayd Certificate. Provided alwaies, That suche Marchaunte shall not in anye wise have by vertue of this Acte anye Recompence for lacke of Lengthe Breadthe or Weight of or for anye Clothe wheronto the Seale of anye Citie Boroughe or Towne Corporate shall bee fixede.

Item, If any persone shall by himselfe or by any other persone by him procured, contrefeit setto or take awaye from any Clothe Karseye Frise Rugge or Cotton, any Seale appointed to be fixed to any Clothe Karseye Frise Rugge or Cotton, either by this Acte or by the said former Estatute, that then every suche psone so offending shall incurre and have lyke penalties forfeitures and punishementes as in the sayd former Acte is appointed and lymited for the lyke Offence.

And for the better execucbn aswell of this pnt Acte as of the sayd former Estatute, and to thintent that all kinde of Karseis Cottons Frises Rugges and other Wollen Clothe made in any Towne shalbe the better knowen;

It ys further enacted, That the Seale of everye Boroughe or Towne Corporate apointed or to bee appointed for the sealing of any suche kinde of Clothe, shalbe fixed to all and everye suche kinde of Clothe being well and substantiallye made within suche Citie Burghe or Towne Corporate, whiche Clothe so sealed w* the Seale of any Citie Bourghe or Towne Corporate, shall not be searched tryed or viewed by any Searcher or Sealer of any other Citie Bourghe or Towne Corporate, by vertue of his said Office; Any thing in this Acte or in the said former Estatute to the contrarye notwithstanding.

Item, Be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd. That every personne and personnes not dwelling and inhabiting within any Citie Boroughe or [Towne Corporate,’] and making any of the Clothes or Karseis aforesayd, maye lawfullye bring the same to the nexte Citie Boroughe or [Towne Corporate’] where anny suche kinde of Clothes or Karseis bee or shalbee comonlye made, ther to bee sealed in maner and fourme as is before expressed.

Item, Wheras dyvers auncient Cities Boroughes and Townes Corporate withein this Realme of Englande, hathe been in tymes past well and substanciallye inhabited occupied mainteined and upholden, aswell by reason of making of Broad Wollen Clothes and Karseis as also by divers other Artificers inhabyting then in the said Townes, at whiche time also the Villages and Husbande townes florished, and Husbandrie and Tillage was well mainteyned, to the greate benefite of the Realme and all the people therin, forasmuche as divers yeres past suche persons as doo use the Feate or Misterye of Clothemaking, not contented to lyve as Artificers and withe the Trade wherin they have been brought uppe, doo daylye plante themselfes in Villages and Townes being no Cities Boroughes nor Corporate Townes, and ther occupieng the Feate and Place of a Husbondman, doo not onely engrosse divers Fermes and Pastures into their Handes, displeasing the Husbondman and decayeng the Ploughes and Tillages, but also drawc withe them out of Cities Bourghes and Townes Corporate all sortes of Artificers, wherby not onely divers ancient Cities Bourghes and Townes Corporate are utterly decaied destroyed and depopulated, but also Husbandrye and Tillages verie muche decayed, to the greate hurte damage and prejudice of this Realme and the people therin, yf spedye Remedye bee not foreseen. And forasmuche also as the Weavers and Worckmen of Clothiers when they have ben traded up in the trade of Clothe making and weaving three or sour yeares, doo forsake their Masters and doo become Clothiers and Occupiers for themselfes, without Stocke Skill or Knowledge, to the great slander of the true Clothemaking, besides a great nomber of Inconveniences which doo growe to the Comonwelthe of this Realme therby, as dayly Experience teachethe: Be it therfore ordeined and enacted by thaucthorite of this put Pliam1, That from and after the first daye of Maye next coming, no person or psons whatsoever shall use or exercise the Feate or Misteric of making weaving or rowing of Wollen Clothes, long or short, or Karseis pinned Whites or playne Streightes, to thintent to put the same to sale, but onelye in a Market Towne where Clothe hathe comonly been used to be made by the space of tenne yeres last past, or in a Citie Boroughe or Towne corporate, upon peine of forfeiture for every suche Wollen Clothe or Karseye made woven or rowed out of suche Citie Boroughe Towne Corporate or Market Town, Five Powndes.

CHAPTER VIII.

An Acte for the Punisheinent of suche as shall take awaye Maydens that bee Inheritoures, being within thage of xvj yeres, or that marrie them without Consent of their Parentes.

WHERE Maidens and Women Children of Noblemen Gentlemen and others, aswell suche as be Heires Apparante to their Auncesto", as others having lefte unto them by their Father or other Ancesto' and Frendes Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes or other great Substances in Goodes and Cattelles moveable, for and to thintent to advance them in Marriage somewhat lyke according to their degres and as might bee most for their Suretie and Comforte as well for theselves as of all their freendes and kinesfolkes. Be often tymes unwares to their said frendes and kinesfolkes, by flattery trifling Giftes and faire promises of many unthriftie and light psonages, and therto by thintreatie of psons of lewde demeano' and others, that for Rewardes bye and sell the said Maidens and Children, secretly allured and wonne to contracte Matrimonie withe the said unthriftie and light psonages, and therupon either w"1 slight or force oftentymes be taken and conveied awaye from their said Parentes Freendes or Kynnesfolkes, to the highe displeasure of Almightie God, dispargem' of the said Children and thextreme contynuall hevines of all their Freendes; whiche ungodly dealing for lack of wholsome Lawes to the redresse therof remainethe a greate familyar and common mischeife in this our Common Welthe: For Remedie wherof be it enacted by the King and Quenes Majesties the Lordes Spuall and Temporall, and the Comons of this pm Plain' assembled, and by thaucthorite of the same. That it shall not be lawful to any pson or psons to take or conveye awaye or cause to be taken or conveyde away, any Mayde or Woman Childe unmaried, being under thage of Syxtene Yeres, out of or from the Possession Custodie or Governance and against the Will of the Father of suche Mayde or Woman Childe, or of suche pson or psons to whom the Father of suche Maide or Woman Childe by his last Will and Testament or by any other Acte in his lyes time hathe or shall appoint assigne bequeathe gyve or grante thorder keping Educac&n or Governance of suche Mayde or Woman Childe, excepte suche taking and conveing away as shalbe had made or doone by or for suche pson or psons as without fraude or covine bee or then shalbe the Maister or Maistres of suche Mayde or Woman Childe or the Gardaine in Socage or Gardaine in Chivalrie of or to suche Mayden or Woman Childe.

And Be it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid. That yf any pson or psons, above thage of xiiij™' yeres, shall from and after the first daye of Aprill next coming, unlawfully take or convey or cause to be taken or conveide any Maide or Woman Childe unmaried, being within thage of xvj"* yeres, out of or from the possession and against the will of the Father or Mother of suche Childe, or out or from the possession and against the will of suche pson or psons as then shall happen to have by any lawfull waies or meanes thorder keping educacon or governance of any suche Maiden or Woman Childe; that then every suche pson and psons so offending, being therof lawfully attainted or convicted by thorder and due course of the Lawes of this Realme, (other then suche of whom suche p6on taken awaye shall holde any Landes or Tenementes by Knightes Service,) shall have and suffer Imprisonement of his or their Bodies by the Space of Twoo whole yeres without Bayle or Mayneprise, or elles shall paye suche Fine for his or their sayd Offence as shalbee assessed by the C5nsell of the Quenes Highnes, her heires or successoures, in the Starre chamber at Westminster.

CHAPTER XI. (')

An Acte of a Subsidie and one XV"' granted by the Lords and Comtinz.

WE the King and Quenes Ma'f most humble faithefull and obedient Subjects the Lordes Spirituall and Tempall, and the Comons in this f?sent Pliament assembled, calling to o' remembraunce the greate and manifolde Chargf w* their Gracf have alredie susteyned by the reason of this psent Warre, that their Highnes have had and yet have againste the Frenche King and the Scottf, the auncient Enymyes of this Realme, and pceiving also that the malice of the same Frenche King and Scottf are suche that they have and daily doo practise by all dishonSable weys and meanes, w'h the Aide and Power of all their Confederaties and Alies, to anoye their Ma'f and this their Realme, and other the Dnions of the same, and by all likelyhode, if oportunytie of Tyme and Place so pmytt, doo mynde to make some Invasion into sundry parts of this Realme, aswell upon the Sea Cost as elswhere, whiche if it shoulde happen wolde be no small Anoyaunce aswell to their Ma'f as to the hole State of this Realme: For the wise pvencon and resistence wherof (lest any suche shoulde happen to be attempted) their Highnes shalbe enforced not onely to maynteyn a convenient nombre and Navy of Ships apon the narrowe Seas, but also a greate Power and Nomber of Soldio's to contynue in dyvers and sundry parts of the Borders and Frountiers of this Realme, redie ppared to all purposes to resist all suche malicious Attemptf or Invasions, and to defende the libtie and honno' therof, whiche cannot be put in order and redynes w*oute greate sdmes of money to be defraied and emploied for the same: And farthermore considering that the same shall not be onely for the suretie of their Ma'f psons (whom we pray to God may long reigne over Us) and likewise for the suretie of this Realme and their Ma'f loving Subjects of the same, but also may be a greate terro' feare and discourage to the said Frenche King and Scottf and all their Confederatf and Alies to attempt any suche Invasion or other Enterprise; The Old Printed Collections do not contain nu. 36 or 31, which are inserted in Modern Printed Collections as Chapters XIX. and XXII. Nu. 19 and 39 are now first printed as Chapters XXIII. and XXIV. CHAPTER II.

An Acte for the Uniformitie of Common Prayoure and Dyvyne Service in the Churche, and the Administration

of the Sacramentes.

WHERE at the Deathe of our late Sovereigne Lorde King Edwarde the Syxte, there remayned one uniforme Order of Common Service and Prayour, and of thadministracon of Sacramentes Rites and Ceremonies in the Churche of Englande, whiche was setfurthe in one Booke, entituled The Booke of Common Prayour and Administracon of Sacramentes and other Rites and Ceremonies in the Churche of Englande, authorized by Acte of Pliament holden in the Fifthe and Sixthe Yeres of our sayd late Sovereigne Lorde Kyng Edwarde the Syxthe, intituled An Acte for thuniformitee of Comon Prayour and Administrac&n of the Sacramentes; the whiche was repealed and taken away by Acte of Pliament in the First Yere of the Raigne of our late Sovereigne Ladye Quene Marie, to the greate Decaye of the due Honour of God and discomforte to the Professoures of the Truthe of Christes Religion: Be it therfore enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliam', That the said Estatute of Repcale and everye thinge therin conteyned, onely concerning the sayd Booke and the Service Administration of Sacramentes Rites and Ceremonies conteyned or appointed in or by the said Booke, shalbee voide and of none effecte from and after, the Feast of the Nativitye of S* John Baptist next coming; and that the sayd Booke withe Thorder of Service and of the Administracon of Sacramentes Rytes and Ceremonies withe Thalteracon and Additions therin added and appointed by this Estatute, shall stande and bee from and after the sayd Feaste of the Natyvitce of Sainte John Baptiste in full force and effecte according to the tenoure and effecte of this Estatute; Annye thing in the aforesaid Statute of Repeale to the contrarye notwithestanding.

And further be it enacted by the Quenes Highnes withe thassent of [the Lordes ’] and Comons in this pnte Pliam' assembled, and by aucthoritie of the same, That all and singler Mynysters in any Cathedrall or Pishe Churche or other Place within this Realme of Englande Wales and the Marches of the same, or other the Quenes Dominions, shall from and after the Feast of the Nativitc of S1 John Baptyst next coming, bee bownden to saye and use the Mattens Evensong Celebracbn of the Lordes Supper and Administration of eche of the Sacramentes and all their Comon and open Prayour, in suche Order and Fourme as is mentioned in the said Booke so authorised

And for due execuc&n hereof the Quenes most Excellent Ma"* the Lordes Temporall and all the Comons in this pnt Pliam' assembled, doothe in Goddes name earnestly requyre and chardge all the Archbishoppes Bishopes and other Ordinaries, that they shall endevour themselves to the uttermost of their knowledges that the due and true execuc&n hereof may be hadde througheout their Diocesse and Charges, as they will aunswer before God for suche evilles and plages wherewithe Almighty God maye justly punishe his People for neglecting this good (') holesome Lawe; And for their aucthoritee in this behalfe, bee yt further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, that all and singler the same Archebishopes Bishopes and all other their Officers exercysing Ecclesiasticall Jurisdiccon, as well in place exempt as not exempte within their Diocesse, shall have full powre and aucthoritee by this Acte to refourme correcte and punishe by Censures of the Churche, all and singler psons whiche shall offende within any their Jurisdice&ns or [Diocesse *] after the said Feast of the Nativitee of S' John Baptist nexte comming, against this Acte and Statute; Anye, other Lawe Statute Privilege Lybertie or Provision heretofore made had or suffred to the contrary notwithestanding.

And it is ordeined and enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That all and every Justices of Oyer and Determiner or Justices of Assise shall have full power and aucthorite in every of their open and generall Sessions, tcnquire here and determine al and al maner of Offences that shalbe comited or doone contrarie to any Article conteined in this pnte Acte within the limites of the Comission to them directed, and to make processe for thexecucon of the same, as they maye doo againste any person being indited before them of trespas or lawfully convicted therof.

Provided alwaies and be yt enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That all and every Archebishope and Bishope shall or maie at al time and times at his lybertie and pleasure, joyne and associate himself by vertue of this Acte to the said Justices of Oier and Determiner, or to the said Justices of Assise at every the said open and generall Sessions to be holden in any place within his Diocesse for and (1) thinquirie hearing and determining of the offences aforesaid.

Provided also and be it enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid. That the Bookes concerning the sayd Services shall at the Costes and Chardges of the Pishioners of every Pishe and Cathedrall Churche, bee attained and gotten before the said Feast of the Nativitee of S' John Baptist next folowing; and that al suche [ Pishe' ] and Cathedrall Churches or other Places where the said Bookes shall bee attayned and gotten before the said Feast of the Nativitie of S' John Baptist, shall within Three Wekes next after the sayd Bookes so attained and gotten, use the said Service and put the same in ure according to this Acte.

And be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That no pson or psons shalbe at any tyme hereafter empeached or otherwise molested of or for any the offences above mentioned hereafter to bee committed or doone contrarye to this Acte, onles he or they so offending be therof indited at the next generall Sessions to be holden before any suche Justices of Oyer and Determiner or Justices of Assise next after any Offence comitted or doone contrary to the tenour of this Acte.

Provided alwaies and be it ordeined and enacted by the thaucthorite aforesaid, That al and singler Lordes of the Pliament for the thirdd offence above mentioned shalbee tryedd by their Peers.

Provided also and bee it ordeined and enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That the Maior of London and al other Maiors Bailiefes and other Heade Officers of al and singler Cities Boroughes and Townes Corporate within this Realme Wales and the Marches of the same, to the whiche Justices of Assise doo not cdmonly repaire, shall have full power and aucthorite by vertue of this Acte tenquire here and determine the Offences abovesaid and every of them, yerely within fiftene days after the feast of Easter and S' Mighell the Archangell, in lyke maner and fourmc as Justices of Assise and Oyer and Determiner maye doo.

Provided alwaies and be yt ordeyned and enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That al and singler Archebishopes and Bishoppes and every their Chancelloures Comissaries Archedeacons and other Ordinaries having any peculiar Ecclesiasticall Jurisdiccon, shal have ful power and aucthoritee by vertue of this Acte, aswell tenquire in their Visitac&n Synodes and elswher within their Jurisdice&n, at any other tyme and place, to take occasions and informations of all and every the thinges above mentioned doone comitted or perpetrated within the limites of their jurisdice&ns and aucthoritie, and to punish the same by Admonition Excommunication Sequestration or Deprivation and other Censures and Processe in lyke fourme as heretofore hathe bene used in lyke cases by the Quenes Ecclesiasticall Lawes.

All Persons thill duly retort to Church, on Pain of Spiritual Censure and is. to the Poor.

Provided alwaies and bee it enacted, That whatsoever pson offending in the Premisses, shall for thoffence first receive punishement of Thordinarie, having a testimonial! therof under the said Ordinaries Seale, shall not for the same Offence eftsoones be convicted before the Justices; And lykewise receyving for the said [Offence firste' ] punishement by the Justices, he shall not for the same Offence eftesoones receive punishement of the Ordinarie; Any thing conteyned in this Acte to the contrarye notwithestanding.

Provided alwaies and bee it enacted, That suche Ornamentes of the Churche and of the Ministers therof shall bee reteyned and bee in use as was in the Churche of Englande by aucthorite of Pliam* in the seconde yere of the Reigne of King Edwarde the Syxthe, untill other order shalbe therin taken b) thaucthorite of the Quenes MaUe, withe the advise of her Comissioners appointed and aucthorised under the Greate Seale of Englande for [Ecclesiasdcall Causes,*] or of the Metropolytan of this Realme; And also that yf ther shall happen any Contempte or Irreverence to be used in the Ceremonies or Rites of the Churche by the misusing of thorders appointed in this Booke, the Queenes Ma"' maye by the like advice of the said Comissioners or Metropolitan ordeyne and publishe suche further Ceremonies or Rites as maye bee most for thadvancement of Goddes glorye, the edifieng of his Church and the due Reverence of Christes holye Misteries and Sacramentes.

And be yt further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That all Lawes Statutes and Ordinances, wherin or whereby any other Service Administration of Sacramentes or Common Prayer ys lymytted established or sett foorthe to bee used within this Realme or any other the Quenes Dominions or Cowntreis, shall from hensfoorthe be utterly voyde and of none effecte.

CHAPTER III.

An Acte of Recognition of the Quenes Highnes Title to the Imperyall Crowne of this Realme.

AS there ys nothing under God (most dreade Soveraigne Ladye wherin wee yor most Humble faithfull and obedient Subjectes the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled, have maye or ought to have more cause to rejoyce then in this onely that it hathe pleased God of his mercifull providence and goodnes towardes us and this our Realme, not onely to provide but also to preserve and kepe for us and our wealthes yor Royall Majestie our most rightfull and Lawfull Sovereigne leige Ladye and Quene most happely to Reigne over us for the whiche wee doo give and yelde unto him from the bottomes of our hartes our humble thanckes laudes and praises; Even so ther ys nothing that we yor said subjectes for our parties can may or ought towardes yo' Highnes more firmely entierly and assuredly in the puritie of our hartes thinke or withe our mowthes declare and confesse to bee trewe then that yor Ma"‘ our sayd Sovereigne Ladye ys and in verye dede and of most meere right ought to bee by the Lawes of God and the Lawes and statutes of this Realme our most rightfull and lawfull Sovereigne leige Ladie and Quene; And that yor Highnes ys rightlye lynyallye and lawfully discended and come of the Bloodd royall of this Realme of Englande in and to whose princely person and theires of yo' bodye lawfully to bee begotten after youe without all doubte ambiguitee scruple or question thimperiall and Royall

estate place crowne and dignitie of this Readme withe all honnours stiles titles dignities Regalities Jurisdic£ttns

and preheminences to the same nowe belonging and apperteyning arre and shalbee most fully rightfully really and entierly invested and incorporated united and annexed as rightfully and lawfully to all internes construccSns and

Highnes Brother, or in the late Quene Marye yo' Highnes Syster at anye tyme since thacte of pi am1 made in the xxxv,h yere of the reigne of yo' said most noble father king Henrye theight, Entituled, An Acte concerning

thestablishement of the Kinges Majesties Succession in the Imperiall Crowne of this Realme: For whiche Cawses

Wee yo' said most Loving faithfull and obedient Subjectes representing the three estates of yor Realme of Englande as theronto constreined By the lawe of God and Man, excepte Wee shoulde over muche forget our duties to yo' Highnes and to theires of yo' Bodye lawfully begotten can no lesse doo But most humblye beseche yo' Highnes That by thauthoritee of this pnte Pliament It maye bee enacted established and declared That wee do Recognise acknowlege and confesse the same yor estate right tytle and succession as ys aforesaid to bee in and to yor Highnes

CHAPTER V.

An Acte whereby certayne Offences be made Treason.

WHERE in the Parliament holden at Westminster the xij"‘ daye of November in the seconde yere of the Reigne of the late Quene Marye, Syster unto our most gracious Sovereigne Ladye the Quenes Ma'k that nowe ys, there was one Acte or Statute made for the better Suretie and Preservad&n of the said late Quene, endtuled An Acte wherby certayne Offences be made Treason, as by the same Acte more at large dothe appeare; And forasmuche as the verie Woordes and Sentences of the said Estatute doo cxtende no further but unto the said late Quene Marye and Theires of her Body, therfore yf any suche lyke offences as bee mentioned and conteyned within the said Statute should hereafter happen to be comitted against or said Sovereigne Lady that nowe ys, ther were no due remedye or condigne punishement provided for the same: In consideration wherof and to thintent that the malice of wicked and evill doers maye the better be restrayned by thextending of theffect and benefite of the matters conteyned in the said Estatute, to our most deere Sovereigne Ladye that nowe ys, and for the more Suretye and Preservacbn of her Highnes Royal Estate; Be it enacted by the Quenes most Excellent Mau*, withe thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall, and the Comons in this presente Pliament assembled, and by thaucthoritee of the same, That yf any pson or psons after the first daye of Maye next to come, doo maliciouslye advisedly and directlye compas or imagyn to depryve the Quenes Ma"' that nowe ys, or theires of her Bodye to bee begotten, being Kinges or Quenes of this Realme, from the Stile Honour and Kingly Name of Thimperiall Crowne of this Realme, or from any other the Realmes and Dominions unto our said Sovereigne Ladie apperteyning and belonging, or to destroye the Quenes Ma"* that nowe ys, or any theires of her Bodye beinge Kinges or Quenes of this Realme, or to levie Warre within this Realme, or within any the Marches or Dominions to the same belonging, against the Quenes Ma,lc that nowe ys, or any theires of her Bodye being Kinges or Quenes of this Realme, or to depose the Quehes Ma"' that now ys, or any Theires of her bodye being Kinges or Quenes of this Realme, from the Imperiall Crowne of the Realmes and Dominions aforesaid ; and the same Compasses or Imaginacons or any of them, maliciouslye advisedly and directly shall or doo utter by open preaching expresse woordes or Sayenges; or yf any pson or psons after the said first daye of Maye next coming, shal maliciouslie advisedlye and directlye say publish maintaine declare or holde opinyon, that the Quenes Ma"' that nowe ys, during her lyes, ys not or ought not to bee Quene of this Realme, or after her deathe that theires of her Highnes Bodye being Kinges or Quenes of this Realme, of Right ought not to bee Kinges or Quenes of this Realme, or that any other pson or psons other then the Quenes Highnes that nowe ys, during her lyes, ought to be King or Quene of this Realme, or any other the Realmes or Dominions aforesaid, or after her death, other then theires of her Bodye, being Kinges or Quenes of this Realme, as long as any of her said Hares of her Bodye begotten shal bee in lyes, of Right ought to have and enjoy Thimperiall Crowne of this Realme, or anye the Realmes and Dominions aforesayd; that then every such Offendour being therof dulye convicted or attainted by the Lawes of this Realme, their Abbettoures Procurers and Coucellers, and all and every their Comforters, knowing the said Offences or any of them to bee done, and being therof dulye convicted or atteinted as ys abovesaid for his or their suche Offence, shall forfeite and lose to the Quenes Highnes, her Heires and Successoures, all his and their Goodes and Cattelles, and the whole Issues and Profittes of his and their Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes for terme of the lyes of every suche Offendo' or Offendo's, and also shall have and suffer during his and their lyves ppetuall Imprisonement.

Provided alwaies and be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid. That all and every Ecclesiasticall Pson beynge convicted or attainted in fourme aforesaid, for every suche his Offence shall immediatlie and pntly upon suche Attaindour hadd, bee judged and remayne in the Lawe to all Intentes deprived from all his Benefices and Promoc&ns Spuall or Ecclesiasticall, in suche maner and fourme that it shalbe laufull for every Patron Founder or Gyver therof to pnt immediatly after suche Attaindo' had, some one other to the same, as thoughe the sayd Offendo' or Offendo's were deceased.

And if anie pson or psones being hereafter convicted or attainted of anye the said Offences in fourme aforsaid comitted, shall after his or their Conviction or Attaindor efftesones comit or ppetrate any of the said Offences in fourme aforesaid, that then every suche seconde Offence or Offences shalbe demed and adjudged Highe Treason, and thoffendour or offendours therin, their Abettours Procurers and Coucellours, and all and every their Aydo" and Comforters, knowing the said Offences or any of them to be done, being therof convicted or attainted according to the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme, shalbee judged and demed Highe Traytours, and shall suffer paines of deathe and lose and forfeite all their Gooddes Cattelles Landes and Tenementes to the Quenes Ma’* her Heires and Successoures, as in cases of Highe Treason by the Lawes of this Realme at this day of right ought to be lost and forfaited.

And be it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid. That yf any pson or psons at any time after the said first daye of Maye next to come, by any writing printing overte dede or acte, maliciouslye advisedly and directlye doo affirme that the Quenes Mav that nowe ys ought not to have and enjoy the Stile Honour and Kingly Name of this Realme, Or that anye pson or psones other then the Quenes Ma,ic that nowe ys, ought to have or injoye the Stile Honour and Kinglye Name of this Realme, or that the Quenes Ma'" that nowe ys during her lief ys not or

And where also one other Acte entytuled An Acte for true tanning of Leather was made at a Pliant* of the said King Edwarde, holden upon prorogacon at Westm the fourthe daye of November in the seconde yere of his most gracious reigne, whiche Acte was made tendure unto thende of the next Pliament then following; and after, the same Acte was revivede at one other Pliam' holden at Westm, the first daye of Marche in the seventh yere of the Reigne of the same King Edwarde the Syxte, to contynue till the last daye of the next Pliament then following; and after, the same Acte was continued in the seconde and last Session of our Sovereigne Ladye Quene Marye, holden upon prorogacon at Westm the xiiiju> daye of October in the first yere of her Graces Reigne, to continue till the [laste1J last daye of the next Pliam' then following, whiche being expired, and the same Acte never since continued, his force and efficacye ys ended: And fcrasmuche as the said Acte ys good and beneficiall for the comonwelthe of this Realme; Be it therfore enacted ordeyned and established by the Quene our Soveraigne Ladye, withe thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliam' assembled, and by thaucthoritee of the same. That the said Acte made in the seconde yere of the said King Edwarde the Sixte, and all Woordes Clauses Articles and Provisions in the same, (except thes woordes Ashebarcke Tapwoorte Meale or Culverdung,) shalbe revived continued stande and endure in his full force and strengthe to all Intentes Constructions and Purposes; And that no Tanner in or aboute the tanning of any Leather, shall use or exercise anny other kinde of stuffe but onely Ashebarck Okebarck Tapwoorte Meale Lyme or Culverdung.

Provided alwaies and be it enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That thone Moietie of all suche forfeitures afore named, shalbe to our Sovereigne Ladye the Quenes Ma'* and her Highnes Heires or Successoures, and thother Moyetie to him or them that sease or first sewe for the same Penalties in any the Quenes Ma'f Cowrtes of Recorde, by Action of Debte Bill Complaynt Informac6n or otherwise, wherin no Wager of Lawe Essoigne Protectyon or Injunction shalbee admitted or allowed for the Defendant in that behalf.

CHAPTER X.

An Acte that the caryeng of Leather Tallowe or Rawe Hides out of the Realme for Marchandyse,

shall bee Felonye.

WHERE at this pnte tyme, tanned Leather Hides and Tallowe and all things therof made, ys growen and come unto suche highe and excessive Price as the lyke within the tyme of Mans memorye hathe not been seen within this Realme, by reason that divers and sundrye covetous and gredye psons nowe of late having more regarde unto their owne singuler lucres and gaynes, than unto the mayntenance and p>fvacon of the comon and publike weale of this (1) Realme of England, have contrary to the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme, conveyed or caused to bee conveyed out of the same, unto the pties beyonde the Seas, ther to bee uttred by waye of marchandise.

CHAPTER XI.

An Acte lymiting the tymes for layeng on Lande Marchandise from beyonde the Seas, and touching Customes

for Sweete Wynes.

MOST humblie shewing Besechen yo' Highnes, your Lordes and Comons in this pnte Parlyament assembled. That where the somes of Money payde in the Name of Customes and Subsidies of Wares & Marchandizes, transported out and brought into this yo' Highnes Realme of Englande by any Marchant Stranger or Denizen, ys an auncyent Revenue annexed and unyted to yo' Imperiall Crowne, and hathe in the tyme of Kyng Edwarde the Thirde, and other yo' most Noble Progenitours, amounted to greate and notable somes of Money, tyll of late yeares many greedye and covetous psons respecting more their pryvate Gayne and Comoditee then theyre Dutie and Allegiance or the Comon Profite of the Realme, have and doo daylye aswell by conveyeng the same their Wares and Marchandizes out of Creekes & Places wher no Custome' ys resident, as also by or throughe the Negligence or Corruptyon of the Customer Searcher or other Officer wher they be resident, as by dyvers other fraudulent undue and subtill Practises and Devises, convey their Goodes and Marchaundizes, aswell brought from the pties beyonde the Sea as transported out of this yo' Realme of Englande, without payment or agreing for the payment of the Customes and Subsidies therfore due; wherby the yerely Revenue aforesayd ys very muche empayred and dyminished, to the greate Losse and Damage of yo' Highnes, and to the greate Burden and Chardge of yo' lovinge Subjectes, who by occasion therof have of late yeares been more chardged withe Subsidies and Payment for the Supplement of the said Losse and Damage then elles wee shoulde have been: That yt maye therfore bee enacted by aucthorite of this pnte Pliament, That yt shall not bee lawfull to or for any pson or psones whatsoever from and after the first daye of September nexte coming, to lade or putt or cause to be laden or putt, of or from any Wharfe Keye or other Place on the Lande, into any Shippe Vessell Crayer Lyghter or Botome, any Gooddes Wares or Marchaundises whatsoever ( Fishe taken by yo' Highnes Subjectes onely excepted) to be transported into anny place of the pties beyonde the Sea, or into the Realme of Scotlande, or to take upp discharge and laye on Lande, or cause or procure to bee taken up or dischardged out of any Lyghter Shippe Crayer Vessell or Bottome, beyng not in a Leake or Wrack, and layde on Lande, any Gooddes Wares or Marchaundises whatsoever (Fishe taken by any (1) yor Highnes Subjectes and Sake onely excepted) to bee brought from any the pties beyonde the Sea or the Realme of Scotlande by waye of Marchaundises, but onely in the daye light; That ys to saye, From the first of Marche untill the last of September betwexte the Sonne rising and the Sonne setting, and from the last of September untill the first of Marche betwen the howres of seven in the Morning and foure at the After noone; and in and upon sume suche open Place Keye or Wharfe Places Keys or Wharfes as yo' Highnes yor Heires or Successoures shall on thisside the sayd first daye of September therfore assigne and appointe, by vertue of yor Highnes Commission or Comissions within yor Graces Portes of London Sowthampton Bristowe Westchester Newecastell and the Suburbes of the same and every of them, and in some open Place Keye or Wharfe Places Keyes or Wharfes in all other Portes Creekes Havens or Rodes, (Hull onely excepted,) wher a Customer Comptroller and Searcher of suche Portes Havens Creekes or Rodes and every of them or the Servantes of any of them, have by the space of tenne yeres last past been accustomablye resident or hereafter shalbee resident; upon payne of forfeyture of all suche Goodes Wares or Marchaundises so laden or dischardged contrary to the true meaning of this Acte, or the value therof.
