CHAPTER XII.

An Acte against the deceiptfull using of Lynnen Clothe.

Abuses in stretching, &c. of Linen Cloth;

Penalty thereon, Forfeiture and Imprisonment.

WHERE certaine evyll disposed and deceyptfull psons usyng to buye and engrose into their Handes greate store of Lynnen Clothe, doo use to cast the pieces of Clothe over a Beame or piece of Tymber made for theyr purpose, and doo by sundry dyvises rack stratche and drawe the same bothe of Lengthe and Bredthe, and that doon, doo then with Batledoores peeces of Tymber and Wood and other Thinges, sore beat the same, ever casting therupon certayne deceiptfull Lyquors myngled withe Chalke and other lyke Thinges, wherby the sayd Clothe ys not onely made to seeme muche fyner and thicker to the Eye then yt ys in dede, but also the Threddes therof bee so losed and made weake, that after three or sour washingf it will scarsely holde together, to the greate Disceipte Hindrance and Losse of the Subjectes of this Realme : Be it therefore enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliament,

That yf any pson or psons shall hereafter willingly use or cause to bee used thaforesayd Deceiptes or any

other Acte or Actes Meane or Meanes to in or withe any kynde of Lynnen Clothe, wherby the same shalbee deceyptfull or worse to and for the good use therof; that then the sayd Clothe shalbee forfeited, and the

Offendour therm to bee punished by one Monethes Imprisonement at the lest, and shall paye suche Fyne as

shalbee assessed for his or their Offence or Offences by the Justices before whom he or they shalbee condempned according to the tenour of this Acte.

'offence!.

That all and every the Justices of Oyer and Determiner and Justices of Assises in all their Sessions, and all Justices of Peace in every Countie and Place of this Realme, or Three of them at the least, wherof one to bee of the Quorum, shall have full power and aucthoritee tinquire here and determine the Offences aforesayd in theyr Sessions, by Information Indictament or upon the Travers of any Presentment or Inditement founde before the said Justices or any of them.

CHAPTER XIII.

An Acte for the shipping in Englishe Botomes.

WHERE by dyvers Statutes made in the tyme of the Quenes Ma"" most noble Progenitoures, It hathe been enacted and provided that no pson borne within the Realme of Englande, or being of the lygeance of the Prynce of the sayd Realme, or any the Domynions of the same, shoulde shippe any maner of Marchaundise either out of the Realme or into the same, but onely in a Shippe or Bottome wherof the sayd Prynce or some other of their Subjectes were Owners Possessioners Proprietaries and Maisters, and the Maryners of the same Vessell for the more Parte to bee also theyr Subjectes, upon dyvers paynes and penalties as in the said Statutes more playnely appearethe: Synce the making of whiche sayd Statutes, other forreyne Prynces fynding themselves agreaved withe the sayd several! Actes, as thincking that the same were made to the Hurte and Prejudice of their Countrye and Navye, have made lyke penall Lawes against suche as shoulde shippe out of their Countreys in any other Vesselles then of their severall Countreys and Domynions; By reason wherof ther hathe not onely growen greate displeasure betwene the forreyne Prynces and the Kinges of this Realme, but also the Marchauntes have been sore greyed and endomaged : For Reformacyon wherof and for encrease of contynuance of Amytye, Be it enacted, That the severall Actes made in the fifthe yere of Kyng Richarde the Seconde the Thirde Chapter, and in the fourthe yere of the late Kyng of famouse memorye King Henrye the Seventhe, intituled Of Wyne and Tholouze Woade, shalbee fromhensforthe derely voide and of none effecte.

And nevertheles for advoyding of great disceipte practised and nowe a days used by sundry Subjectes borne within this Realme of Englande and Dominions of the same, whiche enter in the Customers Bookes Wares and Marchandizes of Aliens borne, in their owne name, wherby the Quenes Ma'1* ys defrauded in her Customes and Subsidies to the greate Decaye of thauncyent Revenues of the Crowne : Be yt enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliament, That all and every p6one and psones being Owner or Owners of any Goodes Wares or Marchandizes whiche after the first daye of Januarye next ensuyng the Session of this pnte Pliament, shall in tyme of Peace and when ther ys no restraynte made of Englishe Shippes, embarck shippe lade or dischardge by waye of Marchandyse, any Wares Marchaundize (Mastes [Rasse*] Pitche Tarre and Come onely excepted) out of or into any Shippe Barck Hoy Vessell or Bottome wherof our sayd Soveraigne Ladye the Quene, her Heires or Successoures, or some of her or their Subjectes of this Realme or the Domynions of the same, bee not Possessioners and Proprietaries and the Masters under God, and the Mariners of the same Shippe or Shippes for the most parte be not Subjectes of our sayd Sovereigne Ladye, her Heires and Successoures, shall aunswer yeelde and paye to thuse of our said Sovereigne Ladye the Quene, her Heires and Successours, suche Custome and Subsydye for suche Wares and Marchaundises so shipped ladon or discharged as ys aforesayd, rate and rate, lyke as Strangers and Alyens borne out of the Obeysaunce of our sayd Sovereigne Ladye the Quenes Ma"' doo and ought to paye for Wares and Marchaundizes of lyke nature and kynde.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte for the continuance of the makinge of Woollen Clothe in dyvers Townes in the Cowntie of Essexe.

WHEREAS by a certayne Acte of Pliament begune at Westfii the twentithe daye of January in the fourthe and fifthe yeres of the Reignes of the late Kyng Philippe and Quene Marye, and ther continued till the seventh daye of Marche in the sayd fourthe and fifthe yeres of the Reygnes of the said late King and Quene, amongst other thinges yt was enacted, that from and after the first daye of Maye then next following, no pson or psones whatsoever shall use or exercise the Feate or Mysterye of making weaving or rowing of Woollen Clothes, long or shorte, or Carseys Pynned Whites or Playne Streightes, to thintent to putt the same to sale, but onely in a Marcket Towne where Clothe hathe continually bene used to bee made by the space of tenne yeres then laste paste, or in a Citye Boroughe or Towne Corporate ; uppon payne of forfeyture for every suche Woollen Clothe or Carseye made woven or rowed out of suche Citie Bourghe Towne Corporate or Market Towne Fyve Powndes; And where also yt ys provided in the said Acte that yt shalbee laufull to any pson then using or exercising the Feate or Misterye of making weaving or rowing of Clothe or Carsey, to inhabite or dwell wher he then dyd dwell, anil there to use the making weaving or rowing of Clothe or Carseye as he hathe heretofore, any thing in the said Acte notwithestanding; And where yt ys further provided by the sayd Acte, that yt shalbee lawfull to all and every pson or psons whiche then dyd or after that tyme shoulde inhabyte or dwell in any of the Shiers of Northewales or Southewales, Chesshire or Lancashire, Westmerlande Cumberlande Northumberlande Bishopricke of Durham Cornewall Suffolk Kente the Towne of Goddelmyne in the Cowntye of Surreye or Yorckshire, being not within twelve myles of the Citye of Yorck, or in any of the Townes or Villages neare adjoyning to the Water of Strowde in the Cowntie of Glocestree wher Clothes hath been usually made by the space of twentye yeares then last paste, and havynge been an Apprentyse to thoccupacbn of Clothe making, or used the same by the space of seven yeares, to set uppe use and exercise the Feate or Mysterye of making weaving or rowing of Wollen Clothe out of a Citie Bourghe or Market Towne, as before that time they might have doon, any thing in the sayd Acte to the contrary notwithestanding; And forasmuche as the Townes or Vyllagies of Bocking Weste Barfolde Dedham and Cockshall in the Countye of Essexe, bee fayre large Townes, and aswell planted for Clothe making as the said Towne of Godlemyne or better, and fewe Townes in this Realme better planted for that purpose, and have been inhabited of a long time withe Clothe makers wch have made and daylye doo make good and trewe Clothe, to the greate Comon Weale of the Countrye there, and nothing prejudiciall to or for the C5mon Wealthe of this Realme: Be it therfore ordeyned and enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliament, That yt shalbee lawfull to all and every suche pson and psons whiche nowe doo inhabyte or dwell or hereafter shall dwell in the sayde Townes or Villages of Bocking Westbarfolde Cockshall and Dedham, or in any of them, nowe using or exercising or that hereafter shall use or exercyse the Feate or Misterye of making weaving or rowing of Clothe or Carseye, by the space of seven yeres at the least, or have been prentyse therto by the sayd space of seaven yeres, to inhabyte and dwell in the sayd Townes or Villages of Bocking Westbarfolde Cockeshall and Dedham, and in every or any of them, and to use the making weaving or rowing of Clothe or Carseye as before this tyme they might have doone yf the sayd Acte hadd never been made; Anny thing in the sayd Acte to the contrary therof made or anny other Acte Statute or Lawe heretofore made or hereafter to bee made to the contrarye heros in anny wise notwithestanding.

CHAPTER XVI.

An Acte to continue Thacte made against Rebellyous Assemblyes.

WHERE in the Pliament holden at Westmynster the xxiiij"’ daye of October in the first yere of the Reigne of the late Quene Marye, Syster unto the Quenes Highnes that nowe ys, there was one Acte and Statute made against Unlawfull and Rebellyous Assembles, to endure and stande in force unto thende of the nexte Pliament then following, as by the same Acte more playnely dothe appeare: Whiche said Acte and Statute in the Plem' holden at Westminster the xij daye of November in the first and seconde yeres of the Reigne of the late King Philippe and Quene Marye, amongest other thinges was then and ther continued unto the last daye of the nexte Pliament; And after, at the nexte Pliam* begune and holden at Westmynster the xxj"1 daye of October, in the seconde and thirde yeres of the sayd late King Philippe and Quene Marye, the said Acte and Statute amonges other thinges was also further contynued to stande in force untill the last daye of the nexte Pliament then following; And also at the next Pliam* holden at Westm the xx*11 day of Januarye in the fourthe and fifth* yeres of the Reignes of the sayd late King and Quene, the said Acte and Statute amongst other thinges was likewise further continued to stande and remayne in force until the last daye of the next Pliament then following, whiche ys this pnte Pliament; And so the sayd Acte and Statute by the Actes of Continuance aforesayd, dothe stande in force but onely unto the last daye of this pnte Pliament: And forasmuche as the sayd Acte and Statute during all the tyme aforesayd hathe been proved by Experience to be a very good and beneficiall Lawe, and meete to be continued and kept in force, aswell for the Preservac&n of the Peace, as also for the Comon Wealthe and Quyetnes of this Realme; Be it therfore enacted by aucthoritee of this pnte Pliament, That the said Acte and Statute, and every Braunche Clause and Article therin conteyned, shall stande remayne continue and bee in full Force and Strengthe to all Intentes and Purposes, for and during the naturall Lyes of the Quenes most Excellent Ma"' that nowe ys (whiche Allmighty God long preserve and contynue), and to thende of the Pliament then next following; and that the said Acte and Statute and the Woordes and Sentences mentioned and conteyned in the sayd Acte, shall extende and be to the Quenes Highnes that nowe ys, as fully and amplye as ever the same dyd extende to the sayd late Quene Marye.

CHAPTER XVII.

An Acte for the preservation of Spawne and Frye of Fyshe.

FOR the preservac6n hereafter of Spawne Frye and yong Breede of Eles Samons Pykes and of all other Fishe, whiche heretofore hathe been muche destroyed in Ryvers and Streames salte and freshe within this Realme, in so muche that in dyvers places they feede Swyne and Dogges withe the Frye and Spawne of Fishe and otherwise (lamentable and horrible to bee reported) destroye the same, to the greate hynderance and decaye of the Commonwealthe: Be it therfore enacted by the Quenes most excellent Ma'" the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Commons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by the thaucthoritee of the same, That no pson or psons of what Estate Degree or Condicbn soever he or they bee, from and after the first daye of June next coming, withe any maner of Net Weele Butt Tayning Kepper Lyme Crele Rawe Fagnett Trollnett Triihenet Trymebote Stalbote Weblyster Seure Lamenett, or withe any Devise or Engyne made of Heere Wooll Lyne or Canvas, or shall use any Heling Nett or Trymle Bote, or by any other Devise Engyne Cawtele Wayes or Meanes whatsoever, heretofore made or devysed or hereafter to be made or devysed, shall take and kyll any yong Broode Spawne or Frye of Eeles Salmon Pyke or Pyckerell, or of any other Fyshe in any Floodgate Pype at the Tayle of any Mylle Weare, or in any Straightes Streames Brookes Ryvers salte or freshe, within this Realme of Englande Wales Barwike or the Marches therof. Nor shall from and after the first day of June nexte coming by any of the wayes and meanes aforesayd or otherwise, in any Ryver. or Place above specified, take and kyll any Samons or Trowtes not being in season, being Kypper Salmons or Kepper Trowtes Shedder Salmons or Shedder Trowtes.

And be it further enacted by aucthoritee aforesayd, That no psone or psones of what Estate Degre or Condicon he or they [ bee,' ] from and after the sayd firste daye of June, by any of the meanes aforesaid, in any of the Ryvers or Places above named, shall take and kill any Pyke or Pyckerell, not being in lengthe tenne ynches Fishe or more, nor any Salmon not being in lengthe syxtene ynches (1) and more, nor any Trowte not being in lengthe eight ynches or more, nor any Barbell not being in lengthe twelfe ynches or more.

And to thintent the said yong Frye Broode or Spawne may bee preserved according to the trewe meaning heros, Be it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesayd, That no maner of psone or psons from and after the first daye of June next coming shall fishe or take Fishe withe any maner of Nett Tramell Keppe Wore Hyvy Crele, or by any other Engyne Devise Wayes or Meanes whatsoever, in any Ryver or other Places above mentyoned, but onely withe Nett or Tramell, wherof every Meshe or Maske shalbee twoo ynches and a half broade ; Angling excepted.

Provided nevertheles and be yt enacted by aucthoritee aforesayd, That in all suche Places where Smeltes Loches Mynneis Bulheades Gudgions or Eeles hathe been used to bee taken and killed, that in all suche Places yt shall bee lawfull onely for the taking of Smeltes Loches Myneys Gudgyons and Eeles, to use such Nettes Leapes and other Engynes Devises Wayes and Meanes as heretofore hathe been used for the taking of the same; so that suche psone or psons using or occupieng suche Nettes or other Engines as is last afore mentioned, doo not take kill or destroye any other Fishe withe the said Nettes or Engines contrary to the tenour and fourme above in this Estatute conteyned.

And be yt further enacted, That yf any pson or psons after the aforesaid day limited in this pnte Acte, offende in any of the Poyntes before rehearsed, contrary to the tenour fourme and purporte of any parte of the same, that then every suche psone and psones so offending shall lose and forfeite for every tyme of his or their Offence the the Some of Twentye Shillinges, and the Fishe so taken contrary to the tenour hereof, and also the unlawfull Nettes Engynes Devises and Instrumentes whatsoever theye bee wherewithe or wherby suche Offence shall fortune to bee made comitted or doone.

And to thintent that a pfite execution maye bee hadd of this presente Acte, Be it further ordeyned by aucthoritee aforesaid, That the Lorde Admirall of Englande and the Mayo’ of the Citie of London for the tyme being, and all and every other Psone and Psones Bodyes Politike and Corporate, whiche by Grante or other lawfull Wayes or Meanes lawfully have or ought to have any Conservation or Preservac&n of any Ryvers Streames or Water, or Punishementes or Corrections of Offences comitted in any of them, shall have full power and aucthoritee by vertue of this Acte tenquyre of all thoffences to bee comitted and doone contrary to theffecte and trewe meaning of this Acte within his or theyr suche lawfull Rule Governement Jurisdiction and Conservacye, by the Othes of Twelve Men or more, and to heare and determyne all and every the same Offences comitted within his or their suche Jurisdiction Conservacye Rule and Governement: And that all suche paynes and forfeitures as shall rise or growe by the reason of any suche Conviction for any thoffences aforesayd, shalbee to thuse of every of the sayd psone and psons being no Bodye Politike or Corporate nor Heade of any Bodye Polytyke or Corporate before whom suche ConviccOn as ys aforesayd shalbee hadd, and to thuse of every suche Bodye Polytyke and Corporate as heretofore have lawfully had any Fynes Forfeitures and Amertiamentes for any Offence unlawfully comitted or doone in any suche their Jurisdiction or Conservacies, uppon Convicccon hadd before the Heade of any suche Bodye Polityke or Corporate: And that also the Lorde of every Leete within this Realme of Englande and Wales or the Domynions of the same, shall have full Power and Aucthoritee tenquire of all thoffences contrary to the purporte teno' and forme of this Estatute within the Precincte of their sayd Leete, suche inquirie to bee hadd in Maner and Forme and after suche sorte as C5mon

Determiner, and Justices of Assise in their severall Circuites, shall have power and aucthoritee to enquyre therof and

to heare and determyne all the Offences commytted contrary to the tenour of this Estatute.

Saving allwaies to all and every pson and psons Bodyes Politike and Corporate and every of them, all suche Right Title Interest Clayme Pryviledge and ConservacSn, and Enquyrye and Punishement of and for any the Offences aforesayd, as they or any of them lawfully have and enjoye, or of Right ought to have and enjoy by any maner of meanes; Any thing in this Acte to the contrary notwithestanding: This Acte to endure to thende of the nexte Pliament.

Provided alwaies. That this Acte or any thing therin conteyned shall not extende unto the Fishing of the Exception^ the Ryver or Water of Tweede, nor to any Ryver or Water, wherof the Quenes Ma'" ys aunswered of anny River* Tweed, yerely Rent or Profitt, nor to the Owners Fermours and Occupyours of the Ryvers of Uske or Wye in the Ulk|,n<i wT*>kc-Countye of Monmowthe, for any Fishe hereafter to bee taken in any the Ryvers or Waters before mentyoned and expresed; but that yt maye be lawfull at all seasonable tyme and tymes hereafter for suche as have or shall have any maner of Interest therein, to take and fishe the sayd Ryvers and Waters, in suche maner and fourme as heretofore hathe been used and accustomed; not using any Nett or Engyne to thintent willingly to take kill and destroy the Spawne Breede or Frye breeding any kynde of Fishe withein the sayd severall Ryvers or Waters;

This Acte or any thing therin mentioned or conteyned to the contrarye notwithestanding.

CHAPTER XIX.

An Acts giving Aucthoritie to the Queues Majestie uppon thadvoidance of any Archebishoppriche or Bishoppriche to take into her Handes certeine of the Temporall Possessions therof, recompensing the same with Psonages Impropriate and Tenthes.

THE Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled, pceyving howe necessarye yt ys for the Imperyall Crowne of this Realme to bee repayred withe Restituc&n of Revenues meete for the same, and having assented and fully accorded to restore to the same Imperyall Crowne the Firste Fruites [of1] Tenthes and Psonages Impropryate, for thencrease of the Revenue therof, bee also desirous to devise some good Meanes wherby the said Revenue of Tenthes and Impropryate Benefices might bee in the governance and disposic&n of the Clergie of this Realme, being most apte for the same, in suche sorte as yet therby the sayd Imperyall Crowne shoulde not bee in any wise dyminished in the sayd restored Revenue; CHAPTER XX.

An Acte of the Subsidye of Tonage and Pondage.

IN their most humble wise shewen unto yor most excellent Ma"*, yor poore and obedient Subjectes and Comons in this yor pnte Pliament assembled, That wher aswell yor noble Grandefather of worthye memorie King Henrye the Seventhe, the most victorious and mightye Prynce King Henry the Eight yo' most deere Father, the late Prynce of worthye memorye King Edwarde the Syxte yor most entyerly beloved Brother, and our late Sovereigne Ladye Quene Marye yor most deere Syster, as other yor right noble and famous Progenitoures Kinges of this yo' Realme of Englande, tyme out of mynde have had and enjoyed unto them, by aucthorite of Pliament, for the defence of the same nowe yo' Realme and the kepyng and saulfgarde of the Seas, for thentrecourse of Marchandyse safely to come into and to passe out of the same; certayne somes of Moneye named Subsidyes of all maner of Gooddes and Marchandise coming in or goyng out of the same yor Realme: And forasmuche as Wee yo' said poore Comons undoubtedly and most assuredly doo trust and have sure confidence in yo' Ma*" goodd favour and will towardes Us yor sayd poore Commons, in and for the keping and sure defending of the Seas against all psons intending or that shall intende the disturbance of us yo' sayd Comons in thentrecourse and thinvading of this yo' Realme, to owre molestacon inquieting and losse, whiche at any tyme cannot bee borne without the greate Excesse and intollerable Costes Chardges and Expenses of yor Malle whiche ys not (when nede shall require in suche Cases) to bee lacked at any tyme; But reither Wee yo' sayd Comons wysshing that suche Furniture of all thinges maye bee had in readynes from tyme to tyme when necessitee shal require for the spedye [undelayed1 ] provysyon and helpe for the suppressing of such Inconveniences Disturbances and Invasions, humbly desyre yo' most Excellent (*) bennignely and favourably to take accepte and receyve theis our poore Grantes hereafter ensuing; as granted of true hartes and good willes whiche we beare unto your Highnes towardes yor sayde greate Costes Chardges and Expenses, whiche maye bee expended and layd out by yo' Matk for the Causes aforesayd when nede shall requyre, as the first fruites of our good willes and hartes towardes yo' Highnes ; althoughe the same doo or hereafter shall nothing in elfecte contervaile the same yo' greate Chardges, nor yet Wee yo' sayd poor C5mons able fully to gratefie yo' Highnes by any meanes 5 yet nevertheles Wee yo' sayd poore Comons by Thadvise and Consent of the Lordes Spuall and Teinpall in this yo' pnte Pliam1 assembled, and by thaucthorite of the same, to thintent aforesayd, gyve and grant to yo" our supreme liege Ladye and Sovereigne, One Subsidye called Tonnage; that is to saye, Of every Tonne of Wyne coming, or that shall or is come into this yo' Realme, by waye of Mar^handize, the some of Three shilingf, and so after the rate; And of every Tonne of Swete Wyne aswell [MalveseyeJ] as other, that shall or ys come into the same yo' Realme by every or any Marchante Alyen, aswell by the Marchauntes of Haunce and Almayne as by any other Marchaunte Straunger of what Natyon soever he bee, Three shillingf, and so after the rate, over and above the three shillingf afore granted; And of every Aume of Renishe Wine coming or that shall or ys come into this yo' Realme by way of Marchaundise, by every or any Marchaunte Denizen or Alyen of what natyon soever he or they bee, Twelfe pens : And also One other Subsidie called Pondage; that is to say, Of all maner of Goodes and Marchaundises of every Marchant Denizen and Alyen whatsoever he bee, caried and to be caried out of this yo' sayd Realme, or brought or to be brought into the same by waye of Marchaundise, of the value of every Twentye shillinges of the same Gooddes and Marchaundise Twelfe pens, and so after the rate; And of every Twenty shillinges value of Tynne and Pewter Vessell caried out of this yo' Realme by any and every Marchaunte Alyen xij d. over and above the xij d. aforesayd.

Excepte and alwayes forprysed out of this Grante of Subsidye of Pondage, all maner of Wollen Clothe made or wrought or that shalbee made and wrought within this yo' Realme of Englande, and by every or any Marchaunt Denizen, and not borne Alyen, caried or to bee caried out of this yo' sayd Realme; And all maner of Woolles Woollfelles and Hides and Backes of Leather also caried or to bee caried out of this yo' Realme; And all Wynes and all maner of fireshe Fishe and Bestyall coming or that ys or shall come into the same yo' Realme.

And further Wee yo' sayd poore Comons, by thadvise assent and aucthoritee aforesayd gyve and graunt unto yo" our sayd (4) liege Ladye and Sovereigne, for the Causes aforesaid. One other Subsidye of all maner of Woll Woollfelles and Leather caried or to be carried out of this yo' Realme in maner and fourme following; that is to saye, Of every Marchaunt Denyzcn of and for every Sack of Wooll, Thirtye three shillingf sour pens, and for every twoo hundrethe fowrtye Woollfelles Thirtye three shillinges foure pens, and of and for every Last of Hides and Backes of every suche Marchaunte Denizen, Three pounds syxe shillingf eight pens; And of every Marchaunt Straunger not borne yo' liege

THE care Whiche we do perceyve yo' Majestie hathe, most noble and redoubted Soveragne, to reduce this Realme and Thempiall Crowne therof now lately so sore shaken so impoverisshed so inffeobled and weakened, into the formor Estate Strength and Glory, doth make Us not onely to [- - - -*] in the greate bounteousnes of Almightie God, who hath so marvelously and beyond all worldly Expectation preserved yor Ma"* in these late diffyculte and daungerous tymes, but also to study and bend all our Wyttes and force of Understanding how we may, like lovyng and obedyent Subjectes, follow o' heade in this so noble and so necessarie an Enterprise; And considering w,h our selves that the decay hath ben, besides many other thinges, especyally in thes three. First, wasting of Treasure, abandoning of Strength, and in dymynishing of the auncyent Authoritye of yo' Imperiall Crowne; We do most ernestly and faithfully promyse to yo' Highness that there shall lacke no good Will Travell nor Force on our Behalfd to the redresse of all this, but we shalbe redy w* Hert Will Strenght Bodie Lyves and Goodes, not only to recover againe that wcU is thus deminished, but if nede be to recover further, (as far as Right and the Will and Pleasure of God shall suffer,) tholde Dignytie and Renowne of this Realme, the tyme and place whereof doth not rest in us, but, as most reason is, in yo' most noble Ma"* w4 thadvice of yo' Honerable Counsayle: Nevertheles since it doth so manifestly appere to us all, what inestimable Wasting and Consumptyon of the Treasure and auncient Revenues of this Realme hath ben of late dayes, and what greate new Charges and intollerable Expenses yo' Highnes is forced now to susteyne, by reason of the Decay and Losse of pcell of your auncient Crowne, so being not ignoraunt that no worthy Enterprise, no noble Attempte, no not so much as the preservacion of a strong and puissant Estate, may be wthout some masse of Treasure p^sently to be hadd and redy against all Occurrentf ; And where in the sayd Statute made in the sayd seventhe yere of the Reigne of the sayd King Henrye Theight, amonges other thinges in the same it is enacted, That yf, sithens the first daye of the same Plem1, any Landes, wch at the same first daye or sithens the same first daye were comonly used in Tillage, were inclosed or from thensforthe shoulde be inclosed and turned onely to Pasture, wherby any House of Husbandrye then was or thereafter shoulde bee decayed, that then all suche Landes shoulde bfee by the Owner or Owners therof, their Heirs Successoures or Assignes, or other for them, wythin one yere nexte ensuyng the same decaye, putt in Tyllage and exersised used and occupied in Husbandrye and Tillage as they were the first daye of the same Parliament or at anny tyme sithence, and after the maner and usage of the Countrey where suche Landes dyd lye; as by the sayd Acte more playnly maye appeare: And Forasmuch as upon the sayd pte of the said Statute, dyvers doubts and questions have been moved heretofore ; Bee it therfore enacted and declared by thaucthorite aforesayd, That yf at any tyme sithens the making of the sayd Acte and before the said Feast of S' George in the sayd xx,b yere of the Reigne of the said late King Henry Theight, any Landes belonging to any suche House of Husbandrye as is aforesayd, have been turned from Tillage to Pasture by any pson or psons, that then the same Landes or so muche other Landes being w"‘in the same Parishe Lordshippe or Manour that heretofore was not lyable or bounde by any Lawe or Statute to bee kepte in Tillage, shalbe turned agayne into Tillage w"‘in one yere next after the Session of this pnte Pliam' and kepte in Tillage for ever, according to the custome of the Cuntreye and nature of the Soyle; whether the sayd House wherunto the sayd Lands dyd belong bee decayed or no, or whether the same Landes were enclosed or not enclosed, or whether some parte therof and not the wholle were kept in Tillage or not; upon the paynes conteyned in the same Statute made in the sayd seventhe yere of the Reigne of the sayd late King Henry the Eight.

Provided alwaies and bee it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesayd, That yf any pson or psones whatsoever having any Pasture Heathe Waste or Barren Grounde, wdl hathe not been heretofore comonly used to bee eared or tilled for Corne, and yet nevertheles the same pson or psons to thintent to better and amende the sayd Grounde, and not to use the same for Tillage, have or hathe at any tyme heretofore turned or put the same into Tillage, or at any tyme hereafter shall tume or put the same into Tillage, and hathe or shall kepe the same Groude for that cause onely in Tillage by the space of foure yeres togethers, that this Acte or any thing therin conteyned shall not compell any pson or psons to continue or put in Tillage the sayd Pasture Heathe Barreyn or Waste Grounde so eared ; Any thing before expressed in this Act to the contrary therof notwithestanding.

Provided alwayes, That this Acte or any Provision Clause or Article therin conteyned shall not bee understande or expounded textende, or be in any wise prejudicial), to those ptes or porcons of Groundes wherin any Oore of Leade Tynne or Iron, or Coles comonly Sea Cole Stone Cole or Moore Cole, have been arr or hereafter shalbee usually gotten, by meanes whereof the same Groundes can not conveniently be put and kept in Tillage; This Acte or any other Lawe Usage or Custome to the contrary in any wise notwithestanding.

Provided also. That this Acte nor any thing therin conteyned shall extende to compell any pson or psons to put in Tillage any Lands or Grounds w^in any Forest or Chase, except the Forest of Snoweden in Northwales, otherwise then before the making of this Statute he or they ought or were bounde to doo; This Acte tendure to thende of the next Sessyon of Parlyament.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte towching dyvers Orders for Artificers Laborers Servantes of Husbandrye and Apprentises.

Insufficiency of existing Laws as to Hiring; and Wages of Servants, Artificers, Apprentices, &c.

ALTHOUGHE there remayne and stande in force pntly a greate nomber of Actes and Statutes concerning the retevning departing wages and orders of Apprentices Servantes and Labourers, aswell in Husbandrye as in divers other Artes Misteries and occupations, yet ptly for thimperfeccon and contrarietie that ys founde and doo appeare in sundrye of the sayd Lawes, and for the varyetie and nomber of them, and cheifly for that the wages and allouances lymytted and rated in many of the sayd Statutes, are in dyvers places to small and not answerable to this tyme, respecting thadvancement of Pryses of all thinges belonging to the said Servantes and Labourers, the said Lawes cannot conveniently wlllout the greate greefe and burden of the poore Labourer and hired man, bee put in good and due execution: And as the sayd severall Actes and Statutes were at the time of the making of them thought to be very good and beneficiall for the CSmon wealthe of this Realme as dyvers of them yet are, So yf the substance of as many of the said Lawes as are meet to bee continued shalbe digested and reduced into one sole Lawe and Statute, & in the same an uniforme Order prescrybed and lymitted concerning the Wages and other Orders for Apprentises Servauntes and Laborers, there ys good hope that yt will come to passe that the same Lawe, beyng duly executed, should banishe Idlenes advance Husbandrye and yeelde unto the hired pson bothe in the tyme of scarsitee and in the tyme of plentye a convenient proportion of Wages: Bee it therfore enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliament,

That asmuche of the Estatutes heretofore made, and every branche of them as touche or conceme the hiring keping departing woorcking wages or order of Servantes Woorckmen Artificers Apprentyses and Labourers or any of them, and the Penalties and Forfeytures concerning the same, shalbe from and after the last daye of September next ensuing repealed and utterly voide and of none effect; And that all the said Statutes and every branch therof for any Matter conteined in them and not repealed by this Statute, shall remaine and bee in full force and effecte, Any thing in this Statute to the contrarye notwithstanding.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That no maner of pson or psons after the foresaid last daye of September nowe next ensuing, shall reteyne hire or take into service, or cause to bee retayned hired or taken into service, nor any pson shalbee retayned (1) hired or taken into service, by any meanes or colour, to woorcke for any lesse tyme or terme then for one hole yere, in any of the Scyences Craftes Mysteries or Artes of Clothiers Wollen Clothe Weavers Tuckers Fullers Clothewoorkers Sheremen Dyers Hosyers Taylours Shoomakers Tanners Pewterers Bakers Bruers Gloovers Cutlers Smithes Farrours Curryers Sadlers Spurryers Turners Cappers Hatmakers or Feltemakers Bowyers Fletchers Arrowheadmakers Butchers Cookes or Myllers.

And bee it further enacted, That no pson wrh shall retayne any Servante shall put away his or her sayd Servant, and that no pson reteyned according to this Statute shall departe from his Mr M'* or Dame before thende of his or her terme, upon the payne hereafter mentioned, unlesse yt be for some reasonable and sufficient cause or matter to bee allowed before twoo Justices of Peace or one at the least w"‘in the said Countie, or before the [ Maio'1 ] or other Chief Officer of the Citie Burghe or Towne Corporate wherin the said Mr M" or Dame inhabitethe to whom any of the pries greyed shall complayne; wch said Justices or Justice Maio' or Chief Officer shall have and take upon them or him the hearing and ordring of the matter [ betwene1 ] the said Mr M" or Dame and Servante, according to thequite of the cause: And that no suche Mr M" or Dame shall put awaye any suche Servante at thende of his terme or that any suche Servante shall departe from his said M' M" or Dame at thende of his terme without one quarter warning gyven before thende of his sayd terme, eyther by the said Master Mastres or Dame or Serv'nte the one to the other, upon the payne hereafter ensuing.

Assembly and Conference togither, thinck yt convenient to retayne and kepe for the Yere then to come the Rates and Proportion of Wages that they certefied the Yere before, or to chaunge or refourme them, or some parte of them, then they shall before the said twelf day of Julye yerely, certefie into the sayd Courte of Chauncerye their Resoluc&ns and Determinacons therin, to the intent that Proclamac&ns may accordingly bee renued and sent downe; And if yt shall happen that ther bee no neede of any Reformac&n or Alterac&n of the Rates of the said Wages, but that the former shalbe thought meete to bee continued, then the Proclamac&ns for the Yere past shall remayne in force, untill newe Proclamac&ns upon newe Rates concerning the said Wages shalbee sent downe, according to the fourme of this Estatute.

And bee it further enacted by aucthoritee of this pnte Pliament, That yf all the said Justices of Peace resiant wu,in the Counties where they are or shalbe Justices of Peace Mayors and Head Officers, doo not before the tenthe daye of June next coming, and afterwarde yerely, appeare and assemble at the sayd generall Sessyons, or w"'in Syxe Weekes next after the said generall Sessions, and lymitt and rate the Wages of the said Servantes and Labourers, or shall not consider whether the former Rates made be meete to be continued or to bee altered and reformed in maner & forme aforesaid, or bee negligent or remisse in the Certificat therof in forme above writton, that then every Justice of Peace of the Countye, and every Mayo' and Heade Officer of the Citie or Towne Corporate in whom any suche Defaulte or Negligence shalbe founde, being w"'in the said Countie Citie or Towne Corporate at the tyme of the said next Assemblye, or at the tyme of the said Sessions, or at the tymes of the said Rates of Wages to bee set w^in Syxe Weekes next after every suche Sessions, and not visited withe any suche Sicknes as he coulde not traveelye thither w^out pill and daunger of his Lyes, or not having any other lawfull and good excuse, to bee allowed by the Justices then assembled for the rating and taxing of Wags as ys aforesaid or by the more parte of them, upon a corporall Othe and Affidavet to bee taken and made openly before the said Justices upon the Holy Evangelistes, by some credible pson assessed and taxed in the Booke of Subsidie of that Countie to the clere value of Fyve Poundes at the least, or by suche other pson as the most part of suche Justices shall allow and accept to take suche Othe, shall for suche Defaulte or Negligence forfeite unto the Quenes Ma"% her Heires and Successours, Tenne Pounds of laufull Moneye of England.

And bee it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That yf any pson after the sayd Proclamac&n shalbee so sent downe and published, shall by any secret Wayes or Meanes directly or indirectly reteyne or kepe any Servante Woorckman or Laborer, or shall gyve any more or greater Wages or other Comoditie contrary to the true Intent and Purporte of this Estatute, or contrarye to the Rates and Wages that shalbee assessed or appointed in the said Proclamac&ns, that then every pson that shall so offende and be therof laufully convicted before any the Justices or other Head Officers above remembred, or either of the sayd Presidentes and Councells, shall suffer Imprysonement by the space of Tenne Dayes, wlhout Bayle or Maynprise, and shall lose and forfeite Fyve Powndes of lawfull Moneye of Englande ; And that every pson that shalbe so reteyned and take Wagis, contrary to this Estatute or any Branche therof or of the sayd Proclamation, and shalbe therof convicted before the Justices aforesaid or any twoo of them, or before the Maio' or other Head Officers aforesaid, shall suffer Imprysonem' by the Space of xxj Days, w'out Baile or Mainprise j And that every Reteyner Promise Gifte or Paiment of Wagis or other Thing whatsoever, contrary to the meaning of this Estatute, and every Writing and Bonde to bee made for that Purpose shalbe utterly voide and of none effecte.

And be yt enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That yf any Servaunte Woorckman or Laborer shall wilfiillye or maliciously make any Assaulte or Affray upon his Mr M" or Dame, or upon any other that shall at the time of suche Assaulte or Fraye have the chardge or oversight of any suche Servante Woorkcman or Laborer, or of the Woorck wherin the said Servante Woorckman or Labourer ys appointed or hired to woorcke, and being therof convicted before any twoo of the Justices Maior or Head Officer aforesayd where the said Offence ys comitted, or before eyther of the said Lordes Presidentes & Councell before remebred, by confession of the said Servante Woorckman or Laborer, or by the Testimonye Witnes & Othe of two honest men. That then everye suche Offendo' shall suffer Imprisonement by the space of one whole yere or les, by the discression of twoo Justices of Peace if it bee w"out a Towne Corporate, and yf it be w,hin a Towne Corporate then by the discression of the Maio' or Head Officer of the same Towne Corporate w1" two others of the discretest psons of the same Corporac&n at the least: And if thoffence shall require further Punishement, then to receive suche other open Punishement, so as yt extende not to lief nor lyme, as the Justices of Peace in Open Sessions or the more pte of them, or the said Maio' or Head Officer and syxe

thinck convenient for the qualitie of the said Offence so done and comitted.

And because ther hathe bene and ys some Question and Scruple moved, whether any pson being w^in thage of one and twentye yeres, and bounden to serve as an Apprentice in any other place then in the said Citie of London, shoulde bee bounden accepted and taken as an Apprentyce; For the Resolution of the said Scruple and Doubte, bee yt enacted by aucthorite of this pnte Pliam1, That all and every suche pson or psons that at any time or times from hensforthe shalbe bounden by Indenture to serve as an Apprentice in any Arte Science Occupacbn or Labour, according to the teno' of this Estatute, and in maner and fourme aforesaid, albeit the same Apprentice or any of them shalbe within the age of one and twentye yeres at the tyme of making of their severall Indentures, shalbe bounden to serve for the yeres in their severall Indentures conteined, as amply and lardgly to every Entent as yf the same Apprentice were of full Age at the time of the making of suche Indentures; Any Lawe Usage or Custome to the contrary notwithestanding.

Provided alwaies that this Acte or any thing therin conteyned shall not extende to any laufull Reteyningf or Covenantes had or made before the making of this Acte; but that all and every the pries to suche Reteyninges or Covenantes shall and may have the same and lyke Advauntages of suche Reteyninges and Covenantes, and of the Statutes heretofore in that Behalfe provyded, as yf this Acte had never been had nor made; Any Clause of Repeale or other Matter whatsoever in this Acte to the contrary in any wise notwithestanding.

An Acte towching certayne Politique Constitutions made for the maintenance of the Navye.

CHAPTER Vin.

An Act towching Tanners Courriours Shoomakers and other Artyficers occupyeng the cutdng of Leather.

WHERE before this tyme dyvers and many good Estatutes have bene made for the true tanning currieng and woorking of Leather, as a Thing verie necessarie for the Comonwelthe and Comoditie for the Quenes Malfc* Subjectes, for that every sorte of People of necessite must use and have Leather for dyvers and sundrye Purposes, wth notwithstanding Leather was never woorse timed curried or wrought then nowe a dayes yt ys, by reason wherof dyvers psons are not onely putto great Losse [Charde1 ] and other Inconveniencf, but also doo take dyvers and sundry Diseases to the shortening of their Lyves, as by the Complayntes of dyvers psons exhibited in this Parlyament yt manifestlye appearethe; Bee It therfore enacted by the Quenes Ma"' w'" thassent of the Lordes and Comons in this pnte Pliam' assembled, and by thaucthorite of the same, That from and after the Feast of Pentecoste next coming, no Butcher or other pson shall gashe slaughter or cutt any Hide of any Bull Oxe Steere or Cowe in fleiyng therof or otherwise, wherby the same shalbe impayred or hurte; And that no Tanner or other pson or psons using or occupieng the Crafte or Mysterie of tanning of Leather shall after the Feast of S' Mighell Tharchaungell next coming, by himself or any other pson or psons, offer or putto sale any such Hide or Skynne so gashed slaughtered or cut, upon payne of forfeyture for every suche Hide or Skinne so offred or put to sale, Twentye pens.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That no Butcher or other pson or psons after the said Feast of Pentecost, shall kill any Calfe to sell, being under Fyve Weekes old, upon payne to forfeite for every Calf so to be killed and soulde vj s. viij d.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthoritye aforesaid. That no pson or psons occupieng the Crafte or Occupation of a Butcher, shall after the Feast of Pentecoste next coming, occupie or use by himself or any other pson or psones the Feate Crafte or Misterye of a Tanner during the tyme that he shall so use the Crafte or Occupation of a Butcher, upon payne of forfeyture of Syxe Shillingf Eight Pens for every Daye that he shall so use the Feate Crafte or Mistery of a Tanner.

And be yt further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That no pson or psons w'" at the Feast of Sl Mighell Tharchaungell wch was in the first yere of the Quenes Ma" Reigne that nowe ys, had not Landes Tenementes Rentes Profiles or Hereditamentes of Estate of Inheritance or for Tetme of Lyes or Lyves, of the clere yerely value of Fourtye Powndes or above, or whose Tannhouse was not at the said Feast ys or shalbee hereafter in a Citie Bourghe Towne Corporate or Markett Towne, where Searchers and Sealers of Leather hath beene and shalbee usually appointed, Except suche pson and psons as then had any Tannehouse, and dyd then occupye the Misterye of tanning of Leather, and except an Apprentice or Apprentices to a Timer or Timers, and except suche as were then or since or hereafter shalbee brought up instructed or tought as covenant or hired Servante for that Purpose by the Space of Seven Yeres, in the Mysterye or Crafte of tanning of Leather, and except the Wief and suche Sonne or Sonnes of a Tanner as hathe been brought up and hathe used the Misterye of tanning of Leather by the Space of Fowre Yeres aforesayd, or the Sonne or Daughter of a Tanner, or suche pson who shall marry suche Wief or Daughter to whom he hathe or shall leave a Tanhouse and Fattes, shall tanne any Leather, or shall use take or have any Profyte Game or Comoditee of or by the sayd Misterie or Crafte of tanning of Leather, upon paine of forfeiting of all suche Leather by him or them so tanned, or wherof he or they shall receive any Profite or Comodite by tanning, or the just Value therof.

And bee it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That after the Feast of Pentecost next coming, no pson or psons whatsoever, wch shall after the said Feast of Pentecost occupye or use by him or themselfe or by any other pson or psons the Crafte or Misterye of tanning of Leather, shall suffer any Hyde or Skinne to lye in the Lymes any longer time than the Heare fallethe of or may bee taken of, nor in any wise to bee putt into the Lymes after the Heere may bee taken of, nor shall use employe occupie or put, by themselfes or by any other pson or psons, any Thing in any Licoure Stuff or Woorckmanship in or aboute the tanning of Leather, but onely Lyme Culver Donge or Henne Donge,

And bee it further enacted for the true execution of this Estatute, That the Mayo' of the Citie of London, and the Aldermen of the same for the tyme being, or the more part of them, upon payne to forfaite Fourtye Poundes for every yere that they make Defaulte, (thone half wherof to bee to the Quenes MaUe her Heires and Successoures and thother Half to him or them that will sue for the same,) shall yerely appoynte Foure or more expert psons by their Discretions to bee Searchers, whoo shall bee sworne before the said Maio' and Aldermen for the tyme being, to doo their Office truely, whiche said Searchers shall by vertue of this Acte, foure times in the yere at the least, that ys to saye, once every Quarter of a Yere or oftener, if nede requyre, as they shall thinck good, make true searche and veiwe of and for all Bootes Buskinnes and other Wares and Thinges whatsoever made of tanned Leather, in all and every House and Houses Place and Places, aswell w,hin the said Citie and Suburbes therof as in every other Place w,hin Three myles of the same Citie where any Shoemaker Saddler Girdler, or other Artificer using cutting of Leather, dothe or shall dwell or occupie any of thoccupacons of cutting of Leather; and after every suche Searche and Viewe to make true Presentment in writing before the said Mayo' and Aldremen for the tyme being, of every Defaulte that they or any of them shall finde in the making selling or putting to sale of any Bootes Buskins Statuppes Shoes Brydles Sadies or other Thinges Stuffe or Ware made of Leather, contrary to the true meaning of this Estatute.

And bee yt further enacted, That the sayd Maior of the said Citie of London, and Aldremen for the tyme being, upon lyke payne lykewise to bee levyed and imployed, shall likewise yerely appoint foure or more other skilfull expert and honest parsones, wherof one shalbe a Sealer, and kepe a Seale for the sealing of Leather to bee prepared, who shall also bee sworne before the said Maior and Aldermen for the tyme being, to doo their Office trulye, whiche said Searchers and Sealer shall vieu & searche all and every tanned Hide Skyn [of1 ] Leather wch shalbee brought aswell to the Markett at Leaden Hall as to any other laufull Faire or Markett therfore usually appointed, w^in three Myles of the said Citie, [whither' ] the same be well and sufficiently tanned according to the Purporte and true Meaning of this Estatute or no ; and finding yt sufficiently and well tanned in suche maner and fourme as by this Estatute ys appoynted, and as yt ought to bee, shall seale the same withe the sayd Seale for that Purpose to bee provided and prepared.

And be yt further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That no pson or psons after the first day of Maye nextexommyng, shall sell exchaunge or put awaye or cause to bee solde exchaunged or put awaye any manner of tanned Leather redde and unwrought, except hee or they register or cause to bee registredd the said tanned Leather and every parte and parcell therof and the pryce therof, upon payne of forfeyture of the value of the Leather so solde exchaunged or put awaye and not registredd.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That it shall not bee laufull to or for any pson or p6ons to bye any tanned Leather before the same shall bee searched and sealed, nor to carrye or cause to bee carryed out of the Fayre or Marcket any Leather untill yt bee registredd as is aforesaid, upon payne to forfaite the said Leather or the value therof so bought and not searched and sealed or carried awaye and not registreud.

And bee yt further enacted, That no Cordewayner Shoemaker or Cobler shall carrye or cause to bee carryed any Oxe or Steere Hydes tanned wherof any sole Leather shalbee cutt, out of any [Fayre1] or Marcket whole, before the Wonibes bee cut of as ys aforsaid, upon payne of forfeyture for every Hyde otherwise carryed out of the same Fa ire or Market, syxe shillinges eight pens and the Hide, or the value therof.

CHAPTER X.

An Act to revyve a Statute made Anno xxj° H. Octavi, towching Servantes embeaselyng theyr Maysters Gooddes.

WHERE in the Parliament holden at London the thirde daye of November in the one and twentithe yere of the Reigne of the late King of most famous and worthy memory King Henry Theight, and fromthence adjourned to Westm, and there holden and continued by divers Prorogations unto the dissolution therof, It was ordeyned and enacted amongst other thinges, That all and singler Servantes to whom any Caskettes Juels Money Goodes or Catteles by his or their Mr or M" shoulde from thensforthe bee delyvered to kepe, that yf any suche Servant or Servantes withedrawe him or them from their said Maysters or Mastresses, and goo away wlh the said Kaskettes Juelles Money Goodes or Cattelles or any parte therof, to thintent to steale the same and defraude his or their said Masters and Mastresses therof, contrary to the Trust and Confidence to him or them put by his or their said M" and Mastresses; or els being in Service of his said Masters or Mastresses w>hout thassent or comaundement of his Masters or Mastresses embesyll the same Caskettes Juels Money Goodes or Cattelles or any parte therof, or otherwise convert the same to his owne use w,b like purpose to steale yt, that yf the sayde Caskettes Juels Money Goodes or Cattelles that any suche Servant shall go away wu or whiche he shall embesell w,h purpose to steale yt as ys aforesaid, bee of the value of fourtye shillinges or above. That then the same false fraudulent and untrewe Acte and Demeanour should fromthensforthe be demed and adjudged Felonye, and that he or they so offending shoulde bee punished as other Fellons for Felonye comitted by the course of the Comon Lawe; as by the sayd Acte amongst other Thinges therin conteyned more at large yt dothe and maye appeare: Whiche said Acte in the Pliament begune and holden at Westminster the fifthe day of October in the first yere of the Reigne of the late Queue Marye, and there continued to the xxj,h day of the same Monethe, That ys to saye in the first Session of the same Pliament, by the generall Woordes of one Acte then and there made, entituled An Act repealing of certeine Treasons Felonies and Preminire, was frothensforthe utterly repealed and made voyde: And forasmuche as sithens the Repeale of the same, the said Acte is thought necessary for the Comonwelthe of this Realme; Bee yt therefore enacted by our Sovereigne Ladye the Quenes Ma,ic w"' Thassent of the Lordes Spuall & Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliam' assembled and by thaucthorite of the same, That the said Acte made in the said one and twentye yere, and every Clause Article Branche Sentence and Provision therein conteyned, bee from hensforthe revived and put in due execution according to thintent and meaning therof, and fromhensforthe shall stande good endure and continue for ever.

Offences were abrogate and taken awaye by the generall Acte of Repeale then made: By reason wherof dyvers false and evill disposed psons pceyving themselfes to bee louse and free from the Severitee and Daunger of the sayd Lawe and Penaltie have been of late the more hardye and bolde to attempte and practise for wicked lucre and gaynes sake, to diminishe impaire and falsefie the Moneis and Coynes currant w"*in this Realme and the Dominions of the same by suche clipping washing rownding and fyling therof, not onely to the great Dishonour of the Quenes Ma,k our Sovereigne Ladye that nowe ys, by whose greate goodnes the newe Moneis or Coynes of the same are nowe reduced to asmuche fynesse as ever hathe been in any tyme of her noble Progenitoures, but also to the greate Losse and Damage of the good Subjectes of this Realme, and more ys like to bee hereafter, yf the same bee not spedely mett witheall: For Remedye wherof be it enacted declared and established by thaucthoritye of this pnte Provided alwaies and bee yt enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That this Acte or any Thing therin conteyned, nor anny Attayndour or Attaindoures of any pson or psons for any Offence or Offences made Treason by this Acte, shall in any wise extende or bee judged interpreted or expounded to make any Corruption of Blood to any Theire or the Heires of any suche Offendour or Offendours, or to make the Wief of any suche Offendour to lose or forfaite her Dower of or in any Landes Tenementes or Hereditamentes, or her Title Action or Interest to the same; Any Thing in this Acte conteyned, or any Attayndour or Attayndoures hereafter to bee had for any Offence or Offences made Treason by this Acte, to the contrary notwithestanding.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Act against the forgyng of Evydences and Wrytinges.

FORASMUCHE as the wicked pernicious and dangerous practise of making forging and publishing of false and untrue Charters Evidences Dedes and Writinges hathe of late tyme been verye muche more practised used and put in ure in all Partes of this Realme then in tymes passed, not onely to the highe displeasure of God, but also to the greate Injurie Wrong Hurte Domage Disherison and utter undoyng of dyvers of the Quenes Ma'1" Subjectes of this Realme, and to the great subvertyon of Justice and Truthe; whiche semethe to have growen and happened cheiflye by reason that the Paynes and Punishem'f lymitted for suche greate and notable Offences by the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme, before this tyme have been and yet arre so small mylde and easye that suche evill People have not been nor yet arre afrayde to enterprise the practysing and doyng of suche Offences: Bee it therefore enacted by the Quenes most excellent Matk w,h Thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same, That yf any pson or psons whatsoever, after the first daye of June now next coming, upon his or theyr owne Heade and Imagination or by false Conspiracye and Fraude w"‘ others, shall wittingly subdllye and falsely fordge or make, or subtilly cause or wittingly assent to bee fordged or made, any false Dede Charter or Writing sealed, Court Roll, or the Will of any pson or psons in Writing, to thintent that the State of Free holde or Inheritance of any pson or psons of in or to any Landes Tenementes or Hereditamentes Free holde or Copie holde, or the Right Title or Interest of any pson or psons of in or to the same or any of them, shall or maye bee molested troubled defeated recovered or chardged. Or after the sayd first daye of June shall pronounce publishe or shewe foorthe in Evidence any suche false and forged Dede Charter Writing Courte Roll or Will as true, knowing the same to bee false and forged as ys aforesayd to thintent above remembred, and shalbe therof convicted either upon Action or Accons of Forger of false Dedes to bee founded upon this Statute at the Sute of the ptie greyed, or otherwise according to thorder and due course of the Lawes of this Realme, or upon Byll or Information to bee exhibited into the Courte of the Starre Chamber according to Thorder and Use of that Courte, shall paye unto the ptie greeved his dooble Costes and Damages, to bee founde or assessed in that Courte where suche Conviccon shalbe, and also shalbee sett upon the Pillorie in some open Markett Towne or other open Place, and there to have bothe his Eares cutt of, and also his nosetrelles to be slytt and cut and seared w'" an hott Iron, so as theye maye remayne for a ppetuall note or marck of his falsehead, and shall forfaite to the Quene o' Sovereigne Ladye her Heyres and Successours, the whole Issues and Profittf of his Landes and Tenementf during hys lyes, and also shall suffer and have ppetuall Imprisonem* during his lief; The said Damages and Costes, to bee recovered at the Sute of the ptie greyfed as ys aforesayd, to be first payde and levied of the Gooddes and Cattelles of the Offendour, and of Thissues and Profittes of the said Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes of suche ptie convicted, or of one or bothe of them, The said Title of our said Sovereygne Ladye the Quene her Heires or Successoures to the same notwithestanding.

And bee it further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That yf any pson or psons, after the said first daye of June, upon his or theyr owne Head or Imaginacon or by false Conspirac&n or Fraude had w,h any other, shall wittingly subtelly and falsely forge or make, or wittingly subtyllye and falsely cause or assent to bee made and forged, any false Charter Dede or Writing, to thintent that any pson or psons shall or maye have or clayme any Estate or Interest for terme of yeres, of in or to any Manoures Landes Tents or Hereditamentes not being Copye holde, or any Annuitee in Fee Simple Fee Tayle for terme of Lief Lyves or Yeres, or after the said daye shall as ys aforesaid forge make or cause or assent to bee made or forged any Obligac&n or Bill Oblygatorye, or any Acquitance Release or other dischardge of anny Debt Accowmte Action Sute Demande or other [thingf1 ] psonall, or yf any pson or psons, after the said first daye of June, shall pronounce publishe or gyve in Evidence any suche false or forged Charter Dede Writing Obligation Bill Obligatorye Acquitance Releas or Dischardge as true, knowing the same to bee false and forged, and shalbee therof convicted by any the ways or meanes aforesayd, that then he shall paye unto the partie greyed hys dooble Costes and Damages, to bee founde and assessed in suche Courte where the sayd Convice&n shalbee had, and shalbee also sett upon the Pillorie in some open Market Towne or other open Place and ther to have one of his Eeres cut of, and also shall have and suffer Imprisonement by the space of one whole yere w,hout Bayle or Maynprise.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That the ptie and pries greyed by reason of any thoffences aforesaid, shall and may at his and their pleasure have and sue his Action of Forger of false Dedes upon this Statute against any Thoffendo" in the same, by originall Writt out of the Quenes Highnes Courte of Chancerie, and shall and

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That all and every Justices of Oyer and Determiner Sc Justicf of Assise in theyr Circuites, and every of them, shall have full power and aucthoritee in every of their open and generall Sessions, tenquire (1 ) faeare and determyne [of* ] all and every thoffences aforesayd comitted or doon w,hin the limittes of their Comission, and to make Processe for thexecuc&n of the same, as they maye doo against any pson beyng indicted before them of Trespas, or laufully convicted therof.

CHAPTER XV.

An Act against fonde and phantasticall Prophesyes.

FORASMUCHE as sithens thexpiracbn and ending of the Statute made in the time of King Edwarde the Syxthe entituled, An Act against fonde and fantasdcall Prophesies, divers evill disposed psons, enclyned to the stirring and moving of Factions Seditions and Rebellions w^in this Realme, have byn the more bolde tattempte the lyke Practise, in fayning imagining inventing and publishing of suche fonde and fantasticall Prophesies, aswell concerning the Quenes Malk as divers honourable Parsonagies Gentlemen and others of this Realme, as was used and practised before the making of the sayd Statute, to the grete disquiet trooble and perill of the Quenes Ma0' and of this her Realme: For Remedie wherof, Bee yt ordeyned and enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliament, That yf any pson or psons, after the first daye of Maye next coming, do advisedly and directly advance publishe and set fourthe by Writing Prynting Synging, or any other open Speache or Dede, to any pson or psons, any fonde fantasticall or false Prophecye upon or by thoccasion of any Armes Fieldes Beastes Badges or suche other lyke thinges accustomed in Armes Cognisaunces or Signettes, or upon or by reason of any Time Yere or Daye name Blodshed or Warre, to thintent therby to make anye Rebellion Insurrection Dissention losse of Lief or other Disturbance w,hin this Realme and other the Quenes Dominions; that then every suche pson, beyng therof laufully convicted according to the due course of the Lawes of this Realme, for everye suche Offence shall suffer Imprysonement of his Bodye by the space of one yere without Baile or Mayneprise, and shall forfaite for every suche Offence the some of tenne powndes:

CHAPTER XVI.

An Act against Conjurac&ns Inchantmentes and Witchecraftes.

WHERE at this present, there ys no ordinarye ne condigne Punishement provided against the Pracdsers of the wicked Offences of Conjurac&ns and Invocations of evill Spirites, and of Sorceries Enchauntmentes Charmes and Witchecraftes, the wch Offences by force of a Statute made in the xxxiij yere of the Reigne of the late King Henry the Eyghthe were made to "bee Felonye, and so continued untill the sayd Statute was repealed by Thacte and Statute of Repeale made in the first yere of the Reigne of the late King Edwarde the vj"1; sythens the Repeale wherof many fantasticall and devilishe psons have devised and practised Invocaf&ns and Conjurac&ns of evill and wicked Spirites, and have used and practised Wytchecraftes Enchantementes Charms and Sorceries, to the Destrucc&on of the Psons and Goodes of their Neighebours and other Subjectes of this Realme, and for other lewde Internes and Purposes contrarye to the Lawes of Almighty God, to the Perill of theyr owne Soules, and to the great Infamye and Disquietnes of this Realme: For Reformac&n wherof bee it enacted by the Quenes Ma"' wth thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled, and by thaucthoritee of the same. That yf any pson or psons after the first daye of June nexte coming, use practise or exersise any Invocac&ns or Conjurac&ns of evill and wicked Spirites, to or for any Intent or Purpose j or els if any pson or psons after the said first daye of June shall use practise or exercise any Witchecrafte Enchantment Charme or Sorcerie, wherby any pson shall happen to bee killed or destroyed, that then aswell every suche Offendo' or Offendo'1 in Invocac&ns or Conjurac&ns as ys aforesayd, their Concello" & Aidours, as also every suche Offendo' or Offendo" in Witchecrafte Enchantement Charme or Sorcerie wherby the Deathe of anny pson dothe ensue, their Aidours and Concello", being of either of the said Offences laufully convicted and attainted, shall suffer paynes of Deathe as a Felon or Felons, and shall lose the Priviledg and Benefite of Sanctuarie & Clergie: Saving to the Wief of such parsone her Title of Dower, and also to the Heyre and Successour of suche pson his or theyr Tytles of Inheritaunce Succession and other Rightes, as thoughe no suche Attayndour of the Auncestour or Predecessour had been hadd or made.

And further bee yt enacted by thaucthoritee aforesayd, That if any pson or psons, after the saide first daye of June nexte comyng, shall use practise or exercyse any Wytchecrafte Enchauntement Charme or Sorcerie, wherby any pon shall happen to bee wasted consumed or lamed in his or her Bodye or Member, or wherby any Goodes or Cattelles of any pson shalbee destroyed wasted or impayred, then every suche Offendour or Offendours their Councelloures and Aydoures, being therof laufully convicted, shall for his or their first Offence or Offences, suffer Imprisonement by the Space of one whole Yere, w,hout Bayle or Mayneprise, and once in every Quarter of the said Yere, shall in some Market Towne, upon the Market Daye or at suche tyme as any Fayer shalbee kepte there, stande openly upon the Pillorie by the Space of Syxe Houres, and there shall openly confesse his or her Errour and Offence; and for the Seconde Offence, being as ys aforesayd laufully convicted or attaynted, shall suffer Deathe as a Felon, and shall lose the Privilege of Clergie and Sanctuarye: Saving to the Wief of suche pson her Title of Dower, and also to Theire & Successo' of suche pson, his or their Titles of Inheritance Succession and other Rightes, as thoughe no suche Attaindo' of Thancesto' or Predecesso' had beene hadde or made.

Provided alwaies, That yf the Offendour, in any of the Cases aforesayd for whiche the paynes of Deathe shall ensue, shall happen to bee a Peere of this Realme, then his Triall thereyn to be hadd by hys Peeres, as yt ys used in cases of Felonye or Treason and not otherwyse.

And further to thintent that all maner of practise use or exercise of Witchecrafte Enchantement Charme or Sorcerye shoulde bee from hensforthe utterly avoyded abolished and taken awaye; Bee it enacted by thaucthoritee of this pnte Pliament, That yf any pson or psons shall from and after the sayd first daye of June nexte c5ming, take

CHAPTER XX.

An Acte for the Punishement of Vagabondes callyng themselfes Egiprians.

WHEREAS sithence thacte made in the first and seconde yeres of the late King and Quene, Kyng Phillip and Quene Marie, for the Punishement of that false and subtile Companie of Vacaboundes calling themselves Egiptians, there ys a scruple and doubte risen whether suche psons as being borne w^in this Realme of Englande or other the Quenes Highnes Dominions, and are or shall become of the Fellowship or Companie of the said Vagaboundes, by transforming or disguising themselves in their Apparell or in a certaine contrefaite Speache or Behavour, are punishable by the said Acte in like maner as others of that sort are, being Strangers borne and transported into this Realme of Englande: Therfore for thadvoyding of all Doubtes and Ambiguites in that Behalf, and to thintent that all suche sturdie and false Vagabondes of that sorte, living onelie upon the spoile of the simple People, maie be condingly met w^all and punished; Be it enacted by the Quene our Sovereigne Ladie the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by the aucthoritee of the same, That the sayd Statute made in the first and seconde yeres of the sayd late King and Quene, concerning those Vagaboundes calling themselves Egiptyans, shall contynue remayne and bee in full Force Strengthe and Effecte.

And yet moreover bee it enacted by thaucthoritee aforesaid, That all and every pson and psons whiche, from and after the first daye of Maye nowe next ensuing, shalbee seen or founde within Realme of Englande or Wales in any Companye or Felowship of Vagaboundes comonly called or calling themselves Egiptians, or counterfeiting transfourming or disguising themselves by their Apparell Speache or other Behavour like unto suche Vagaboundes comonly called or calling themselves Egiptians, and so shall or doo continue and remayne in the same, either at one time or at severall times by the space of one monethe, That then the same pson or psons shall by vertue of this Acte bee demed and judged a Felon and Felons, and shall therfore suffer Paynes of Deathe Losse of Landes and Gooddes as in cases of Felonye by Thorder of the Comen Lawes of this Realme, and shall upon the Tryall of them or of any of them therein, bee tried in the Countie and by Thinhabitantes of the Counrie or Place wher they or he shalbee apprehended or taken, and not P medietatem Lingue, and shall lose the Priviledge and Benefite of Sanctuary & Clergie.

Provided always and bee it enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid. That this Acte shall not in any wise extende to any Childe or Children being w^n Thage of fourtene yeres; nor to any of the said psons being in Prison the last Day of this pnte Pliament, so that he or they so being in Prison doo within fourtene dais next after his or their

II.

CHAPTER XXV.

An Acte to fill upp Juries De Circumstantibus lacking in Wales.

WHERE in the Parlament holden at Westmynster in the xxxv,h yere of the Reigne of our late Sovereigne Lorde Kyng Henry Theight, Father to our most deare Sovereygne Ladye the [Quenes1] Ma'1' that nowe ys, one holsome & profitable Acte and Estatute amongst other was then established and enacted, intituled by the name of an Acte concerning thapparance of [Juries1] in Nisi Prius, where amongst other thinges in the Acte, it was establsyhedd, that where a full Jurye returned betwixte ptie and ptie dyd not appeare before the Justices of Assise or Nisi Prius, or els after Apparance of a full Jurye by challendge of any of the pties the Jurye was lyke to remayne untaken for default of Jurours, that the same Justices upon request made by the ptie Playntyf or Demandant should have aucthoritee, by vertue of the same Acte, to comaunde the Sheryf, or other Minister or Ministers to whom the making of the said Retume shoulde appteyne, to name and appoynt as often as nede shoulde require, so many of suche other liable psons of the said Countie then pnte at the said Assise or Nisi Prius as shoulde make up a full Jury, wrt psons so to bee named and impanelled by suche Sheryf or other Minister or Ministers, shoulde bee added to the former Panell, and their Names annexed to the same; and further as in the same Acte more playnely maye appeare; Whiche sayd beneficiall Acte dothe not extende unto the Twelve Shires of Wales, ne to the Countye Palatyne of Chester, nor to the Countye Palatyne of Lancaster, nor to the Countye Palatyne of Durham; By reason wherof manye Juries remayne untaken betwext the pties, what for lacke of Apparence of Jurers, and some because of Chalengf, to the greate hynderance of Justice, and greate Expenses and Chardges to the pties: For Reformacon wherof bee yt enacted by the Quene our Sovereygne Ladye, wth thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pham* assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same. CHAPTER XXVI.

An Acte for thenrollem' of Indentures of Bargayne and Sale in the Quenes Ma'" Courtes.

WHERE in the Parliament holden upon Prorogation at Westminster, the Fourthe Daye of February in the xxvijlh yere of the Reign of our late Sovereigne Lorde of most famouse Memorye King Henry Theight, and there continued and kept till the xiiijlh daye of Aprill then next ensueng, It was enacted, That from the last daye of Julye w* was in the yere of our Lorde God One Thousande fyve hundrethe thirtie syxe, no Manours Landes Tenementes or other Hereditamentes shoulde passe alter or chaunge from one to an other, wherby any Estate of Inheritance or Freeholde shoulde bee made or take effect in any pson or psons, or any Use therof to bee made by reason onely of any Bargayne and Sale therof, except the same Bargayne and Sale were made by Writing indented sealed and inrolled in one of the Kings Courtes of Recorde at Westni, or els wthin the same Countie or Counties where the same Manours Landes or Tenementes so bargayned and solde lye or bee, before the Custos Rotulorum and twoo Justices of the Peace, and the Clarck of the Peace of the same Countie or Counties or two of them at the least, (wherof the Clarck of the Peace to bee one,) and the same Inrollementes to bee hadd and made within syxe monethes next after the date of the said Writing indented; as by the same Acte of Pliam' amonge other thinges theryn conteyned more at large yt dothe appeare: And Forasmuche as the same Acte of Pliam' dothe not extende to make any Inrollmentes of any Deedes indented of suche Bargaynes and Sales, made of any Mano" Lands Tentes or Hereditamentes heng and beyng wuin the Counties Palatyne of Lancaster Chester and the Bishopriche of Duresme, to bee good or of any force in the Lawe, in any the Quenes Courtes of Recorde w^in the sayd Counties Palatyne of Lancaster Chester or Bishopriche of Duresme: Bee it nowe therfore enacted by the Quene our Sovereygne Ladye w"’ thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall of this pnte Pliam' assembled and by thaucthorite of the same, That from the Feaste of Easter next coinyng, all Inrollementes of suche Writinges indented, of any Bargayne and Sale after the said Feast of Easter to bee made of any Manours Landes Tenementes or other Hereditamentes sett heng or being in the sayd Counties of Lancaster Chester and Byshopriche of Duresme, beyng made and inrolled, w"*in syxe monethes nexte after the Date of any suche Writinges indented, in the Quenes Court of Chancerye at Lancaster, or before the Quenes Justice or Justices of Assises at Lancaster aforesaid, concerning any Manours Landes Tentes or Hereditamentes w^in the sayd Countye of Lancaster, or in the Quenes Courte of Thexchequer at Chester, or before the Quenes Justice or Justices of Assises at Chester aforesaid, concerning any Maours Landes Tentes or Hereditamentes w^yn the said Countie of Chester, or in the Courte of Chauncerye at Duresme, or before the Justice or Justices of Assises at Duresme aforesaid, concerning any Manours Landes Tentes or Hereditamentes w"4n the said Countie of the Bishopriche of Duresme, shalbee accepted reputed deemed and taken by thaucthoritee of this Acte, to bee as good and avayleable in the Lawe to all Internes Constructions and Purposes, as yf the same Writinges indented had bene made and inrolled in any of the Quenes Courtes at Westminster ; Any Thing conteyned in the said former Acte to the contrary in any wise notwithestanding.

Provided alwayes. That this Acte nor any Thing theryn conteyned extende to any Mano" Landes Tenementes or Hereditamentes lyeng and beyng w’ln any Cirie Borowghe or Towne Corporate, w^n any of the said Counties, wherein the Maiours Recorders Chaumberlaynes Bayliefes, or other Officer or Officers, have aucthoritee and have laufully used tenroll any Evidences Deedes or other Writinges withein their Precincte or Lymites; Any Thing in this Acte conteyned to the contrary notwithestanding.

CHAPTER XXVII.

An Acte towching Fines to bee levied in the County Palatyne of Durham.

Fines levied before the Justices of the County Palatine of Durham, proclaimed at three Sessions, in Presence of the Justices of Assise, declared valid.

IN most humble wise shewen unto yo' most excellent Ma'te, yo' trewe and faithfull Subjectes and liegemen thynhabytantes of the Countye Palatine of Durham, That Whereas by aucthoritee of Pliam' dyvers necessarye and beneficiall Estatutes have been made for and concerning the levyeng of Fines w"1 Proclamac6n, wcb arre not onely necessarie for the preservation of Quietnes and Concorde amongst yo' loving Subjectes, and for thadvoyding of Stryfe and Contention, but also for the greate and perfecte Assurance of all suche psons to whom suche Fynes are levyed of anye Landes Tenementes or Hereditamentes; whiche sayd beneficiall and necessarye Estatutes doo not extende to anye Fines to be levyed withein the sayd Countie Palatyne of Durham: In tender Consideration wherof, pleasithe it yo' most excellent Mau', that yt maye bee enacted by yo' Highnes, and the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliament assembled and by thaucthoritee of the same, That all and singler Fynes which at any tyme hereafter shalbee levyed or knowledged before the Justice or Justices of the said Countie Palatine for the tyme beyng, aucthorised for that purpose and cause, of any Landes Tenementes or other Hereditamentes lyeng or beyng wu,iii the said Countie Palatyne of Durham, w^ shalbee openly redde and proclaymed twoo severall days in the Open Sessions in the presence of the Justices of Assises [at1] Durham, or one of them for the tyme being, at the same Sessions that the same Fyne shall fortune to be engrossed, and also that shalbee openly redde and proclaymed in the presence of the Justices of Assises at Durham, or one of them for the tyme beyng, at the twoo next General Sessions that shalbee holden in the Countie Palatyne of Durham before the Justices of the same Countie, comonly called Justices of Assises at Durham or one of them, next after the levyeng or ingrossing of suche sayd Fyne, shalbee of like and the same Force Strengthe and Effecte in the Lawe, to all Internes Constructions and Purposes, as Fynes beyng duly levyed withe Proclamations before the Quenes Justices of her Comon Please at Westmynster bee or ought to bee.
