CHAPTER XXVin.

An Acte for the translating of the Bible and the Dyvine Service into the Welshe Tongue.

’WHEREAS the Quenes most Excellent Ma"*, Iyke a most godly and virtuous Prynces having cheif Respect V ▼ and Regarde to the Hono' and Glorye of God and the Soules helthe of her Subjectes, did in the first yere of her Reigne by the Aucthoritee of her Highe Courte of Pliam*, cheifly for that purpose called, set for the a Booke of Comon Prayour and Order of Thadministraf&n of Sacramentf, in the vulgar Englishe Tongue, to bee used throughe all her Realme of Englande Wales and the Marches of the same; that therby her Highnes most loving Subjectes understanding in their own Language the terryble and fearfull Threatningf rehearsed in the Book of God ageynst the wicked and malefacto", the pleasant and infallible promises made to the Electe and chosen Flock, w01 a just Order to rule and guyde theyr Lyves according to the Comandem’f of God, might muche better learne to love and feare God, to serve and obey theyr Prynce, and to knowe their Dudes towards their neyghbou"; w* Book being receyved as a most precious Juell w'h an inspeakable joye of all suche her Subjectes as did and doo understande Thenglishe Tongue, the w* Tongue ys not understanded of the most and greatest nouber of all her Ma"" most lovyng and obedient Subjectes inhabiting w^in her Highnes Dominion and Contrey of Wales, being no small parte of this Realm, who therfore arre utterly destituted of Gooddes Holy Woorde, and doo remayne in the like or reyther more Darcknes & Ignorance then they were in the tyme of Papistrye: Bee it therfore enacted by the Quene our Sovereigne Ladye the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this pnte Pliam* assembled and by thaucthorite of the same, That the Byshoppes of Hereforde S* Davydes Assaphe Bangor and Landaphe, and their successoures, shall take suche Order among themselfes for the Soules helthe of the Flockes comitted to their Chardge w^in Wales, That the whole Byble conteyning the Newe Testam* and Tholde, w"* the Booke of C5mon Prayo* and Administrac&n of the Sacram'f as ys nowe used wthin this Realme in Englishe, to bee trulye & exactly translated into the Brittishe or Welshe Tongue; and that the same so translated, beyng by them vieued pused and allowed, bee imprinted to suche nomber at the least that one of eyther sorte may bee hadd for every Cathedral! Collegia! & Pishe Churche & Chappell of Ease, in suche Places & Countreys of every the said Diocesses where that Tongue ys comonly spoken or used, before the first daye of Marche that shalbee in the yere of or Lorde God XV c lxvj"1; And that from that daye foorthe the whole Dyvyne Service shall bee used and sayd by the Curates & Ministers, throughout all the said Diocesses where the Welshe Tongue ys comonly used, in the said Brittishe or Welshe Tongue, in suche maner and fourme as ys nowe used in the Englishe Tongue, and dyffering nothing in any Order or Fourme from Thenglishe Book; for the wd" Bookes so imprinted, the Pishioners of every of the said Pyshes shall paye thone half or moytee, and the Parson & Vicar of every of the said Pishes (where bothe bee) orels thone of them where there ys but one, shall paye thother half or moytie; the prices of w* Bookes shalbee appoynted and rated by the said Bishoppes and their successoures, or by three of them at the least; the w* things yf the said Bishoppes or their successoures neglecte to doo. That then every one of them shall forfeit to the Quenes Matt her heires and successoures the some of fowrtye powndes to be leviede of their Goodes and Cattelles.

Bee it further enacted by thaucthorite aforesaid, That every Minister and Curate w°4n the Diocesses beforesaid, where the Welshe Tongue ys comonly used, shall from the Feast of Whitsontyde next ensueng untill the foresaid (•) daye of Marche wch shalbee in the yere XV c lxvj, at all tymes of Comgnion declare or reade Thepistle and Gospell of the day in the Welshe Tongue to his or their Pishioners in every of the said Churches & Chappelles; and also once every Week at the least, shall reade or declare to their said Pishioners in the said Churches, the Lordes Prayo* Tharticles of the Christian Faithe the Tenne Comaundementf and the Letany, as they are set foorthe in Thenglishe Tongue, in the said Welshe Tongue, w*h suche other pte of the Comon Prayer & Divine Service as shalbee appointed by the Bishoppe of the Dyoces for the tyme beyng.

CHAPTER XXIX.

An Acte for the Confirmac&n of a Subsidye granted by the Clergye.

consideringe allso the greate Debtes wherew"1 Thimperiall Crowne of this Realme was charged when it pleased Almightie Godde first to call your Highnes to the Gouvem*nce of the same ; And further wayinge the greate and intollerable Charges wherew'1' your Mau* of late hath byn burdeyned, in the repayring and fumishinge of your Ma’" Navye and Provision of Armour and Munic&ns moste necessarie and requisite for the defence and saufegarde of this Realme, wherof the same at the begynninge of your Highnes Reigne was voyde and destitute; CHAPTER I.

An Acte declaringe the manner of makinge and consecratinge of the Archbushopes and Busshops of this Realme

to be good lawful and parfecte.

Doubts respecting the Consecration of Bishops, &c.

SpiritualSupremacy of K. Henry VIII. acknowledged;

aj H. VIII. c. 20. as to Consecration of Bishops

Form of Consecration, in the Common Prayer Book, sanctioned by St. J.6E.VI. c. 1.

FORASMUCHE as dyvers questions, by overmuche boldnes of Speache and Talke amonges many of the common sorte of people being unlearned, have lately growen uppon the making and consecrating of Archbyshops and Byshops w^n this Realme, whether the same were and be duely and orderly done according to the Lawe or not, w4 is muche tending to the slaunder of all the State of the Cleargie, being one of the gretest States of this Realme; Therfore for the avoydyng of suche slaunderous Speache, and to the intent that everie man that is willyng to know the trueth, maye playnely understande that the same evill Speache and Talke is not grounded uppon anye just Matter or Cause; It is thought convenyent hereby partly to touche suche aucthorities as dothe allowe and approve the making and consecrating of the same Archbyshops and Bishops to be dulye and orderly done according to the Lawes of this Realme, and theruppon further to provide for the more suretie thereof as hereafter shalbe expressed: Fyrst, It is verye well knowen to all Degrees of thys Realme that the late Kyng of moost famous memorye Kyng Henry the Eight, as well by all the Cleargie then of this Realme in their severall Convocacions, as also by all the Lordes Spiritual! and Temporall and Commons assembled in dyvers-of his Parliamentes, was justly and rightfully recognized and knowledged to have the supreame Power Jurisdkc&n Order Rule and Aucthoritie over all the State Ecdesiasticall of the same, and the same Power Jurisdiccbn and Aucthoritye dyd use accordingly; And that also the sayd late Kyng in the xxv" yere of his Raigne, dyd by aucthoritye of Parliament amonges other things set foorth a certayne Order of the maner and fourtne howe Archbyshops and Byshops w^in this Realme and other his Dominyons shoulde be elected and made; as by the same more playnly appeareth : And that also the late Kyng of worthy memorye Kyng Edward the Sixt, did lawfully succeade the sayd late Kyng Henry his father in the Imperiall Crowne of this Realme, and dyd justly possesse and enjoye all the same Power Jurisdyction and Aucthoritie before mencioned as a thing to hym dyscended w* the same Imperiall Crowne, and so used the same during his lyfe: And that also the sayd late Kyng Edward the Syxt in his tyme by aucthoritye of Parliament, caused a godly and vertuous Booke intituled, The Booke of Common Prayer and Adminvstration of Sacramentes and other Rightes and Ceremonyes in the Churche of England, to be made and set fourthe ; CHAPTER II.

An Acte whereby the Defendant maye recover his Costes beinge wrongfully vexed.

WHERE dyvers parsons, of their malicious Mindes and w"*out any just Cause, do many tymes cause and procure others of the Quenes Mau" loving Subjectes to be very muche molested and troubled by Attachementes and Arrestf made of their Bodyes, aswell by Processe of Latitat alias and plures Capias sued out of the Courte comonly called the Kings Benche, as also by Playnt Byll or other Suite in the Courte comonly called the Marshalsey, and w^in the Citye of London, and other Cities Townes Corporate and Places where any Libertie or Privilege is to holde Pleas of Debt Trespasse and other personall Actions and Suites; And when the Parteis that be arrested or attached are brought foorthe to aunswere to suche Actions and Suites as shoulde be objected against them, then rnanye tymes there is no Declaracion or Matter layed against the Parteis so arrested or attached, whereunto they maye make any Aunswere ; and so the Partie arrested is verie maliciously put to great Charges and Expences w^out any just or reasonable Cause; And yet neverthelesse hitherto by order of the Lawe the Partie so greyed and vexed coulde never have any Coostes or Damages to hym to be judged or awarded for the sayde Vexacion and Trouble: For Remedie wherof be it enacted and ordeined by the aucthoritie of this psent Parliament, That when and as often as anye parson or parsons, after the first daye of January next comyng, shall sue foorth or by anye Meane cause or procure to be sued foorth of the sayd Courte comonly called the Kyngf Benche, any of the Wrytes or Processe before mencyoned against any parson or parsons wcU upon the same Wryte or Wrytes shall happen to be arrested, or wc" shall appeare uppon the Retoume of any of the sayd Wrytes or Processe, and shall put in his or their Baile or Bailes to aunswere suche Suite as shalbe objected against hym according to the common order of that Courte; that then in everye suche Case if the Partie or Parties, at whose Suite Meanes or Procurement the same Write Writes or Processe was obtayned or sued foorth, doo not w"*in three dayes next after suche Bayle had and taken, put into the same Court his or their Declaracion against the same Partie or Parties against whome suche Writes or Processe hath ben or shalbe sued, Or if after Declaracion had and put into the same Courte, the Plaintyfe in suche Case shall not prosecute the same w® Effect, but shall willingly and apparauntly to the same Courte suffer his or their sayd Suite to be delayed, or shall after Declaracion so had suffer the same Suite to be dyscontinewed, or otherwyse shalbe nonsuite in the same, that then in every suche Case the Judges of the sayd Court for the tyme being shall, by their dyscrecions from tyme to tyme as they shall see or parceyve any suche Default to be in the Partie or Parties at whose Suite Meanes or Procurement suche Writes or Processe was sued foorth, awarde and judge, to every suche parson and persons so arrested vexed molested or troubled by such Wrytes or Suite, his and their Costes Damages and Charges by any meanes susteyned, by occasion of any suche Writes Processe Arrestes or Suites taken sued or had against hym, to be payde by suche person or persons that so dothe or shall cause or procure anye such Writes or Processe to be sued foorthe as is aforesayd.

CHAPTER IIL An Acte againste carryinge over Sea Rames Lambes and other Shepe alyve.

FOR sundry good Causes and Consideracions mooved in thys Hygh Court of Parliament, Bee it enacted by the Aucthoritye of the same, That no maner of parson or persons of what Estate Degree or Condicion so ever he or they be, shall after the last daye of February next ensuyng, bryng delyver sende receyve or take, or procure to be brought delyvered sent or receved into any Shippe or Bothome, any Ranimes Sheepe or Lambes or any maner of other kynde of Sheepe being alyve to be caryed and conveyed oute of thys Realme of England Wales or Irelande or out of anny of the Queenes Highnes Dominyons, uppon the payne that every suche person and persons their Ayders Abetters Procurers and Coforters shall for hys or their first Offence or Offences so done contrary to the true meanyng of this Estatute, forfayte and lose all hys Goodes for ever; whereof the one moitie shalbe to the Queenes Ma!ie her Heyres and Successors, the other moitie to hym or them that will sue for the same in any Court of Recorde wherein no Essoigne Protection nor Wager of Lawe for the Defendaunt shalbe admytted or allowed: And further every suche Offender or Offenders shall suffer imprisonment by the space of one whole yere w^out Bayle and Maynepryse; and at the yeres ende shall in soome open Market Towne in the fulnesse of the Market on the Market Daye have his lefte hande cut of and that to be nayled up in the openest place of suche Market: And that everye person or persons eftsoones offending against this Statute shalbe adjudged a felon and shall suffer deathe as in cases of felonye.

Provyded allwayes, That this Acte shall not extende to any Corrupcion of Blood or be prejudiciall or hurtful! to any Woman claimyng Dowre by or from any suche Offender or Offenders; Any thing in thys Acte to the contrary notw^standing.

And bee it further enacted by the aucthoritie aforesayd, That the Justices of Oyer and Termyner Justices of Gayle Deliverye and Justices of Peace in every Countie and Shire w"*in this Realme of England and Wales and other the Quenes Ma"" Dominyons, shall have full power and aucthoritie by vertue of this Acte, to enquire of every Offender and Offenders contrary to the Fourme and Effect of this Act, and to here and determyne every Offence and Offences comytted perpetrated and done contrary to the Fourme and Effect of the same, according to the course of the Lawes of this Realme.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte to take awaye the benefitte of Clargye from certen feloniouse Offendors.

WHERE a certayne kynde of evill disposed persons comonly called Cutpurses or Pyckpurses, but in deede by the Lawes of this Lande very Eellons and Theeves, doo confeder togethers making among themselves as it were a Brotherhed or Fraternitie of an Arte or Mysterie, to lyve idellye by the secrete Spoyle of the good and true Subjectes of this Realme, and aswell at Sermons and Prechyngf of the Woorde of God, and in places and tyme of doing fvice and common Prayer in Churches Chappelles Closettes and Oratories, and not only there but also in the Princes Palace House, yea and presence, and at the Places and Courtes of Justice, and at the tymes of Mynystracion of the Lawes in the same, and in Fayres Markettf and other Assemblies of People, yea and at the tyme of doing of Execucion of suche as ben attaynted of anye Murder Felonye or other crimynall Cause ordeined chieflye for Terrour and Example of evill doers, do wthout respect or regarde of anye tyme place or person, or anye feare or dreade of God, or any Lawe or Punyshment, under the cloke of Honestie, by their owtwarde Apparell Countenance and Behaviour subdltie privilye craftelye and felonyously take the Goodes of dyvers good and honest Subjects from their persons by cutting and pycking their Purses and other felonious Slaightes and Devices, to the utter undoing and impoverishment of many: Bee it therefore enacted by the aucthorite of this present Parliament, That no person or persons wch hereafter shall happen to be indyted or appealed for fellonious takinge of any Money Goodes or Cattelies from the person of any other privylye w^out his Knowledge in anye place whatsoe9, and thereuppon founde gyltie by verdyte of Twelve Men, or shall confesse the same upon his or their Ariaignement, or will not aunswere directly to the same according to the Lawes of this Realme, or shall stande wilfully or of malyce or obstinately muet, or chalenge peremptorye above the number of Twentye, or shall be upon such Indytement or Appeale outlawed, shall from hensforthe be admytted to have the benefyte of his or their Cleargie, but utterly be excluded therof, and shall suffer Death in suche maner and fourme as they shoulde if they were no Clarkes.

And Where also as dyvers persons done [oftentymes1 ] corny t and doo dyvers and sundry detestable Murde's hey nous Robberies and Felonyes and other capitall Offences, for the w* Cleargie is not allowable by the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme, and after the same Offences so done, eyther flee out of the Countie or other partes of this Realme into the partes beyonde the Seas, or kepe themselves secrete in other places where they are not knowen for a greate tyme, and after happen to comytt soome other Felonye, for the wch they maye have their Cleargie, and being arraigned for the same have their Cleargie to them allowed, and thereupon comytted to the Custodye of the Ordinarye according to the Lawe and Custome of this Realme, the former Offence wherein Cleargie is not grauntable being not then knowen ; and so by that meanes cannot after be impeached for the sayd other horrible and great Offences by the Lawe and Customes of thys Realme, to the great encouraging of Offendours, using suche practyses of Foreknowlege and set Purpose for their dyscharge of the same : For Reformacion whereof bee it further enacted by the aucthoritie aforesayd. That every person and persons wch shall hereafter upon his and their Arraignement for anye Felonye be admytted to the benefit of hys Cleargie by the Lawes of this Realme, and delyvered to the Ordinarie for the same, and shall make his due purgacion for the same Offence or Offences, whereupon he was so admytted to his Cleargie, and shall before the same Admyssion to his Cleargie have comytted any other suche Offence, whereupon Cleargie by the Lawes or Statutes of this Realme is not allowable, and not being thereof before indyted and acquyted convicted or attainted or pardoned, shall and maye be indyted or appealed for the same, and thereupon put to aunswere, and ordered and used in all Thinges according to the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme in such and lyke maner and forme as though uo such Admission of Cleargie had ben: Any Lawe Custome or Usage to the contrary notwithstanding.

CHAPTER V.

An Acte for thabridgement of Appeales in Suites of Cyvill and Maryne Causes.

Definitive Sentence* on Appeal* in Civil and Marine Caute*, by Delegates thereto commiuioned, declared final.

FOR the avoidyng aswell of long and tedious Suites as also of great Charges and Expences in prosecuting of Civile and Marine Causes, by reason of dyvers Appeales permytted to bee made by order of the Lawes Civill in suche Causes, and to thintent that aswell Straungers as also others the Subjects of this Realme, that shall have Cause of Suite in those Matters, maye have suche Expedition in the same as their Natures and Qualities doe requyre: Bee it enacted by the Queenes Mati* our Sov’aigne Ladie the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Commons in this present Parliament assembled and by the aucthoritie of the same. That from the last daye of this present Session of Parlyament, all and everie suche Judgment and Sentence diffinytyve as shalbe gevin or pronounced in anye Civile and Marine Cause upon Appeale lawfully to be made therein to the Queenes Ma"' in her Highnes Court of Chauncery, by suche Comyssioners or Delegates as shalbe nomynated and appointed by her Ma* her heyres or successours, by Comyssion under the Half Seale as it hath ben heretofore used in such Cases shall be finall, and no further Appeale to be had or made from the sayd Judgement or Sentence diffinytyve, or from the sayd Comyssioners or Delegates for or in the same; Any Lawe Usage or Custome to the contrary notwithstanding.

FOR the better Employment and Reliefe of greate multitudes of the Queenes Ma'1" Subjects using the Arte and Labour of Clothe woorking, It maye please the Queenes moost Excellent Ma* at the moost humble suite of her sayd Subjects that it bee enacted, and bee it enacted by the aucthoritye of thys present Parliament, That from hensfourth for everye nyne Clothes unwrought hereafter to be shypped or carryed into any the partes beyonde the Seas contrary to the fourme of any Statute heretofore made and nowe remayning in strength, by force of anye License hereafter to be graunted, the partie that shall shipp or carry over the same, shall shippe and carry over also one lyke woollyn Clothe of lyke sorte length bredthe and goodnes reddye wrowght and dressed, That is to saye, rowed barbed first coursed and shorne from the one ende to the other, so that everye tenthe Clothe passing over the Seas in forme aforesayd, maye and shall be dressed w,hin this Realme before the same shalbe shipped or transported over, uppon payne to forfayte for everie suche nyne Clothes so to be shipped or transported contrarye to the meanyng of this Acte, Tene poundes: Provided alwaye, That everye such tenth Clothe so to be transported reddy wrowght, shall not bee accompted anye of the Clothes permytted to be transported by force of suche Licence, but that suche person as shall have suche Licence maye transporte according to suche Licence, the full number of Clothes unwrowght mencyoned in the same Licence, over and above the number of suche tenth Clothes w*" they shall bee compelled to shyppe and carrye over by force of this Statute.

CHAPTER X.

An Acte for Bowyers and the pryces of Bowes.

MOOST humbly complainyng sheweth unto yo' Highnes and to yo' High Courte of Parlyament, yo' obedient Subjectes the Bowyers dwelling and inhabityng wuin the Citie of London and the Suburbes of the same; That where in the Parlyament of the late Kyng of moost famous memorye Kyng Henry the Eight, begune and holden at Westmynster the xvj"1 daye of January in the xxxiij,h yere of the Raigne of the sayd late Kyng, and there continewed untill the first daye of Aprill then next following, there was one Acte and Statute then made and provided intituled, An Acte for the Mayntenaunce of Artyllerie and debarring of unlawfull Games; in w* Acte and Statute araongest other Things there is one Braunche conteined and specyfied, the Tenour whereof is as heereafter followeth, That is to saye ; And to thintent that everie person maye have Bowes of meane pryce, bee it enacted by the aucthoritie aforesayd, that everie Bowier dwelling out of the Citie of Londo shall after the Feast of the PuryficacSn of our Ladie then pext comyng, for everie Bowe that he maketh of Ewe, make three other Bowes meete to shote in of Elme Wichsasell Asshe and other Woodde apte for the same, under the payne to lose and forfaite for ePy suche Bowe so lackyng. CHAPTER XI.

An Acte for true makinge of Hattes and Cappes.

WHERE greate multytudes of the Queenes Ma,k* true Subjects using the Arte of makyng [of1] Wollen Caps, are impoverished and decayed by the excessyve use of Hattes and Feltes, and thereby dyvers good Cities and Townes browght to desolation, great plentie of straunge Comodyties w^out necessitie consumed, and greate number of people enforced to depende upon the having of foraine Woolles, to the discomoditie of this Realme the disfumyture of Service to be done to the Queenes Mau' and greater evident Daungers, if Remedy be not provided: It maye therefore please the Queenes moost Excellent Ma‘" at the lamentable Suite and Complaynt of her sayd poore Subjects that it be enacted by the aucthoritye of this present Pliament, That no person by hym or herself or by any other, shall after the Feast of the Nativity of S' John Baptist next comyng make or worke any Felte or Hatte of or w,h any forraine Wooll or Stuife, unlesse suche person shall fyrst have ben Apprentice or Covenaunt Servaunt to suche Mysterie of Felt or Hatte making by the space of sevin yeres at the least, upon payne to forfayte all suche Hattes or Feltes as he shall make or cause to be made whyle he woorketh contrary to the fourme of this Acte, and fyve poundes in money for everie moneth that he shall so continewe.

And bee it enacted by the aucthoritie aforesayd, That from the fyrst daye of Aprill next comyng, no person whatsoever shall make sell or cause to be made or solde, any Cappe or other thing of Felte, but onely Hattes ; nor shall make sell or cause to be made or solde any Cappe of any Wollen Cloth not knyt; And that no person after the said fyrst daye of Aprill shall die or cause to be dyed black, any Cappe w,h Barke or Swarfe, but only w*" Copperas and Gall or w,h [Wood and Madder : And (for the setting of many poore and impotent persons to woorke, and for the better making of Cappes,) That no person after the sayd first daye of Apryll shall thicke or full in any Myll, or cause to be thicked or fulled in any Myll, any Cappe untyll suche tyme as the same Cappe be first well scoured and closed upon the Banke and half thicked at the least in the Footestocke: And that no Man under the Degree of a Knight or of a Lordes soone, shall after the sayd fyrst daye of Aprill, weare any Hatte or upper Cappe of Velvet or covered w,h Velvet, on payne to forfayte for everie Hatte Cappe or other Thinge to be made dyed thycked fulled solde or wome contrary to the meanyng of this Acte Tenne shillingf, whereof the one moitye shalbe to the Queenes Ma,lc her heyres and successours, the other moitye to suche person then using the Feate of Capp making, as will sue for the same in any Courte of Recorde, wherein no Essoigne Protection or Wag1 of Lawe for the Defendaunt shalbe admytted or allowed.

And for the better and truer making of Cappes and Hattes wlhin this Realme j Bee it enacted by the auctority aforesayd. That it shalbe lefull to the Maister and Wardens of the Company of Haberdasshers w,hin the Citie of London and to their Successours for the tyme being, calling to them one of the Companye of the Cappers, and another of the makers of Hattes as often as neede shall require, w"*in the sayd Citie or w^in three myles of the same, to searche all and all maner of Cappers and makers of Hattes and the Offendours and Defaultes by them founde to correct and punyshe by Fines and otherwyse as in lyke cases they doo other Offendours and Defautes w^in the sayd Companye; And that it shalbe lefull to all Mayors Baylieffes and other Head Officers in all other Cities and Townes Corporate to doo the lyke.

Provided allway and be it enacted by the aucthoritye aforesayd, That every Hatmaker that is nowe a maker or worker of Hates and being a Housholder Apprentice Covenaunt fv*nt or Journeyman, shall or maye during suche persons naturall Lyfe, continewe making of Hattes and Feltes, albeit suche person were not bounden Apprentice to the same Arte for the space of sevin yeres.

An Acte for Thalnegers Fees in Lancasheire, and for lengthe bredthe and waighte of Cottons Frezees

and Rugges.

FORASMUCH as dyvers Clothyers inhabityng w,hin the Countie Palantine of Lancaster, seeking inordinatly their owne singuler Gaynes, have of late practized privilye to convey and carry awaye out of the sayd Countie, dyvers Cottons Fryzes and Rugges there made to be solde before suche tyme as the Queenes Aulneger of the sayd County hath fixed unto everie suche Cloth the Queenes Seale in that behalf appointed ; and soome tyme counterfayting and setting to suche their Clothes Seales of their owne, mynding thereby not only to defraude the sayde Aulneger of his accustomable Fees due to be payd to the Queenes Highnes use for the sealing of every suche Cloth Cotton Fryze or Rugge, but also to cover and hyde the untrue and deceiptfull making of many of the sayd Clothes, contrarie to the true meanyng of sundry good and wholsome Estatutes and Lawes heretofore made, aswell for the true making of the Clothes beforesayd, as also for the searching tryeng and sealing of the same, to the no lyttle Prejudyce and Damage of the sayd Aulneger who standeth charged w’" the payment of a great aiiuall Farme to the Queenes Ma* for the sayd Aulnege, in desceipt of her Highnes Subjects, and discredite of the Commoditie of the sayd Clothes: For Reformacyon whereof, be it enacted by our sayd Sov*aigne Ladie the Queene the Lordes Spyrituall and Temporall and the Comons in this present Pliament assembled and by the aucthoritie of the same. An Acte touchinge Sea markes and Maryners.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte touchinge transportinge of tawed Lether.

rORASMUCHE as in one Acte made in the first Session of this present Parliament, intituled An Act against the carrieng of Shepe Skynes and Peltes over the Sea, not being Staple Ware, there is conteyned one Braunche against the makyng of any Peltes by any person other then suche as are permytted to make the same by the sayd Statute, the Execution of wch Braunche hath ben put in suspence by reason that soome other Partes of the same Statute are supposed to be against the Entercourse of the Lowe Coontryes of the Kyng of Spayne; Bee it therefore declared and enacted by the aucthoritie of this present Pliament, That the sayd first Braunche of the sayd Statute being not against the sayd Entercourse shall from hensforthe be put in due Execucyon.

And forasmuche as great Multitudes of the Quenes Ma'" liege People have ben set on worke by converting of Sheepeskynnes and Lambe skynnes into tawed Leather and Parchement here w'bin this Realme, wrt by one other braunche of the sayd Statute is prohibited to be transported out of the Realme in Leather ; And where the convening of suche Skynnes into Leather and Parchment hath ben great Mayntenaunce of many Thowsandf of the Subjects of this Realme, and greater daily wyll be, to the great Benefyte of thys Realme, if the sayd first Braunche concerning making of Peltes be duely put in Execution, where otherwise yf the sayd Peltes shoulde be transported into other Realmes, the same wolde be an occasion of the impov'ishing of many of the naturall Englishe People of this Realme ; Bee it therefore enacted by aucthoritye of this present Parliament, That so muche of the sayd Statute as concemeth the transporting of tawed Leather to be made of Shypp skynnes and Lambe skynnes, shall from hensforthe as towching only the transporting of suche tawed Leather be repealed and voyde ; Any Thyng in the sayd Statute to the contrary notw^standing.

CHAPTER XV.

An Acte for p'servacon of Grayne.

THERE in the Parliament holden at Westmynster upon Prorogation, the Fourth Daye of February in the V V xxiiij’1 yere of the Raigne of the noble Prynce of famous Memorie Kyng Henry the Eight, amongest other [Thyngf and '] Acts one Estatute was made and provyded for the Destruction of Crowes Rookes and Chawghes; in w^ Estatute is conteyned one Braunche concemyng the Provision putting in ure and maynten'nce of Nettes and Shrapes, which Braunche being veiy good and beneficyall long tyme sythens was expyred ; Bee it therefore ordeyned and enacted by the Quene our Sovaigne Ladie, w,h the Assent of the Lordes Spyrituall and Temporall, and of the Comons in this present Pliament assembled, and by the aucthoritie of the same. That only the sayd Braunche of the same Estatute concernyng the Provision Use and Maynten*nce of Nettes and Shrapes for the Destruccyon of Crowes Rookes and Chawghes, and all and every Article Forfayture and Penaltie conteyned in the sayd Braunche for and concernyng the Provysion and putting in ure of the same Nettes, and for the Mayntenaunce thereof according to the fourme therein limytted, shall from hensfoorth be revived and put in due Execucion, and that all and every other [Braunche and Article *] conteyned in the same Estatute shalbe from hensfoorthe utterly repealed and made voyde to all Intentf and Purposes.

And further be it enacted by the aucthoritye aforesayd, That in everie Pisshe the Churchwa'dens for the tyme being, w,h others of the Pisshioners to the number of syx persons, to be required by the Churchewardens, shall after the Feast of S* Mychaell Tharchangell next coomyng yerely in one of the festivall Dayes in the Easter Weeke, and at e$y other tyme when and as often as it is and shalbe needeful, taxe and assesse everie Propriatour Farmour and other person having the Possession of any Lande or Tythes wlhin their severall Pishes, to paye suche soome of Money as they shall thinke meete, according to the Quantytie and Portion of suche Landes or Tythes as the same person so assessed do or shall have or holde; And if the sayd soomes of Money, or any of them so taxed and assessed be or shalbe denyed to be payde or be not payde w‘hin Fooretene Dayes next after the Request thereof made by the sayd Churchewardens or one of them, then everie person so denyeng or making suche Defaute of payment, shall forfaite for every tyme fyve shillingf; and the same, together w* the sayd soome or soomes assessed and taxed as is aforesayd, shalbe levied by Dystresse of the Goodes and Cattells of suche person and persons so assessed and refusing to paye suche soome to bee taken by the Churchewardens or one of them, wch Dystresse shalbe ordered and used in suche maner and fourme as Dystresses taken for Amercyamentf in any Letes; And the same soomes so taxed and assessed, and the sayd penaltyes, if any be so by them levyed as is aforesayd, shalbe yerely by the sayd Churchewardens for the tyme being or one of them of everie suche Pisshe delivered by Bill or Byllf indented to two honest and substanciall persons of everie suche Pisshe wc« shalbe elected and appointed by the sayd Churchewardens for the tyme being, to have the yerely distrybucion thereof, and shalbe named the distrybutours of the Provysion for the destruccyon of noyfull Fowles and Vermyn; And the sayd dystributours so appointed as is aforesayd, shall gyve and paye of the same Moneye so to them delyvW to everie person that shall bring to them any Heades of old Crowes Chawghes Pyes or Rookes taken w^in the sev’all Pisshes, for the Heades of ePy three of them a peny, and for the Heades of everie syxe young Crowes Chawghes Pyes or Rookes taken as is aforesayd a peny, and for everie syxe Egges of anye of them unbroken a peny, and lykewise for everye twelve Stares Heades a peny; All w* sayd Heades and Egges the sayd dystributours in soome convenyent place shall kepe, and shall everie moneth at the least bring foorth the same before the sayd Churchwardens and Taxours or three of them, and then and there to them shall make a true Accompt in Wrytyng what Money they have layde foorthe and payd for suche Heades and Egges and for the Heades of suche other [ravenyng3] Byrdes and Vermyn as are hereafter in thys Act mencioned, That is to saye; For everie Heade of Martyn Hawkes Fursekytte Moldkytte Busarde Schagge [Carmerat«] or Ryngtayle, two pence; and for every two Egges of them, one penny ; for everie Iron or Osprayes Head, sower pence; for the Head, of everie Woodwall Pye Jaye Raven or Kyte, one peny ; for the Head of everie Byrde which is called the Kyngf Fyssher, one peny; for the Head of everie Bulfynche or other Byrde that devoureth the blowth of Fruite, one peny; for the Heades of every Foxe or Gray, twelve pence; and for the Heade of everie Fitchewe Polcatte Wesell Stote Fayre bade or Wilde Catte, one peny; for the Heades of everie Otter or Hedgehogges, two pence; For the Heades of everie three Rattes or twelve Myse, one peny; for the Heades of everie Moldwarpe or Wante one halfpeny: For the Heades of everie w1*1 Byrdes and Vermyn last mencyoned, the sayd Dystributours shall likewise paye and gyve to the bringer of them for everie Heade kylde and taken wu,in their sev*all Pisshe as before is limyted, and shall kepe the same to be shewed foorthe upon their Accompt in maner and forme as is aforesayd; All wch said Heades and [Egges shalbe foorthwth after suche Accompte made, in the presence of the sayd Churchwardens and Taxours or of three of them, burned consumed or cut in sunder; And if upon any Accompte to be made in the ende and determynacion of the Office of any suche distrybutours it shall appeare that any soome of Money is remainyng in the Handes of the said dystributours or of any of them, then the same shalbe by Byll indented as is aforesayd delivered over to suche persons as be or shalbe elected to the same Office for the yere next following, by them to be distrybuted as is aforesaid.

And for the better execucion of this Acte, bee it also enacted by thaucthoritye aforesayd. That it maye and shalbe lawfull to and for everie person and persons w* hereafter will travell for the taking of Crowes Rookes Chawghes and other the Vermyn abovesayd, to enter for the same purpose and intent into any place therefore meete and convenient, w* the consent of the Owner or Occupier of the same, and there to use suche Nettes Engynnes and other resonable

CHAPTER XVI.

An Acte that in div'se Counties there shalbe but one Sheriffe in one Countye.

WHEREAS [in'] the Countyes and Shyres of Surrey and Sussex, Essex and Hertforde, Sofiset and Dorset,-Warwycke and Leycester, Nottyngham and Derbye, Oxon and Barfef, of long tyme have had but one Sheriffe to serve for two of the sayd Countyes, That is to saye, One for Surrey and Sussex, and one other for Essex and Hertford, and one other for SoSset and Dorset, and one other for Warwyche and Leycester, and one other for Nottingham and Derby, and one other for Oxon and Barkf ; The occasion whereof in the beginnyng, as it shoulde seeme, was for that everie of the sayd severall Countyes were not then so well inhabited w,h Gentlemen of good Abilitie to fve in the sayd Office as (Thankes be to God) they be at this present; And Forsomuche as the fvice and Charges of that Office of Sherifwyke of the sayd Counties is more then in tymes past it hath ben, and is nowe comonly greater then one Sheryffe is able to serve and supplie. Therefore suche Gentlemen as doo dwell in the sayd severall Counties are verie desirous to have for everie of the sayd Countyes one Sheriffe, to be yerely made and appointed for the same: And for that the having of severall Sheriffes accordingly cannot be hurtfiill to any, but thereby maye growe soome ease of Charges and Troble to suche as shall hereafter be appointed to suche Office, and also the sayd Office better served and executed then heretofore hath ben: Bee it therefore enacted by the aucthoritye of this pWit Parliament, That the Queenes moost Excellent Ma'1* her Heyres and Successors Kyngf or Queenes of this Realme, shall and maye, from and after the fyrst daye of November wck shalbe in the yere of our Lorde God a thousand fyve hundred threescore and seven, yerely chose and make for every of the sayd Counties before named, one sufficyent and able person to be Sheryffe of the same, in suche lyke maner and forme as is and hath ben used to be chosen made and done for any other Countie or Shire w"'in thys Realme; Any Lawe Custome or Usage heretofore had or used to the contrarie thereof notw"standing: And that everie person w" after the sayd fyrst daye of November shalbe made and appointed Sheryffe for any of the sayd Countyes shalbe accomptable and used in the Order of his Accompte and all other things and Allowance to hym to be made in the Courte of Exchequer and all other Courtes and Places, in suche maner and form as is commonly used for Shreiffes in lyke Cases.

Provided allwayes and be it further enacted by the aucthoritie aforesayd, That the Barons of the Queenes Highnes her Heyres and Successours of the Courte of the Exchequer for the tyme being, calling unto them aswell her or their Graces Officers of Remembrauncer and the Treasourers Remembrauncer together w"1 the Clark of the Pype of the same Courte, as also the severall Sheryffes the w* next after the sayd fyrst daye of November shalbe by her Highnes her Heires and Successours constituted named and appointed, of e9y of the sayd sev*all Counties of Surrey and Sussex, Essex and Hertforde, SoiSset and Dorset, Warwycke and Leycester, Nottingham and Derby, Oxon and Barkes, shall have by vertue of this Act of Parliament full power and aucthoritye to sever and devide, by the discrecion and judgement of the sayd Barons, all and singter the proffers of the sayd Countyes of Surrey and Sussex, Essex and Hertforde, Soifiset and Dorset, Warwyck and Leycester, Nottingham and Derby, Oxon and Barkf: The w* sayd severance and Devision of the sayd proffers shalbe entred of Recorde in the sayd Courte of Exchequer, and shalbe fynall and perpetual), during so long tyme as this present Acte of Parliament shall endure and have continewance.

There shall be one Sheriff for each of certain Countiea named ; where formerly one Sheriff served for Two such Counties.

Provided alwayes and be it further enacted by the aucthoritye aforesayd, That no Sheriffe, hereafter to be chosen and made of any one of the sayd Coundes in this Acte mencyoned, shall paye in any Courte of Recorde for any dude belonging properly to the Office of Sherieff, any other Fees or Charges then only the one half of the Charges and Fees wck he should be compelled to have payd, if he had ben Sheriffe of two of the sayd Shyres and Counties, as before the making of this Acte was used ; Any Lawe Usage or Custome to the contrarie notwithstanding.

This Acte to continewe and endure unto the ende of Three whole yeres, to be accompted from the Feast of All Saynctf, in the yere of our Lord God a thousand fyve hundred threescore and seaven; and from thence to the ende of the nexte Parliament then next following the ende of the sayd three yeres.

CHAPTER XVII. (')

An Acte for Confirmafon of a Subsedie graunted by the Clergye.

Grant of Subsidy by the Clergy of the Province of Canterbury:

WHEARE the Prelates and C.largie of the Provynce of Cantorbury have lovingly and lyberally for certeyn Consideracbns, given and gr*unted to the Queenes Ma" a Subsedye of Fowre shillingf of the pownde, to be taken and levyed of all and singuler there Promotyons Spuall within the same Provynce during the terme of Three yeeres nowe next ensewing, in soch certeyn manner and forme and with soch Exceptyons and Provisyons as bee specyfied and conteyned in a certeyn Instrument by them therof made and delyvered to the Queenes Highnes under the Seale of the moste Reverend Father in God Mathew now Arcliebusshop of Cantorburye and Primate of all England ; Which Instrument is now exhibited in this present Parlament to bee ratefyed; the tenor wherof enseweth in these wordes:

Tenor of the said Grant:

Subsidy of 4s. in the Pound on all Spiritual Promotions, as valued to the King’s Tenth under 26 H.VIII. c.3.

The Prelates and Clargyb of the Provynce of Cantorburye, being lawfully congregated and assembled togither in a Convocacon or Synode, calling to their remembr*unce the greate and manifolde Benefictf which they have manny and sondry Wayes receyved of your Ma'f moste gracyous Bountifulnes, princypally for the setting furth and advancing of Goddes holy Woorde, his syncere and trewe Relygion, and abolishing all forain powre, contrary to the same; Considering also the greate Debts wherewith the Imperyall Crowne of this Realme was charged, when yt pleased Allmighty God fyrst to call yor Highnes to the Govern*nce of the same: And further, waying the greate Charges wherewith yo' Ma,ie bothe hathe been and ys lyke to be burthened hereafter, for the defending and prefving your Highnes Realme and naturall Subgectf in Christyan Peace Tranquiletye and Safetye: In Consideuac&n therof and for a trewe dedaracion of our bounden dewtyes good Hartes and Myndes towardes yor Ma", with one uniforme Agreement Accorde and Consent together with moste harty good wyll, have geven and gr*unted and by thies Presents doo give and gr*unte to yor Highnes yo' heyres and successors. CHAPTER XIX. (')

An Acte of the Quenes Ma'f Free and GeSall Pardon.

THE Quenes moste Excellent Majestye consyderyng the greate zeale and affeccftn wch her lovynge and obedyent Subjectes beare to her Highnes, as by manye wayes they have declared and shewed from tyme to tyme sythens the begynnyng of her Majesties Reigne, and callynge to her most gracyous Remembrans into howe many Pennalties and Daungers of her Maj’f Lawes sundrye of her seide lovynge Subjectes be fallen, and covetyngc rather theyre Amendementes by gentill and mercyfull Meanes then w"‘ severe Execucon of her Heighnes Lawes, to be enryched by theyre evyll Deades and Offences, and trustynge assuredly that her seide lovynge Subjectes wyll contynue in theyre due Obediens and lovynge Hartes towardes her Majestye, and that they from hensforth wyll endevor theymselfes as obedyent Subjectes to lyve accordynge to her Heighnes Lawes; her Majestye ys therefore mercyfully enclyned and moved to graunte and geve unto her seide lovynge Subjectes a generall free and benefycyall Pdon, and thereby to dely9 her seyde Subjectes from suche Daungers Pennalties and Forfaytures as throughe theyre Offences they have justely des'ved ; CHAPTER XX.

An Acte for the Repeale of a Braunche of a Statute made An0 16 H. 8. touchinge Tryall of Offences in the Countie of Merioneth in North Wales.

Recital of Stat.

36 H.VIII. c. 6. f 6, io, aa to Trial of Offence* committed in the Marchea of Wale*, or in Merioneth.

35 H.VIIL c. 6. §33. a* to Merioneth.

26 H.VIII. c.6. i 10. aa to Merioneth, repealed.

WHERE in the Pliament holden at Westm in the xxvjUl yere of the Reigne of the late Kyng Henry the Eighte, amongest other Thyngf it was enacted, That all Murders Robberyes Felonyes and other felonious Offences w'h shoulde from that tyme be comytted in any Lordships Marchers or other Place in Walles, might be inquyred of harde tryed and examoned in the next Englisshe Shire therunto adjoinynge; and also by one other Braunche conteyned in the Statute it is ordeyned, that suche of the same Offences as shoulde be comytted w*n the Countie of Meryoiith, one of the Three olde Shyres of North Walles, might at the Dyscrecion of the Justices there, be inquyred of harde tryed and determyned in the Countyes of Anglesey and Caernarvon, being Two other Counties of North Walles; as by the same Acte more plainly dothe appeare; And yet neverthelesse in the Pliament holden at Westm in the xxxiiij,h and xxxv,h yere of the Raigne of the sayd late Kyng Henry Theight, by one Acte and Statute there made towching certain Ordin*ncf in Walles, it is by one Braunche thereof amongf other Thinges enacted and establysshed, that all Offencf Murders Robberies and other Felonyes w* from hensfoorthe shoulde be comitted in the sayd Countye of Merioneth, shoulde and myght be inquired of harde and determyned before the Justices wUlin the sayd Countie of Meryonethe, or ells in the Countie of Salopp being the next Englishe Countie adjoinyng therunto, in such maner and forme as the lyke Offences comytted in other the sayd Countyes in Walles shoulde or might be inquyred of harde and determyned; as by the sayd Acte more at lardge doothe appeare: By reason of wch sayd severall Braunches conteyned in the said severall Statutes, the sayd County of Meryoneth standethe now not only chargeable to such lyke Tryall, in the next Englishe Sheire, for the sayd Offences as other Countyes of Walles at thys present bee, but also by force of the sayd Estatute made in the sayd xxvj"' year of the sayd Kyng Henry the Eighte, the sayd County of Meryoneth is also subject to suche Inquirye and Tryall to be hadde wll,in the sayd Counties of Caemvon and Anglesey, being boothe Welshe Shyres; muche to the descredytte of the Inhabytauntf of the sayd Countie of Merioneth, for that no other Countye of Walles for suche Offencf are chargeable w,h the lyke Tryall: Wherefore be it enacted by the aucthoritie of this present Pliament, That so muche of the sayd Acte and Statute made in the said xxvj"1 yere of the Raigne of the said late King Henry the viijUl, as doothe limytte or appoint any of the sayd Offences before mencyoned comitted w^in the sayd County of Meryonethe, to be inquired of tryed harde and determyned w'"in the said Countyes of Carnivon and Anglesey, or eyther of them, shall from hensfoorth be utterly repealed voyde and of none Effecte.

Imagining the Death or Bodily Harm of the Queen, or the deposing her, or the levying War, or exciting Foreigners to invade the Realm, and declaring the same by Printing or by Words, or advisedly denying the Queen's Title, or affirming her to be a Heretic or Usurper, 4cc. declared High Treason;

CHAPTER I.

An Acte whereby certayne Offences bee made Treason.

FORASMUCH AS it is of some doubted, whether the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme, remayning at this present in force, are vayleable and suffyeient anough for the suerde and pservacion of the Quenes moste Royall Pson, in whom consisteth all the Happines and Comforte of the whole State and Subjectes of the Realme, w"1 thing all faithfull lovynge and duetyfull Subjectes ought and will w"* all carefoll studie & zeale consider foresee and pvyde for; by the neglecting and passing over whereof wlh wynking eies, there might happen to growe the subvertion and ruyne of the quyet and moste happy State and present Government of this Realme, (wcb God defend:) Therefore at the humble Suite and Pericion of the Lords and Comens in thys present Parliament assembled, Bee yt enacted declared and established by aucthoritie of the same Parliament, That yf any person or persons whatsoever, at any tyme after the laste daye of June next cominynge duryng the naturall Lyfe of or moste gracious Sovereigne Ladye Quene Elizabeth (whome Almightey God preserve & blesse w* longe and prosperous Raigne over this Realme) shall w,hin the Realme or w'foute, compasse imagyn invent devyse or intend the Deathe or Destruccon or any bodely harme tending to Death Destruccon Mayme or Wounding of the Royall Pson of the same our Sov'aigne Ladye Queene Elizabeth; Provyded alwayes, That this Acte or any thing in the same contaigned shall, shall in no maner of wyse extend or be deemed or taken hereafter to extend to the Right Honorable the Lady Jane Duches of Feria, nowe being in Spayne, Daughter unto S' William Dormer Knight, nor unto the Lady Jane Dormer Wydowe Graundmother unto the said Duchesse; Any Thing in this Acte to the contrary in any wyse notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER Vin.

An Acte against Usurie.

WHEREAS in the Parliament holden the seven and thyrtey yere of the Raigne of our late Soveraigne Lord Kyng Henrye the Eight of famos Memory, there was then made and established one good Act for the Reformation of Usurie; by which Act the Vice of Usurie was well repressed, and specially the corrupt Chevisaunce and bargaynyng by way of Sale of Wares and Shiftes of Interest; And where synce that tyme by one other Acte made in the syst & sixe yeres of the Raigne of our late Sov^aine Lord Kynge Edward the Syxte the said former Acte was repelled, and newe Provisoes for repressing of Usurie devised and enacted; wd> said latter Acte hathe not done so muche good as was hoped it shoulde, but rather the said Vyce of Usurye, and specially by waye of Sale of Wares and Shiites of [Interest'] hathe much more excedingly abounded, to the utter undoinge of many Gentlemen Marchauntes Occupiers and other, and to the importable Hurte of the Comon wealth, aswell for that in the said latter Acte there is no pvysion against such corrupt Shyftes and Sales of Wares, as also for that there is no dyfference of payne forfayture or punyshement uppon the greater or lesser exactions and oppressions by reason of Lones upon Usurie: Bee yt therefore enacted, That the said latter Statute made in the fyfte and syxe yeres of the Raigne of Kyng Edward the Syxte, and every Braunch and Article of the same, from and after the fyve and twenty daye of June next comming, shalbe utterly abrogated repelled and made voyde; and that the sayd Acte made in the said seven and thyrtey yere of Kyng Henry the Eight, from and after the said fyve and twentey daye of June next commyng, shalbe revived and stand in full Force Strengh and Effecte.

And bee yt further enacted, That all Bondes Comrades and Assuraunces, collateral! or other, to be made for payment of any Principall or Mony to be lent, or Covenaunt to be pformed upon or for anye Usurye in lendynge or doyng of any Thinge agaynste the said Acte nowe revyved, upon or by w"* Loane or Doinge there shalbe reserved or taken above the Rate of Tenne Pounds for the Hundred for one yere, shalbe utterly voyde.

And bee yt further enacted, That all Brokers Solicitors and Drivers of Bargaynes for Contractes or other Doinges against the said Statute nowe revyved, whereupon shalbe reserved or taken more then after the Rate of Tenne Poundes for the Loane of a Hundred Poundes for a yere, shalbe to all Intentes and Purposes judged punyshed and used as Counsellors Atturneys or Advocates in any case of Premunire.

And forasmuch as all Usurie being forbydden by the Lawe of God is synne and detestable; Bee it enacted, That all Usurie Loane and forbearing of Monye, or gevyng Dayes for forbearing of Monye by way of Loane Chevysaunce Shyftes Sale of Wares Contracte or other Doynges whatsoever for Gayne mentioned in the said Statute w* is now revyved, whereuppon is not reserved or taken or covenaunted to be reserved payde or geven to the Lender Contracter Shyfter Forbearer or Deliverer above the Summe of Tenne Poundes for the Loane or Forbearinge of a Hundred Poundes for one yere, or after that Rate for a more or lesser summe or tyme, shalbe from the fyve and twentey daye of June next coming, punished in fourme folowinge, that is to saye; That every suche OfFendor against this Braunche of this present Statute shall forfayte so muche as shalbe reserved by way of Usurie above the Principall for any Money so to be lent or forborne; All such Forfaytures to be recovered and imployed as is lymited for Forfaytures by the saide former Statute nowe revyved.

And bee it further enacted, That Justices of Oyer and Terminer and Justices of Assise in theyr Circuites, Justices of Peace in theyr Sessions Maiors Sheryffes and Bayliffes of Cyties, shall also have full Powre Sc Aucthorytie to enquyre heare and determyne of all and singul' Offences commytted against the sayd Statute now revyved.

And be yt further enacted, That the sayde Statute nowe revyved shalbe most largely and strongly construed for the repressing of Usurie, and against all psons that shall offend agaynste the true meaning of the said Statute by any Way or Devyce dyrectly or indyrectly.

Provyded alway. That this Statute doth not extend nor shalbe expounded to extend unto any Allowaunces or Paymentes for the finding of Orphanes accordinge to the auncient Rates or Customes of the Citie of London or any other Citie where lyke Order is for the Custodye of Orphanes and theyr Goodes, as is in the said Citye of London.

CHAPTER X.

An Acte against Fraudes, defeating Remedies for Dilapidations, &c.

WHERE dyvers and sundry Ecclesiasticall Psons of this Realme being endowed and possessed of auncient Palaces Mansion Houses and other Edyfices and Buildynges belonging to theyr Ecclesiasticall Benefyces or Lyvinges have of late yeres not onely suffered the same for want of due reperations partly to run to greate ruine and decay and in some part utterly fall downe to the Ground, converting the Tymber Leade and Stones to theyr owne Benefyte and C5mod ytye, but also have made Deedes of Gyfte & coulourable Alienations & other Conveyaunces of lyke Effect of theyr Goodes and Chattelles in theyr Lyves tyme, to Thintent and of Purpose after theyr Deathes to defeate and defraude theyr Successors of suche just Actions & Remedies as otherwyse they might and should have had for the same against theyr Executors or Administratours of theyr Goodes by the Lawes Ecclesiasticall of thys Realme, to the great defacing of the state Ecclesiasticall & intollerable Charges of theyr Successors and evyl President and Example for others, if spedye Remedie be not pvyded : Bee yt therefore enacted by the Queenes most Excellent Ma'" the Lordes Spyrituall and Temporall and the Comons in this present Parliament assembled & by thaucthoride of the same, That yf anye Archbysshop Bysshop Deane Archedeacon Provost Treasorer Chaunter Chaunceller Prebendary or any other havyng any Dygnitie or Offyce in any Cathedrall or Collegiate Church w'hin this Realme; Or yf any Parson Vycar or other Incumbent of any Ecclesiasdcall Lyvyng whereunto do belong any House or Houses or other Buildinges wch by Lawe or Custome he is bounde to keepe and maynteyne in reparation, do from henceforth make any Deede or Deedes of Gyft or Alienadon or other lyke Conveyaunces of his moveable Goodes or Chattelles to Thintent & Purpose aforesayd, That then the Successour and Successours of hym that shall make suche Deede or Deedes of Gyft or Alienation, shall and maye commence Suite and have such Remedye in any Court Ecclesiasdcall of thys Realme competent for the Matter against him or them to whome such Deede or Deedes of Gyfte or Alienadon shalbe so made, for the Amendment & Reperation of so much of the sayd Dilapidations and Decayes or just Recompence for the same as hath happened by hys Facte or Default in such sort as he might should or ought lawfully to have yf he or they to whom such Deede or Deedes of Gyft or Alienation shalbe so made, were Executour or Executours of the Testament and last Wyll of hym that made suche Deede or Deedes of Gyft or Alienation or were Administratour or Administratours of his Goodes or Chattels; Any Law Custome or other Thing to the contrary in any wyse notwithstanding.

CHAPTER XI.

An Acte for the Mayntenaunce of the Navygation.

WHERE at the Parliament holden at Westni in the fyfth yere of your Ma*? Raigne, there was among other made and pvided an Act touching certayne polityke Constitutions made for the Maynten*nce of the Navie, and in the same amongst other Thinges it was enacted, That from the fyrst daye of Aprill in the yere of our Lord God a thowsand fyve hundrede threescore and foure, and so from thencefoorth, it should be lawfull to all and everye the Subjectes of your MaB% your Heyres and Successors, at his and theyr Wyll and Pleasure, to carry and transport out of this Realme in theyr Shippes and other Vessells of any the Subjectes aforesaid, all and every kynd of Hearing and other Sea Fyshe to be taken upon the Sea by any the Subjectes aforesaid ; any Acte of Parlyament or Lawe to the contrary notwithstanding: And that al and every pson and psons wch should by vertue of that Acte transporte or carry any Hearing or Sea Fyshe from out of any Port or Harborowe of this Realme to any place out of the Domynions of your Ma1' your Heyres and Successors, should be free from Payment of any Custome Subsidie or Pondage Monye for the same Fyshe so carryed or transported duryng the space of Foure whole yeres, beginning at the saide fyrst day of Aprill 1564, and so further during your Mu1? Pleasure; »* tearme of Foure yeres is nowe expired and ended: And where it is by experience found that the said Act hath ben a very good Act, and greatly encreased the Navy and Fyshermen, and causeth many poore Men to be set a worke, and is in greate lykelyhood dayly to increase the same more and more: It maye please your most excellent Mall* of your aboundant Grace that it maye be enacted by aucthoritie of this present Parlyament, That so much of the said Act as ys above recited for Lybertie of transporting of Hearyng and Sea Fyshe by the naturally borne Subject? of your Ma"* your Heires or Successors, and for freedome from paying of any Custome Subsidye or Pondage Money shalbe revyved, and shall from henceforth continue for the Space of Syxe yeres from thend of this Session of Parlyament, and from thenceforth to thend of the next Parlyament after the said Syxe yeres to be summoned, and from thenceforth during yor Ma‘? most gracious Pleasure; so that such transporting be in Vessels w* crosse Sayles.

And where also in the said Act made in the said fyfth yere, amongst other Thynges, al maner of persons are generally forbydden to bring into this Realm any Coddes or Lynges in Barrels or other Caskes, upon payne of forfayture of all the Coddes and Lynges so to be brought in or the value thereof contrary to the Tenour of that Act: Forasmuch as by that Braunch of the saide Statute, it was well intended and ment to meet w,h the Fraude of Strangers and other weh brought into this Realme great quantyty of Coddes and Lynges deceiptfully packed in Barrels, and not meant to hynder any the Queenes Ma‘? Subjectes using upryghtnes k trueth in the barrelling of such Fishe; Maye it therefore please your Ma"' that it be further enacted by thaucthoritie aforesaid, That after the Feast of Easter, wch shalbe in the yere of our Lord God a thowsand fyve hundred seventye fyve, it shall be lawfull from thenceforth to all yo’ Ma1? loving Subjectes borne w'Nn this Realme or w,bin any other yo' Ma'? V.

No foreign-taken Fish shall be dried for Sale in England.

And for the avoyding of the lewde Outrages comytted and doone uppon the Sea Coastes of Norfolke and Suffolke, by the Catches Mongers and Picardes pretendyng to buy fressh Herrynges, and w* do cut in sunder dyvers Peeces of Fyshermens Nettes traveling the Hyghe Seas to take fresh Hearringes, to the utter undoing of the said poore Fyshermen; Bee it therefore enacted ordeyned and established by thaucthorytye of this present Parlyament, That no pson or psons using any Ship Boate or Vessell called Catche Monger or Picarde, or other Vessell of lyke use, shall in the tyme of comon Fysshing upon the saide Sea Coastf of Norffolke and Suffolke, betwene the fouretene daye of September and the fouretene daye of November, firon Sonne setting to sonne Rysing, ancker upon the mayne Sea or in the comon Streame or Trade of Fyshing where the Fyshermen use to dryve, uppon payne to forfaite theyr Catch Monger Pycker or Vessel, wlh the Tackle and al the Fysh in the same, or the value thereof; Thon half to your Ma°' your Heyres and Successors, the other halfe to the Bayliffes Burgeses and Commynalde of the Towne of Greate Yarmouth, to be imployed to the recompencyng his Damages to the ptye whose Nettes shall so be cut, and to the building and repayring of the decayed Haven there, and to be taken by waye of Seasure or otherwyse, to be recovered by Byll Action or Information in any of your Ma’f Courtes of Record ; Any Statute Lawe or Usage to the contrary notwithstanding.

And where yo' Subjectes using the Trade of fyshing for Hearting have of many yeres, and tyme out of mynde used to packe theyr Hearring in Caske [of'] Barrels conteyning aboute thyrtey two Gallons of usuall Wyne Measure, and with such Assise hath ben usually gaged and alowed at your honorable C.ytye of London, and do conteyne the said Measure of xxxij Gallons, according to suche usuall Brasse Measure as is out of your honourable Court of Exchequer delyvered to your said honorable Citie of London ; w1*1 Measure yet hath lately ben quarrelled at by c?tayne Infourmers, for that the same conteyne not two and thyrtey Gallons by the old Measure of Standerd, w* they never did, though padventure thextremitie of old Statutes in Wordes by some Mens construction might be stretched to requyre so muche; And for that the usual Barrels nowe be as great as ever w"in the tyme of any memory they have ben knowne to be, and the Alteration thereof woulde be a great Decay and Prill of undoing to the saide Fysshermen; It maye also please your most Excellent Ma'* that it be also ennacted and declared, That the sayde Assise of thyrtey two Gallons of Wyne Measure, wd‘ is about eight and twentey Gallons by olde Standerd well packed, and conteyning in every Barrel usually a thousande full Hearringes at the leaste, is and shalbe taken for good true and lawfull Assise of Hearring Barrels, throughout the whole Liberty of the said Towne of Greate Yarmouth and els where; Any auncient or former Lawe or Statute to the contrary notwithstandynge.

Bee yt further enacted, That no Fyshe hereafter to be taken or brought into this Realme by any Straunger, nor any Fyshe comonly called Scottishe Fishe or Flemish Fishe shalbe dryed w,hin England to be solde, upon payne of forfayture of all such Fysh to be dryed contrary to the meaning of this Act, or the value thereof; wch forfeyture shalbe to such pson dwelling at any Towne where is any Port Peere or Haven, as wyll sease the same Fish or will sue for the same value in any Court of Record, to be imployed to the Reparation and Mayntenaunce of suche Porte Peere or Haven as is next to the Place where the Offence shalbe comytted.

All Prints, haring been conGecrated &c. otherwise than in the Form authorized, temp. Edw.VI. or Eliz. shall subscribe, &c. certain Articles of Religion agreed on in Convocation in 1562, on Pain of Deprivation.

An Act to refourme certayne Dysorders touching Ministers of the Churche.

THAT the Churches of the Queenes Malf Domynyons maye be served w,h Pastors of sounde Religyon, Be it enacted by thaucthoritie of thys present Parlyament, That every pson under the degree of a Bysshop w1" doth or shall pretend to be a Priest or Minister of Godes holy Word and Sacraments, by reason of any other fourme of Institution Consecration or Orderyng then the fourme set forth by Parlyament in the tyme of the late Kinge of most worthye Memorie Kynge Edwarde the Syxt, or nowe used in the Raigne of our most gracious Soveraygne Ladye, before the Feast of the Natyvitie of Christ next folowing shal in the presence of the Bysshop or Gardian of the Spyritualties of some one Diocesse where he hath or shal have Ecclesiastical Lyving, declare his Assent and subscribe to all the Artycles of Religion wch onely conceme the Confession of the true Christian Faithe and the Doctrine of the Sacramentf, comprised in a Booke imprinted entituled, Articles whereupon it was agreed by the Archbisshops and Bishops of both Provinces, and the whole Cleargie in the Convocation holden at London in the yere of our Lorde God a thousande five hundred six tie and two, according to the Computation of the Church of Englande, for the avoydyng of the diversities of Opinions and for the establishing of Consent touching true Religion ; put foorth by she Queenes aucthoritie; And shall bryng from such Bysshop or Gardyan of [Spyritualides *] in Wryting under his Seale autentike, a testimoniall of such Assent and Subscription, and openly on some Sunday in the tyme of the publique servyce afore noone in every Churche where by reason of any Ecclesiasticall Lyvyng he ought to attende, reade both the said Testimonial and the said Artycles; upon payne that every suche pson wctl shall not before the said Feast do as is above appoynted, shalbe (ipso facto) depryved, and al his Ecclesiasticall Emotions shalbe voyde as yf he then were naturally dead.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte for the bringing of Bowestaves into this Realme.

Benefits of Archery;

St. 12 E.IV. c.2. for Importation of Bowstaves, confirmed and extended to Merchants of the 72 Hans Towns.

WHERE as the use of Archerie not onely hathe ever ben but also yet is by Gods special Gyfte to the English nation a singuler Defence of this Realme, and an occasion of many noble Victoris and both a very wholesome Exercise for the Health and Strengh of Mens Bodies, and a Maynteyn*nce of a greate nuber of the Queenes true Subjects and Artificers as Bowyers Fletchers Stringers Arrowheadmakers, and other of this Realme ; and for that among other Causes of the Decaye of Archerie, one great Cause is, the excessive pryce of Bowe Staves, w* groweth principally by the Scarcitie of Bowe Staves brought into this Realme : For Reformation whereof. Bee yt enacted by thaucthoritie of this present Parliament, That all the Statutes made in the Twelf yere of the Raigne of Kyng Edward the Fourth, concerning bringing in of c?tayne number of Bow Staves according to the Wayght or Value of other Wares to be brought into this Realme, shall from hencefoorth be duely put in Execusion; And bee yt enacted and declared by this present Statute, That al Merchaunt Straungers using to bring Wares into this Realme from the East Partes, aswel from the threescore twelve Hanse Townes be comprised & meant under the name of and bound as the nichauntes mentioned & bound by the said Statute to bring in Bowe Staves upon lyke paynes and forfeytures as by the said Statutes are appoynted.

CHAPTER XV.

An Acte that no Hoy or Plate shall crosse the Seas.

WHERE at the Parlyament holden at Westni in the fyrst yere of yo' Highnes Raigne, it was amongest other St. i Eliz. c. a. $ j.

Things enacted, that no Hoye or Plate, whereof any English Subjects or Subjecte then was or should bee jf^crowng' Owner or Owners, at any tyme after the fyrst daye of January next ensuing the Session of the same Parliament, ,hc Sca*! from any Porte Creeke or Place of this Realme of England or any of the Domynions of the same, should traverse or crosse the Seas into or for any of the Portes beyond the Seas, w"' any Wares Goodes or Merchandizes; upon payne that the said Owner or Owners should forfayte and lose the same Hoye or Plate, w"‘ all and every the MunytionTackling and other Necessaries pteyning thereunto, as by the same Statute more at large doth and may appere ; And whereas by *u'"dby St\t-, an Estatute made in the fyfth yere of your Hignes Raigne, it is amongest other Thinges enacted, that from thenceforth al English Hoyes and Plates might crosse the Seas as farre as Cane in Normandie, and Eastward as farr as Norwaye, the said Estatute made in the fyrst yere of your Hygnesse Raygne to the contrary thereof notwithstandinge;

And forasmuche as the said Braunche in the said Estatute made in the fyfth yere of your Raigne, tendeth greatly to the decay of Maryners and Shypes by the marveylous Encrease of Hoyes; Be yt therefore enacted by thaucthorytie aforesaid, That from the Feast of Sl Mychael Tharchaungell next coming, the said Clause conteyned in the said Estatute made in the said fyfth yere of yor Raigne, for the crossing of the Seas by Hoyes and Plates, shalbe utterly repealed and made voyde and of none effect; And that from the said Feast of S' Mychael Tharchaungell next, the said Estatute made in the fyrst yere of your Raigne phibiting the crossing of the Seas by Hoyes & Plates be observed and kept; the said Estatute made in the fyfth yere of your Ma'f Raigne to the contrary hereof notwithstanding: Thys Acte to contynue untyl thend of the next Parlyament.

CHAPTER XIX.

An Acte for the makinge of Cappes.

IN most humble wyse shewen unto the Queenes Ma"* the Lords Spyritual & Temporall and y' Comons in this present Parlyament assembled. The Felowship and Company of Cappers of this noble Realme of England; That whereas they and others occupy eng the Trade and Scyence of Capping, have in tymes past untill nowe of late, w,h the only Travell and Industrye of theyr said Trade and Science of Capping, not onely maynteyned themselves theyr Wyves Children and Famylie in good reasonable and convenyent Estate & Degree according to theyr Vocation and Calling; but have also set on worke a great nuber and multytude of other poore persons the Queenes Ma'f Subjectes bothe Men Women and Chyldren, and also the haulte decrepite and lame, usyng them in sundry Exercises belonging to the Occupation and Art of Cappers, as Carders Spynners Knitters Part era of Woll Forsers Thyckers Dressers Walkers Diers Battelere Shearers Pressers Edgers Lyners Bandmakers and other Exercises, who have in lyke maner thereby maynteyned and releved themselves aftd theyr Famylies, and by reason of theyr Labour and Exercise therin have eschewed and avoyded not onely the greate Annoyaunce of the Townes they dwelled in, who for lacke of Exercyse must have ben enforced to begg, but also hathe kept them from raungyng and gadding throughe the Realme in practising and exercising sundry kyndes of lewdnes, as to many of them doth in these dayes, as it is evident, the more is the Pytye: And also by the meane of this good Exercise and Occupation, a greate number of psonable Men have at all tymes been redye and well able, when they should or have ben called, to serve your Highnes most Noble Pgenyto's and also your Ma*" in tyme of Warrf or elswhere; untill nowe of late dayes that moste and in maner all Men have forborne and left the using and wearing of Cappes, to the great ympoverishing and utter undoynge of all the aforesaid Companye and Felowship of Cappers, and to the greate decaye ruyne and desolation of dyvera auncient Cities and Boroughes wthin this Realme of Englande, w1* have ben the Norishers and bringers up in that Facultye of great Nombers of People, as London w"* by good report maynteyned eight thousande psons exercised in this Faculde, also Excester Brystowe Monmouth Hereford Rosse Bridgenorth Bewdeley Glocestre Worcester Chester Nantwich Newcastle Ulcestre Stafford Lychefeeld Coventrie Yorke Beverley Richemonde Darbye Leycester Northampton Shrewysburye Wellington Southampton Canterburye and dyvers others, aswell bordering and adjoyning upon the Coastes of the Seas as in other Places : In Consideration whereof, and forasmuch as the sayde auncient and laudable Science and Trade of Cappynge hathe ben of longe tyme pmytted and alowed in this most Noble Realme as a thynge very comodious and pffytable, aswell for the maynten*nce and lyvyng of a greate Nomber of psons w^in the same, as also for the upholdyng and replenishing and fortifyeng of the said auncient Cities and Bouroughes, and specially for the trading and exercising of the poorest sorte of People in honest Labour and vertuous Exercyse, and therefore pfitable to the Common wealth ; and for that also the wearyng of the same Cappes are very decent and comelye for all Estates and Degrees, and especially for all psons inhabiring w^in the Cities Bouroughes Townes Vyllages [or'] Hamlettes w,hin this Realme: For Reformation whereof it may please the Queenes Highnes and the Lordes Spyrituall and Temporall and the Comons in this present Parlyament assembled and by thaucthoritie of the same, That it maye be enacted and established, That all and every pson and psons above Thage of syxe yerf (except Maydens Ladyes and Gentlewomen) inhabiting commoratinge and abyding w^in any of the Cities Bouroughes Townes Villages of Hamlettes of this Realme of England, And except also al Noble Psonages and every Lorde Knight and Gentleman of the Possessions of Twentye Markes Land by the Yere & theyr Hey res, And except also al such as have borne Office of Wourehip in any Citye Borough Towne Hamlet or Shyre, And also al such as have borne the Offyce of Wardens of the Wourshipfull Companyes of the Cytie of London, shall use and weare upon the Saboth and Holy Daye, onles in the tyme of theyr travel out of the said Cities Bouroughes Townes Villages or Hamlettes, upon their Head one Cappe of Woll Knytt, thicked and dressed in England, made w°'in this Realme of England, and onely dressed and fynished by some of the Trade or Science of Cappers; upon payne of forfeture for every daye not so wearing, the Sume of Three Shilling^ Foure Pence of lawfull Mony of England.

And further be it enacted by thaucthoritie aforesaid, That Justices of Assise in their Cyrcuites Justices of Peace in theyr Sessions, Shyriffes in theyr Turnes, Stewardes in theyr Leetes and Lawdayes, Mayors Shyrefes and Bailiffes of Cities Boroughes and Townes Corporate in theyr Courts, shall and may enquyre heare and determyne from tyme to tyme all and every the said Offences comitted and donne w,hin the Lymites of theyr several Jurisdictions and Aucthorities; And where any such Forfeytures shall happen to be founde wu,in the pkynct of any City Borough Towne Corporate Leete or Lawdaye, then the Mayo" Sheryffes and Bayliffes of the said Cities Boroughes and Townes, and Owners of the said Leete or Lawedaye, shall have and enjoy thone Moytie of the said Forfaytures, and thother Moytie to be distributed at the discretion of the Rulers and Cheese Governors of every such Citie Borough Towne or Hamlet where the Trespas shalbe tried and found, among the Poore inhabiting w'^in the same.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthoritie aforesaid, for the better Execution of this Statute, That the Parentes Gardyans GovWs and Maisters shall lose and forfayte the Penalty aforesaid, for every such Child Servaunt or Warde as shalbe above thage of syxe yeres, and und' thage of one and twenty yeres, and remayning dwelling and abydinge w"‘ any suche person, w* shall offend or do contrary to this Acte or any Thing therein conteyned.
