CHAPTER XXm.

An Acte for pavyng of a Streete without Algate.

WHERE as one Waye betwene two Postes next Algate, sometyme called the Barres next Algate, in the Parrysh of S* Butolphe in the Suburbs of the Citie of London, and a corner House in the said Parrysh nowe in thoccupation of Thomas Sparrowe, and one Waye extending and leading from a Place called Thold Cage in the said Prysh of S' Butolphe to the North End of a Lane called Nyghtingale Lane in the Prish of S' Mary Matfellon at Whyte Chappell, and one other Waye betwene the said Place called Thold Cage and one Myll called the Crasse Mill in the said Parish of S' Marye, by reason aswell of dyvers the Queenes Ma'f Caryages passynge by and throughe the said Wayes from her Highnes Store Houses of Minories Marie Graces and Ratcliffe to the Towre of London, and other Caryages, as also the greate Passage Course and Recourse of dyvers her Subjectes on Horsebacke and one Fotote are become so myerie and fowle in the Wynter tyme as hard it is to have any Passages for the same through the said Wayes : For Reformation and Amendment whereof. Bee yt enacted ordeyned and established by the Queenes MaM' the Lordes Spyrytuall and Temporall and the Comons in this p>sent Parlyament assembled, and by thaucthorytye of the same. That all and every pson and psons Bodies Polityke and Corporate, theyr Heyres and Successors that nowe be, or at any tyme hereafter shalbe seased of any Manours Landes Tenementes or Heredytamentf in any wyse next adjoyninge to the said Hyghe wayes, or any of them, be it on thon side or on thother side or sydes of them or any of them, of any Estate of Fee Simple Fee Tayle or for tearme of Lyfe or Lyves, shall before the Feast of S* Mychel Ttharchaungel w* shalbe in the yere of our Lord God a thousand fyve hundreth threescore and twelve, sufficiently pave or cause to be paved w'h Stones the said Wayes, and every of them, along by his & theyr Manours Landes and Tenementes adjoyning to the saide Wayes, and every or any of them, unto the myddest of the same Wayes; and shall at all tymes after the said Feast of S' Mychell Tharchaungell, wch shalbe in the yere of our Lorde God M. D. lxxij. sufficiently mayntayne the Pavementes of the said High wayes against every of theyr said Landes and Tenementes, in such lyke manor and fourme as is above declared; upon payne to forfayte unto the Quenes Ma'1', her Heyres and Successors, for every Yarde square of the saide Pavements not sufficiently paved repayred amended or maynteyned Three Shillinges Foure Pence; Thone Halfe thereof to be to the Queenes Ma'k, her Heyres and Successo's, and thother Halfe to hym or them that wyll sue for the same.

And because the Waters fallynge to and upon the said Wayes betwene the saide two Postes next Algate, and the said comer House nowe in the occupation of the said Thomas Sparrowe hathe and doth comonly overflowe into the Ditch of the Towre of London when greate aboundance of Water falleth in the same Waye, whereof the said Towre Dych is the rather to be in short tyme filled up j It is therefore ordeyned enacted and established by thaucthoride aforesaid, That the said Waters on both sides of the said Hygh waye shall have the Fall and Course onely from the said Waye downe to the said comer House, and from thence into the Dyche lyeng on the North side of Hogg Lane, and so to the Comon Sewer at the East end of the said Hogg Lane; And that al and every pson and psons Bodies Politike and Corporate, theyr Heyres Successors and Assignes, that have or hereafter shall have any Landes Tenementes or Heredytamentes in Fee Simple Fee Tayle or for Terme of Lyfe or Lyves, adjoyning to the said Diche on the North syde of Hogg Lane either on thon side or on the other, shall sufficiently before the said Feast of S' Michael wch shalbe in the yere of our Lord God 1572, skowre and cleanse and so kepe skowred and cleansed the said Dyche alonge the saide Landes Tenementes and Heredytamentes to the myddest of the saide Dyche; upon payne that every peon and psons Bodies Polytike and Corporate, theyr Heyres and Successors and Assignes, wch shall suffer the same or any part thereof to be unskowred and uncleansed after the saide Feast Daye of S' Mychael, shall forfayte and loose to our said Soveraigne Lady the Queenes Ma'1*, her Heyres and Successours, the sume of Three Shillinges Foure Pence for every Pole or Rod in Lengthe conteyninge Sixteene Foote and a Halfe, for every Moneth that the same shalbe unskowred and uncleansed after the same Feast.

CHAPTER XXIV.

An Acte for the pavyng of the Towne of Ipswiche.

FOR that it is very convenyent and necessarie for the Towne of Ipswich in the County of Suffolke that the Pavementes of the Streetes there be repayred and newe made, according to the Necessitye thereof, the Inhabitantes of the saide Towne humbly praye, That it maye be enacted by our Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, the Lords Spyrituall and Temporall and Comons of this present Parlyament assembled, and by thaucthoritye of the same, That all and singuler psons theyr Heyres and Successors now being or wch hereafter shalbe imediate Owners Landlordes or Terretenauntes of any Houses Landes or Tenementes w^in the said Towne or the Suburbes of the same, of any Estate or Estates in Fee Simple Fee Tayle [or'] for Lyfe or Yeres, shall from tyme to tyme and at all tymes from and after the last daye of this present Session of Parlyament, at the Assignement or Appoyntment of the Bayliffes of the said Towne for the tyme being, aswell pave or cause to be paved w* good pavyng Stones, along from and against his or theyr Houses Landes and Tenementes adjoyning to the Streete, so much of the said Streete in lengh as his or theyr saide Houses Landes or Tenementes so adjoyning extendeth unto, and in breadth during all the said lengh to the Chanel, or to such Place as the Chanell there shalbe by the saide Bayliffes for the tyme beinge appoynted to; upon payne to lose or forfayte for every Yard Square not sufficiently paved in fourme aforesaid w^n Two Monethes after Warnyng thereof geven to the Baylifff for the tyme befog, the same befog presented before the Bayliffes of the said Towne for the tyme beyng by the Twelve Headboroughes of the same Towne, Twelve Pence of lawfoll Mony of England ; And that the saide. CHAPTER XXVII. (* )

An Acte of a Subsidie and Two Fifteenes and Tenthes graunted by the Temporaltye.

CONSIDERINGE youre Majesties bothe carefull Travaile and happie successe, by the greate Provydence of God, in Govemement of this youre Realme, (moste myghtie and redowted Sovereigne) whereby not only Wee have ben so longe tyme kepte in Peax w,h forreyne Realmes, and quyet w^n oure selves, more happely then in anye former tyme we can fynde to have ben; And that the same moste happy Estate hathe ben of late attempted by certen evell disposed unnaturall and unkynde Subjects of youre Majesde, Enemyes to God and to yo' Highnes, to be interrupted; w* evell unnaturall Popishe and and Rebellyouse Attempte, allthough by the greate Grace of God (to whome allwaies bee geven moste humble Thanckf) and youre Highnes greate Provydence and inestymable Charges, was and hathe ben sone broughte to an Ende, yett it hathe ben discomforth to Us yo' lovinge Subjects, greif to yo' Highnes and greate waiste unto yo' Treasaure; Therefore Wee moste humble lovinge and obedyent Subjects the Lordes Spirytuali and Temporall and the Comens in this present Plyament assembled, have thought yt for those and other manye greate and urgent occasions, no lesse then owre Dewtie to offer to yo' Highnes for parte of a Supplye of that yo' Majestie hathe borne and is like to beare, not onlye in repressinge the sayd Rebellf butt also in provydinge againste forreigne Attemptes wcl1 in and after suche Cases are not wont to be unreadye, One lyttell and smale Present, the whiche moste humbly and on o' Knees Wee praye yo’ moste excellent Majestye to accepte in good part, nott weyinge the smalenes therof, butt the good wyll of our Myndf ; that is, Twoo Fyftenes and one Subsidye, and that it wold please yo' Majestie that it be enacted by authorytie of this Pliament, as hereafter followeth: Be it Inactbd, That yo' Highnes, towards the greate Charges of this yo' Realme, and for the better Mayntenaunce of yo' Royall Estate, shall have by Aucthorytie of this present Plyament, Twoo Fyftenes and Tenthes to be payde taken and levyed of the movable Goods Cattallf and other Things usuall to suche Fyftenes and Tenthes, to be contrybutorye and changeable, w^n the Sheyres Cyties Boroughes Townes and other Places of this yo' Majestyes Realme, where the lyke Fiftenes and Tenthes have been heretofore paid, in maner and forme afore tyme used; And the sayd Twoe Fyftenes and Tenths (the Exception and DeduccSn aforesayd thereuppon had deducted and allowed) to be payde in Maner and Forme followinge. That is to saye; The firste whole Fyftene and Tenthe (excepte before excepted) to be payde to yo' Highnes in the Receipte of yo' Highness Exchequer before the twentieth daye of October nexte comynge; And the sayd second Fyftene and Tenth (except before excepted) to be payde to youre Highnes in the said Receipte of yor sayd Eschequer, before the twentieth day of October, which shalbe in the yeare of o' Lord God One thousand fyve hundred threscore and twelve.

CHAPTER XXVm. (')

An Acte of the Quenes Highnesse moste gracious Generali and Free Pardon.

THE Quenes moste Excellent Malie well understandynge the great good will and iaithfull hartes of all her lovynge and obedyent' Subjects towardes her Highnes, aswell for the good governaunce as also for the Defence of this her Realme at all tymes; And nowe pceyvynge that the same her lovynge Subjects have many wayes fallen into the daunger of dyverse Forfeytures and Penalties of the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme, hath therefore thought it convenyent to extend her mercy and clemency towardes her said obedient Subjects with her liberall and free Pardon ; and thereby to discharge some part of suche great Paynes Penalties and Forfeytures wherewith her said Subjects stand nowe burdened and charged; trustynge assuredly that fromhensfoorthe her said lovynge Subjects will contynue in all good Obedience and Faithfulnes towardes her Ma*1*, and hereafter so to obey the good Lawes and Statutes of this Realme as to them of Right and Dutie apperteyneth: And therefore her Ma1" is well pleased and contented that it be enacted by the Aucthoritie of this pnt Pliament, in manner and fourme followynge, That is to saye; that all and every of her said Subjects, aswell Spiritual! as Temporall of this her Highnes Realme of England, Wales, the Isles of Jemesey and Gernesey, and the Towne of Barwyck, the Heires Successo's Executo's and Admynystrato's of them and every of them, and all and synguler Bodies in any manner of wyse corporated, Cities Boroughes Shyres Rydynges Hundredes Lathes Rapes Wapentakes Townes Vyllages Hamelettf and Tythynges, and everye of them, and the Successo' and Successo's of every of them, shalbe by Aucthorytye of this pnt Parlyament acquyted pardoned releassed and discharged, against the Quenes Mall' her Heyres and Successo's and every of them, of all manner of Treasons Fellonyes Robberyes Offences Contemptf Alienacons wihout License Trespacf Intrucons Entrees Wrongs Deceiptf Mysdemeano's Forfeytures Penaltyes and Somes of Money, Paynes of Deathe, Paynes corporall and pecunyarye, and generally of all other Thynges Causes Quarrellf Sutes Judgementf and Execucons, in this pnt Acte hereafter not excepted nor foreprysed, whiche may be or can be by her Highnes in any wyse or by any meanes pardoned, before and unto the fouretenth daye of February last past, in this present thirtenth yere of her most gracious Reigne, to every or any of her sayd Subjects Bodyes Corporate Cytyes Borowghes Shyres Rydynges Hundredes Lathes Rapes Wapentakes Townes Villages and Tythynges or any of them.

And alsoe the Quenes Highnes is contented that it be enacted by Aucthoryty of this pnt Parlyament, That her said free Pdon shalbe as good and effectuall in the Lawe to every of her said Subjects, Bodyes Corporate, and other before rehersed, in and against all Thynges whiche be not hereafter in this pnt Acte excepted and forprysed, as the same Pardon shoulde have bene, yf all Offences Contemptf Forfeytures Causes Matters Suytes Quarrellf Judgementf Execucons Penaltyes and all other Thynges, (not hereafter in this Acte excepted and forprysed,) had bene partyculerly syngulerly specyally and playnely named rehersed and specyfyed, and also pdoned by proper and expresse Wordes and Names in theyr Kyndes Natures and Qualytyes, by Wordes and Termes thereunto requysyte to have bene putt in and expressed in this pnte Acte of free Pardon ; And that her said Subjects, nor any of them, nor the Heires Executours or Admynystrators of any of them, nor of the said Bodyes Corporate and others before named and rehersed, nor any of them, be nor shalbe sued vexed or inquyeted in their Bodies Goodes Chattellf Landes or Tents, for any manner of Matter Cause Contempt Mysdemeano' Forfayture Trespace Offence or any other Thyng, suffered done or comytted before the saide fouretenth day of February against her Highnes her Crowne Dygnyty Prerogatyve Lawes or Statutes, but onely for suche Matters Causes and Offences as be playnly rehersed in the Excepcons of this present Acte hereafter menebned, and for none other; Any Statute or Statutes Lawes Customes or Usages heretofore had made or used to the contrary in any wyse notwithstandynge.

Also the Quenes Highnes of her bounteous Lyberalytye, by Aucthorytye of this pnt Parlyament, graunteth and freely geveth to every of her said Subjects, and to every of the said Bodyes Corporat and other before rehersed, and every of theym, all Gooddes Cattellf Debtes Fynes Issues Proffittf Amarcyamentf Forfeytures and Somes of Money by any of them forfeyted, which to her Highnes doo or sholde belonge or appartcyne, by reason of any Offence Contempt Trespace Entree Mysdemeano' Matter Cause or Quarrell suffered done or comytted by them or any of them before the said fouretenth day of February, whiche be not hereafter in this present Acte playnely foreprysed Sc excepted j And that all and every the Quenes said Subjects, and all & syngler Bodies Corporate & other before rehersed, may by hym or themself, or by his or their Deputye or Deputyes or by his or their Atto'ney or Atto'neys, accordynge to the Lawes of this Realme, pleade and mynyster this present Acte of free Pardon, for his or their Discharge of and for every Thynge that is by vertue of this present Acte pardoned discharged geven or graunted withoute any Fee or other Thynge in any wyse paienge to any parson or psons for Wrytynge or Entree of the Judgement or other Cause concemynge suche Plee Wrytynge or Entree, but only sixtene pence to be paid to the Offycer or Clerke that shall enter the Plee Matter or Judgement for the Ptyes Discharge in that Behalf; Any Statute Usage or Custome to the contrary notwythstandynge.

And furthermore the Quenes Highnes is contented and pleased that it be enacted by thaucthorytie of this present Plyament, That her said free Pardon by the generall Wordes before rehersed, shalbe reputed demed adjudged expounded allowed & taken in all manner of C.ourtes of her Highnes and elswhere, aswell in the Wordes and Clauses

CHAPTER I.

An Acte for the Punyshement of suche as shall rebellyously take or deteyne, or conspire to take or deteyne from the Queens Ma"% any of her Castelles Towers Fortresses Holdes, &c.

FOR the better avoyding of all suche unlawfull Practises secret Conspiracies and Devises, as latelye have been stirred and moved by some evell disposed psons againste our moste gratiouse Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, in seeking by false Conspiracyes and undue Meanes to surpryse and take from her Majestie some of her Castelles Towres Fortresses Shippes Ordinances Artillerye & other Munitions of Warre: Bee yt enacted by the Queenes moste Excellent Majestye, with Thassent of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall, and the Commons in this p'sent Parliament assembled, and by [Aucthorytye1] of the same, That yf any pson or psons whatsoever at any Tyme hereafter doe, within this Realme or elswhere, unlawfully and of his or their oWne Aucthorytie, compasse imagine conspire practyse or devyse by any Wayes or Meanes with Force or by any Crafte Devyse or Sleight, maliciously and rebellyously to take, or to deteyne or keep from our said Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, anny of her Castelles Towres Fortresses or Holdes, or malytyously and rebellyously to rase bume or destroye any Castell Bulwercke or Forte, or any parte of them, having any Munic&n or Ordinance of the Queenes Ma"" therein, or appoincted to bee garded with any Souldiours for Defence thereof, within this Realme or within any of her Ma1" Dominions or Countreis or the Marches of the same, and the same Compasses Imaginacbns Practises Conspiracyes or Devices or any of them, shall and doe advisedly by any expresse Woordes Speache Acte Deed or Wryting expresse utter or declare for any the malytiouse and rebelliouse Intentes aforesaid, that then everye suche pson and psons so hereafter offendinge in any the pmisses, their Aydours Councellours Comforters Consentours and Abettours knowing thereof, being thereof lawfully convicted according to the Lawes of this Realme, shalbe judged a Felon and Felons, and that every suche Offence shalbe judged to bee Felony, and the Offendoure and Oflfendours therein, their said Aydours Comforters Counsellours and Abettours, being thereof lawfullye convicted, shall have and suffer paynes of Deathe as in cases of Felonye, without having any Benefyte of Cleargye or Sainctuarye, and also shall forfayte and lose all his Goodes and Cattelles Landes & Tentes as in other cases of Felonye hathe been used and accustomed.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthorytye aforesaid, That yf any person or persons doe at any tyme hereafter with Force malyciouslye and rebellyouslye deteyne keepe or wthhold from the Queenes Malit, any of her Castelles Towres Fortresses or Holdes, within this Realme or within any her Ma"" Domynions or Countreis or Marches of the same, or do malytiously rebellyouslye and with Force detayne keepe or withhold from her Ma* any of her Shippes Ordinaunce Artyllerye or other Munitions or Forty fycac6ns of Warres, and doe not rendre and give up the same to our said Soveraigne Ladye, or to suche person as her Ma*" shall appointe to receave the same to her Ma8' use, within syxe dayes next after hee or they so offending shalbee comaunded by our said Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, by open Proclamations under the Greate Seale of England to bee made in any Place or Markett Towne within the Countye where any suche Offence shalbee committed. Or shall wyllfullye malytiously and rebellyously burne or destroye, or cause to be burned or destroyed, any of the Queenes Shippes, Or malytiouslye and rebellyouslye barre or cause to bee barred any Haven within any of the Queenes Ma"" Domynions, That then everye suche person and persons so offending, their AydoUrs Councellours and Abettours, being thereof lawfully convicte according to the Lawes of this Realme, shalbee adjudged Traytou", and their Offences in any of the Premysses, shalbee accepted judged and taken for Highe Treason, and the Offendours therein, their Aydours Councellours and Abettours, being thereof lawfullye convycte according to the Lawes of this Realme, shall have and suffer suche paynes of Deathe, and also shall forfayte and lose, as in Cases of Highe Treason is lymyted and accustomed.

This Acte to endure during the Queenes Ma'* Lyes that nowe is onlye.

CHAPTER IL

An Acte againste suche as shall conspyre or practyse the enlargement of any Prisoner committed for

Highe Treason.

FORASMUCH AS greate Daunger maye ensue to the Queenes Mau" Person, and great trouble to the State of the Realme, by unlawfiill Conspiracyes Devyces and Imaginacftns, to enlarge and sett at lybertye suche psons as bee or shalbee coomytted to any Pryson Gard or Custodye for any Treason touching the Royall Person of our said Soveraigne Ladye; againste whiche Devyces Conspiracyes and Imaginations sufficyent Remedye by the Lawes of this Realme hathe not been heeretofore had ne provided, unles the same Conspyracyes Imaginations and Devyces were executed and brought to Effecte : Bee yt therefore enacted by our said Soveraigne Ladye the Queene the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Commons in this Parlyament assembled and by the Aucthorytye of the same, That yf any person or persons, at any tyme after the Ende of this psent Session of Parlyament, shall imagine conspyre devyse invent or goe about unlawfully and maliciouslye to enlardge or sett at Lybertye anny person or persons comytted or to be comytted to any Pryson Garde or Custodye by her Highnes especyall Comaundement, for any Treason or suspition of Treason concerning the person of our said Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, before any Indyctament of suche person so sought or intended to bee sett at Large or Lybertye as ys aforesaid; And the same Conspiracies Imaginacbns Devyses or Inventions, shall by expresse Woordes Wryting or other Matter or Acte expressely or manyfestly set for the utter or declare. That then every person so offending shall incurre the Penaltye & Forfayture of myspryssion of Treason, and that all and every Offence and Offences to bee commytted and donne as is aforesaid shalbee deemed and taken for mysprysion of Treason.

And bee yt also enacted by the Aucthorytee aforesaid, That yf any person or persons, at any tyme after thend of this p>sent Session of Parlyament, shall imagyne conspyre devyse invent or goe aboute unlawfullye and malytiouslye to enlarge or set at Lybtie any person or persons comytted or to bee comytted to any Pryson Garde or Custodye, being or which hereafter shalbe indycted of any Treason in any wyse concerning the person of our said Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, and the same Conspyracies Imaginacbns Devyses or Inventions shalby expresse Woordes Wryting or other Matter or Acte expressely or manyfestly sett for the utter or declare, that then every suche person so offending, shalbee deemed & adjudged a Felon, and suffer [losse and forfayture'] as in cases of Felonye by the due course of the Lawes of this Realme.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthorytye aforesaid, That yf any person or persons, at any tyme after thend of this psent Session of Parlyament, shall imagine conspyre devyse invent or goe about unlawfully and malitiouslye to enlardge or sett at Lybertye any pson or psons being comytted to any Pryson Garde or Custodye, after the same person or persons ys or shalbee attaincted or convicted of anny Treason in anny- wyse concurring the Royall Person of our said Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, and the same Conspiracyes Imaginations Devyses or Inventions shalby expresse Woordes Writing Matter or Acte, as is aforesaid, sett for the utter or declare, that then everye suche person so offending shalbee deemed and adjudged an Highe Traytour and shall suffer [losse*] and forfayte as in cases of Highe Treason by the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme.

This Acte to endure during the Queenes Majesties Lyes that nowe ys onelye.

CHAPTER III.

An Acte againste the forging and counterfayting of Forraine Coygne, being*' cur raunte within this Realme.

FORASMUCH AS by the Lawes or Statutes of this Realme small or no condigne Punyshement ys at this tyme provided for suche evell disposed persons as shall counterfayte or forge suche kynd of Golde or Silver of other Realmes as ys not the proper Coygne of this Realme, nor currante in payment within this Realme; by reason whereof divers evell disposed persons, aswell without this Realme as within, are encouraged and bouldened daylye to counterfayte or forge suche kind of Gold and Sylver and utter the same in this Realme, in great Deceipte of her Majesties Subjectes: Bee yt enacted by our said Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, the Lordes Spuall and Temporall & the Comons in this p*sent Parliament assembled, and by thaucthorytye of the same. That yf any pson or psons hereafter falsely forge or counterfayte any suche kind of Coygne of Gold or Silver as ys not the proper Coigne of this Realme, nor permitted to bee curraunte within this Realme, That then everye suche Offence shalbee deemed and adjudged mysprision of Highe Treason, and the Offendours therein theire Procurers Aydours and Abettours, being convicte according to the Lawes of this Realme of such Offences, shalbee imprysoned and forfayte suche Lands Goodes and Chattelles as in cases of mysprysion of Treason, for concellement of Highe Treason.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte to revive a Statute made Anno Primo of the Queens Ma"" Raigne, inhibiting the carrieng of Leather Tallowe and Rawe Hides out of the Realme.

St. i Eliz. c. io. against the Exportation of Leather, kc. revived for Seven Years, &c.

WHERE in the Parliament begune at Westminster the three and twentye daye of Januarye in the firste yeere of the Raigne of our Soveraigne Ladye the Queenes moste Excellent Mau% there was one verye good Acte and Statute made prohibyting the transporting and carieng of Leather Rawe Hydes and Tallowe out of this Realme, endtuled. An Acte that the conveying of Leather Tallowe or Rawe Hydes out of [this1] Realme for Merchaundise, shalbee Felonye; whiche Acte and Statute was made to continue but for a certeyne tyme, and nowe ys expired and determyned for want of contynuaunce at the last Parlyament: And Forasmuche as by Experience yt hathe well appeared that, since the determinaefin of the said good Lawe and Statute, there hathe been and yet daylye is suche greate transportac&n of Leather Rawe Hydes and Tallowe out of this Realme, that therby greate Scarsytye and Dearthe thereof is nowe growen amonges the Queenes Ma"" moste loving and obedient Subjectes, and specyallye amonges those of the pooreste sorte, who are nowe compelled to paye for their Bootes and Shoes almoste double the Pryse that they did beefore the determinaf&n of the said good Law & Statute: For Remedy whereof, Bee yt enacted by the Queenes moste Excellent Ma1*, with Thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this p'sent Parliament assembled, and by thaucthorytye of the same. That the said Acte and Statute made in the said Parlyament begune the said three and twentye daye of Januarye in the said firste yere, entytuled as ys beforesaid, and all and everye Braunche Article Clause and Sentence therein conteyned, shall from and after the Feaste Daye of Saint Bartholomewe Thapostle next comynge bee revived, and stand and bee in full Force and Effect for and during the space of seven yeres then next following; and also after thend of the said seven yeres, then to thend of the next Parlyament next following thend and determinac&n of the said seven yeeres j Any thing heretofore had made or donne or suffered to the contrary thereof notwithstanding.

It ys therefore enacted by the aucthoritye of this psent Parlyament, That the Justices of Peace of all and singuler the Shyers of England and Wales within the Lymytes of their Comyssions, and all other Justices of the Peace, Maiors Sheryffes Baylyffes, and other Officers of all & every Cytye Borough Rydinge and Fraunchesies within this Realine, whereof they be Justices at Peace, within the Lymittes of their Aucthoritie, shall at or before the said Feaste of Saint Bartholomewe next comynge devide themselves, and so beinge devided shall within every of their severall Divisions and Authorities make diligent Searche and Enquierye of all aged poore ympotent and decayed persons borne within their said Divisions and Lymittes, or whiche were there dwelling within Three yeres next before this psent Parliament, whiche lyve or of necessitye be compelled to lyve by Aimes of the Charytye of the People that be or shalbe abydynge within the Lymyttes of their Comyssions and Aucthorytyes, and shall uppon that Search made, make a Register Booke conteyninge the Names & Surnames of all suche aged decayed and ympotent pcore People as be within their said Lymittes and Authorities, which shall alwayes remayne with the said Justicf Maiors Bayliffes or other Head Officers or any one of them; And when the number of the said poore People forced to lyve uppon Aimes be by that meanes truely knowen, then the said Justices Maiors Sheryffes Baylyffes and other Offycers shall within lyke convenient tyme devise and appointe, within evrye there said severall Divisions, meete and convenient places by their dyscredons to settle the same poore People for their Habitacbns and Abydynges, yf the pishe within the whiche they shalbee founde shall not or wyll not provide for them ; and shall also within lyke convenient tyme number all the said poore People within there said severall Lymyttes, and thereuppon (having regarde to the number) set downe what porcftn the weekely Charge towardes the Releefe and Sustentacon of the said poore People wyll amounte unto within everye their said severall Division 8c Lymyttes; and that donne, they the said Justices Maiors Sheriffes Baylyffes and other Officers within every their severall Commyssions Authorities Divisions 8c Lymyttes, shal by their good discretions taxe and assesse all and every the Inhabitauntes, dwelling in all and every Cytye Boroughe Towne Village Hamlet and Place knowen within the said Lymyttes and Divisions, to suche weekely Charge as they and everye of them shall weekely contribute towardes the Releef of the said poore People, and the names of all suche Inhabitauntes taxed shall also entre into the said Register Booke togeather with their Taxac&n, and also shall by their discretion within every their said Divisions and Lymyttes appoint or see Collectoures for one whole yere to bee aypointed of the said weekely porc&n, which shall collect and geather the said proporf&n, and make delyverye of so muche thereof, accordinge to the discretion of the said Justices Maiors Sheryffes Baylyffes and other Officers, to the said poore People, as the said Justices Maiors Sheryffes Bayliffes and other Officers shall appointe them ; And alsoe shall appointe the Overseers of the said poore People by their discretions, to continue also for one whole yere; and yf they doe refuse to bee Overseers, then everye' of them so refusinge to forfayt tenne shillinges for every suche default.

And bee yt further enacted by the aucthorytye aforesaid,That yf any of the said poore People, uppon the Appoyntment of the said Justices or other Officers, refuse to bee bestowed in any of the said Abydinge Places before mentioned, but covet styll to hold on their Trade of Begging, or after they be once bestowed in the said Abidinge Place or Places doe departe and begge, then the said pson and psons so offendinge, for the firste Offence to be accompted a Roge or Vacabond, and to suffer as a Roge or Vacabound in the firste degree of punyshement set for the by this Acte in all poyntes, and yf hee she or they doe the second tyme offend, then to be estemed as a Roge or Vacabounde, and to suffer as a Roge or Vacabound in the last degree of ponnishement set foorthe by this Acte in all poynetes.

And Further be yt enacted, That the said Collectours and every of them so to be chosen as ys aforesaid, shall make their juste Accompte halfe yerely of their said Collection and Gathering, to two Justices of the Peace dwelling next to the said Abydynge Place or Places, not beinge within any Cytye Boroughe or Towne Corporate, or to the Maior Sheriffes or other Chief Officers of the said Cytyes Boroughs or Townes Corporate; And when they go out of their Offices they shall delyver or cause to bee delyvered foorthwithe upon their Accomptes, all suche Surplusages of their Collection & gatheringe as shall then remayne undystributed, to be ordered by the said Justicf Maiors

Bayliffes or other Head Officers, upon the said payne of Tenne Poundes; if any suche Collectour shall refuse to

there to remayne without Bayle or Mainepryse tyll he have made his said Accompte and ymmedyate payment and

delyverye of all suche Surplussages as he hathe receaved.

And bee yt further enacted, That yf any pson or psons beinge able to further this charitable Worcke will obstinatly refuse to geve towardes the Helpe and Relief of the said poore people, or doo wylfully discourage others from so charitable a Deede, the said obstinate pson or wyllfull dyscourager shall yPsently be brought before two Justices of the Peace, whereof one to be of the Quorum, of the same Countye, to shewe the cause of his obstinate Refusall or wilfull discouragement, and to abyde suche Order therein as the said Justices shall appointe; yf hee refuse so to doo, then to be comitted to the next Gaole for the said Shier, ther to remayne untyll hee be contented with their said Order and doo pfourme the same.

And yt ys also further enacted, That yf any of the said aged and ympotent persons not being so diseased lame or ympotent but that they maye worke in some maimer of worke, shalbe by the Overseers of their said Abydyng Place appointed to worke yf they refuse, then in fourme aforesaid to be whipped and stocked for their firste Refusall, & for the second Refusall to be punyshed as in case of Vacabondes in the said firste degree of Punyshement.

Provided alwayes and be yt further enacted by thaucthoritye of this psent Parlyament, That three Justices of Peace, whereof one to bee of the Quorum, of and with the Surplusages of the said Collections and Forfaytures, (the said poore and ympotent people satysfyed and provided for,) shall by their dyscretions in suche convenient place & places within their said Sheres as they shall thincke meete, place and settle to worke the Roges & Vacabondf that shalbee dysposed to worke, borne within there said Countyes or their abydynge for the moste parte wthin the said three yeres, there to be holden to worcke by the oversight of the said Overseers, to get their Livinges & to lyve and to bee sustayned onely upon their labour and travayle.

Bee yt also further enacted by the Aucthorytye of this psent Parlyament, That yf any Beggers Chylde beinge above thage of fyve yeres and under fourteene yeres, beinge Male or Female, shalbe lyked of by any Subjecte of this Realme of honest callinge, who shalbe wyllynge to take the said Chylde into Service, the said Subject shall at the nexte Generali Sessions to be holden for the said Countye, by order of the Justices there or the moste parte of them, have the said Chylde bound with him, yf yt be a Man Childe, tyll thage of foure and twentye yeres, yf yt be a Woman Chylde, tyll thage of Eyghteene yeres; If the Chylde doo after departe or bee taken or be intysed from the said Maister or Maistresse, the Maister or Maistresse to have their Remedye by Order of the Statute of Labourers as for their Servaunt, eyther by Waye of Action or otherwyse, aswell against the Chylde as againste the Taker or Intyser thereof.

Bee yt also enacted by thaucthontye of this psent Parlyament, That all the Forfaytures appoineted or to growe by this Statute (except the Forfaytures of Justices of Peace) shall wholy goe & bee employed to thuse of the Poore aforesaid, & shalbe levied by Dystresse by the dyscretion of the Justices of the same Countye or two of them, or other Head Officers aforesaid : And that the Justices of Peace in all Shires of England, shall in their Quarter Sessions next after Easter, yerely examyne the pfourmaunce or not pfourmaunce of this Statute, accordinge to the Tenor thereof, as they are bounde to doe the Statute of Labourers; And at their said Sessions shall yerely appointe newe Collectours & newe Overseers for the Causes aforesaid, and shall then also agree uppon newe Viewes and Searches of the saide ympotent people within everye their Lymyttes for the yere followinge, yf need shalbe ; And further at their said Sessions shall take order by their good dyscretions for all & every thinge and thinges that may in any wyse further the intent of this Acte.

And bee yt further enacted by thaucthorytye aforesaid, That three Jusdces of Peace within all the Shires of this Realme, whereof one to bee of the Quorum, shall have full power by Aucthoritye of this psent Parlyam' to heare and determyne all Causes (excepte Forfaytures of Justices of Peace) that shall come in question by reason of this psent Acte.

And Whereas a greate number of pore and dyseased people do resorte to the Cytye of Bathe in the Countye of Sommerset, and the Towne of Buckston in the Countye of Derbye, for some Ease and Releife of their Diseases at the Bathes there, and by meanes thereof the Inhabitauntes of the same Cytye of Bathe and Towne of Buckstone are greatly overchardged with the same poore people, to their intollerable Chardge: Bee yt enacted by the aucthoritye aforesaid, That no dyseased or ympotent poore pson living on Aimes, at any tyme after the Feaste of Sainte Bartholomewe the Apostle next commynge, shall resorte or repayre from their Dwellinge places to the said Cytie of Bathe and Towne of Buckston, or eyther of them, to the Bathes there for ease of their Greef, unlesse suche p6on be not onely lycensed so to do by two Justices of the Peace of the Countye where such pson doth or shall then dwell & remayne, but also provided for by the Inhabitauntes of suche Hundreds Parishes or Places from whence

they shall so be lycensed to travayle, of suche Releife for and towardes his Maynten*nce as shalbee necessarye

for the same pson, for the tyme of suche his Abode at the said Cytye of Bathe and Towne of Buckstone, or eyther of them, and [turninge'] home againe as shalbe lymyted by the same Lycense, uppon payne to bee

reputed punyshed and used as Vacabondes by the purvewe of this Estatute; and that the Inhabitauntes of the

same Cytye and Towne shall not in any wyse bee chardged by this Acte with the fyndinge or relief of any suche poore people.

And for the better pfourmance of this charitable Acte, It ys ordeyned and establyshed by aucthoritye aforesaid. CHAPTER VIII.

An Acte for the avoyding of Recoveryes suffered by Collusion by Tenantes for tearme of Lyes and

suche others.

WHERE divers persons, being seised or that had ben seised of Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes as Tenantes by the Curtesie of England, Tenantes in Tayle after possibilitie of Issue extincte, or otherwyse onely for tearme of Lyes or Lyves, or of Estates determinable upon Lyes or Lyvcs, have heretofore permitted and suffered other persons, by Agrement or Covine betwene them had, to recover the same Landes and Tenementes and other Hereditamentes against the same particuler Tenantes in the Queenes Mi'" Court, or have pmitted and suffered themselves to bee vouched by other persons, by Agreement or Covine betwene them had, in Recoveryes suffered of the same Landes Tenementes and other Hereditamentes in the Queenes Ma*'" Court, to the greate p'judice of those to whom the Reverc&n or Remaynder therof hath apperteyned or ought to apperteyne: For Remedy whereof be it enacted by the Queenes most excellent Ma,le, with the Assent of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Comons in this p>sent Parlyament assembled and by Aucthoritie of the same, That all suche Recoveries, hereafter to bee had or prosecuted, by Agreement of the Partyes or by Covine as ys aforesaid, against any suche particuler Tenaunt of any Landes Tenementes or Hereditamentes, whereof the same particuler Tenaunt ys or hereafter shalbe seised of any suche particuler Estate as ys aforesaid, or against any other with Voucher over of any suche particuler Tenant, or of any having or that had Right or Tytle to any suche particuler Estate or Tenancye as ys aforesaid, shall from henceforth, as against such person or psonnes to whome any Revercbn or Remaynder thereof, by force of any Conveyaunce or Device before that tyme had or made, shall ought or lawfully may apperteyne, and against their Heires and Successours, be clearly and utterly void and of none effect; Any Lawe or Usage heretofore had to the contrarye thereof in any wyse notwithstandinge.

Provided alway, That this Acte nor any Thing therein conteyned shall extend or bee p^judiciall to any pson or psons that shall hereafter by good Tytle recover any Landes Tenementes or Hereditamentes, without Fraud or Covine, by reason of any former Right or Tytle ; but that all and everye suche Recoverye and Recoveryes, so to be had or prosecuted uppon former Rightes or Titles, shall stand and bee in lyke Force Strenght and Effect as they were before the making of this Acte; Any Thing herein conteyned to the contrary in any wyse notwithstanding.

Provided also. That all and every suche Recoverye and Recoveryes, to bee had or prosecuted of any Landes Tentes or Hereditam'f as aforesaid, by the Assent and Agrement of any pson or psons to whom any Revertion or Remayneder thereof then shall or ought to appteyne, (so that the same Assent and Agreement do appeare of Recorde in any Court of our Soveraigne Ladye the Queenes Ma*, her Heires or Successours,) shall stand and bee in lyke Force Strength and of lyke Effect, against such pson and psones that shall so assent and agree their Heires & Suscessours, as they were before the making of this Acte; Any Thing herein conteyned to the contrarye in any wyse notwithstanding.

CHAPTER X.

An Acte to refourme the excessyve Length of Carseis.

WHEREAS within this Realme of England, Karsies called ordinarye Karsies have not nor doo not usually conteyne above Seventeene Yardes, and the fyner sort called sorting Karsies not above Eyghteene Yardes, and according to the proportion of the said Lengthes, the Weyght hathe ben lymited by the Statutes nowe remayning in force for true making of Wollen Karsies; and where the Queenes Majestie hath ben, is and ought to bee aunswered of her Majesties Customes and Subsidies of the said Karsies according to the number of Peeces or Whole Karsies, and not according to the Quantytye or Number of Yardes in everye of the said Karsies conteyned ; And where certeyne Marchaunt Straungers and others using the Trade of transporting Karsies by way of Marchaundize beyonde the Seas, have of late devised and procured to have Karsies made of muche greater Lengthes as of fyve & twentye and syxeand twentye Yardes and more, and intende as yt maye be well gathered to have them made of greater Length from tyme to tyme, by which Policie they doo not onely deceive the Queenes Majestye of One Third Part of her Customes and Subsedies due for the same Karsies, for that everye two Karsies nowe payeng Custome but for two Karsies doo by the said meane conteyne more then three Karsies that were wont to yeld Custome for three Karsies, but also the poore Artyfycers Weavers and other Woorkemen occupyeng making of the said Karsies, are lytle or nothing more considered in their Wages for making of the said Longe Karsies ; Moreover the Marchauntes of England using the Trade of bying the said usuall ordinary sortes or others, are easely eaten up and undonne by the said Straungers, for that the said Straungers conveying by Deceipte so much of her Majesties Custome, are able by selling beyond the Seas under the Englyshe Marchauntes Price, to drive all the Englyshe Marchauntes to losse, and Englyshe Subjectes makers of ordinarye Karsies are by the said subtyll Advauntage dryven from their Trade, and l;kely to bee shortly enforced to chaunge their Loumes Milles and other Instrumentes, for that no other sort of Karsies in respecte of the Gaine in deceyving her Ma1* are lykely to bee usually bought; whiche newe devyse is to the greate defrauding of her Majestye to the undoyng of her Subjectes the Englyshe Marchauntes and of the Clothiers using the makinge of Karsies, and of an infynite number of poore Famylies susteyned by Workemanshippe about the same: Bee yt therefore enacted by the Queenes Highnes the Lordes Spuall and Temporall, and the Comons in this psent Parlyament assembled, That from and after the Feaste of Saint Bartholomewe the Apostle next ensuing, it shall not bee lawfull for any pson or psons using or that shall use the Trade of making of Karsies, to make or cause to bee made any Karsies of the sort called ordynarye Karsies or any sorting Karsies, or any other Karsies, by what Name or Names soever they bee called, above the Length of Eyghteene Yardes at the most, to bee measured by Yarde, and ynche being redy made; but that all Karsies shalbe made of the said usuall Lengthes, and accordyng to the proportion of weyght lymited by the Statute in that Behalfe made and provided the fourth and fyfthe yeeres of the Raignes of the late King Phillippe and Queene Marye, upon payne that every pson or psonnes that shall make or cause to bee made any suche Karsie or Karsies of more or greater Length then Eyghteene Yardes, shall forfayte for every suche Karsie fourtye shillinges, the one Moytie whereof shalbee to the Queenes Ma,ie her Hares and Successours, and the other Moytye to him or them that wyll sue for the same by Byll Playnte or Information in any of the Queenes Ma* Courtes of Recorde, wherein no Essoigne Pteccfin or Wager of Lawe for the Defendaunt shalbe admitted or allowed.

Provided, That yf any Karsie or Karsies being purposely made to conteyne Eyghteene Yardes in Length and no more, shall by occasion happen to conteyne above Eyghteene Yardes, and being under Nynteene Yardes in Length, that the Maker or Makers of any such Karsie or Karsyes shall not incurre the Penaltye above conteyned; Any Thing before mentioned to the contrary notw^standing.

And where sundrye evyll disposed psons have defrauded the true meaning of the said last mentioned Statute made in the said xiij11' yeere, by Bondes and Covenauntes of suffering other psons to enjoye Ecclesiasticall Livinges and the Fruites therof, for that such Bondes and Covenauntes are not in Law taken to bee Leasses, althoughe in deed they amount to as muche; Bee yt therefore enacted, That all Bondes Contractes Promyses and Covenauntes hereafter to bee made, for suffering or permitting any pson to enjoye any Benefyce or Ecclesiasticall Promotion with Cure, or to take Profittes or Fruites thereof, other then such Bondes and Covenauntes as shalbee made for assuraunce of any Leasse heretofore made, shalbe to all Internes and Purposes adjudged of suche force and valydytie and not otherwyse as Leasses by the same psons made of suche Benefices and Ecclesiasticall Promotions with Cure.

And bee yt further declared and enacted, That all Leasses Bondes Promises and Covenauntes of and concerning Benefices & Ecclesiasticall Livinges with Cure, to bee made by any Curate, shalbee of none other nor better force validitie or continuaunce then yf the same had ben made by the beneficed pson himself that dimysed or shall dimise the same to any such Curate.

CHAPTER XII.

An Acte for the Repeale of a Statute made Anno Octavo of the Queenes Mau" Raigne, towching the Towne

of Shrewesburye.

WHERE at the Parliament holden at Westminster the last daye of September in the Eyght yeere of the Raigne of our Soveraigne Lady the Queenes moste Excellent Majestye, there was [an'] Acte made, entituled An Acte towching Drapers Cotteners and Fryzers in the Towne of Shrewesburye in the Countye of Salop ; And in the same Act there is conteyned Matter then supposed for the Benefyte of the said Towne of Shrewesburye, in advauncing the Corporac&n of Drapers Cottoners and Frizers of the said Towne; And it was therbye enacted, That from and after the Feaste of Easter then next ensuing, no manner pson or persons whatsoever inhabiting and dwellyng within the said Towne of Shrewesburie or the Lyberties or [Franchises'] of the same Towne, other then such as then had or then after should serve as Apprentyse in the Occupac&n or Science of Drapers, or then had ben or thereafter should bee free of the said Science or Mysterye) should occupye use exercyse or frequent the said Trade Arte Misterye or Science of buying of the said Welshe Clothe or Lyning Cottens Frizes or Playnes, nor have any Factour or Dooer for him or them in the same, nor by any Colour Engyn or Fraude buye any of the said Frizes Lininges Cottons and Playnes, uppon payne that everye pson and psons inhabiting as is aforesaid, and occupieng using or exercysing the said Trade Arte Misterye Occupation or Scyence of buying of Welshe Clothes and Lyninges, &c. and not authorised by the Acte, should lose & forfayte for every Peece of the said Clothes bought, Syxe Shillinges Eyght Pence: And where sythence the making of the said Acte, Experience hathe playnely taught in the said Towne, that the said Acte hathe not onely not brought the good Effecte that then was hoped and surmysed, but also hathe been and nowe ys lykely to bee the verye greateste cause of the impoverishing and undoing of the poore Artyfycers and other, at whose Suite the said Acte was procured; for that there bee nowe sithence the making of the said Statute muche fewer persons to sett them a woorke then before; And by restrayning all other inhabitours of the said Towne of Shrewesburye from the former lawfull Trade ever heretofore used, of buying of Welshe Clothes Fryzes Cottons Lining f and Playnes (leaving the same nevertheles free for all the Subjectes of England without any Restraynt, saving for the said Inhabitauntes of the Towne of Shrewesburye and the Lybertyes and [Fraunchesies*] of the same Towne onlye) hath ben the evident occasion of greate decaye, not onely to the sayd Towne and the

CHAPTER XIU.

An Acte for the annexing of Hexham and Hexhamshire to the Countye of Northumberland.

WHERE for the space of divers yeeres nowe past, the Queene her Highenes and her most noble and dearly beloved Father King Henry the Eyght, King Edward the Syxt her Highnes Brother, Queene Marye her late Sister, as in the Right of the Ymperiall Crowne of this Realme of England, by reason of one Exchaunge had and passed betwene the said late King Henry the Eyght and the late Reverend Father Robert Archebisshoppe of Yorke in the (’) yeere of the most noble Raigne of the said late King Henry, have ben, and her Ma"* * yet ys, seased of and in the Fraunchyse and Lybertye of Hexham and Hexhamshire lying within the bodye and middle of the Countye of Northumberland, which said Lybertye and Territorie when yt was in the Handes of the said Archbisshoppe, was comonly tearmed and named a Countye Palentyne, where in Right or Proofe there was none suche; yet by reason of that Errour, ever since and yet there hathe ben and are divers Opinyons besyde some question and doubtes, whether the said Lybertye and Territorye of Hexham and Hexhamshire should and ought to bee part of the said Countye of Northumberland, or otherwyse exempted; and whether the Dwellers and Inhabitours there, should and ought to bee justifiable and aunswere to Jusdce, as other of the said Countye of Northumberland are and ought, or not, and the lyke question and doubt yet ys and remayneth; By reason whereof not onely Plees of the Crowne and Suites betwixt Partye and Partye have suffered continuall Stayes Lettes and also have had no end of Tryall, and besydes the most and greatest Offendours to the Crowne and their Countrey have and dayly rune thither, as unto a Sanctuarye, upon hope and truste of Refuge and Safegard thereby, to the greate Coiuforte and Encouragement of many the vilest and worst Subjectes and Offendours in all the North Parties, and to the greate Offence of the Almightye, and most manyfest Hinderaunce of good Execucbn of Lawes and Justice: la and for due Remydye and Redresse of suche greate Enormyties and apparaunt Mischieves, May it therefore please the Queene her Majestie, that by her Highnes the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and [theComons in this fPsent Highe Court of Parlyament nowe assembled, that yt may bee enacted manifested and declared by aucthoritye of the same, That the said Territory Fraunchise and Lybertye of Hexham and Hexhamshire, with the Lyberties of the same, may bee ys and shalbe from hensforth taken to be within and Part Parcell and Member of the said Countye of Northumberland ; And that aswell the Plees of the Crowne, as also all Suites betwixt Partye and Partye, may proceed and have their due End and Triall within the said Countye of Northumberland, by and before the Sherife and Coroners of the said Shire, and also before the Justices of Peace, Justices of Gaole Delyverye, Justices of Assise Nisi Prius Oyer and Determiner, and other Officers, and eche and everye of them as the case shall requier, and take Effectes as any of the lyke have ben or ought to bee whiche have happened or shall here after happen within the said Countye of Northumberland; and that from hensforth the Sherife and other Officers of the Countye of Northumberland for the tyme being may have full Power and Aucthorytye to execute his or their Office, and all Processes to him or them directed, within Hexham and Hexhamshire and Lyberties of the same, in as ample and large manner as he or they maye should or ought to doe within any other Part of the said Countye of Northumberland; Any Graunt Priviledge Custom Usage Liberty or Thing els what ever heretofore made claymed used had put in ure or execuc&n or enjoyed to the contrary notwithstanding : Saving to the Baylyffe of the Lyberties or other Officers of the said Town of Hexham and Hexhamshire or the Lyberties thereof, all Lyberties and Priviledges for executing of Processe Returne of Writtes and otherwyse as they or any of them of right ought to have before the making of this Acte.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Actb for the Assuraunce of Gyftes Grauntes, &c. made and to bee made for the Relyef of the Poore in

Hospitalles, &c.

WHERE our late Soveraigne Lord of famouse Memorye King Edwarde the Syxte, by his Ires patentes dated the xxvj,h daye of June in the seventh yere of his moste gratious Raigne, did found erecte and establyshe three Hospitalles in and near to the Cytye of London, called the Hospitalles of King Edwarde the Syxte, of Christe, Bridewell, and Sainte Thomas the Apostle, and by his said Ires patentes gave and graunted power and lybertye for purchasing of Landes Tenementes and Heredytamentes for the Releife and Sustentac&n of the Poore in the said Hospitalles, as by the said ires patentes more playnelye appearethe: And whereas also our late Soveraigne Lord King Henrye the Eyght, by his ires patentes dated the Thirteenth of Januarye in the eyght and thirteth yere of his Raigne, did found an Hospitall in West Smythfeld called Lytle Sainte Bartholomeus nere London: And where divers well disposed and charytable parsons have given Landes Tenementes and Heredytamentes to the Relyef and Sustentac&n of the Poore, not onlye in the said Hospitalles but also in other Hospitalles, and as yt ys hoped many moe hereafter wyll Iykewyse charytably gyve ; and where many of suche Gyftes and Assuraunces have been and are lykely to bee made by the laste wylles of the Givers thereof, at whiche tyme for want of Councell or other Opportunityes, yt maye happen that the right name of the said Corporac&n hathe not or shall not bee truelye named or expressed, whereby maye growe some

question of the valydytye of suche Grauntes Giftes or Devises: Bee yt therefore Inacted by the Queenes most excellent

Ma^ the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Commons in this p'sent Parliament assembled and by the aucthoritye of the same, That all Gyftes Grauntes Legacyes Devyses and Assuraunces, made or to bee made of any Landes Tenementes and Heredytamentes by Wylie Feoffamentes or otherwyse, to the use or for the Relyef of the Poore in any Hospitalle nowe remayning & being in Esse, and imployed to the Relief or Maynetenaunce of the Poore in the said Hospitalles or any of them, shalbee as good and avayleable in Lawe, according to the true meaning of any suche Donor Grauntor Testator Devysor or Assurer, as yf the said Corporac&n hadd been or were in the Wrytinges or Deedes of suche Gyftes Graunte Devise or Assuraunce, or in suche laste Wylie or Testament, rightlye or

truely named j Any suche Mysnamynge Mysrecyting or not true namynge or recytinge of the said Corporac&n to

the contrarye notwithstanding.

Saving to all and every person and persons Bodyes Polytique and Corporate, their Heires and Successors, other then suche Donor Grauntor Testator Devysor and Assurer, their Heirs and Successours, all suche Right Tytle and Intereste as they or any of them have or shall have in or to any Landes Tentes or Heredytaments so given graunted devysed or assured, as yf this Acte had never been had nor made.

(1) And where in the laste Parlyament holden at Westminster, it was provided and enacted amonges other Thinges, That from thensforthe all Leasses Gyftes Grauntes Feoffamentes Conveyaunces or Estates to bee had made or suffered by any Maister and Fellowes of anny Colledge, Deane and Chapter of anny Cathedrall Churche, Maister or Gardyan of any Hospitall, Parson Vicar or any other having any Spirituall Lyving, [of1] any House Landes Tentes or Heredytamentes percell of the Possession of any suche Colledge Cathedrall Churche Hospitall Psonage Vicaredge or other Spuall Promotion, or perteyning to the same or any of them, to any parson or parsons Bodyes Polytyque or Coporate, other then for tearme of one & twentye yeres or three lyves, in manner and fourme as ys mentioned in the said Acte, should bee utterly void and of none effecte: Bee yt enacted and declared by thaucthorytye of this p*sent Parlyament That thes Woordes ( Maister or Gardyan) of any Hospytall mencioned in the said former Acte, were intended and ment of all Hospitalles Maysondewes Beadehowses and other Howses ordeyned for the Sustentac&n or Relyef of the Poore; and so shalbee expounded declared and taken for ever.

The Acts not distinguished by Roman Numerals are merely private, and have never been inserted in the Printed Collections. No Titles are entered in the Margins of the several Acts on the Roll i but it has been thought convenient to reprint the Titles in the above List at the Head of each Chapter printed.

CHAPTER I.

An Actb against the deminisheing and empayring of the Queenes Ma"" Coigne and other Coignes lawfullye

curraunt w^in this Realme.

WHEREAS the Offences of clipping rounding wasshing and fyling, for wicked Lucre or Gaines sake, of any the proper Moneys or Coignes of this Realme or the Domynions thereof, or of the Moneys or Coignes of any other Realme, allowed by proclamac&n and suffered to be currant w,hin this Realme or the Domynions thereof, by a Statute made in the fyfth yeere of the Queenes Ma"" Raigne, are taken deemed and adjudged to be Treason, and the Offendours therein, their Counsellors Consentours and Aydours lykewyse deemed and adjudged as Offendours in Treason, and being thereof lawfullye convicted or attaineted according to the due Order and Course of the Lawes of this Realme, are to suffer paynes of Deathe and to lose and forfayte all his and their Goodes and Cattayles, and also all his and their Lands and Tenementf during his and their naturall Lief or Lyves onely; as by the said Estatute thereof made amonge other Things therein conteyned more at large yt dothe and maye appeare: Sythen the making of w* good Lawe and Statute divers false and evell disposed persons, knowing that the said Lawe being as yt ys penall, ought to bee taken and expounded strickte according to the Woordf thereof, and the lyke Offencf not by any equitye to receyve the lyke punishement and paynes, have sythen the making of the said Lawe and Statute, moste wickedly devised and practised, for wicked Lucre and Gaines sake, other Artes undue Wayes and Meanes to falsifie ympayre deminishe and lighten aswell the proper Monyes and Coignes of this Realme, and the Dominions thereof, as also the Monyes or Coignes of other Realmes, allowed and suffered to bee currante w,hin this Realme and the Dominions thereof by her Ma"" Proclamac&n, to the greate Damage Losse Hurte and Deceipte aswell of her Ma'*", as of all her faythefull and loving Subjects; and more ys lyke hereafter to bee practised and done yf the same bee not speedily met w'ball: For. Reformac&n and Remedye whereof bee yt enacted declared and established by aucthorytye of this p>sent Parlyament, That yf any person or persons, of what Estate Degree or Condic&n soever hee or theye bee, shall from and after the firste daye of Aprill next comingc, for wicked Lucre or Gaines sake, by any Arte Wayes or Meanes whatsoever, impayre deminishe falsefye skale or lighten the proper Moneys or Coignes of this Realme or any the Dominions thereof, or the Moneys or Coignes of any other Realmes allowed and suffered to bee currant at the tyme of the Offence committed w,hin this Realme of England or any the Dominions of the same, by the Proclamac&n of the Queenes Ma1' her Heires or Successors, shalbe taken adjudged and deemed to bee Treason, and the Offendours therein their Counsayllours Consentours and Ayders shalbee lykewyse deemed and adjudged as Offendours in Treason, and being thereof lawfullye convicted or attaineted according to the due Order of the Lawes of this Realme, shall suffer paynes of Deathe, and lose and forfayte all their Goods and Cattayles to the Queenes Mall' her Heires and Successors, and shall also lose and forfayte to the Queenes Highenes her Heires and Successors, all their Landes Tents and Hereditametf during his or their naturall Lyes or Lyves onlye.

An Actb for the setting of the Poore on Worke, and for the avoyding of Ydlenes.

FOR some better Explanac&n and for some nedefull AddiccSn to the Estatute concerning the punishement of Vacaboundf and Releife of the Poore, made in the Session of Parlyament houlden the fourtenth yere of the Queenes MaM" Raigne; Bee yt ordeyned declared and enacted by Aucthoritye of this pPsent Parlyament, in Manner and Fourme following, That ys to saye; Firste, concerning Bastardf begotten and borne out of lawfull Matrimonye, (an Offence againste Gods Lawe and Mans Lawe,) the said Bastardf being now lefte to bee kepte at the Chardgf of the Parishe where they bee borne, to the greate Burden of the same Parishe and in defrauding of the Releife of the impotente and aged true Poore of the same Parishe, and to* the cvell Example and Encouradgement of lewde Lyes: It ys ordeyned and enacted by the Aucthorytye aforesaid, That two Justicf of the Peace, whereof one to bee of the Quorum, in or nexte unto the Limits where the Parishe Churche ys, w,hin w* Parishe suche Bastarde shalbee borne, (upon Examinac&n of the Cause and CircomstanceJ shall and maye by their discretion take Order aswell for the punishement of the Mother and reputed Father of suche Bastarde Childe, as also for the better Releefe of everye suche Parishe in part or in all; and shall and maye lykewyse by lyke discretion, take order for the kepinge of everye suche Bastarde Childe, by chardging suche Mother or reputed Father w* the paymente of Monie Weekely or other Sustentafbn for the Releefe of suche Childe, in suche wise as they shall thincke meete and convenient: And yf after the same order by them subscribed under their Hands any the said psones, viz. Mother or reputed Father upon Notyce thereof shall not for their parte observe and pfourme the said Order, That then everye suche partye so making Defaulte in not pfourminge [of1 ] the said Order, to bee committed to Warde to the Comon Gayle, ther to remaine w^out Bayle or Maineprise, excepte hee she or theye shall put in sufficient Suertye to pfourme the said Order, or els psonally to appeare at the next Generali Sessions of the Peace to be holden in that Countye where suche Order shalbee taken, and also to abyde suche Order as the said Justices of the Peace or the more parte of them then and there shall take in that Behalfe (yf theye then and there shall take any,) And that yf at the said Sessions the said Justicf shall take no other Order, then to abyde and pfourme the Order before made as ys abovesaid.

II.

Rogues shall be conveyed by Constables from Parish to Parish, until they reach the Common Gaol.

Also concerning Roges, in as muche as by the former Acte they are to bee conveyed to the Gayle or Prison by the Constable or other Officer at the Chardgf of the Parishe where suche Roge ys apprehended, For avoyding of greate Travaile and Chargf risinge thereby, manye are suffered to passe and wincked at; Bee yt ordeyned and enacted by the Aucthoritye of this p'sent Parlyament, That from henceforth everye suche Roge apprehended shalbee conveyed by the Constable or other Officers of the Parishe where suche Apprehencftn shalbee, but to the Constable Tythingman or other Officer of the nexte Towneshipe or Parishe in the nexte Hundred, and so from one Hundred to another, by the Constables Tythingmen or Officers of everye suche Towneship or Parishe w* shalbe next in every suche Hundred, the directe waye untill they shall come to the Gayle or Pryson appointed for suche Roges and Vagaboundf; And that everye suche Constable Tythingman and Officer shall accordinglye conveye suche Roge and Vagabounde under the paynes and penaltyes by the said former Estatute lymited to the Constable Tythingman or other Officer in whose Parishe suche Roge or Vagabound shalbe first apprehended.

CHAPTER V.

An Acte to redresse Disorders in Comon Infourmers upon Penall Lawes.

FOR redressinge of divers Disorders in Comon Informers, and for better Execucbn of Penall Lawes, Be yt enacted, That everye Informer upon any Penall Statute shall exhibite his Suite in proper person, and p'sue the same only by himself, or by his Attorney in Courte; and that none shalbe admitted or receyved to p'sue against any pson or personns uppon any Penall Statute but by waye of Informacon or originall Action and not otherwise, nor shall have ne use any Deputie or Deputies at all; And that uppon every suche Informacon wth shalbe exhibited, a spiall Note be made of the verye Daye Moneth and Yere of the exhibitinge thereof into any Office or to any Officer whiche lawfully may receave the same, w,howte any manner of Antedate thereof to be made; and that the same Informacon be accompted and taken to be of Recorde from that tyme forwarde and not before.

Informers on Penal Statutes shall sue by Information, &c. in Person, &c. and true Time of exhibiting each Information shall he noted thereon.

And be yt likewise enacted for the Consideration aforesaide, That no Processe be sued owte uppon anye suche -phe Prosecutor’s Informacon untill the Informacon be exhibited in fourme aforesaid; and that uppon every suche Processe shalbe Na™e Act indorsed aswell the parties name that p'sueth the same Processe, as also The statute uppon wcl‘ the Informac&n in that indorsed on Process Behalf made is grounded ; And that every Clerke makinge owte Processe contrary to the Tenor and Provision of this j^Jrnuabn. Acte shall forfayte and lose xl s. for every suche Offence; the one halfe to be to the Quenes Mat,c her Heires and Penalty, 40s. And be yt further enacted, That no Jurye shalbe compelled to appeare in any of the Queenes Ma,h’ Cowrtes at Westminster for the Tryall of any Yssue, in any suche Sute uppon any penall Lawe, for anye [suche ‘3 Offence comytted above xxx1" Miles from the Cyttie of Westni, excepte in case where the Attorney Getierall for the tyme beinge for some reasonable Cawse in that Behalf to be shewed, shall require the same to be tried at the Barre in any of the Courtes of the Quenes Ma,ic her Heires or Successo" at Westiii aforesaide; wd" Requeste shalbe noted on the backside of the Writt of Distringas thereuppon awarded, to thend the Shrieff or his Bayliffe may and shall signifie the same to the Jurye that are in suche Case impanelled.

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte againste the transporting of Leather Tallowe and Rawe Hydes out of the Realme.

WHERE in the Parliament holden at Westm in the firste yere of the Raigne of the Quenes moste Excellent Majestie, one Acte was made. That the carienge of Leather Tallowe and Rawe Hydes owte of the Realme for Marchandizes, shoulde be Fellonye; whiche Acte was made to endure but for a certeyne tyme, and afterwardes was discontinued, and sythens, viz. in the Firste Sessyon of this present Parlyament, renued to have Conrynuance for certeine yeres yet to come : And where also in the Parlyament holden in the fifthe yere of her Majesties Raigne, one other Acte was made uppon greate Advice Conference and Deliberation, concerninge Tanners Curriers Shoemakers and other Artyficers occupienge the Cuttinge of Leather, and therebie all former Actes were repealed concerninge the same ; by w* Meanes yt was hoped that the goodnes of Leather, and the excesse Pryses thereof, as also of Tallowe, shoulde have ben remedied, wrt notw^standinge daylye hathe encreased and yet doth; the cawse whereof is that beinge shipped for Forraigne Parties, [are1] transported owte of the Realme, noe Forfeyture ys geven to him or them that will sease or sue for the same: For Remedie whereof, Be it enacted by the Quene our Soveraigne Ladye, and by thaucthoritye of this present Parliament, That the said Acte made in the saide firste yere, and contynued in the firste Session of the present Parliament, shalbe repealed; and that somuche of the saide Acte made in the saide fifthe yere and the Provisoes therein conteyned, as doe or dothe concerne the transportinge of Leather or Hydes, shalbe continued and dulye put in Execution.

An Acts for the Tryall of Nisi Prius in the Countye of Midd.

WHEREAS heretofore all Yssues joyned in any of the Courts of Recorde at Westminster, tryable in the Countye of Mydd, have been usuallie tried at the Barres in the saide Courtes in Westinynster: And whereas a greate nurpher of Acc&ns have of late yeres been broughte in the saide Countie of Midd for speedynes of Triad, and that for small Causes; by reason whereof the Judges of the same Courtes have not onlye been letted and hindered in their Proceedingf in Matters of greate Waighte dependinge before them by Demurrer or otherwise, to the greate Delaye of Justice, and occasion of greate Expenses and Chardges of a number of the Quenes Ma"" moste lovinge Subjects , but also to the greate Trouble and Chardge of the Freholders of the saide Countie, who are compelled to geve daylie Attendaunce at the severall Barres of the same severall Courtes for the Triad of the saide Yssues: For Reformacbn whereof, be yt enacted by the Ouenes moste excellent Ma,ie our Soveraigne Ladye w,h thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Commons in this present Parlyament assembled, and by thauctoritie of the same. That from hencefoorth the Chief Justice of England for the tyme beinge, upon Issues joyned or to be joyned in the Courte called the Kings Benche or in the Courte of Chauncerie, the Chief Justice of the Common Plees for the tyme beinge, upon Yssues joyned or to be joyned in the Courte of Common Plees, and the Chief Baron of Thexchequer for the tyme beinge, upon. CHAPTER Xm.

An Actb concenyng the Offices fownde w>hin the Countyes Palentynes.

WHEREAS the Quenes moste Royall Mane by the Lawes and Statutes of this her Highnes Realme of England, ought to have the Custodie Wardeshippe and Mariage of the Bodie Landes and Tents of the Heyres of everie of her Highnes Tenauntf, holding of her Ma* by Knightf Service in Cheife as of her Crowne, or otherwise by Knightf Service, or of a thirde parte thereof, and also primer season and lyverie of their Lands Tenementf and Heredytamentf, as the case dothe require, aswell wthin the Countie [Palantyne'] of the Duchie of Lancaster and the Earldome of Chester, and in the Countie Palantyne of the Bishopprick of Duresme, as also [w^in *] all other places w^in the Domynions of of this her Highnes Realme of Englande and Wales: And whereas heretofore all suche Offices and Inquisic&ns as hathe been founde by vertue of Wryttf of Diem clausit extremu, or by other Wryttf or Comyssions, or Virtute Officii, concerninge Lands or Hereditamentf after the death of anye of her Mau" saide Tenauntf within the saide Countie Palantynes, are alwayes and have been returned into the Courte of the saide Duchie of Lancaster, and into Thexchequeres of the saide Countie Palantynes of Chester and Duresme, or into some suche Officf or Officers Hands therefore speciallie appoynted, and so beinge returned, there do remayne: By reason whereof, and for that the saide Offices and lnquisic&ns are not transcripted into her Ma'* Courte of Wardes and Lyveries like as other Officf and Inquysic&ns are certyfied out of her Highnes Courte of Chauncerie, her Ma‘f Tytle hath been oftentymes Ionge delayed and deferred from the knowledge of the Mr and Counsayle of the saide Courte of Wardes and Lyveres, so that sundrie tymes yt hath happened that the heyres of dyvers of her Majesties Tenauntf being w'hin age have died before Composic&n made for their Wardeshippf and Manages, and other of full Age likewise died before they have entered into Bands or payde their primer season [or *] sued their Lyveries, whereby oftentymes greate Intrusions and Arrerages of the Rents Issues and Profittf of their Lands have accrued and growen before Lyverie sued, to the greate prejudice and hinderaunce, as well of her said Highnes and other her Ma'f Progenitors for tymes heretofore passed and also to dyvers her Majesties Subjects Occupiers Farmours and Takers of the Rents Yssues and Proffittf of the saide Lands Teiitf and Heredytamentf: For spedie Remedie whereof be yt therefore enacted by the Quenes Ma"* w*1 thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this present Parlyament assembled. That all suche Inquisic&ns and Officf to be founde, from and after the firste daye of Julye nexte cominge, before anye Escheatours or Comyssioners, by vertue of any suche Writtf or Comyssion or otherwise, w,hin the saide Countie Palantynes of the said Duchie of Lancaster Chester and Duresme or anye of them, shalbe returned by the saide Eschetours and Comyssioners w^in one Monethe nexte after the takinge of any suche Office or Inquisic&n into suche place or places and to suche office and officers as heretofore they have usuallie been accustomed to be certyfied and returned into, uppon payne to forfeyte for everie defeulte xl li. to the use of our said Soveraigne Ladie her heires and successor; And that the Clerke of the said Duchie of Lancaster, the Vice Chamberlayne of the saide Earldome of Chester, and the Chauncelo' of the said Countie Palantyne of the said Bisshoppricke of Duresme, or other the saide Officers or Mynisters w,kin the saide Countie Palantynes, [of *] their Deputie or Deputies and everie of them for the tyme beinge, havinge aucthoritye to receyve any suche Office or Inquisic&n, to whose Hands any suche Office or Inquysic&n shall com to, shall certyfie or cawse to be certyfied under his or their Hands in Parchement, the trewe Transcripte of everie suche Office or Inquisic&n taken before any of the said Escheato" or Comyssioners, unto the M' of the saide Courte of Wardes and Lyveries, in suche like manner fourme and sorte as ys lymytted and appointed to the Clerkf of the Petyebagge in her Highnes saide Courte of Chauncerye to transporte the same, upon payne to forfeyte for everie suche Defeulte v li. to the use of o' saide Soveraigne Ladie her heires and successor; w"* Transcript so to be certyfied shall there remayne of Recorde in like manner and fourme to all intentf and purposes as the Transcriptf of other Officf alreadie certyfied into the said Courte by the Clearkf of the Petibage in her Majesties Highe Courte of Chauncerye are used; Anye Custome Statute Acte Proviso or Provisoes heretofore had made or used to the contrarye in any wise notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte for Refourmac&n of Jeofayles.

BE it enacted by the Qenes moste excellent Ma"* the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons of this present Parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same, That yf anye Verdite of xij Men or more shalbe hereafter geven in anye Acc6n Suite Bill Playnte or Demaunde in anye Courte of Recorde, the Judgemente thereuppon shall not be stayed or reversed by reason of any defaulte in fourme or lacke of fourme towchinge fals Lattin, or variaunce from the Register, or other Defaultes in fourme in any Wrytte originall or judiciall Counte Declarac&n Playnte Bill Suyte or Demaunde, or for wante of anye Wrytte originall or judiciall, or by reason of any impfecte or insufficient Retume of any Shiriffe or other Officer, or for wante of anye Warraunt of Attumey, or by reason of anye manner of Defaulte in Proces upon or after anye Ayde-prier or Voucher, nor any suche Recorde or Judgment after Verdicte to be geven hereafter shalbe reversed for anye the Defectf or Cawses aforesaide; Anye Lawe Statute or Usage to the contrarie notwithstandinge.

Provided alwayes and be yt further enacsed by thauctoritye aforesaide, That this Acte or anye Thinge therein conteyned shall not extende to anye Writte Declarac&n or Suyte of Appeale of Felonie or Murder, nor to anye Inditement or Presentement of Felonie Murder Treason or other Matter, nor to anie Processe upon anye of them, nor to anye Writte Bill Action or Informac&n upon anye populer or penall Statute; Anye Thinge aforesaide to the contrarie notw^standinge.

Provided also and be yt enacted by thaucthoritye aforesaide. That all Attumeyes in anye Suyte or Action in anye Courte of Recorde, shall deliver in the Warrante of Attumeyes in suche Action or Suyte wherein they be named Attumeyes, to be entered or fyled of Recorde in suche manner and fourme as heretofore by the Lawe or Statutes in that behalfe made, they shoulde or ought to have done; uppon payne to forfaytc Tenne poundes for everie suche Offence, the one moytie thereof to be to the Quenes Ma‘" her heires and successours, and thother moytie to suche Officer or Officers to whome or in whose Office the same Warrant shoulde be delyvered entred or fyled, and to suffer Imprisonment by the discrec&n of the Justicf of the Courte for the tyme being where any suche Defaulte shall fortune to be had or made, the said Tenne poundes to be recovered by Actyon of Debte Byll or Informacbn, in w* noe Essoigne Protection nor Wager of Lawe shalbe allowed.

After Verdict in a Court of Record, Judgement shall not t>c stayed or reversed for any Default in Form, or for false Latin, Variance, Want of Writ, defective Return, &c.
