CHAPTER XV.

An Acte for Refourmacon of Abuses in Goldsmythes.

WHERE certeyne evill disposed Goldsmythes deceytfullie do make and sell Plate and other Golde & Sylver Wares, to the greate defraudinge of her Matie and her good Subjects : For Remedye whereof, Be yt enacted by thauctorytie of this present Plyament, That no Goldsmythe from the XXth daye of Aprill nexte cominge, shall worke sell exchaunge or cawse to be wroughte solde or exchaunged any Plate or other Goldsmythes Wares of Golde lesse in fynesse then that of xxij Carrottf, and that he use noe Sother Amell or other Stuffingf whatsoever in anye of their Workes more then ys necessarie for the fynyshing of the same, and that they take not above the rate of xij d. for the ownce of Golde (besides the fashion) more than the Buyer shall or maye be allowed for the same at the Quenes Exchaunge or Mynte, upon payne to forfayte the valewe of the Thinge so solde or exchaunged; and that from the said xx,k daye of Aprill no Goldesmythe shall make sell or exchaunge in anye place w^in this Realme anye Plate or Goldesmithes Wares of Sylver lesse in fynesse then that of eleven ownces two penye waightes, nor take above the rate of xij d. for everie pounde waighte of Plate or Wares of Sylver, besides the fashion, more than the Buyer shall or may be allowed for the same at the Quenes Exchaunge or Mynte; nor put to sale exchaunge or sell anye Plate or Goldesmithes worke of Silver before he hath sett his owne Marke to so muche thereof as convenientlie may beare the same, upon payne to forfayte the vallewe of the Thinge so solde or exchaunged ; And yf anye Goldesmyth shall make anye Goldesmythes Worke or Plate, and the same after the said xx. daye of Aprill shalbe towched marked and allowed for good by the Wardens or Maysters of that Mysterie, and in the same there shalbe founde any Falshood or Deceipte, then the Wardens and Corporac&n of that Mysterie for the tyme beinge shall forfaite and paye the vallewe of the Thinge so exchaunged or solde; thone moytie of all wch Forfaytures shalbe to the use of the Quenes Majestie, and the other moytie to the use of suche partye greyed and susteininge losse therebie as will sue for the same in anye Courte of Recorde, by Action Bill Playnte Informac&n or otherwise, wherein no Essoigne Protection or Wager of Lawe shalbe admytted for the Defendaunte.

Finene» of Gold Plate, Ac. aa Carati:

ild. per Ounce for Workmanship.

Fineneii of Silver Plate, 11 ox. i dwts.

nd. per Pound for Workmanship.

Silver Wares shall be marked by the Maker.

If Plate marked by the Goldsmiths' Company be found deceitful, the Company shall forfeit the Value.

CHAPTER XVI.

An Acte for the Tollerac&n of certeyne Clothyers in the Countyes of Wiltes Sofiset and Glocester, to inhabite out

of Townes Corporate.

Recital of Stat.

4, y P. & M. c. y. §31. against making Clotha out of Market Towns, tec.

Clothiers in Places not Market Towni, in Wiltshire, Somersetshire, and Gloucestershire:

Recited Provision repealed as to Clothiers in the said Counties.

"X T 7" HE REAS in the Parliament holden at Westmynster in the Fowerth and Fifth yeres of the Raignes of our late V T Soveraigne Lorde and Ladie Kinge Phillippe and Quene Marie, one Statute was made, entituled An Acte towchinge the makinge of Wollen Clothes, whereby (among other Things, yt was ordeyned and enacted by thauctorytie of the saide Parliament, That from and after the firste daye of Maye then nexte cominge, no person [nor1] persons whatsoever should use or exercyse the Feate or Misterie of makinge weavinge or rowinge of Wollen Clothe longe or shorte, or Karseyes pynned Whites or playne Straytes, to thentent to put the same to sale, but onlye in a Market Towne where Clothe had comonlye been used to be made by the space of Tenne yeres then laste paste, or in a Cittie Borough or Towne Corporate, upon payne of forfayture for everie suche Wollen Cloth or Karsey made woven or rowed owte of suche Cyttie Borowgh Towne Corporate or Markett Towne, five poundes ; as by the said Acte amongest dyvers Clauses Articles & Provisoes conteined in the same more playnelye ys expressed : And Forasmuche as dyvers and sundrie psons have heretofore of longe tyme used and exercysed and at this present do use and exercyse the Feate and Misterie of Cloth makinge in the Counties of Somerset Wilteshire and Gloucester, and have to their greate Costes and Charges planted themselves and their Dwellinge Howses dispersedlye throughowte the saide Counties, and neyther in Citdes Boroughes Townes Corporate, or Market Townes, as might and maye serve moste conveniently for thuse & exercyse of the saide Feate and Mysterie, as namely aboute the Ryvers of Frome water Kingswood water the Ryvers of Aven Willibourne and Salisburie bournes, and Stroudewater, in the said Counties of Somersett Wilteshire and Gloucester and the Braunches of the same Waters; And also for that the saide Places and Waters are verie good and apt for Clothinge, together w"1 the greate number of Fullinge Mylnes and other Workehowses thereunto adjoyninge maynteyned onlye by the Clothmakinge in the Villages and Parishes thereaboutes: And Forasmuche also as a greate multitude of poore People as Weavers Tuckers Spinsters and suche like, have of longe tyme heretofore and at this present do inhabite and dwell nere unto the said Places and Waters, by meanes of the greate Clothmakinge there, heretofore and nowe used, and have been only relyved and susteyned by the same; and also for that greate inconvenience mighte ensue w^in the saide Counties of Somersett Wilteshire and Gloucester, in remoovinge and placinge of suche a Multitude in or wthin anye Cyttie Boroughe Towne Corpate, or Markett Towne, accordinge to the meaninge of the said Acte: Be it therefore enacted by the Quenes moste excellent Ma'1' wth thassent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this present Parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same, That the said Braunche and Clause of the saide Estatute as towchinge onlye the use or exercyse of the Feate or Misterie of makinge weavinge or rowinge of any Wollen Clothes, to thintent to putt the same to sale, but only in a Market Towne Cyttie Boroughe or Towne Corporate, and all and everie the Penalties and Forfeytures by reason of the saide Braunche, onlye as againste anye suche psons as hath used, or hereafter shall use and exercye, the saide Feate and Misterie of makinge weavinge or rowinge of anye Wollen Clothe wthin the saide Counties of Somerset Wylteshire and Gloucester, or any of them, shalbe from henceforth repealed and made voyde; Any Thing conteyned in the sayde Acte or in anie other Acte heretofore made to the contrary thereof in anye wise notw^standinge.

And further bee yt enacted by the aucthoritie afforesaide. That noe pson or psons nowe dwellinge or abidinge or wch hereafter shall dwell or abide w^in the saide Counties of Somersett Wilteshire and Gloucester or anye of them, onljMn Peaces usual shall from henceforth use or exercyse the said Feate and Misterie of makinge weavinge or rowinge of anye Wollen Clothe or Clothes owte of anye Cyttie Boroughe Towne Corporate or Market Towne, excepte onelie w’Mn suche Howses and Places in the saide Counties of Somersett Wilteshire and Gloucester or anye of them, as suche Wollen Clothes have been moste commonlye used to be made woven or rowed by the space of Tenne yeres nexte before the makinge of this Acte, upon payne of forfayture for everie suche Clothe made woven or rowed contrarie to this present Acte five poundes; the one Moytie of whiche Forfayture shalbe to owr Soveraigne Ladye the Quenes Ma"* her Heires and Successours, and thother Moytie to him or them that will sue for the same.

CHAPTER XVII.

An Acte for the perpetuall Mainten*nce of Rochester Bridge.

FOR the good Repayre and perpetuall Mainten*nce of Rochester Bridge in Rente, and for the good Order of the Rentes and Revenues aswell of the Landes geven for the Maynten'nce of the saide Bridge as of the Landes of auncient tyme contributorie to the Repayre of the same Bridge: Be yt ordeyned and enacted by thauctoride of this present Parliamente, That [one1] the Morowe after the generall Quarter Sessions of the Peace holden in the said Counde of Rente next after the Feaste of Easter next cominge, the Wardens and Cominalde of the Landes contributorie to the said Rochester Bridge, or as manye of them as convenientlye maye, shall assemble themselves at the Castell of Rochester, nere to the said Rochester Bridge, and there, by the moste number of their Voyces then present, to make an Election ofTwoo persons of the same Cominalde to be the Wardens of the saide Rochester Bridge, suche as then shalbe moste comonlye resident and howsekepinge wthin the saide Counde of Rente, and then not knowen to be of anye suche Debillitye or Sicknes but that they maye execute the same Office, and of twelve persons of the saide Comynalde to be Assistantf to the saide two Wardens for one whole yere, after the firste daye of Pentecoste then nexte ensuinge; and so from thenceforthe for ever at the saide daye and place a yerely Election to be made of two Wardens for the saide Bridge and of twelve Assistauntf; And the two Wardens so chosen (for that yere wherein they are to serve as Wardens) shall do their dilligent Endevoure for the Benefit of the saide Bridge, and shall receyve the Fynes Rents and Revenues of the Lands and Tefitf belonginge to the saide Bridge, and of all Contribufbn Money payable to the use of the same Bridge, and shall answere and paye owte of the same as cawse shall requyre; And everie suche of the same twoo Wardens so chosen as then shalbe there presente, shall then and there become bounde in a competente siime of Money to the former Wardens, that he his Executors or Admynistratours accordinge to the meaninge of this Statute, shall make an Accompte of all those Fynes Rents and Revenues of the saide Bridgf Lands and of all Contribuf&n Money or other Dewties whatsoever, whiche for or conceminge the saide Bridge shall come to his Handes, and shall make Payment of the Arrerages founde upon suche Accompte; And of everie suche Election of anye person to be Warden (whiche shalbe then absente) Notice shalbe given by a Letter thereof sent from one or both of the former Wardens, and delyvered at the Dwelling Howse of suche absent person elected, upon payne of fyve poundes for not delyvery of suche Letter in fourme aforesaide; Provided furthermore. That suche as be the present Fermoures of anye of the saide Lands proper belonginge to the Bridge, shall have the preferment in takinge newe Leasses, so as they will geve, for the Proffite of the saide Bridge, as muche as anye other bona fide will.

And moreover, That yf anye present Fermour not lykinge to geve as another will, shall not take a newe Lease, but another shall fortune to have the same newe Lease, that then the olde Fermoure shall for his betteringe or Buildings, have suche recompence as shalbe thought reasonable by Agrement betwene the saide Wardens and Assistauntf and the saide Fermour; and in defaulte of Agrement betwene them, then suche Recompence as shalbe thought mete by the Lorde Chauncellour or the Lorde Treasourer of Englande for the tyme beinge.

Provided also, That this Acte or anye Thinge therein conteyned extende not to alter any Thinge, but that in Accons and Suytf towchinge the Landes or Rents or other Interests and Dewties conceminge the saide Bridge, the Wardens alone, w^owte the Assistauntf or anye of the Comynaltie, be and shalbe able to sue and be sued, accordinge to the meaninge of the Statute in that behalfe made in the Ninthe yere of the raigne of Kinge Henry the Fifthe.

CHAPTER XVIII.

An Acte for the repayring of Chepstowe Bridge.

LAMENTABLIE showeth and complayneth in this present Parliament, the Inhabitauntf of the greatest parte of Sowthwales, that whereas a certayne greate Bridge of Wood called Chepstowes Bridge, ys standinge over the Water of Wye, wch parteth the Counties of Gloucester and Monmouthe, seperateth the Lordeshippe of Chepstowe aforesaide in the said Countie of Monmouth and the Lordshippe of Tyddenham in the said Countie of Gloucester, and ys the meeteste and moste necessarie Passage and Highe waye that leadeth into the partes of Sowthwales, and owte of the same to London Bristowe and other partes of Englande; w* Bridge havinge nothinge to maynteyne the same ys of late fallen to greate Ruyne and Decaye, and ys likelye daylye to falle, wherebie the saide Highe waye shalbe from henceforth utterly taken awaye, to greate noysaunce and hurte of a greate multitude of the Quenes Majesties Subjects travaylinge those partes; And albeit one Acte of Parliament was made in the twoo and twenteth yere of the Raigne of o' late Soveraigne Lorde of famous memorie Kinge Henrye the Eight, entytuled An Acte concerninge repayringe and amendinge of Bridges in Highe wayes, in w* Acte amongste other things yt ys enacted, that yf parte of anye decayed Bridge happen to be in one Shire Ryding Cittie or Towne Corporate, and the other parte therof in another Shire Ridinge Cyttie or Towne Corporate, or yf parte be w"4n anye Lymettf of any Cyttie or Towne Corporate and parte w^owte. or parte w^in one Ridinge and parte w'*in another, That then in everie suche case thinhabitauntf of the Shires Ridingf Citties or Townes Corporate shalbe charged and chargeable to amende make and repayre suche parte and porcbn of suche Bridgf so decayed as shall lye and be w,kin the Lymyttf of the Shire Ridinge or Towne Corporate wherin they be inhabited at the tyme of the saide Decayes; as by the saide Acte (amongste other Things) more playnlye doth and maye appeare: Yet for that at the tyme of the makinge of the saide Statute, the foresaide Parishes of Tyddenham and Towne of Chepstowe were not as then united and annexed to the saide Counties of Gloucester and Monmoth, but sithence in the xxvij"1 yere of the saide late Kinge Henrie Theight, by force of one Acte, intytuled An Acte for Lawes and Justice to be mynistred in Wales in like Fourme as yt ys in the Realme; and nowe by reason of certeyne Woordes conteyned in the saide laste Acte, as also by reason of greate povertye of the Inhabitantf of the foresaide Towne of Chepstowe, dyvers Questions and Doubtes have arysen howe and by what Meanes the foresaide Bridge shalbe repayred amended or newe made: For Declaractin and Explanac&n whereof, and for Remedye in the Premysses, Be yt enacted by the Quene owre Soveraigne Ladye, and by the Consent of the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and Comons assembled in this pnte Parlyament, That the Shire or Countie of Gloucester and the Shire or Countie of Monmothe shall stande for evermore chargeable for the maynten’nce repayringe amendinge and newe makinge of the foresaide Bridge, when and as often as nede shall require, viz. CHAPTER XX.

An Acte for the repayring and amending of the Bridgf and Highewayes nere unto the Cyttye of Oxforde.

FORASMUCHE AS yo' Highnes Univereitie and Cyttie of Oxford hath receyved from yo' Highnes and yor noble Progenitors greate Privileges and Prerogatives, as also the Inhabitant snd Dwellers w"4n the Compasse and Precincte of five Myles thereunto adjoyninge, as chieflie by a Statute made in the seconde & thirde yeere of Kinge Phillipp and Quene Marye, intytuled An Acte that no P'veyo' shall take anye Grayne Come or other Victual! wlbin the Compasse [and'] Precincte of sieve Myles of the saide Cyttye, and in the thirtenthe yeere of yo' Mau* Raigne hath benne renewed and enlarged; by [meanes1 ] whereof thinhabitauntf aforesaide, not onlye to themselves but to their Posteritie, by the Markettf of yor saide Cyttye, ys like to reape muche Gayne Proffitt Comodytie and Advantage by utteraunce of their Come Grayne and Victual; savinge that the Wayes Bridges and Passages leadinge from yor Highnes Manno" and other Places of this Realme to yor Highnes Cyttie (beinge for the moste parte Water Woorkes) w^in [this *3 twoo yeeres, by force of Waters are so decayed fallen down and ympayred, that yor Highnes and Subjects w" yo' and their Cariage travaylinge that waye, as others travaylinge owte of all partes of this Realme, are muche anoyed and incumbred, and thinhabitauntf there are not able w^owte greate Daunger to travell or repaire unto the saide Cyttie, or bringe to the Markettf their Come Grayne Victuall or other necessaries, to the greate Hurte of the saide Cyttye as Dearth like to ensue w^in the Universitie and Cyttie: May yt therefore please yo' Highnes that yt may be enacted by this present Pliament, That everie pson and psonnes, resiaunt dwellinge or inhabitinge w,hin the Compasse Circuite or Precinct of five Myles of yo' Highnesses Univereitie and Cyttie of Oxforde or Francheses of the same, havinge in his or their Handes or Occupacon to the use of himself or anye other the Quantytie of one Yarde Lande or upwarde in Tyllage Pasture or other Grounde, or havinge kepinge usinge or occupienge a Draught Carte Plowghe or Wayne, at his and their owne proper Costs and Chardges, shall finde and sende or cawse to be founde and sente, for and to the mendinge repayringe and upbuildinge of the decayed Bridges Wayes and Passages, scytuate henge and beinge w^in one Myle of the saide Citrie of Oxford, for everie Yarde Lande one Wayne or Drawght Carte furnished after the Custome of the Countrey w* Oxen Horse or other Cattell, with all other necessaries mete and convenient to carry Thinges for suche manner of ppose, w01 able Men to loade and unloade the same Draught Carte or Wayne ; And every other Howseholder Cottager or Laborer dwellinge or inhabitinge w,hin the foresaide Compasse Precincte or Circuite (beinge no hired S'vaunte) shall, by his or their selves or other sufficiente Labourer, havinge with them sufficient Tooles at their like proper Costs and Charges finde and sende, in and to the mendinge repayringe and upbuildinge of the decayed Bridges Wayes Cawsies and Passages, one sufficient Man or Labourer to woorke and laboure in and uppon the aforesaide decayed Premysses; And that every psonne or psonnes, that by the meaftfnge of this Acte ys chargeable with Carte Cariage Woork or Laboure, shall by the Comaundement or Comaundementf of certeyne Supervisors, hereafter to be appointed and nominated by the Vicechauncello' and Mayo' with other Justices of the UnivWie and Cyttye of Oxforde for the tyme beinge, [for4] the space of sixe whole dayes, shall do their Carriages kepe their Woorke fetch their Carriages and do their Laboure at suche place and places and in suche Woorkes as to them shalbe nomynated and appointed; And uppon payne that every psonne [and1 ] psonnes makinge defaulte abovesaide, for everie dayes defaulte or any parte thereof, shall lose and forfayte v s. to be levied and ymployed only to the mendinge of the saide Bridges and Causies.

And that yt shall be lawfull to and for the aforesaide Supervisors for the tyme beinge, for the more spedye Amendem' of the aforesaide Decayes, in suche Place and Places as by the disc recon of the Vicechauncello' Mayor or Supervisors shalbe thought necessarye, to digge or cawse to he digged within the severall Groundes of anye psonne or psonnes for Gravell Sande Rubbishe Stone or Cynder and other Things, accordinge to the Statute made in the seconde and thirde yeres of Kinge Phillippe and Quene Marye for Highe wayes; And that the aforesaide Sixe Dayes Carriages Woorkes or Laboures, accordinge to the trewe Meaninge Interne and Pporte of this present Acte, shalbe doonne finished and pfourmed, by all manner of psonne or psonnes by this Acte chargeable, betwene the Feaste of S’ John Baptiste next after this present Session of Parliament and the Feaste of All Sainctf nexte after that; And uppon twelve dayes waminge, given or sente in Wrytinge from the Vice Chauncello' and Mayor of the Cyttie of Oxford for the tyme being or from eyther of them, to the Constable or other Officer of any Boroughe Parishe Head Officer or Governor of every other Place whatsoever that by this Acte ought to serve.

And for the pfourmaunce of this Acte be yt enacted, That yf any pson or psons shall make any Defaulte as ys aforesaide, havinge not made any mariner of resonable Composicftn or Agreament for the same Defaulte, that then yt shalbe lawfull for the Vice Chauncello' and the Mayor of the Cyttie of Oxforde for the tyme beinge, or other their Officers appointed, to distraigne within any the Boroughes Townes Parishes or other Places where suche psone or psonnes dwelleth that maketh Defaulte or refuseth; And the same Distresse to leade dryve and carrye awaye, and the same to withholde till they and every of them have or shall paye the Forfaytures lymytted and appointed in this present Acte, as also the Charges of kepinge of suche Distresse so taken.

(4) Provided alwayes and be it enacted, That this Acte shall endure for the space of seaven yeres nexte ensuinge the ende of this present Pliament, and from thence to the ende of the Parliament then nexte followinge, and no longer.

CHAPTER XXI.

An Acte for the Releife and reedifyeng of the Boroughe of Newe Woodstocke in the Countye of Oxforde.

WHERE the Boroughe Towne of Newe Woodstocke in the Countie of Oxforde ys fallen into greate Poverde Ruine and Decaye, wth was woonte to be chiefelie supported by thaccesse of the Kings and Queenes of this Realme, the Quenes Ma*" noble Progenito", unto their Manno' of Woodstocke, whiche hath verie seldome happened for manye yeeres nowe paste; wch Boroughe beinge reedyfied woulde be verie necessarie for manye Artyficers of sundrie Occupacons and Misteries, yf anye vente or trafficke might there be had and maynteyned, wherebie the saide Artificers drawen thyther might lyve and maynteine themselves and their famylies: And where yt ys thought and certeynlie knowen that the free buyenge and sellinge of Wolle Yame and Clothe makinge in the saide Boroughe, beinge in the Myddeste of the Realme farre distante from the Seas, and in Cotsolde from whence greate Store of verie good Wolles are gotten, woulde be a greate advauncement and enrichinge to the same, w^owte Prejudice or Hurte to anie, and a speciall meane whereby many poore People there and in the Countreys invironinge shoulde be sett [one ‘ ] workes and releeved, as in spinninge cardinge weavinge fullinge and suche like; And forasmuche as the said Towne and Boroughe is a verie fitte place both to dispatche and make a Staple of Woolles, w* wooulde be also verie comodious and profitable to the Countrey there aboutes: Be yt therefore enacted by thaucthorytie of this present Pliament, That from henceforth yt shall and maye be lawfull to and for all and everie pson & psons fireelie to buy and sell, wthin the saide Boroughe of Newe Woodstocke, all manner of Woolles and Yames brought or to be broughte into the saide Boroughe uppon the usuall Markettf and Fayre Dayes, and the same Woolles and Yames to use and imploye to their beste Profite and Advantage; Any Statute or Statutes Usage or Prescription heretofore had made or provided to the contrarie in any wise notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER XXIII. (')

An Acte of Two Fyfteenes and Tenthes and One Subsydye graunted by the Temporaltye.

Motives of this Subidy

Grant of Two whole Fifteenths and Tenths on Personalty, payable in Two Years; deducting j?6,oooo out of each for Poor Towns, &c.

II.

Collectors shall be appointed by the Members of Parliament for the several Shires, he.;

r[E View of the long and present Miseries in other Realmes so nigh us on every Side, (most mighty and redoubted Sovereigne,) causeth Us your Majesties humble Subjects to enter into due Consideration of the great Blisse and Happinesse which God hath and doth dayly powre out upon Us, in most bountifull and fatherly sorte, under your Majesties most happy Rule and Govemement over Us, and to acknowledge Our selves infinitely bound to render unto him with all Humblenesse of Heart and Soule our most hearty Praise and Thanks for the same, as also to desire the blessed [Countenance * 3 of his fatherly Protection over Us, by preserving your Majestie in Health and Safety against the Attemptes of all your Enemies, who cease not to practise against your Highnesse his annoynted, and our most gracious Sovereigne, intending thereby to bereave us of that Benefite of Peace which maketh all our Hearts joyfull, the same being (as it is) so clearely joyned with your Majesties safety, as without which all Peace to us could bee but Warre, and all Tranquilitie most cruell Bloodshed; And therefore considering with Our selves the inestimable Treasure of our so happy Peace, for the Mainteinance and Continuance whereof no small Portion of Treasure hath beene employed, which oft times falleth out to bee no lesse well bestowed, (a Thing we finde by experience) in preventing Mischiefes before they breake out to open Flame, then in quenching them when they are once kindled; And againe, laying before ouer Eyes the great Malice borne to those Kingdomes which make profession of the Gospel, and what Wee may undoubtedly looke for being forwarned thereof sundry Wayes, for the preventing whereof it is no lesse requisite to have some Masse of Treasure in Redinesse then to have a Preservative against Poyson; And considering the great and excessive Charges which your Majestie hath beene at divers wayes farre surmounting your Majesties Ordinary Revenewes, the same having growen partly through the dearenesse of the Time (a Thing which each of us findeth in our private Expences) but chiefely through sundry extraordinary Accidentes which the Necessitie of your State required to be provided for; Web your Majesties most humble loving and obedient Subjectes the Lords Spirituall and Temporall and the Commons of this present Parliament assembled, meaning and freely intending of our selves, as we are bound aswell in all dutifulnesse, to make some Declaration Shew and evident Testimonie how much and how infinitely Wee thinke our selves bound and indebted to your Majestie, for your singuler Care and Watchfulnes for the Preservation of Us our Lives and Goods, being in no wise able to render suche due and thankefull Recomptnce for the same, as hath beane and is duely deserved; As also that your Highnesse may have in Redinesse such Provision and Store as whereby any Enemie whatsoever that shall hereafter attempt against your Majesties most Royall Person of State, may speedily and easily bee resisted and our Lives and Liberties preserved, as your Majesties most humble obedient and loving Subjects, humbly on our Knees beseech your Highnesse to accept in good part our redy Willes in this our Present of One Subsidie and Two Fifteenes, which Wee offer unto your Majestie; most humbly beseeching the same to measure it not by your Highnesse Disertes, but with your accustomed Clemencie, respecting alwayes not the Gift but the Hearts of the Givers; And for the Acceptation thereof to cause it to bee by your Highnesse the Lords Spirituall and Temporall and the Commons in this present Parliament assembled, and by order of the same enacted as followeth: Be it enacted, That your Highnesse, toward the great Charges of this your Realme, and for the better Mainteinance of your Royall Estate, shall have by Authority of this present Parliament, Two Fifteenes and Tenthes, to bee payed taken and levied of the moveable Goods Cattells and other Things, usuall to such Fyfteenes and Tenthes to be contributory and chargeable, within the Shires Cities Boroughs Townes and other Places of this your Majesties Realme, in maner and forme aforetime used; excepte the summe of Twelve thousand pounds thereof fully to be deducted, that is to say, Six thowsand pounds of either of the said whole Fifteenes and Tenthes, in Reliefe Comfort and Discharge of the poore Townes Cities and Boroughes of this your said Realme, wasted desolate or destroyed or over greatly impoverished, after such Rate as was and hath afore this time beene had and made to every Shire, and to be divided in such maner and forme as heretofore for one whole Fifteene and Tenth hath beene had and divided ; And the said Two Fifteenes and Tenthes (the Exception and Deduction aforesaid thereupon had deducted and allowed) to be payed in Maner and Forme following. That is to say; The first whole Fifteene and Tenth (except before excepted) to be payed to your Highnesse in the Receipt of your Highnesse Exchequer before the fourth day of lune next comming; And the said second Fifteene and Tenth (except before excepted) to bee payed to your Highnesse in the said Receipt of your Exchequer, before the tenth day of May which shall be in the yeere of our Lord God M. D. lxxvij.

D. lxxvij. accordinge to the tenor of this Acte: And if defaulte of any suche certifying be had or made in forme as is aforesaid, then the Lord Chauncellour of England, or Keeper of the Great Seale for the time being, shall immediately after name and appoint Coliectours for the Collection of eyther of the sayde Fifteenes and Tenthes, in such^like manner and forme as the sayde Knights of the Shire Citizens of Cities and Burgesses of Boroughs should have done, and as aforetime hath beene used; The which said Coliectours and every of them so to be named and appointed as is aforesayde, shall have Allowance upon their Accomptes for their Fees Wages and Rewardes for the Collection of the said Fifteenes and Tenthes, in as large manner and forme as any Collectour or Coliectours of any Fifteene and Tenth have had att any season in time paste; And that the Barons of the Queenes Exchequer for the time being shall and may from time to time award suche processe for the speedy Payment of the said severall Fifteenes and Tenthes against the Collectour and Coliectours of the same, as by their Discretions shall be thought convenient.

Provided allwayes and be it enacted by the authority of this present Parliament, That the said Lord Chauncellour or Keeper of the Great Seal for the time being, Knights of the Shire, Citizens of Cities Burgesses of Boroughs Townes and other Places, having authority by this present Act to nominate the said Coliectours of or for the Collection of the said severall Fifteenes and Tenthes, shall upon their Nomination and Election had and made, take by authoritie of this present Parliament, sufficient Recognizance or Obligation of every person so by them to bee named, to be bound to the Queenes Majestie in the double sum of the sum of their Collection, & to be endorsed upon such condition, that if the same Collector or Collectors of the said First Fifteene and Tenth, and likewise the Collector or Collectors of the said Second Fifteene and Tenth, doe truely content and pay to the use of the Queenes Majestie in her Receipt of the Exchequer for the said First Fifteene and Tenth, at or before the said fourth day of June next comming, and for the said Second Fifteene and Tenth at or before the sayde tenth day of May which shall bee in the yeere of our Lord God M. D. lxxvij. so much of the said summe of Money allotted and appointed to his Collection, as the same Coliectours shall have collected and gathered, doe likewise after the sayde fourth day of the said moneth of June and the said tenth day of May in every of the said two yeeres, content and pay to the Quenes Majesties use at the same Receipt, the Residue of his Collection and Charge, within one Moneth next after such time as hee shall have gathered and collected the same Residue, That then the sayd Recognizance or Obligation to be voyd, or else to stand in his full strength and power; which Recognizance or Obligation so taken, the same Knights of the Shire Citizens and Burgesses and every of them taking any such Recognizance or Obligation, shall certifie and deliver to the Lord Treasourer and Barons of the same Exchequer before the same fourth day of June and tenth day of May in every of the sayde two yeeres, upon paine of forfeiture of x li. to the Queenes Highnesse for every Recognizance or Obligation so to bee taken and not certified ; And that every such Collectour upon Request to him made, shall make and knowledge the same Recognizance or Obligation accordingly, upon like paine of forfeiture of x li. to the Queene for his refusal! thereof; And that the Treasourer and Barons of the Exchequer for the time being, upon the payment of the same Collection at the said Dayes, shall cansell and deliver the said Recognizance or Obligation to the said Collectour or Coliectours withoute anye other Warrant, and without any Fee or Reward to bee payed to any person for the same.

And it is further enacted, That yf the sayd Taxours or Assessours shall not dulye behave themselves in their Inquirie Taxation Assessement or Certificate, but shall affectionately corruptly or partially demeane themselves in that behalfe, in such wise that the Commissioners shall by their Consideration deeme them Offenders worthy of punishment for not dooing their Dueties therein, That then foure or more of the Commissioners in that Countie for this Subsidie, shall have power and authoritie by their discretions, either to charge the sayde Assessours upon theire corporall Othes for the better service aforesayd in that behalfe, or els by their discretions to taxe and set upon every of the sayd Assessours for their Misdemeanours in that behalf, such a Fine or Paine as they shall thinke good, so that it exceede not the summe of Tenne poundes ; And the same Fine or Paine at their discretions to estreate into the Courte of Exchequer ; every which Fine so taxed and set by foure of the sayd Commissioners or more and being estreated, with the Scedule and Bookes of that Limite, shall be levied and answered to the Queenes use, in like manner and forme to all internes and purposes as any other summes that shall be taxed and become due by vertue of this Statute and Acte of Subsidie, and not in any other wise or maner: And if any person certefied or rated by vertue of this Acte, whether he be Commissioner or other, to any maner of value, doeth finde himselfe grieved with the same presentment sessing or taxing, and thereupon complaine to the Commissioners before whom he shall be called sessed or taxed, or before two of them, before the same Taxation be certified into the Court of Exchequer, That then the sayd Commissioners, or two of them, shall by all waies and meanes, examine particulerly and distinctly the person so complayning, upon his Othe, and other his neighbours by their discretions, of every his lands and Tenements above specified, and of every his Goods Cattelles and Debtes above mentioned; And after due examination and perfect knowledge thereof had and perceived by the sayde Commissioners, or two of them, which shal have power by Authoritie aforesaid, the sayd Commissioners or two of them to whom any such Complaint shall be made, by their discretion, upon the Othe of the said person so complayning, may abate defaulke encrease or enlarge the same Assessements according as it shall appeare unto them just upon the same Examination; And the same summe so abated defaulked encreased or enlarged, shall be by them estreated in forme as hereafter ensueth: And if it be prooved by witnesses or by the parties owne Confession or other lawfull waies or meanes, within a yeere after any such Othe made, that the same person so taxed and swome was of any better or greater value in Landes Goodes or other Things above specified at the time of his said Othe, that then every such person so offending shall loose and forfeit to the Queenes Majestie so much in lawfull Money of England as he the same person so sworne was set at or taxed.

And also it is enacted by the same Authoritie, That every person to be rated at the said Taxation as aforesaid, shall be rated taxed and set, and the summe on him set to be levied, at such Place where he and his Familie at the time of the same presentment to be made, shall keepe his House or Dwelling, or where he then shall be most conversant abyding or resyant or shall have his most resorte at the time of the said Certificate to be made, and no where els; And that no Commissioner for this Subsidie shall be rated or taxed for his Goods or Lands but in the Shire or other Place where he shall be Commissioner; And that if any pson chargeable to this Acte at the time of the same Assessing happen to be out of this Realme or out of Wales or farre from the Place where he shall be knowen, then he to be set where he was last abyding in this Realme or within Wales, and after the substance value and other profites of every person, to be knowen by the Examination Certificate or other maner of wise as is aforesaid: And that the sayd Commissioners, or as many of them as shall be appointed by the Queenes Majesties Commission or Commissions, shall after the Rate and Rates aforesaid, cause every person so to be set rated and taxed according to the Rate of the substance and value of his Lands Goods Cattels and other profites chargeable by this Acte, whereby the greatest and most best summe or summes according to his most substance by reason of this Acte might or may be set or taxed: And that every person taxed in any County or Place other then where he is most resiant or hathe his Familie, or in any Countie or Place other then where he is a Commissioner for this Subsidie yf he be a Commissioner, upon Certificate made to the said Court of Exchequer, under the Hands and Seales of two Commissioners for this Subsidie in the same Countie or Place where such person is most resiant or hath his Familie, or where he is a Commissioner for the Taxation and Paiment of this Subsidie, testifying such his moste Resiauncie having of Familie or being a Commissioner, shall be a sufficient Discharge for the Taxation of that person in all other Places, and of and for all other Summes of Money upon such person so set and taxed, save only the Taxation made in that Countie or Place from which such Certificate shalbe made as is aforesaid and for the summe of Money upon suche person there assessed or taxed; And that such Certificate without any Plea or other Circumstance shall be a sufficient Warrant, aswell to the Barons and Auditor and Auditors of the said Court of Exchequer as to all and every other Officers to whom the Allowance thereof shall appertaine; paying for such Discharge and Allowance, only six pence and no more.

And it is also enacted by the said Authority of this present Parliament, That every of the said High Collectoure which shall accompt for any part of the said Subsidy in the said Exchequer, upon their several Accompts to be yeelden, shalbe allowed at every of the said Payments of the said Subsidy for every poundc lymited to his Collection, whereof any such Collectour shalbe charged and yeeld Accompt, sixe pence, as parcell of their Charge; that is to say, Of every pound thereof for such person as then have had the particular Collection of the Townes and other places as is aforesaid specified in his Collection, two pence; and other two pence of every pounde thereof, every of the said Cheiff Collectours or their Accomptants, to reteine to their owne use for their labour and charge in and about the premisses; and two pence of every pound residue, to bee delivered allowed and payd by the said Collectour so being thereof allowed, to such of the Commissioners as shall take upon them the businesse and labour for and about the premisses; that is to say, every Collectour to pay that Commissioner or Commissioners which had the ordering of the writings of and for the said Subsidy, where the said Collectour or Collectours had their Collection, for the expences of the said Commissioners so taking upon them the said busynesse, and labour of their Clarkes writing the said Precepts and Extractes of the said Collections; the same last two pence of every pound to be divided amongst the said Commissioners, having regard to their labour and businesse taken by them and their said Clarkes in and about the premisses ; for which part so to the said Commissioners attaining, the said Commissioners sixe five foure three or two, or as many of them as shalbe thereunto appointed by the Queenes Majesties Commission, and every of them, joyntly and severally for his and their said part, may have his remedie against the said Collectour or Collectours which therefore beene or might have beene allowed, by Action of Debt, in which the Defendant shall not wage his Law, neither Protection neither Injunction or Essoigne shalbe allowed.

And that no person now being of the number of the Company of this present Parliament, nor any Commissioner, shalbe named or assigned to be any Collectour or Subcollectour or Presentour of the said Subsidy, or of any part therof, nor no Commissioners shalbe compelled to make any Presentment or Certificate, other then in the Queenes Majesties said Exchequer, of for or concerning the said Subsidies or any part or parcell thereof; and likewise that no other persons that shalbe named and assigned to bee Commissioners in any place to and for the execution of this Act of Subsidy, bee or shalbe assigned or named Head Collectours of any of the payments of the said Subsidy, neither of any part thereof; and that every such person or persons which shalbe named and appointed as is aforesaid to bee Head Collectours in and for the first payment of this Subsidy, shall not bee compelled to bee Collectour for the second payment of the said Subsidy, nor for any part thereof: And the said Collectours which shalbe assigned for the Collection of the said Subsidy, or for any part thereof, and every of them, bee and shalbe acquired and discharged of all maner Fees Rewardes and of every other Charges in the Queenes Majesties Exchequer or elsewhere, of them or any of them, by reason of that Collection Payment or Accompts, or any thing concerning the same to bee asked; and that if any person receive or take any Fees Rewards or Pleasures of any such Accoinptant, that then hee shall forfeit to the Queenes Majestie for every peny or value of every peny so taken, five shillings, and suffer Imprisonment at the Queenes Majesties Pleasure.

And after the Taxing and Assessing of the said Subsidie (as is aforesaid) had or made, and the said Extractes thereof in Parchment unto the Collectour in maner and forme before rehearsed delivered, the said Commissioners which shall take upon them the execution of this Act within the limittes of their Commission, by their Agreementes shall have Meeting together, at which Meeting every of the said Commissioners which then shall have taken upon them the execution of any part of the said Commission, shall by himselfe or by his sufficient Deputie, truely certifie and bring forth unto the said Commissioners named in the said Commission, the Certificate and Presentment made before him and such other Commissioners as were limited with him in one Limit, so that the same Certificate may bee accompted and cast with the other Certificates of the other Limits within the same Commission ; and then the said Commissioners and every number of them unto two at the least as is aforesaid, yf any bee in Life, or their Executours or Administrateurs of their Goods, if they then bee dead, shall joyntly and severally as they were divided within their Limittes, under their Seales by their Discretion, make one or severall Writings indented conteining in it as well the Names of the said Collectours by the Commissioners for such Collection and Accomptes in the Exchequer and payment in the same Receipt deputed and assigned, as the grosse and severall summes written unto every such Collectours to receive the saide Subsidie; And also all Fines Amerciaments and other Forfeitures, if any such by reason of this Act happen to bee within the Precinct and Limit of their Commission, to bee certifyed into the Queenes Majesties saide Exchequer by the saide Commissioners; so that none of the said Collectoure so certified in the saide Exchequer, shall be compelled there to accompt or to bee charged, but onely to and for the summe limited to his Collection, and not to or for any summe limited to the Collection of his Fellow, but every of them shall bee severally charged for their part limitted to their Collection: And yf the saide Commissioners joyned in one Commission among themselves in that Matter cannot agree, or if any of them bee not ready, or refuse to make Certificate with other of the same Commissioners, That then the same Commissioners may make severall Indentures in forme aforesaid of their severall limits or separations of Collectoure within the limits of their Commission, upon and in the Hundreds Wards Wapentakes Lathes Rapes or such other like Divisions within their said severall limits of their Commission, as the Places there shall require to be severed and divided, and as to the same Commissioners shall seeme good, to make Divisions of their limits or Collections for the severall Charges of the same Collectours; Provided alwaies and be it enacted by the Authoritie aforesaid. That the Inhabitants of the Parish of Saint Martin, called Stampford Baron, in the Suburbes of the Borough and Towne of Stampford in the South part of the Water there, called Welland, which hereafter shall be contributorie to the payment of this present Subsidie graunted to the Queenes Majestie her Heyres and Successours, shall be assessed rated and taxed for this time by such Commissioners which shall be appointed for the taxing rating and sessing of such Subsidie within the Countie of Lincolne, and shall be for this time contributory and pay the said Subsidie to the Collectour or Collectours which shall be assigned and appointed for the levying and gethering of the same with the Aldermen and Burgesses of the said Borough and Towne of Stampford.

Provided alwaies, and be it further enacted by the Authoritie aforesaid, That all and every person and persons having Mannours Lands Tenements and other Hereditaments chargeable to the payment of the Subsidie graunted to the Queenes Majestie by this Act, and also having Spirituall Possessions chargeable to her said Majestie by the Grant made by the Cleargie of this Realme in their Convocation, and over this, having Substance in Goods and Cattels chargeable by this said Act, that then if any of the said person or persons be hereafter charged assessed and taxed for the said Mannors Lands and Tenements and Spirituall Possessions, and also assessed charged and taxed for his or their Goods and Cattels, that then he or they shalbe only charged by vertue of this Act for his and their said Mannors Lands Tenements Hereditaments and Spirituall Possessions, or onely for his said Goods and Cattels, the best thereof to be taken for the Queenes Majestie, and not to bee charged for bothe or double charged for any of them; Any Thing in this Act conteined to the contrary in any wise notwithstanding.

Provided also. That all Letters Patterns granted by the Queenes Majestie or any of her most noble Progenitors to any Cities Boroughes or Townes within this Realme, of any manner of Liberties Priviledges or Exemptions from the Burden and Charge of any such Grantes and Subsidies, which be at this present time in force and vayleable, shall remaine good and effectuall to the said Cities Boroughes and Townes hereafter, according to the purports thereof, though the Inhabitants of the same shall upon the greate and weightie Consideration of the Grante abovesaid, [before this*] charged and contrybutory, in like manner forme and sort as other Citties Boroughes and Townes which be not in any wise privileged but by this Act charged.

Provided alwaies and be it enacted by the Authoritie aforesaid, That no Orphan or Infant within the Age of twentie-one yeeres, borne within any of the Queenes Majesties Dominions, shall be charged to any Payment of this Subsidie, for his or her Goods and Cattels to him or her left or bequeathed ; Any Thing in this Act conteined to the contrary notwithstanding.

Provided also, That this Act nor any Thing therein conteined, shall not extend to the Goods or Lands of any Colledge Hall or Hostell within the Universities of Oxford and Cambridge, or any of them, or to the Goods or Lands of the Colledge of Wynton founded by Bishop Wickham, or to the Goods or Lands of the Colledge of Eaton next Windsor, or to the Lands Tenements or Revenues onely assigned or appointed for the Sustentation and livings of the poore Knights, founded in the Castle or Colledge of Windsor by our late Soveraigne Lord King Henry the Eight, or to any of the Goods or Cattels of the said Knights or any of them, or to the Goods or Lands of any common Free Grammer Schoole within this Realme of England or Wales, or to the Goods of any Reader Schoolemaister or Scholler, or any Graduate resiant or remaining for Studie, without Fraud or Covin, without any of the said Universities and Colledges or Townes of Cambridge and Oxford or Suburbes of the same, or any of them, or to any their Servants daily attendant upon any of them, nor to the Goods of any Officer Minister Aimes Man or Servants belonging to any of the said Universities Colledges Halles or Hostels, and dwelling and resiant within the said Universities or either of them, or within either of the said Townes of Cambridge and Oxford and the Suburbes of the same, without Fraud or Covin; Nor to the Goods and Lands of any Hospitall Measondue or Spittelhouse prepared and used for the Sustentation and Releefe of poore People; Any thing in this Act conteined to the contrary in any wise notwithstandinge.

Provided also, That the said Grant of Subsidie or any Thing therein conteined, doe not in any wise extend or be prejudiciall or hurtfull to the Inhabitants or Resiants at this present time within the Five Ports Corporate, or to any of their Members incorporate or united to the same Five Ports, or to any of the same Five Ports, of or for any part or parcell of the said summes graunted in this Parliament of the said Inhabitants now resiant, or any of them, to be taxed sett asked levied or paid ; but the said Inhabitaunts or Resiants in the saide Five Ports and their Members be and shall be of and from the said Graunt and Payment of the saide Subsidie, during there Resiance there and no longer, clearely acquited and discharged; Any Matter or whatsoever thing in this present Act had or made to the contrary notwithstanding.

Be yt likewise enacted, That Justices of Oier and Terminer and Justices of Assise and of Gaole Delyverye in their severall lymittes, shall have power to enquier heare and determine of all Offences againste this Statute, and Justices of Peace in their open Quarter Sessions of Peace shall have power by vertue of this Acte to enquier heare and determine of all Offences againste this Acte, (excepte Treason and Misprision of Treason) : Provided alwaye, that everye pson guiltie of any Offence againste this Statute, other then Treason and Misprision of Treason, which shall before he be thereof indicted, or at his Arrainement or Tryall before Judgement, submit and conforme himselfe before the Bisshop of the Diocesse where he shalbe resident, or before the Justices where he shalbe indicted araigned or tried, (havinge not before made like submission at any his Tryall being indicted for his firste lyke Offence,) shall uppon his Recognicion of such Submission in open Assies or Sessions of the Countie where suche person shalbe resident, be dischardged of all and everye the said Offences againste this Acte, (excepte Treason and Misprision of Treason,) and of all Paynes and Forfeytures for the same.

Provided also, That everye pson whiche usuallye on the Sundaye shall have in his or their Howse the Devine Service which ys establyshed by the Lawe in this Realme, and be thereat himselfe or herselfe usuallye or most comonlye p*sent, and shall not obsdnatelye refuse to come to Churche and there to doe as ys aforesaid, and shall also sour tymes in the yeare at the leaste be p*sent at the Devyne Service in the Churche of the Pishe where he or she shalbe resident, or in some other open Comon Churche or suche Chappell of Ease, shall not incurre any Payne or Penahie lymyted by this Acte for not repayringe to Churche.

And be yt likewise enacted and declared, That everye Graunte Conveyaunce Bond Judgement and Execuc&n had or made since the beginninge of this Session of Parliament, or hereafter to be had or made, of covenous Purpose to defraude any Interest Right or Title, that maye growe to the Queene or to any other pson by meane of any Conviction or Judgement, by vertue of this Statute or of the said Statute of the said xiij yeare, shalbe and be adjudged to be utterlye voide, againste the Queene and against suche as shall sue for any parte of the said Penalties in fourme aforesaid.

Provided allwaye, That yf any Peere of this Realme shall happen to be indicted of any Offence made Treason or Misprision of Treason by this Acte, he shall have his Triall by his Peeres as in other lyke cases is accustomed.

Provided also, That neither this Acte nor any Thing therein conteyned shall extend to take awaye or abbridge the Aucthorite or Jurisdice&n of the Eccleiasticall Censures for any Cause or Matter, but that the Archebisshoppes and Bisshoppes and other Ecctiasticall Judges maye doe and proceed as before the makinge of this Acte they lawfullye did or mighte have done; Any Thinge in this Acte to the contrarye notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER II.

An Acte against sedicious Wordes and Rumors uttered againste the Queenes moste excellent Majestie.

WHEREAS in and by the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme, alreadye made and ordeyned againste sedicious Wordes and Rumors uttered againste the Queenes moste excellent Ma"e, there ys not sufficient and condigne Punishement provided for to suppresse the Malice of suche as be evell affected towardes her Highenes : Bee yt therefore enacted by the aucthoritie of this psent Parliament, That yf any person or persons, after thend of sortie dayes next ensuinge the end of this psent Session of Parliament, shall advisedlye and with a malicious Intent, of his or their owne Imaginac&n, speake any false seditious and slaunderous Newes Rumors Sayengs or Tales againste our said moste naturall Soveraigne Ladye the Queenes Majestie that nowe ys, that then all and everye suche pson and psons so offending, being thereof lawfullye convicted or attainted in fourme hereafter in this psent Acte expressed, shall for everye suche firste Offence, eyther be in some Market Place within the Shire Cittie or Boroughe where the sayd Wordes were or shalbe so spoken, set openlye upon the Pillorie by the Sheriffe or his Ministers, yf yt shall fortune to be without any Cittie or Towne Corporate, And yf yt shall happen to be within any Cyttie or Towne Corporate, then by the principall Officer or Officers of suche Cittie or Towne Corporate, or his or their Ministers, and there to have both his Eares cut of; or at the Eleccbn of the Offendour, paye two hundreth poundes to the Queenes Highenesses Use in her Majesties Receipte of the Exchequer, within two monethes next after the Judgement gyven of his said Offence, and also shall suffer Imprisonment by the Space of syxe monethes after suche his or their Conviction, without Bayle or Maineprise.

And be yt further enacted by the aucthoritie aforesaid, That all and everye person and psons which after thend of the said sortie dayes shall advisedlye, and with a malicious Intent againste our said Soveraigne Ladye, reporte any false seditious and slannderous Newes Rumors or Tales, to the slaunder and defamac&n of our said Soveraigne Ladye the Queenes Ma"1 (that nowe ys), of the speaking or reporting of any other, that then all and everye suche person or psons so reportinge, being thereof convicted and attainted in fourme hereafter in this Acte expressed, shall for every suche firste Offence, eyther be in some Market Place within the Shire Cittie Boroughe or Towne where the said Wordes were or shalbe so reported, set openlye upon the Pillorie by the Sheriffe or his Ministers, yf yt shall fortune to be without any Cittie or Towne Corporate, and yf yt shall happen to be within any Cittie or Towne Corporate, then by the principall Officer or Officers of suche Cittie or Towne Corporate, or his or their Ministers, and there to have one of his Eares cut of; or at the Election of the Offendour, paye two hundreth Markes to the Queenes Highenesses use in her Mau" said Receipte of the Exchequer, within two Jdonethes next after the Judgement given of his sayd Offence, and also shall suffer ymprisonment by the space of three monethes after suche his or their Conviction without Bayle or Maineprise.

And be yt further enacted by thaucthoritie aforesaid, That yf any pson or persons, once lawfully convicted for any of the Offences aforesaid, do afterwards eftsones offende in any of the Offences aforesaid, that then everye suche secound Offence to be deemed and adjudged Felonye, and the Offendour and the Offendors therein to suffer suche paynes of Deathe and Forfeyture as in case of Fellonye, without any Benefitte of Cleargie or Sanctuarye to be alowed unto the Offendour in that Behalfe.

And be yt further enacted by the aucthoritie aforesaid, That yf any pson or persons, after the ende of the sayd fortye dayes, eyther within this Realme or in any other the Queenes Dominions, or in any other place out of the Queenes Dominions, shall advisedlye and with a maliciouse intente againste our sayd Soveraigne Ladye, devyse and wrighte prime or setforthe, any manner of Booke Ryme Ballade Letter or Writing, conteyning any false sedicious and slaunderous Matter to the Defama£6n of the Queenes Ma‘" that nowe ys, or to the encoraging stirring or moving of any Insurrection or Rebellion, within this Realme or any the Dominions belonging to the same, or yf any pson or psons, after thend of the said sortie dayes, eyther within this Realme or other the Queenes Dominions or in any other place out of the Queenes Dominions, shall advisedlye and with a maliciouse intent against our said Soveraigne Ladye procure or cause any suche Booke Ryme Ballade Letter or Writing to be written printed published or set forth, and the said Offence not being punishable by the Statute made in the xxv'h yeare of the Raigne of King Edwarde the Thirde, conceminge Treason or Declarac&n of Treason, or by any other Statute wherebye any Offence ys made or declared Treason, that then everye suche Offence shalbe demed and adjudged Felonye, and the Offendors therein beeing thereof convicted and attaineted, shall suffer suche paynes of Deathe and Forfeyture as in case of Felonye ys used, without any Benefitte of Cleargie or Sanctuarye to be alowed unto the Offendour in that Behalfe.

And for that divers persons wickedlye disposed, and forgetting their Duetie and Allegiaunce, have of late not onlye wisshed her Ma"" Deathe, but also by dyvers meanes practised and sought to knowe howe longe her Highenes should lyve, and who should raigne after her Decease, and what Chaunges and Alterations shoulde therebye happen; To the entent that suche Mischeifes and Inconveniences as maye thereby growe in the Comon Weale, to the greate Disturbance of the same, maye be cut of and pVented; Be yt also enacted by the aucthoritie aforesaid. That yf any person or psons, of what Estate Condic6n or Degree soever he or they bee, at any tyme, after the ende of the said

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte for the fortifieng of the Borders towardes Scotland.

FORASMUCHE as greate Care hath byn heretofore taken for Maynetenaunce of good Strength and Force upon the Borders and Frontiers against Scotland; and to the end that Inhabitauntes and Ten*ntes there might bee better able and more encouraged for the Defence of the same Borders, when any occasion should bee offered in that Behalfe, all Chardges of Subsidies and Taxes have byn forborne to bee layed or chardged upon the said Inhabitauntf; & for lyke respecte yt hath byn heretofore also used in divers Places within the Counties of Northumberland Cumberland Westmerland & the Bisshoppricke of Durham, that dyvers and a greate parte of the Inhabitauntes there have enjoyed their Tenementes and Farmeholdes in dyvers favorable sortes and formes of Tenure; And for that the Queenes Mau* hath of late yeares byn oftentymes infourmed, by Reporte and Certificat of her principall Officers havinge Chardge of her Borders, that the Force of her said Borders both of Horsemen and Footmen are greately decayed, and lykelye daylye to growe weaker by manye occasions, and amonge other by Decaye and Ruine of sundrye the Habitaf&ns of those Borders, whereby the number of the auncient Inhabitauntes able for Service have byn deminished, and that parte of the same Habytac&ns Tenauncyes & Farmes have byn reduced rather to pasturing of Cattell then to the Maynteyn*nce of Men of Service; And that also in some partes the Ten*ntf and Inhabitauntes themselves have demynished their owne Strength, by deviding

And to that end yf yt shall appeare to the said Comissioners or suche syxe of them as ys aforesaid that the Faulte of the said Ruynes or Decayes have byn onelye in the Lordes and Owners or their principall Officers, or in the Officers and Fartnours of her Ma"" Mannors Landes or Tenementes or any their Assignes, then the said Comissioners or suche syxe as ys aforesaid shall order commaunde & enjoyne as well her Ma" Officers Farmors or their Assignes, as others the Lordes and Owners and their Officers or Farmours, to reedifye or repayre the same Tentes and Howses of Habitacbn, and speciallye the capitall Howses and Barnekins within a convenient tyme at their owne Chardges, with restoring lyke quantities of Landes thereunto as with the same hath byn occupied in the said twentie seaventh yeare of King Henrye the Eyght, and shall sett paynes for everye defaulte of suche reedifieng or restoring in reasonable tyme, not excedinge one hundreth Markes for everie suche defaulte; And yf they shall fynde defaulte of Furniture of the Ten*ntes with Horse Weapon or Armour according to their Dueties then they shall by perswasion in Respecte of the Queenes Ma'1" Service and in Defence of their Natyve Countrye, treate with suche Lordes and other whom yt maye conceme, and the Freeholders Leassees or Tenauntes, for order to be taken by their mutuall Assentes for the renewing and contynuaunce of the said Service; and for wante of reasonable Conformitie on eyther part, maye enjoyne the said Lordes and all others under them, and also all the Queenes Ma"'* Officers Farmors and their Assignes, to give suche helpe as the said Comyssioners or suche syxe as aforesaid shall thincke fytt, towarde the enhabling of the said Ten*nte or Tenauntes to bee furnished according to the auncient duetye of the said Tenement, and to take order howe the said Tenaunte shall therebye be furnished and able for Service, and so to see that the same bee duelye executed ; and the said Comissioner shall take Bondes in good sommes to her Ma‘‘" use, of everye suche person of whome yt shall be requisite that the saide auncient Duetye of suche Tenementes respectyvelye shalbee furnished kept and executed, on payne of reasonable Forfeytures, not exceding fourtye pound for everye Defaulte, and shall assesse Fynes and set downe Paynes for suche Defaultes or wantes of Furniture as shall in that Behalf bee requisite; And yf the unhablenes of the saide Tenauntes shall be found to have growen or to growe hereafter by their owne default or Wilfulnesse, without just occasion, The said Comissioners or suche syxe of them as ys aforesaid, shall order injoyne and directe the said Tenauntes within some reasonable spedye tyme to fumishe themselves with Horse Armour and Weapon, or with Armour and Weapon, according to their auncient Usage and their uttermoste reasonable Abilytie, at their owne Chardges, without any Contribution of the Lordes but at their owne good Willes, upon payn to be expelled by the Lord Owner or Superiour Farmors or their Assignes, which so expelling shall place in suche holding or forme another Tenaunte that shalbe furnished and readye for suche Service as ys aforesaid, or else shall within one moneth gyve notice to the Comissioners or to the Warden of the same Marches of his not placing of suche Ten*nte, upon suche payne as the Comissioners or suche Syxe of them as ys aforesaid shall assesse, not exceding one hundreth markes; and the said Comissioners or Warden after suche Notice given, shall place one other Tenante sufficient for the Services aforesaid, and in her Ma" Landes by the Officers of the Revenewe, within some tyme to bee lymited: And the said Landlordes Owners Superior Farmors or their Assignes, and also her Ma'"* Officers, to bee also injoyned and bound upon some payne to cause the same to bee executed, and that a newe Ten*nte shalbe placed sufficiently furnished to hold the same: And further where yt shall appeare that within the space of thirtye yeares any Tenement or Habitacbn of Householde, which have mayneteyned any Horsemen or Footemen by auncient Usage or Service towardes the Frontiers, have byn by Tenauntes and Owners themselves or by any other meanes divided into sondrye Habitacbns, or the Landes thereunto belonginge distributed to other Tenauntes, whearebye any one principall Tenement so devided, or the same Tenemet with the Lande therewith nowe occupied, shall not bee able to mayneteyne the Inhabitaunte thereof to bee furnished according to the auncient Duetie of Service, That in suche cace the said Comissioners or suche Syxe of them as ys aforesaid, shall take order that for the p'sent tyme the psons which shall have the Use and Pfitte of any Part of the same Tenementes, or of the said Landes so withdrawen from the said principall Tenement, during the tyme of their p'sent Tearmes shall yearely contribute unto the principall Tenaunte there resyding to bee readye and furnished for the said Service, some reasonable yearelye Ayde by Money, or otherwise towardes his Furniture meete for Service.

CHAPTER V.

An Acte towching Yron Milles neere unto the Cittie of London and the Ryver of Thames.

WHEREAS by reason of the late Erection of sondrye Iron Milles in divers Places of this Realme, not farre distaunte from the Cittye of London & the Suburbes of the same, or from the Downes and Sea Costes of Sussex, the necessarye Provision of Wood, aswell Tymber fytt for Building and other uses, as also all other felleable Woodes serving for Fewell, dothe daylye decaye and become scant, and will in tyme to come become muche more scarcer; by reason whereof the Prices are growen to bee verye greate and unreasonable, and in tyme to come will bee muche more yf some Remedye bee not pvided, to the greate Domage not onelye of the Inhabitauntes of the said Cittye of London and the Suburbes of the same, but also to all others the Queenes Ma"" moste lovinge Subjectes having occasion daylye from all partes of the Realme to repayre unto the same and the Places abovesaid; For Remedye whereof, bee yt therefore enacted by the Queenes moste Excellent Ma'* the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Comons in this p^sent Parliament here assembled, and by the aucthoritie of the same, That no pson or psons, from and after the Feaste daye of the Natyvitye of Saint John the Baptiste nexte coming, shall converte or ymploy or cause to bee converted or employed to Cole or other Fewell, for the making of Iron or of Iron Mettell in any Iron Milles Fumes or Hammer, any manner of Wood or Underwood nowe growinge or whiche hereafter shall growe within the Compasse and p>cincte of xxij myles from and aboute the Cyttye of London or the Suburbes of the same, or within xxij myles of the River of Thames from Dorchester in the Countye of Oxforde, downewardes the said River of Thames, nor within sour miles of the Foote of the Hilles called the Downes betwixte Arundell and Pemsey in the Countye of Sussex, nor within sour myles of any of the Townes of Winchelsey and Rye, nor within two myles of the Towne of Pemsey, nor within three myles of the Towne of Hastinges in the said Countye; upon payne to forfeyte for everye Loade of Woode so to bee employed or converted into Cole or other Fewell, for the makinge of Iron or Iron Mettell in any Iron Mille Furnace or Hammer as ys aforesaid, Fowrtie Shillinges of lawfull Money of England, the one halfe of all whiche Forfeytures to bee to our Soveraigne Ladye the Queenes Ma" and to her Heires and Successors, and the other moytie to him or them that will sue for the same by originall Writte Byll Playnte or Information, wherein no Essoigne Protection or Injunction or Wager of Lawe shalbee admitted or allowed.

Provided allwayes, That this Acte shall not extend to any Woodes growing or to growe in any suche parte of the Weildes of Surrey Sussex or Kent, within the said twentye two miles of the said Cittye of London & the Ryver of Thames, as ys distaunte above eyghtene miles from the Cyttye of London and eight myles from the said River of Thames.

And be yt lykewyse further enacted, That fromhenceforth no newe Iron Woorkes shalbee erected within twentye two miles of the said Cyttye of London, nor within fourteene myles of the Ryver of Thames, nor within sour myles of the Downes aforesaid, or of the said Townes of Pemsey Winchelsey Hastinges or Rye, upon payne of One hundreth poundes of lawfull Money of England lykewyse to bee recovered and employed as ys aforesaid.

Provided also, That this Acte nor any Thing therein conteyned, shall extend to any Woodes or Underwoodes nowe standing or growinge, or which hereafter shall stand or growe, in or upon any Landes of Christopher Darrell Gentleman, in the Parishe of Newdigate, within the Weilde of the Countye of Surrey; whiche Woodes of the said Christopher have heretofore ben and be by him ^served and coppysed for the use of his Iron Woorkes in those Partes.

CHAPTER VI.

An Acte for the repayring of Dover Haven.

H°rboPair'ff)the "TX7 WHEREAS the Marchauntes of this Realme, and other passing thorowe the narrowe Seas, susteyne yerely greate

a Tonnage Duty"' ’ ▼ domages for want of convenient Harbour upon the Coast of the said narrowe Seas, whereunto they maye

of|d. andD^uesof enter to avoyde immynent Daunger of Tempestes Pyrates or the comon Enemye in time of Warre; Her Ma,ie myndyng of Sea-Coal and°n to provide for their Safetye, understandyng by the Lordes of her Honorable Privye Counsell and other, that Dover made^payable was the moste convenient place for Harbour, and that skilfull Men have contrived a probable Plat, and undertaken for Seven Years. the fynishing and perfecting thereof for a competent summe of money; In accompli..ing whereof, aswell her Majestie of her Highenes Lyberalitye, as the Inhabitauntes of the said Towne of Dover to their Abilitye, have alreadye bestowed greate sommes of money in and about the same: Nowe for the better furtheraunce and fynishing thereof, Be it enacted by the aucthoritye of this p>sent Parliament, That for everye Shippe Vessell or Crayer, whereof any of her Ma0* Subjectes shalbee Owners or parte Owners, of the Burden of Twentye Tonnes or upward, loading or discharging within this Realme, and passing to or fro any forren Countrey, during the space of seaven yeares next commyng from sortie dayes after the end of this Session of Parliament, there shalbee payed for everye suche Vopge, by the Master or Owner of suche Shippe Vessell or Crayer the summe of iij d. for everye Tonne of the Burden of suche Vessell or Crayer (excepte Vessells laden with Seacoale or Grindstones) & for everye Chadron of Seacoale or Grindstone, Peny halfepeny; the same to bee payed unto suche Customer or Customers or Collector of Customes or Subsidies with whome the entrye shalbe made, or their Deputies within this Realme, from whence suche Shippes shall come, or where suche Shippe or Shippes or any of them shall arrive, before they loade or unloade suche Goodes within the Realme, taking of the said Customer Officer or Deputye a Writing testifyeng the Receipte thereof to the said use, for which Writing he shall paye nothing; The said sommes so to bee collected, to bee payd over by suche Customer or Officer to the Receipte of her Mati" Exchequer, and to bee from thence delivered to the use aforesaid, by Warraunte of the Lord Treasurer or Chauncelor of the Exchequer for the tyme being, without further Warraunte from her Ma*; the Accompt of the number of the said Tonnes to bee made according to the entrye of everye suche Shippe Vessell or Crayer in the Custome HowSe: And that no Entrye of suche Vessell shalbe receyved or allowed in any Office of her Ma"c' Customes or Subsidies, without true Information by the Othe of suche Owner Master or Shipper, concerning the Burden of suche Shippe Vessell or Crayer, nor without or before payment of the Summes aforesaid by the Shipper Master or Owner of suche Shippe Vessell or Crayer, of which payment the said Maister Owner or Shipper shall have Allowaunce of the Marchauntes according to the rate of the Goodes in suche Shippe Vessell or Crayer by waye of Average; And that everye Customer or Officer in whose wilfull defaulte the said somes shall not bee truelye collected and aunswered as ys before appointed, shall forfeyte to the use aforesaid Tenne Times as muche as so shall not bee collected or aunswered by his wilfull Default, to be recovered by the Maior and Jurates of the Towne of Dover to the said use, against suche Customer or Officer by Accon of Debtc in any Courte of Recorde, In whiche Acc&n no Essoyne Protection or Wager of Lawe shalbe admitted or allowed.

CHAPTER VII.

An Acte for the encrease of Mariners, & for the mainten*nce of Navigac&n.

Evili resulting from Importation of foreign-cured Salt-Fish;

No Subject or Denizen shall import foreign-cured Fish or Herrings, on Penalty of Forfeiture thereof.

WHERE the Marchauntes and Fyshemongers of divers places of this Realme have, for their private Gaynes, gone and sent into other Countryes and forreine Realmes, and there ingrossed into their Handes greate Nombers and Quantitye of Fyshe taken by Alienes and Straungers, being in goodnes farre inferiour to the Fyshe taken by Englyshemen in the Island Voyages, and for the buying of the same Fyshe have conveyed and carried greate Masses of Money forth of this Realme, and have victualled and furnished this Realme with forraine Fyshe and Herring, the Subjectes whereof have byn accustomed in tymes paste to serve the same with Fyshe and Herringes gotten by their owne Travell, and divers other forraine Regions & Countries; by reason of whiche unnaturall Dealinges of the said Marchauntes and Fyshemongers, and usuall eating of Fleshe on the accustomed and usuall Fyshe dayes, there be of late decayed, not onelye the number of two hundereth sayle and more of good and serviceable Shippes which yerely traded to Island for taking of Fyshe in this Realme usuallye solde, but also a greate nomber of Mariners and Seamen fitt for the Service of her MaUt and her said Realme for the Defence thereof in tyme of Warres: For redresse whereof Be yt enacted by the Queenes Ma,ie our Soveraigne Ladye the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Commons in this p>sent Parliament assembled, and the aucthoritye of the same. CHAPTER Vm.

An Acte for the true melting making and working ofWaxe.

WHERE by the goodnes of God this Land doth yeeld great plentie of Honye and Waxe, as not onelye (' ) dothe suffice the necessarye uses of the Queenes Mau' and her Subjectes to be spent within this Realme, but also a greate quantitie to be spared to be transported unto other Realmes and Countreys beyonde the Seas by waye of Merchaundize, to the greate Benefite of her Malle and the Realme; And yet nevertheles a greate parte of the Waxe made and melted within this Realme hathe byn founde to bee of late verye corrupt, by reason of the deceyptfull mixture thereof; and the Makers and Sellers of Honye also have not onelye used to put the said Honye in Caske of deceyptfull Assize, but have used also deceyptfull mixtures of the same : Be yt therefore enacted by the Aucthoride of this Psent Parliament, That everye person within this Realme or the Dominions of the same, which shall after the Feaste of Pentecost next ensuing, in the making and melting of Waxe, by any waye or meanes use or practise or cause to bee used and practized any manner deceypte, by myxture and mingling the same with Rosen Tallowe Turpentyne or any other deceyptfull thing, to the intent to sell and utter the same or offer the same to bee solde or uttered for Waxe to any person or persons whatsoever, shall forfeyte and lose the same mingled or corrupted Waxe; And yf the same corrupted Waxe shall happen to bee solde before suche Faulte and Corruption shalbe founde, that then the said Melter Myngler or Corrupter Causer or Procurer thereof, shall forfeyte for everye pounde. Two Shillinges ; whereof the one Halfe to the Queenes MaUc, the other Halfe to the Partye deceyved, yf hee will sue for yt, or any other Person that will sue for the same in any of the Queenes Mau" Courtes of Recorde.

And to the intent that the Offendors in these kind of deceyptes maye bee the better and sooner knowne and found out, Be yt enacted by the aucthoritie aforesaid. That everye Melter and Maker up of unwrought Waxe, shall have for himselfe a Stampe or Marke of the Breadeth of Sixe Pence, wherein Two Letters shalbee playnelye graven, signifieng his Name and Surname, and with the same shall stampe everye Piece of Waxe, to bee printed or stamped Triangle in three places, uppon the outsyde of the upper parte of everye piece so melted and cast; upon ’he payne to forfeyte the valewe of everye piece or cake solde or offered to bee solde, and not so stamped or marked.

And bee yt further enacted by the Aucthoritie aforesaid. That no maner of person ne persons within this Realme or the Domynions thereof, shall from the said Feaste of Pentecos’e, melt myxe worke or sell any maner of wrought Waxe, Stuffe or Wares wrought with Waxe, as in Lightes Staftorches Red Waxe or Sealing Waxe Booke candle Searing candell Searing of dead Corpes Lynckes Greene Waxe Red Waxe, or any other worke or thing whatsoever to be done or wrought with Waxe to be put to sale, but with good holsome pure and convenient Stuffe meete in suche wares or worke in convenient quantytie to bee used ; And that everye person or persons, that shall worke or sell suche Stuffe or wares of Waxe, have a Marke Stampe or Seale to set on his or their Worke by him or them wrought or solde ; to the intent that yf any deceipte bee used or done, it maye be knowne who were the

Workers thereof, and suche person or psons as shalbe founde or knowne to worke or sell or to sale put any

suche false Waxe or Wares wrought with Waxe to bee put to sale, shall forfeyte and lose the same corrupted or deceyptfull Waxe and Wares j the one halfe to be to the Queenes Ma’" her Heires and Successors, and the other to the Partye deceyved, yf hee shall sue for the same (*) by Acc6n of Debte Byll Playnte or Informacbn in any the Queenes Ma"" Courtes of Recorde, wherein no Essoyne Protecc&n or Wager of Lawe shalbe allowed.
