deceyved yf hee shall sue for the same, or otherwise to him or them that will sue for the same as ys aforesaid.

And that all Barrells Kilderkins and Firkins fylled with Honnye by the Maker and Fyller shalbe marked with two letters standing for his Name and Surname, eache Letter of an Inche and a halfe of length at the leaste, burnt upon the head of the Caske with a hote Yron, upon (J ) payne to forfeyte vjs. viijd. for everye Barrell Kilderkine Firken or Caske sould or offered to be soulde, and not so marked; and that yf any person or persons doe or shall, after the xxiiij Daye of Auguste next coming after the Ende of this Session of Parliament, fill and sell or cause to bee filled or soulde or offered to be solde, any Barrell Kilderkine or Fyrkyn with Honny, for or in the Name of a Barrell Kilderkine or Fyrkine, conteyning lesse then Thirtye two Wyne Gallons the Barrell, Syxtene Wyne Gallons the Kylderkine, and Eyght Wyne Gallons the Fyrkine, Everye person and persons so offending, shall forfeyte and lose for everye Halfe Gallon so lacking, v s. of Englyshe money: And everye person and persons that shall corrupte the Honny so solde or to bee soulde with any deceyptfull myxture, shall forfeyte the Barrell or Vessell and Honye therein conteyned ; the one moytie whereof to bee to our Soveraigne Ladye the Queenes Ma'", and the other to him or them that will sue for the same as aforesaid.

CHAPTER X.

An Acte for the preservacon of Fesauntes and Partridges.

WHERE the Game of Fesauntes and Partridgf is within thes fewe yeres in manner otterlye decayed and destroyed in all partes of this Realme, by meanes of suche as take them with Nettes Snares and other Engins and Devices, aswell by daye as by night; and also by occasion of suche as doe use Hawking in the beginning of Harvest, before the younge Fesauntf and Parteridgf be of any bygnes, to the greate Spoyle and Hurte of Come and Grasse then standing and growing in the Feildf: For Reformacbn thereof Bee yt enacted establyshed and ordeyned by the Queene our Soveraigne Ladye, the Lordes Spuall and Temporall, and the Comons in this p>sent Parliament assembled, and by the aucthoritye of the same, That no manner of person or psons of what Estate Degree or Condic&n soev*, shall at any tyme or tymes, from and after the firste daye of Aprill next ensuing, take kill or

destroye any Fesauntes or Parteridgf, with any manner of Nettes Snares Ginncs Engins Rowsting Lowffing or

other devices whatsoev5 in the Night tyme; upon payne of forfeyture for everye Feasaunte so taken killed or

destroyed contrarye to the true meaning of this Acte the some of twentye shillingf, and for everye Partridge so

taken killed or destroyed the some of tenne shillingf : the whiche said Penalties & Forfeytures yf everye person or persons doe not paye within tenne dayes next after his or their Conviction, then to have one monethes ymprisonment without Bayle or Maineprise; and further over and besydes suche forfeyture or ymprisonment, to put in bonde with good suerties for the space of two yeeres, that he shall not take kyll or destroye any Partridgf or Fesauntes contrarye to the true meaninge of this Acte, the same Bonde to bee taken by some Justice of the Peace of the Countye where the said Offence shalbe comitted ; The one halfe of whiche said severall Forfeytures to bee to the cheife Lorde or Lordes of the Liberties Lordshippes or Mannors upon and in which the same shalbee soe taken killed or destroyed, And the other moytie to suche person or persons as will sue for the same in anye of her Ma'" Courtes of Recorde by Byll Plainte or InformaC&n, In whiche Sute no Essoigne Protecc&n or Wager of Lawe shalbe alowed: Provided allwayes, that yf suche person to whome the one Halfe of the said Forfeyture ys appointed for the taking killing or destroyeng of Parteridges and Feasauntes contrarye to the tenour and true meaning of this Acte, shall dispence with Lycence or peure any taking killing or destroyeng of any Partridges or Feasauntes contrarye to the fourme of this Acte, That then all suche Forfaytures and Penalties as suche pson or psons shoulde have by vertue of this Acte, shalbe to the Poore of the Parishe where suche taking killing or destroyeng shalbe comitted ; And that to bee levied or recovered in maner and fourme aforesaid by any one of the Churchewardens of the pishe were the Offence shalbe comitted.

And bee yt likewise further enacted by the aucthoritie aforesaid, That no manner of pson or psons from and after the said firste daye of Aprill, shall hawke or with his Spaniels hunt in any Ground where Corne or other Graine shall then growe, (excepte yt bee in his owne Grownd,) at suche tyme as any eared or codded Corne or Graine shalbe standing and growing upon the same, nor before suche tyme as suche Corne and Graine shalbe shocked cocked hiled or copped; upon payne of forfeyture for everye tyme that he shall so hawke or hunt as aforesayde, (without the Consent of the Owner of the Come or Graine,) to suche pson or psons as shalbee Owner of the said eared or codded Come or Grayne, fortye shillingf, and the same to bee levied or recovered in manner and fourme aforesaid.

CHAPTER XI.

An Acte for the reedifieng of Cardiffe Bridge in the Countie of Glamorgan.

WHEREAS the Bridge latelye standing upon the River of Toffe neere the Towne of Cardyffe, being an auncient Boroughe in the Countye of Glamorgan in Sowthwales and the onlye cheife Shiretowne of the same Countye, ys psentlye in utter Ruine and Decaye, and so hath contynued by the space of three yeres last past and more: By reason whereof divers the Queenes Ma"" Subjectes not onelye of that Countye and Neyghbourhood but also many Straungers travayling to and thoroughe the said Towne, being the onelye comon Porte Waye to all the rest of Southwales aforesaid, have utterly perisshed, and divers others hardlye escaped, to the great terror and ymminent pill of all suche as have occasion to travayle that waye, and also to the ympoverisheing and Hinderaunce of bothe the said Towne and Countrye thereabout ( and adjoyning thereunto, yf speedye Remedye bee not provided in that Behalfe ; And notwithstanding dyvers good pfitable Lawes and Statutes have byn heretofore in suche Cases moste charitablye provided, and especiallye one Acte intituled An Acte concerning repayring and amending of Bridgf in Highe Wayes, made at the Parlyament holden by progac&n at Westm the xvj daye of Januarye in the xxij yeare of the Raigne of our late dreade Soveraigne Lorde of famouse Memorye King Henry the Eyght, yet suche Doubtes and Ambyguities hath risen betwene the said Towne and Countye, towching certeine Woordes and Sentences in the same Statute, that more Money was lyke to be spent, in the explaning and determining of the same, then happelye might have suffised to have reedified the said Bridge; which being by this present Parham1 duelye considered, with the poore Estate of the said Towne of Cardyffe and the Unhabilytye thereof to pfourme so greate a Chardge, thoughe of Right the building of the said Bridge had properlye belonged unto them without all Doubte or Controversie : Bee yt therefore enacted and establyshed by the Queenes moste excellent Ma"' the Lordes Spuall and Tcmporall the Commons in this p>sent Parlyament assembled and by the aucthorite of the same, for the avoyding of further Controvlsies, That the said 1'owne and Countye shall joynctlye togeather after the rate and ^portion herein specified pceed to the reedifieng of the said Biidge, (that ys to saye) that the Countye shall allwayes bestowe fyve partes of the Chardgf thereunto belonging, and the Towne of Cardyffe one parte, and so for everye fyve poundes payable by the Countie by this Acte, the Towne of Cardyffe and I.ybries of the same shall allwayes stand chardged with Twentie shilling^, untill the whole summe be defrayed and the Bridge newelye reedified and builded.

And to the intent that overlonge Delaye maye not be used in setting forwardes of so necessarye and charitable a Worke, and also that the Countye maye have all necessarye and convenient Assistaunce in that Behalfe : Bee yt lykewise enacted by lyke aucthoritie. That the said Bridge shalbe whollye builded and finished within the space of two yeres next after the End Dissoluc&n or ^rogation of this psent Session of Parliament; upon payne of forfeyture of the some of One hundreth powndes for everye yeare after the said two yeares that the said Worke or Bridge shall happen to bee behind unfinished and unpfourmed, whereof the Countie shall alwayes lose and paye fourescore poundes, and (1) Corporac&n or Towne of Cardiffe twentye powndes ; The moytie whereof shalbe to the Queens Ma"% her Heires and Successours, the other moytye to him that will sue for the same in any the Queenes Ma"" Courtes of Recorde by Action of Debt Byll Playnte or Informac&n wherein no Essoigne Pteccon or Wager of Lawe shalbee admitted or allowed; And that all other Boroughes Corporacons and Lybties within the sayd Countye of Glamorgan (the Towne of Cardyffe and Libties of the same onelye excepted) shalbe Contributors and beare their ratable and reasonable Portions towardes the same, joyntlye and togeather with the Countrye (*) of Glamorgan.

And for the speedye levyeng of all suche somes of Money as shalbee requisite and necessary in this Behalfe, Bee yt hereby enacted by the aucthoritie aforesaid, That the Justices of Peace of the Countye aforesaid, or any sour three or two of them whereof one to bee of the Quorum, out of the Lybties of the said Towne of Cardyffe, and the Maior and Bayliffes or any Two of them within the said Towne Jurisdice&n and Lyberties of the same, shall herebye have full Power and Aucthoritie at all tymes hereafter and from tyme to tyme as often as neede shall requier, untill the said Bridge shalbee fullye reedified, to rate and assesse the Countye aforesaid, with the severall Hundreds and everye Towne Corporate Parishe Village and Hamlet within the same, 8c everye Inhabitaunte and Dweller within everye 8c any of them, to suche reasonable sume and somes of Moneye as to them shalbee thought

Definition of the Street to be paved.

CHAPTER XIII.

An Acte for the ynninge of Earith and Plumsted Marshe.

WHERE in the fyfte and eyght yeares of the Raigne of our moste excellent Soveraigne Ladye Queene Elizabeth (1) two severali Statutes were made towching the ynninge and fencing of certeyne Groundes and Marshes lyeng in the Parishes of Earithe Lysnes and Plumsted in the Coumie of Kent, then comonlye knowne by the Names of Earith Lysnes and Plumsted Marshe, from the Water and Flood es of the River of Thames, and for the Partic&n and Division of the said Groundes and Marshes which so shoulde happen to bee ynned fenced and wonne within certeyne tymes therein lymited, with dyvers and sondrye other Clauses and Braunches in the said two severali Statutes made towching the said Groundes and Marshes, as by the same more fullye appeareth; Amongest which said Clauses and Braunches, yt ys by and in the said Statute made in the said eight yere of the Raigne of our said Soveraigne Ladye, amongest other Thinges enacted, that it shoulde and might bee lawfull to John Baptista Castilion one of the Groomes of the Queenes Ma"" privye Chamber, John Gresham, Frauncys Robinson, Richarde Younge, Symon Horsepoole and Henrye Maye, their Heires and Assignes, and to everye other their Servauntes Factours Deputies Laborers and Woorkemen and to everye of them, at the Costes and Chardges of the said John Baptista, John Gressam, Frauncys Robinson, Richard Younge, Symon Horsepoole and Henrye Maye their Heires or Assignes, at all and everye tyme and tymes after the Tenth daye of Marche then next ensuing, during the tearme of eyght yeeres then next following, to inne fence and winne the Residue of all and singuler the Groundes and Marshes aforesaid, then surrounded and overflowne with Water, or any parte or parcell of them or any of them, at their Willes and Pleasure; and to laboure worcke and travaile from tyme to tyme during the said tearme of eyght yeares, in about and upon the ynning fencing and wining of any parte or parcell of them or any of them; as by the same Statute made in the said eyght yeare more fullye and playnlye appeareth : Since the makinge of whiche said Statute, the said John Gresham lawfullye constituted one Thomas Allen to bee his Assignee, and the said Henrye Maye lykewyse constituted one Walter Fissher to be his Assignee, to and for the [foresaid J] Affayres; And Where forasmuche as syxe yeares parcell of the said eyght yeares were almoste expired the eyght daye of Maye in the fourtenth yeere of the Raigne of our said Soveraigne Ladye, and that the ynnyng fencing and winninge of the said Groundes and Marshes was a huge Charge, and requiered so muche Laboure as that yt coulde not bee fynished without longer tyme ; And for that duringe the tyme of Restraynte betwene this Realme and the Lowe Countryes, Workemen moste fytte for that purpose coulde not bee had by any meanes, and for that also the said Groundes and Marshes, being once ynned fenced and wonne woulde bee greatlye profitable to the Comon Wealthe by the occasion of greate Numbers of Cattell that might ther bee kepte; CHAPTER XIV. (■)

An Acte of a Subsidie graunted by the Cleargye.

WHERE the Prelatf and Cleargye of this Province of Canterburye, have moste lovingelye and liberallye for certeyne Considerac&ns, gyven and graunted to the Queenes moste Excellent Ma'*, a Subsidye of Syxe Shillingf of the Pounde, to bee taken and levyed of all and singuler their Promoc&ns Spirituall w,hin the said Province, during the terme of three yeres nowe nexte ensuinge, in suche certeyne manner and forme and with such Exceptions and Provisions as bee specyfied and conteyned in a certeyne Instrument by them thereof made and delyvered to the Queenes Highenes under the Seale of the moste Reverende Father in God Edmunde nowe Archebisshoppe of Canterburye and Primate of all Englande; W1*1 Instrumente ys nowe exhibited in this p'sent Parliament to bee ratified and confirmed : The Tenour whereof ensuethe in these Woordes:

The Prelates and Cleargie of the Province of Canterburye beinge lawfullie congregated and assembled together in a Convocation or Synode, consideringe their bounden Duetyes to yo' Ma'" their moste natural)' and gracyouse Soveraigne Ladye, and havinge in remembraunce the manifolde and ample Benefittf whiche theye daylye receyve, not onlye by yo' moste gracyouse and goodlye Governemente, wherebye theye bee conserved in Peace and Quietnes, and so more able to serve God and intende to their Office and Vocac&n, but also, and that moste cheifelye, by the settinge for the and advauncynge of Goddes moste hollye Worde and his sincere and true Religeon in this yo* Realme, and abolyshinge of all forraine Power contrarye to the same; Consideringe also aswell the greate Chardges wherew,b yt cannot bee but that your Ma’* from tyme to tyme ys lyke to bee burthened in defendinge and pservinge this yor Realme wlh other yo' Highenesse Dominions, as also the greate Chardges wherew*" yor Ma" hathe byne in Irelande and pntlye ys chardged, by reason of Popishe Mutynies and Attemptes to Thoverthrowe of the true Religeon and yo' Highenesse Estate, as muche as suche Practises eyther coulde or canne pervayle: In Consider ac&n of the p>misses and for a true Declaration of their bounden Duetyes good Hartes and Mindes towardes yo' Ma,ic, w*1’ one uniforme Agreement Accorde and Consent together w,h moste hartye good Wyll, have gyven and graunted, and by these psentf doe gyve and graunte to yo’ Highenesse yo' Heires and Successo", One Subsidye in manner and fourme followinge, That ys to saye; That everye Archebisshopp Bisshopp Deane Archedeacon Provest Maister of Colledge pbendarye Parson Vicar, and everye other parson and psons of whatsoever Name or Degree hee or theye bee w,hin the Province of Canterburye enjoyenge any Spuall Promoc&n or other Temporall Possession to the same Spirituall Promoc&n annexed, nowe not devided nor separated by Acte of Parlyament or otherwise from the Possession of the Cleargye, shall paye to yo1 Highenes yo' Heires and Successo", for everye Pounde that hee maye yerelye dispende by reason of the said Spuall Promoc&n, the somme of Syxe Shillingf: And for the true and certeyne value of all the Promoc&ns and everye of them wherof the payment of this Subsidye shall bee made, the Rate Taxac&n Valuation and Estimac&n nowe remayninge of Recorde in yo' Ma" Courte of Exchequer for the payment of perpetuall Disme or Tenthe graunted to yo' Ma*‘" moste Noble Father in the syxe and twentithe yere of his Raigne concerninge suche Promoc&ns as nowe be in the Possession of the Cleargie or of any other not devided by any Acte of Parlyament, or otherwise alienated from the Possession of the Cleargye, shall onelye bee followed and observed, w^out makinge any Valuac&n Rate Taxac&n or Estimac&n other then in the saide Recorde

II.

The said Subsidy shall be levied by Spiritual Censures, or by Distress; and when paid by Farmers shall be allowed out of their Rents ; unless on express Covenant to the contrary.

III.

Subsidy upon Impropriations may be levied on the Farmers thereof.

CHAPTER XVI. (■)

An Act for the Queenes Ma"" most graciouse generall and free Pardon.

THE Queenes most Excellent Majestie well perceiving and understanding that her loving Subjects by manie and sundrie wayes and meanes have of late diversly offended against the good I.awes and Statutes of this her Highnesse Realme, and thereby are fallen into grievous Paynes Forfeytures and Penalties, out of which they cannot bee delivered but onely by her Majesties great Mercie; and withall, considering that Justice and Mercie doe chiefely appertayne to her Princely Estate and Function to be delivered and distributed to her Subjects as occasion shall serve; and at this present, her Highnesse by Gods Providence, beeing rather inclined with Mercie and Clemencie to allure provoke and stirre her Subjects to live and continue in their due Obedience towards her Majestie then otherwise by severe Justice to correct them according to their Deserts and the Severitie of her Lawes; And having a speciall Trust and Confidence in her said loving Subjects, that they will from henceforth diligently applie and endevour themselves to serve her Majestie in all Obedience and due Observaunce of her Majesties Lawes, hath thought it convenient at this time with her Highenesse Free and Generali Pardon, to discharge her sayd Subjects of manie great Paines Forfeitures and Penalties wherewith they stand now charged and chargeable, by reason of their manifold Offences Disobedience and Contempts; And Therefore her Highnesse, of her most gratious Disposition, is contented and pleased that it bee enacted by the aucthoride of this presente Parliament, in manner and forme followinge, that is to say; That all and every her said Subjects, as well Spirituall as Temporall of this her Highnesse Realm of England, Wales, the Isles of Jernesey and Garnesey, and the Towne of Barwick, the Heires Successors Executors and Administrators of them and every of them, and all and singuler Bodies in any manner of wise corporated, Cities Boroughs Shires Ridings Hundreds Laths Rapes Wapentakes Townes Villages Hamlets and Tythings, and every of them, and the Successor and Successors of every of them, shalbe by the authority of this present Parliament acquitted pardoned released & discharged, against the Queenes Majesty her Heires & Successors and every of them, of all maner of Treasons Felonies Offences Contempts Trespasses Entries Wrongs Deceits Misdemeanors Forfeitures Penalties and Sums of Money, Paines of Death, Paines Corporal and pecuniary, and generally of all other Things Causes Quarrels Sutes Judgements and Executions, in this present Act hereafter not excepted nor foreprised, which may be or can be by her Highnesse in any wise or by any meanes pardoned, before and unto the first day of January last past in this present xxiij yeere of her most gracious Reigne, to every or any of her said Subjects Bodies Corporated Cities Boroughes Shires Ridings Hundreds Lathes Rapes Wapentakes Townes Villages & Tithings or any of them.

And also the Queenes Highnes is contented that it be enacted by the authority of this present Parliament, That her said free Pardon shalbe as good and effectuall in the Law to every of her said Subjects, Bodyes Corporate, and other before rehearsed, in for and against all Things which be not hereafter in this present Acte excepted

And yet neverthelesse whensoever the said persons or any of them shall willingly submit themselves in their obedience to her Majestie, and will come to the Church to heare Divine Service, and willingly refuse their said wilfull obstinacie, and conforme themselves in the said causes of Religion and Doctrine, and continue in such their conformity and due obedience to her Majestie, according as by the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme they ought to doe, then and from thenceforth all and every such person and persons so submitting and yeelding themselves in their due obedience towards her Majestie, and so continuing in the same shall forthwith be received and enabled by force of this Act to have and enjoy the full benefite of this generall Pardon as largely and fully in all respects as any other of her Majesties good Subjects have or ought to enjoyne by virtue of this Act: And also except out of this Pardon, all such persons as the last day of this present Session of Parliament be and remain as persons restrained from liberty in the custody of any other person or persons in her Highnesse expresse commandement for any Offence or Offences whatever: And also except all other persons which before the said last day of this Session of Parliament have bene are or hereafter shal be upon just cause impeached or accused of or for any such like Offence or Offences, wherewith those persons now restrained as aforesaid, be or shall be justly charged; And also all other Offences wherewith any of those persons so impeached or accused be or shall be justly charged : And also except all Offences committed or done by any person or persons contrary to the form and effect of the Statute made in the first yere of her Majesties Reign, touching the uniformity of Common Prayer and the Administration of Sacraments in the Church, and whereof any person or persons at any time since the twentieth day of June last past have bene or is lawfully indicted or convicted.

All Lands and Tenements within the County of the City of Exeter, heretofore partible between Heirs Males and Females, shall in future cease to be so partible, and shall be and become descendible according to the Course of the Common Law.

• There is a Duplicate Roll of this Year, the Introduction to which does not contain the List of ‘ Private Acts.’ Besides the Nineteen Acts in the Lists of Public Acts, and inrolled on both Rolls, which have always been printed as Chapters I. to XIX. of the Acts of this Session, Eleven others, Chapters XX. to XXX, have also been uniformly printed as part of the Statute: These latter Acts, not appearing on either of the Inrollments in Chancery, have been printed from the Original Acts in the Parliament Office. No Titles are entered in the Margins of the several Acts on either Roll} but it has been thought convenient to reprint the Titles in the above List at the Head of these Chapters. The Titles of the Acts printed from the Originals are from the Indorsements on the several Acts. The Act for the Government of Westminster («. 5. in the List of Private Acts,) is now first printed, from the Original Act; It is frequently referred to by subsequent Acts printed in all Collections of the Statutes. Neither this nor any others of the Private Acts are entered on either of the Inrollments. It will be seen that the Duplicate Roll agrees with the Original Acts, in the several Corrections suggested in the Notes.

CHAPTER I.

An Act for Provision to be made for the Suertie of the Queenes Majesties most Royall Person, and the continuaunce of the Realme in Peace.

FORASMUCH as the good Felicitie and Comforte of the whole Estate of this Realme consisteth (onely next under God) in the Suertie and Preservation of the Queenes most excellent Majestie; And for that it hath manifestly appeared that sondrie wicked Plottes and Meanes have of late bene devised and laide, aswell in forreine partes beyonde the Seas as also within this Realme, to the greate endangering of her Highnesse most Royall Person, and to the utter Ruine of the whole Common Weale, if by Godes mercifull Providence the same had not bene revealed : Therefore for preventing of suche greate Perrils as might hereafter otherwise growe, by the like detestable and devilish Practises, at the humble Seute and earnest Petition and Desier of the Loordes Spirituall and Temporal], and the Commons in this present Parliament assembled, and by the authoritie of the same Parliament, Be it enacted and ordeined. If at any tyme after the ende of this present Sessione of Parliament, any open Invasion or Rebellion shall be had or made into or within any of her Majesties Realmes or Dominions, or any Act attempted tending to the hurte of her Majesties most Royall Person, by or for any Person that shall or may pretende any Title to the Crowne of this Realme after her Majesties Decease; or if any thing shall be compassed or imagined, tending to the Hurte of her Majesties Royall Person, by any Person or with the Privitie of any Person that shall or may pretend Title to the Crowne of this Realme, That then by her Majesties Commission under her Great Seale, the Lordes and others of her Highnesse Previe Counsell, and such other Lordes of Parliament to be named by her Majestie as with the saide Privie Counsell shall make up the nomber of xxiiij at the leaste, having with them for theyr assistance in that Behalfe such of the Judges of the Courtes of Recorde at Westminster as her Highnesse shall for that purpose assigne and appointe, or the more parte of the same Counsell Lordes and Judges, shall by vertue of this Acte have authoritie to examine all and everie the Offences aforesaide, and all circumstances theirof, and thereupon to geve Sentence or Judgement as upon good prose the Matter shall appeare unto them : And that after such Sentence or Judgement given, and Declaration thereof made & published by her Majesties Proclamation under the Great Seale of Englande, all Persons, against whome *uch Sentence or Judgement shall be so given and published, shall be excluded and

dishabled for ever to have or clame, or to pretende to have or clame, the Crowne of this Realme, or of any her Majesties Dominons; Anye former [Lawes 1 ] or Statute whatsoever to the contrarie in any wise notwithstanding: And that thereupon all her Highnesse Subjectes shall and maie lawfully, by vertue of this Acte and her Majesties Direction in that Behaulfe, by all forcible and possible Meanes pursue to Death everie of such wicked Person, by whome or by whose Meanes Assent or Previtie any such Invasion or Rebellion shall be in forme aforesayde denounced to have bene made, or such wicked Act attempted, or other Thing compassed or imagined against her Majesties Person, and all their Aydours Comfortours and Abettours: And if any such detestable Act shall bee executed against her Highnesse most Royall Person whereby her Majesties Life shall bee taken away, (which God of his great Mercie forbid,) That then everie such person by or for whome any such Act shall be executed, and their Issues being any wise assenting or previe to the same, shall by vertue of this Acte be excluded and dishabled for ever to have or claime, or to pretend to have or claime, the saide Crowne of this Realme or of any other her Highnes Dominions; Any former Lawe or Statute whatsoever to the contrary in any wise notwithstanding : And that all y* Subjects of this Realme and all other her Majesties Dominions shall and may lawfully, by vertue of this Acte, by all forcible and possible Meanes pursue to Death every such wicked Person by whome or by whose Meanes any such detestable Fact shall be in forme hearafter expressed denounced to have bene committed, and also their Yssues being any way assenting or privie to the same, and all their Aydours Comforters and Abettours in that Behalfe.

And to the end that the Intention of this Lawe may be effectually executed, if her Majesties Life shall be taken away by any violent or unnatural Meanes, (which God defend) : Be it further enacted by the authoritie aforesaid. That the Lords and others which shall be of her Majesties Previe Counsell at the tyme of such her Decease, or the more parte of the same Counsell, joyning unto them for their better Assistance five other Earles and seavene other Lordes of Parliament at the least, (foreseeing that none of the saide Earles Lordes or Counsell be knowne to be persons that maye make any Title to the Crowne,) those persons which were chiefe Justices of everie Benche Master of the Rolles and Chiefe Baron of the Exchequer at the tyme of her Majesties Death, or in default of the saide Justices Master of the Rolles and Chiefe Baron, some other of those which were Justices of some of the Courtes of Recorde at Westminster at the tyme of her Highnesse Decease to supply their places, or any xxiiij or more of them, whereof eyght to be Lordes of Parliament not being of the Previe Councell, shall to the uttermoste of theire Power and Skill examine the cause and mannor of such her Majesties Death, and what Persons shall be any waye giltie thereof, and all circomstances concerning the same, according to the true meaning of this Act; and thereupon shall by open Proclamation publish the same, and without any delay by all forcible and possible Meanes prossecute to Death all such as shall be founde to be Offendoures therein, and all theire Aydours and Abettours; And for the doing thereof, and for the withstanding and suppressing of all such Power and Force as shall any way be levyed or stirred in disturbance of the deue execution of this Lawe, shall by vertue of this Act have Power and Authoritie not onely to rayse and use such Forces as shall in that behalfe bee needefull and conveniente, but also to use all other Meanes & Thing? possible and necessarie for the Mayntenance of the same Forces and prosecution of the saide Offendours; And if any such Power and Force shall be levyed or stirred in disturbaunce of (*) due execution of this Lawe, by any Person that shall or may pretende any Tytle to the Crowne of this Realme, whereby this Lawe in all Thinges maye not be fully executed according to the effecte and true meaning of the same, that then everye suche person shall by vertue of this Act, be therefore excluded and dishabled for ever to have or clame, or to pretende to have or clame, the Crowne of this Realme, or of any other her Highnesse Dominions; Any former Lawe or Statute whatsoever to the contrayry notwithstanding.

And be it further enacted by the authoritie aforsaid, That all and everie the Subjectes of all her Majesties Realmes and Dominions, shall to the uttermost of theire Power aid and assist the saide Councell, and all other the Lordes and other persons to be ajoyned unto them for assistance as is aforesaicle, in all Thinges to be donn and executed according to the Effecte and Intention of this Lawe : And that noe Subject of this Realme shall in any wise bee impechid in Bodie Landes or Goodes at any tyme hereafter, for any Thinge to be done or executed according to the Tenour of this Lawe; Any Lawe or Statute heretofore made to the contrarie in any wise notwithstanding.

And Whereas of late many of her Majesties good and foithfull Subjectes have, in the name of God and with the testimonie of good Consciences, by one uniforme maner of writinge under their Handes and Seales, and by there severall Othes voluntariely taken, joyned themselves together in one Bonde and Association, to withstande and revenge to the uttermost all such malicious Acctions and Attemptes againste her Majesties most Royall Person : Nowe for the full explayning of all such Ambiguities and Questiones as otherwyse might happen to growe, by reason of any senester or wrong Construccion or Interpretation to be made or inferred of or uppon the Wordes or Meaning thereof. Be it declarede and enacted by the Aucthoritie of this present Parliament, That the same Association, and everie Article and Sentence therein conteyned, aswell concerning the disallowing excluding or dishabling of any Person that may or shall pretende any Title to come to the Crowne of this Realme, and also for the pursuing and taking reveng of any Person for any such wicked Acte or Attempt as is mentioned in the same Association, shall and ought to be in all Thinges expounded and adjudged according to the true Interne and Meaning of this Acte, and not otherwise nor against any other Person or Persons.

and may with their Abettors, &c. be pursued to Death by all Subjects;

and, in case of the Queen’s Death, the Party causing the same shall be excluded, and pursued to Death.

II.

In case of the violent Death of the Queen, the Privy Council, See. shall, on Examination, proclaim the guilty Parties, and use force in pursuing them to Death ; and all who resist the Execution of this Law shall be excluded from the Crown.

III.

All Subjects shall assist the Privy Council, and shall not be therefore impeached, in Body Lands or Goods.

IV.

Associations in Defence of her Majesty's Person and Title, declared consonant to this present Act.

CHAPTER IL

An Act againste Jesuites Semynarie Priestes and such other like disobedient Persons.

WHEREAS divers Persons called or professed Jesuites Seminarie Priestes and other Priestes, which have bene and from tyme to tyme are made in the Partes beyonde the Seas, by or according to the Order and Rietes of the Romishe Church, have of late yeres comen and bene sent, and dayly doe come and are sente, into this Realme of Englande and other the Queenes Majesties Dominions, of Purpose, (as hath a] peared aswell by sundrie of their owne Examinations and Confessions as by divers other manifest meanes and proofes,) not onely to withdrawe her Highnesse Subjectes from their due obedience to her Majestic, but also to stire up and move Sedition Rebellion and open Hostilitie within (* ) her Highnesse Realmes and Dominions, to the greate [daungering * ] of the safetie of her most Royall Person, and to the utter Rube Desolation and Overthrow of the whole Realme, if the same bee not the sooner by some good meanes foreseene and prevented: For Reformation whereof be it ordeyned established and enacted by the Queenes most excellent Majestie, and the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Commons b this presente Parliament assembled and by the authoritie of the same Parliamente, That all and everie Jesuites Sembarie Priestes and other Priestes whatsoever, made or ordeyned out of the Realme of Englande or other her Highnesse Dominions or within any of her Majesties Realmes or Dominions by any Authoritie Power or Jurisdiction derived chalenged or pretended [forme3] the Sea of Rome, sence the Feast of the Nativitie of Sabt John Baptist, b the first yeere of her Highnesse Reigne, shall within sortie dayes next after the ende of this presente Session of Parliament depart out of this Realme of England, and out of all other her Highnesse Realmes and Dominions, if the Winde Weather and Passage shall serve for the same; or els soe soone after the ende of the saide fourtie dayes, as the Wbde Weather and Passage shall so serve.

And be it further enacted by the authoritie aforsaide, That it shall not be lawfull to or for any Jesuite Sembarie Priest or other such Priest Deacon or [any *] Religious or Ecclesiasticall Person whatsoever, being borne within this Realme or any other her Highnesse Dominions, and heretofore sence the saide Feast of the Nativitie of Saint John Baptist b the first yeere of her Majesties Reigne made ordeyned or professed, or herafter to be made ordeyned or professed, by any Authoritie or Jurisdiction derived challenged or pretended from the Sea of Rome, by or of what name title or degree soever the same shall bee called or knowne, to come into be or remayne b any parte of this Realme or any other her Highnesse Dominions after the ende of the same sortie dayes, other then in such speciall cases, and upon such speciall occasions onely, and for such time onely as is expressed in this Acte; and if hee doe, that then everie such Offence shall be taken and adjudged to be High Treason; And everie person soe offending shall for his Offence be adjudged a Tray for, and shall suffer lose & forfaite as in case of High Treason: And everie person which after the ende of the same sortie dayes, and after such tyme of departure as is before limited and appointed, shall wittingly and willingly receive relieve comfort aide or mainteyne any such Jesuite Seminarie Priest or other Priest Deacon or Religious or Ecclesiasticall Person as is aforesaide, being at libertie or out of holde, knowing him to be a Jesuite Seminarie Priest or other such Priest Deacon or Religious or Ecclesiasticall Person as is aibresaide, shall also for such Offence be adjudged a Fellone without Benefite of Clergie, and suffer Death, lose and forfaite as in [cause5 ] of one attainted of Felonie.

And be it further enacted by the authoritie aforesaide, If any of her Majesties Subjectes, (not bebg a Jesuite Seminarie Priest or other such Priest Deacon or Religious or Ecclesiasticall person as is before mencioned,) nowe bebg or which hereafter shall be o or brought up in any Colledge of Jesuites or Sembarie, alreadie erected or ordeyned or hereafter to be erected or ordeyned in the Partes beyonde the Seas or out of this Realme in any forrabe partes, shall not, within Sixe Moneths next after Proclamation in that behalfe to bee made in the Cittie of London under the Greate Seale of England, retume into this Realme, and therupon, within two dayes next after such Retume, before the Bishop of the Dioces or Two Justices of Peace of the Countie where he shall arrive, submit himeselfe to her Majestie and her Lawes, and take the Othe set foorth by Act b the first yeere of her Reigne; that then every such person which shall otherwise retume come bto or be b this Realme or any other her Highnesse Dominions, for such Offence of returning or bebg b this Realme or any other her Highnesse Dominions, without Submission as aforesaide, shall also be adjudged a Tray tour, and suffer lose and forfeite as in case of High Treason.

And be yt further enacted by the authoritie aforesaide, If any Parson under her Majesties Subjection or Obedience shall at any time after the ende of the saide fourtie dayes, by way of Exchange or by any other shift way or meanes whatsoever, wittingly and willbgly, eyther directly or indirectly, convey delever or sende or cause or procure to be conveyed or delivered to be sent, over the Seas or out of this Realme, or out of any other her Majesties Dominions or Territories bto any forrabe Partes, or shall otherwise wittingly and willbgly yeeld give or contribute any Money or other Reliefe, to or for any Jesuite Seminarie Preist or such other Priest Deacon or Religious or Ecclesiasticall Person as is aforesaid, or to or for the Maintenance or Releife of any Colledge of Jesuites or Seminarie, alreadie erected or ordebed or heareafter to be erected or ordeyned b any the partes beyonde the Seas or out of this Realme b any

Provided alwayes, yf it happen at any tyme hereafter, any Peere of this Realme to be indited of any Offence made Treason Felonie or Premunire by this Acte, that hee shall have his Triall by his Peeres as in other [causes*] of Treason Felonie or Premunire is accustomed.

Provided neverthelesse, and it is declared by authoritie aforesaide, That if any such Jesuite Seminarie Priest or other Priests abovesaide, shall fortune to be so weake or infirme of Body, that he or they may not passe out of the Realme by the tyme herein limited, without imminent danger of life, and this understoode as well by the corporall Othe of the partie as by other good meanes, unto the Bishop of the Dioces and two Justices of Peace of the same Countie where such person or persons doe dwell or abide ; that then and upon good and sufficient Band of the Person or Persons, with suirties of the somme of CC" at the least, with condition that he or they shall be of good behaviour towardes our Soveraigne Lady the Queene and all her liege people, then he or they so lycensed and doing as is aforesaide, shall and may remaine and be still within this Realme, without any losse or danger to fall on him or them by this Acte, for soe longe time as by the same Bishoppe and Justices shall be limitted and appointed, so as the same time of Abode excede not the space of Sixe Monethes at the most; and that no Person or Persons shall susteine any losse or incurre any danger by this Acte, for the receiving or mainteininge of any such Person or Persons so licensed as is aforesaid, for and duringe such time only as such Person or Persons shall be so licensed to tarry within this Realme; Any Thinge conteined in this Acte to the contrary notwithstanding.

And be it allso further enacted by aucthoritie aforesaid, That everie Person or Persons beinge Subject of this Realme, which after the said fourtie dayes shall know & understand that any such Jesuite Seminarie Priest or other Priest abovesaid, shall abide stay tarrie or be within this Realme or other the Queenes Dominions and Countries, contrarie to the true meaning of this Acte, and shall not discover the same unto some Justice of Peace or other higher Officer within twelve dayes next after his said knowledge, but willingly conceale his knowledge therein; that everie such Offender shall make Fine and be imprisoned at the Queenes pleasure: And that if such Justice of Peace or other such Officer to whome such matter shall be so discovered, do not within xxviij dayes then next following, give information thereof to some of the Queenes privie Counsell, or to the President or Vice President of the Queenes Counsell, established in the North or in die Marches of Wales for the time beinge, that then he or they so offending shall for everie such Offence forfaite the some of Two hundered Markes.

CHAPTER III.

An Act for the explanacion of the Statute made Anno xiij of the Queenes Majesties Reigne intituled, An Act to make the Landes Tenementes Goodes and Chattels of Tellors Receivors, &c. liable to the paiment of their Debtes.

WHERE in the Parliament holden at Westminster the seconde daye of April in the xiij yeere of the Reigne of our Soveraigne Lady Queene Elizabeth, there was amongst other Things an Acte made entituled An Acte to make the Landes Tenements Goods and Cattels of Tellors Receivers, &c. liable to pay their Debts ; upon which Acte some Doubte and Question hath bene moved, whether the Queenes Highnesse her Heires and Successors might for the Satisfaction of her and their Debtes and Farmes, by her or their Letters Patterns under the Great Seale of Engeland, make Sale of any the Landes Tenementes or Hereditaments, whereof her Highnes her Heires or Successors have Power or Authoritie to make Sale by vertue of the same Acte, after the Death of such Accomptant or Debtor as is mentioned in the said Acte, or where the Accompt of such Accomptant or Debtor was not or is not made, or his or their Debt knowen in the Life time of the same Accomptat or Debtor: For declarac&n and explaining whereof Be it declared and enacted by the aucthoritie of this present Parliament, That the said Acte and everie parte thereof, touching the Power given by that recited Acte unto her Highnesse her Heires and Successors, to make Sale of any the Lands Tenementes or Hereditaments by the same Acte limitted to be solde, is shall and ought to be expounded and extended aswell in case where the Sale is to be made after the Death of such Accomptant or Debtor as where it is to be made in his or their Life time: And allso aswell in case where the Accompte is made or the Debt knowen within viij yeeres after the Death of such Accomptant or Debtor, as where the same Accompt is made or Debt knowen in the Life time of the same Accomptant or Debtor; Any Ambiguitie or Question that hath risen or growen, or may arise or grow or be conceived upon the Letter of the same Acte, to the contrarie thereof in any wise notwithstanding.

Provided always and be it enacted by the authoritie aforesaide, That after the Death of such Accomptant and Debtor as is mentioned in the said recited Acte, and before such time as any the Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes disended unto the Heire of such Accomptant or Debtor, as Heire unto the same Accomptant or Debtor, shall be (1) as aforesaid, a Sire facias shall be awarded out of her Majesties Court of Exchequer unto the Sheriffe of thee Countie where any such Landes do lye, to garnish the same Heire to shew cause why the same Landes Tenements and Hereditamentes, so to him desended as aforesaide, shoulde not be put to sale for satisfaction of the sayd Debts or Fermes in the same Acte mentioned, according to the tenor of the saide Act; whereupon if the Heire do not within a convenient time, upon a Garnishment or two Nichils returned, shewe & prove unto the saide Court, that the Executors or Administrators of such Accomptant or Debtor have sufficient, which ought to answere or be liable for the same Debte or Farme, & whereby the said Debte or Farme shall and may be dulye and fully satisfied, that then after ten Moneths next after such two Nichils or Garnishment returned, the same Landes Tenements and Hereditaments shall be solde by her Majestie her Heires or Successors, and the Money thereof comminge disposed according to the true Intent and Meaning of the saide former recitede Acte.

And be it further enacted by the authoritie aforesaid, That the said recited Acte and this Statute of Explanation [and4] as touching onely the Sale of any Landes Tenementes or Hereditaments to be made after the Death of such Accomptant or Debtor as is aforesaid, shall not extend to any Landes Tenements or Hereditaments which any person or persons, not being privie or consenting unto any such Intent to defraude the Queenes Majestie her Heires or Successours as in the saide recited Acte is mentioned, nowe have or enjoy and have purchased or obteined.

Provided always and be it enacted, That this Acte or any Thing therein conteined, shall not extende to the Sale of the Landes Tenements or Hereditamentes of any such Heire or Heires, for or by reason of any Accompt Debt or Farme, whereof any such Debtor or Accomptant have or shall have a Quietus est or Discharge, in his or their Life time.

CHAPTER IV.

An Act against covenous and fraudulent Conveyaunces.

F)RASMUCH as not onely the Queenes most excellent Majestie, but also divers of her Highnes good and lovinge Subjectes and Bodies Politique and Corporate, after Conveiances obtained or to be obtained and Purchases mad or to be made of Landes Tenementes Leases Estates and Hereditamentes for Money or other good Considerations, may have incurre and receive great Losse and Prejudice, by reason of fraudulent and covenous Conveiances Estates Gittes Grauntes Charges & Limitations of Uses, heretofore made or hereafter to be made of in or out of Lands Tenementes or Hereditaments so purchased or to be purchased; which said Giftes Grauntes Charges Estates Uses and Conveiances were or heareafter shal be meant or intended, by the parties that so make the same, to be fraudulent & covenous, of purpose and entent to deceive such as have purchased or shall purchase the same, or els, by the secret entent of the Parties, the same be to their owne proper Use and at their fre Disposition,

CHAPTER V.

An Acte for the expedicion of Justice in Causes of Demurrers and Pleadinges.

FORASMUCH as excessive Charges and Expences, and greate delay and hinderance of Justice, hath growne in Actions and Suits betwene the Subjectes of this Realme, by reason that upon some smale mistakinge or wante of forme in pleading, Judgementes are often reversed by Writtes of Errour, and often times upon Demurrours in Lawe given otherwise then the Matter in Lawe and verie right of the cause doeth require; whereby the Parties are constrained eyther utterly to lose their right, or els after loung time and greate Trouble and Expences to renewe againe their Suites: For Remedy thereof, Be it enacted by the Queenes moste excelent Majestie the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Commouns in this present Parliament assembled, and by the authoritie of the same. That from henceforth after Demurrer joyned and entred in any Action or Suite in any Court of Recorde within this Realme, the Judges shall proceed and give Judgement, according as the verie right of the Cause & Matter in Lawe shall appeare unto them, without regarding any Imperfection Defect or Wante of forme, in any Writte Returne Plainte Declaration or other Pleading Procese or course ol Proceding whasoever, Excepte those only which the Partie demurringe shall specially and particularly set downe and expresse together with his Demurrer; And that no Judgement to be geven shall be reversed by any Writte of Error for any such Imperfection Defecte or Wante of Forme as is aforesaid, excepte such onely as is before excepted.

And be it further enacted, That after Demurrers joyned and entred, the Courte where the same shall be, shall and may by vertue of this Acte from time to time amende all and every such Imperfections Defects and wantes of forme as is before mentioned, other then those onely which the Partie demurring shall specially and particularly expresse and set downe together with his Demurrer as is aforesaide.

Provided alwayes and be it further enacted by the authoritie aforesaid. That this Acte or any thinge therein conteyned shall not extend to any Writte Declaration or Suite of Appeale of Felony or Murder, nor to any Indictment or Presentment of Felony Murder Treason or other Matter, nor to any Processe upon any of them, nor to any Writte Bill Action or Information upon any popular or penal! Statute; Any Thing aforesaid to the contrary notwithstanding.

CHAPTER VI.

An Act for the retuminge of sufficient Jurors and for the better Expedicion of Trialls.

FOR the retourninge of mor able and more sufficient Jurors for Trials to be hereafter had betweene partie and partie, and for Reformation of Abuses in Shriffes and other Ministers, who for Rewarde oftentimes doe spare at home the most able and sufficient Freeholders and returne the poorer and simpler sort least able to discerne the Causes in question, and most unable to beare the charges of Aparance and Attendances in such Cases; Be it ordained and enacted by authoritie of this present Parliainente, That in all Cases where any Jurours, to be retoumed for Triall of any Issue or Issues joyned in any of the Queenes Majesties Courtes of the Kings Bench Common Pleas and the Exchequer, or before Justices of Assise, by the Lawes of this Realme nowe in force ought to have state of Freehold in Landes Tenements or Hereditaments of the cleare yearely value of sortie shillinges, that in every such case the Jurours, that shall be retourned from and after the ende of this present Session of Parliament, shall every of them have Estate of Freeholde in Landes Tenementes or Hereditamentes to the cleere yeerely value of foure poundes at the least; and that the Wryttes of Venire facias which from and after the ende of this present Session of Parliament shall be awarded and directed for the impanelling of Juries in the cases aforesayde, shall be in this forme: Regina, 8rc. CHAPTER VUI.

An Act for Redresse of erronious Judgementes in the Courte comonly called The Kinges Benche.

FORASMUCH as erronious Judgementes given in the Courte called the Kinges Bench are only to be reformed by the High Courte of Parliamet, which Court of Parliament is not in these Dayes so often holden as in aundent time it hath bene, neither yet in respecte of greater Affaires of this Realme such erronious Judgements can be well considered of and determined during the time of the Parliamente, whereby the Subjects of this Realme are greatly hindered and delayed of Justice in such Cases: Be it therefore enacted by the authoritie of this present Parliament, That where any Judgment shall at any time hearafter be give in the said Court of the Kings Bench, in any Sute or Acrion of Debte Detinue Covenaunt Accompt Accion upon the Case Ejection Firme or Trespasse, first commenced or to bee first commenced there, other then such only where the Queenes Majestie shal be Partie, the Partie Plaintiffe or Defendant, against whom any such Judgement shal be given, may at his Election sue forth out of the Court of Chauncerie, a special Writ of Error, to be devised in the said Court of Chauncerie, directed to the Chiefe Justice of the said Court of the Kings Bench for the time being, commanding him to canse the said Record and all thinges conceminge the said Judgement, to be brought before the Justices of the Common Bench and the Barrons of Theschequer, into Theschequer Chamber, there to be examined by the said Justices of the Commoun Bench & Barrons aforesaid; which said Justices of the Common Bench [of1] such Barons of Theschequer as are of the Degree of the Coyfe, or Sixe of them at the least, by vertue of this present Acte, shall thereupon have full Power and Authoritie to examine all such Errors as shall be assigned or found in or upon any such Judgement; and thereupon to reverse or affirme the said Judgement as the Law shall require, other then for Errors to be assigned or founde for or conceminge the Jurisdiction of the said Court of Kings Bench, or for any want of forme in any Writt Retume Plaint Bill Declaration or other Pleading Processe Verdict or Procedinge whatsoever: And that after that the said Judgement shall be affirmed or reversed, the said Record, and all thinges concerning the same, shall be removed and brought backe into the said Court of the Kinges Bench, that such further Preceding may be thereupon aswell for execution as otherwise as shall apperteyne.

And be it further enacted, That such Reversall or Affirmacion of any such former Judgement, shall not be so finall but that the partie who findeth him greived therewith, shall and may sue in the High Court of Parliament for the further and due examination of the said Judgement in such sorte as is nowe used upon erroneous Judgements in the saide Courte of Kinges Bench.

CHAPTER IX.

An Act for Reformacion of Errors in Fynes and Recoveries in the xij Shieres of Wales, Towne and Countie of Haverforde West, with the Counties Palentine.

WHEREAS in the Parliament by Prorogation holden at Westminster in the xxiij yeere of her Majesties Raigne that nowe is, [On1 ] good and beneficial! Statute was made and ordeyned for the appeasinge of Suites, the avoyding of false Practises Deceites Devices and Misdemeanors, and for helping of Negligences and Misprisions of Clarkes and Officers, dangerous to Assurances of Mens Landes and Hereditamentes, entituled An Acte for the Reformation of Errours in Fynes and Recoveries; Forasmuch as the saide Statute, or sundrie good and necessarie Clauses and Partes thereof, doth not extend to Fines and Recoviries levied had and suffered in the xij Shires of Wales, that is to saye, Glamorgan Brecknocke Radnor Carmerthen Pembroke Cardigan Mountgotnerie Denbigh Flint Carnarvon Anglesey and Merionneth, the Towne and Countie of Haverfordwest, and the Counties Palantines of Chester Lancaster and Duresme: Bee it therefore enacted by our Soveraigne Laidie the Queenes most excellent Majestie the Lords Spirituall and Temporall and the Commons in this presente Parliament assembled and by the authoritie of the same. That everie Writ of Covenant, and other Writ whereupon any Fine heretofore hath bene levied or hereafter shalbe levied, the Returne therof, the Writ of Dedimus potestatem made for the acknowledging of any of the same Fines, the Returne thereof, the Concorde Note and Foote of everie such Fine, the Proclamacions made thereupon, and the Kings Silver, And also everie originall Writ of Entrye in the Post, or other Writ whereupon any common Recoverie hath bene suffered or heareafter shall be suffered or passed, the Writs of Summons Ad Warrantizandum, the Returnes of the saide Originals and Writts of Summons Ad Warrantizandum, and everie Warrant of Attoumey had or to bee had, aswell of everie Demandand and Tenant as [Vouche1], extant and remayning, or that shalbe extant and in beinge, in the Courts of Assises or Great Sessions within the said xij Shires of Wales, Towne and Countie of Haverfordwest, and Counties Palantines, or in the Custodie of the Officers to whome the Charge of keping thereof doth apperteine, may upon the Request or Election of any person or persons be inrolled in Rolles of Parchment, by such persons and for such Considerations as hereafter in this Acte shalbe mentioned ; And that the Inrollments of the same or any parte thereof, shalbe of as good force and validitie in Lawe to all intents respects and purposes, for so much of any of them so inrolled, as the same beinge extant and remayning were or ought by Lawe to be.

St. 23 Elis. c. j. for Amendment of Fine*, Jtc. not extending to Wale*, Clieiter, Lancaiter, or Durham;

Be it further enacted by the authoritie aforesaid, That no Fine, Proclamations upon Fines, or common Recoverie, heretofore had levied suffered or passed, or hereafter to be had levied suffered or passed, in any of the said xij Shires of Wales, Towne and Countie of Haverfordwest, or Counties Palantine, shalbe reversed or reversable by any Write of Errour for false or incongrue Latine, rasure, enterlininge, misentring of any Warrant of Attoumey or of any Proclamation, misretourninge or not returning of the Sherife, or other want of forme in Wordes, and not in Matter of Substance.

CHAPTER X.

An Act for the Continuaunce of a former Statute entituled An Act to redresse Disorders in edraon Informers upon penall Statutes, made in the xviij yere of the Queenes Majesties Reigne.

WHERE in the Parliament holden at Westminster the Eyght Day of Februarie in the xviij yere of the Raigne of our most gratious Soveraigne Ladie Queene Elizabeth, there was amongst others an Acte made entituled, An Acte to redresse Disorders in Common Informers upon penall Lawes, which Acte is to continue in force and effecte, but unto the ende of this Session of this presente Parliament : Forasmuch as the saide Acte is founde by Experience since the makinge of the same Acte to be very necessarie beneficiall and expedient for the Commonwealth, Be it therefore enacted by the authoritie of this present Parliamente, That the same Acte above remembred, and al and every the Branches Clauses and Provisions in the same conteined, shall remaine continue and be from hencefoorth in full force and effecte for ever.

CHAPTER XI.

An Act for the revivynge continuaunce explanation and perfectinge of divers Statutf.

■XT'THERE in the first Session of Parliament begune in the Citie of London the thirde day of November in V v the xxj yeere of the Raigne of our late Soveraigne Lord of famous Memorie Kinge Henry the Eight, and from thence adjourned and proroged to the Pallace of Westminster, an Acte or Statute was made intituled An Acte for the true making of Cables Halsers and Ropes : And where in the Parliament holden upon prorogation at Westminster the iiij day of Februarie in the xxiiij yeere of the Reigne of the said Kinge, one other Acte was then and there made intituled An Acte against kyllinge of younge Beastes called Weanelinges: And where in the Session of Parliament ended at Westminster the first day of Fabruary in the iiij yere of the Raigne of our late Soveraigne Lord Kinge Edwarde the Sixt, one Acte was made coceming the buyinge and selling of Rother Beastes and [Cattellf' ] : And also one other Acte was then and there likewise made, intituled An Acte for the buying and selling of Butter and Cheese : And where also in the Parliament begune at Westminster the xxiij day of Januarye in the first yeere of the Reigne of thee Queenes Majestie that nowe is, and ther continued by Prorogation untill the Disolution thereof, one Acte was then and there made, intituled An Acte for Preservation of Spawne and Frye of Fish : And where also in the first Session of the Parliament holden at Westminster the xij day of Januarie in the fifth yeere of her Highnesse Reigne, one Act was then and there made, intituled An Acte for the Maintenance and Encrease of Tillage : And one other Acte was then and there likewise mad, intituled An Acte for the avoyding of divers forraine Wares [mad*] by Handicraftes men beyond the Seas: And one other Acte for the Punishment of such persons as shoulde procure or committ any wilful! CHAPTER XII.

An Act for the swearinge of Under Sherifes and other Under Officers and Mynisters.

FORASMUCH as grievous Complaintes are many tymes made of the Misdemeanour and evill Behaviour of Under Sherifes, who oftentymes having to them committed by the High Sheriffe the whole or parte of the exercising and executing of the Office of the High Sheriffe, and not taking any Corporal Othe as the High Sheriffe doth for the executing and discharging of the same Office, doe therefore dailye and most injuriously through Corruption and Affection impanell Jurours, for the Queenes Majestie and betwixt Partie and Partie, to the greate losse damag and hinderance of divers her Majesties lovinge Subjectes of this Realme: Foe Reformation whereof, Be it enacted by the authoritie of this Parliament, That all and everie person and persons that, from and after the laste day of the Session of this present Parliament, shall be admited to or take upon him the execution of the Office of an Under Sheriffe in any Shire or Countie within this Realme of Englande, before he entermeddle with the use or exercise of the saide Office, shall receive and take a Corporall Othe upon the Holy Evangelistes, before the Justices of Assise or [on1 J of them, of the same Circuite wherein that Countie is whereof he shall be Under Sheriffe, or before the Custos Rotulorum, or two Justices of the Peace whereof one to be of the Quorum, of the saide Countie whereof he shall be Under Sheriffe as aforesaide, for and concerning the Supremacie, in such manner and fourme as that Othe is expressed and declared in one Acte of Parliamente made and ordeyned in the first yeere of the Raigne of our saide Soveraigne Ladie the Queenes Majestie; together with which Othe he shall in like sorte, before the same person or persons, receive and take [on1 ] other Corporall Othe as followeth ; (that is to say):—I A. B. shall not use or exercise the office of Under Sheriffe corruptly during the iyme that I shall remaine therein, neither shall or will accept receive or take by any Colour Meanes or Devise whatsoever, or consent to the taking of, any maner of Fee or Rewarde of any person or persons, for the impanelling or returning of any Inquest Jurie or Tales in any Court of Recorde for the

That every Bailife of Francheis, Deputie and Clarke of everie Sherif and Under Sheriffe, and every other person and persons, which after fourtie dayes after the end of this Session of Parliament shall have authoritie to take upon him to empanall or returne any Inquest Jurie or Tales, or to entermeddle with execution of Processe in any Court of Record, shall before he or they intermeddle with any further execution thereof, receive and take the Othes aforsaide corporally, before the person or persons appointed by this Acte to minister the same, or before the Head Officer of the Place, if it be a Towne Corporat, changeing only the Wordes, the Office of Under Sheriffe, contained in the Othe expressed in this Acte, to such Wordes as are convenient for the Deputation Office or Place in which the partie which taketh the Othe is to be exercised in; And if any the said persons limitted to take the Othe aforesaid, do take upon him to impanall or retume any Inquest Jurie or Tales, or to intermeddle with the execution of Processe, not having before taken the Othes aforesaid, that then every such person shall lose and forfait the summe of xl. poundes of currante Engelish Money; the one Moitie to be to the use of our Soveraigne Ladye the Queene, the other moytye to him or them that will sue for the same.

IV.

Penalty on Sheriffs, See. transgressing this Act, Treble Damages to Parties grieved.

And be it further enacted by the authoritie aforesaid, That if anye Under Sheriffe or other person mentioned in this Acte, or any of them, at any time and times from and after fourtie dayes next ensuinge the last day of this present Session of Parliament, shall doe or committe any Acte or Actes contrari to the Othes aforesaide, or either of them, or contrari to the true entent and meaninge of this Acte, that thein everie such person so offending shall forefaite and lose for everie such Offence to the partie or parties grieved his or their Treble Dammages ; All which severall Forfeitures before mentioned shall or may, by the authoritie of this present Acte, be recovered had and levied by Action of Debt Bill Plainte or Information in any of the Queenes Majesties Courtes of Recorde, in which Actions Suites Plaintes or Informations no Wager of Lawe Essoyne or Protection shall be allowed.

V.

Justices of Assize, &c. m*y determine Offences.

And be it further enacted by the authoritie aforesaid. That the Justices of Assise and Justices of Peace in there Open Sessions, shall have full Power, within the Limittes of their Authoritie, to heare and determine the Defaultes done contrary to this Acte, as well by Presentment and Information as Indittement; And upon Convictione of the Offendours to award Executione for the levie of the Forfeitures aforesaide by Firie Facias or by Attachement Capias or Exigendum.

CHAPTER XIII.

An Act for the followinge of Huye and Crye.

Recital of Statutes Wynton, 13 Ed. I. stat. 2. cc. 1, 2.; 28 Ed. III. c. 11. as to Hue and Cry and Insufficiencies thereof.

WHEREAS by two aundent Statutes, the one made in the Parliament holden at Winchester in the therteeneth yeere of the Rdgne of Kinge Edwarde the First, and the other in the eight and twentieth yeere of the Reigne of Kinge Edwarde the Thirde, it was for the better [expressing'] of Roberies and Felonies amongst other thinges enacted to this Effecte; That if the Countrey do not answere for the Bodies of suche Malefactors, that then the paine should be such, That is to wit, That the people dwellinge in the Countrey shalbe answerable for the Robberies done and the Dammages; so that the whole Hundered where the Robberie shalbe done, with the Franchises which are within the Precincte of the same Hundered, shall answer the Robberies done: And if the Robberie chaunce to be donne in the Devision of two Hundereds, that then both the Hundreds together, with the Franchises within the Precinct of them, shalbe answerable ; as in the saide two severall Statutes it doth more at lardg appeare: Forasmuch as the saide partes of the saide severall Statutes being of late dayes more commonly put in Execution then heretofore they have beene, are founde by Experience to be verie harde and extreeme to many of the Queenes Majesties good Subjectes, because by the same Statute they doe remaine charged with the penalties therein contained, notwithstanding ther unhabilitie to satisfie the same, and though they doe as muche as in reason might be required in pursuinge such Malefactours and Offendours, whereby both lardge scope of negligence is given to the Inhabitaunts and Resiaunts in other Hundreds and Counties not to prosecute the Huie and Crie made followed and brought unto them, by reason they are not chargeable for any portion of the Goodes robbed, nor with any Dammages in that behalfe geven ; and also great incoragement and [enbolding *j] is likewise given unto the Offendors to commite dayly more Fellonies and

And for that also the partie robbed, having Remedie by the aforesaid Statutes for the recovering of his Goodes robbed and Dammages against the Inhabitantes and Resiantes of the Hundered wherein the Robberie was committed, is many tymes negligent and careles in prosecuting and pursuing the saide Malefactors and Offenders: Our Soveraigne Lady the Queenes Majestie, not willing therefore that her people should be impoverished by any such paine or penaltie which should be hard or grievous to them, and having speciall Regarde to abate the power of Felons and to represse Felonies, doeth for Remedy hereof, with the Consent of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and of the Commons in this present Parliament assembled, and by the authoritie of the same Parliament, establish and enact. That the Inhabitauntes and Resiants of everie or any such Hundred (with the Franchises within the Precinct thereof) wherein Negligence Fault or Defecte of Pursuite and freshe Suite, after Huy and Crie made, shall happen to be from and after Fortie Dayes next after the ende of this present Session of Parliament, shall answere and satisfie the one moitie or halfe of all and everie such summe & summes of Mony and Dammages as shall, by force or vertue of the saide Statutes or either of them, be recovered or hade against or of the said Hundred, with the Franchises therein, in which any Robberie or Fellonie shall at any tyme hereafter be commited or done: And that the same moytie shall and may be recovered by Action of Debt Bill Plaint or Information in any of the Queenes Majesties Courtes of Recorde at Westminster, by and in the Name of the Clarke of the Peace for the tyme being of or in everie such Countie within this Realme where any such Robberie and Recoverie by the Partie or Parties robbed shalbe, without naming the Christian Name or Surname of the saide Clarke of the Peace; which moitie so recovered shalbe to the onely use and behoofe of the Inhabitants of the saide Hundred where any such Robberie or Fellonie shall be committed or done.

And be it further enacted by the authoritie aforesaide, That if any Clarke of the Peace, of or in any Countie within this Realme, shall at any time hereafter commence or preferre any such Suyte Action or Information, and shall after [them'] same so sued commenced or prefered, happen to die or to be remooved out of his Office, before Recoverie and Execution had, that yet no such Action Suyte Bill Plaint or Information, sued commenced or preferred, shall by such displacing or Death be abated discontinued or ended; but that it shall and may be lawfull to and for the Clerke of the Peace next succeeding in the said Countie to prosecute pursue and followe all and everie such Action Bill Plainte Sute and Information, for the Causes aforesaide so hanging and depending, in such maner and forme and to all Intentes and Purposes as that Clarke of Peace might have done which first commenced or preferred the said Sute Bill Plaint or Information.

And although the whole Hundered where such Robberies and Fellonies are committed, with the Liberties within the Precincte thereof, are by the saide two former Statutes charged with the answering to the Partie robbed his Damages; yet neverthelesse the Recoverie and Execution, by and for the Partie or Parties robbed, is had against one or a verie fewe persons of the saide Inhabitantes, and he and they so charged have not heretofore by Lawe had any meane or way to have any Contribution of or from the Residue of the saide Hundred where the saide Robberie is committed, to the greate Impoverishment of them against whome such Recoverie or Execution is had: For Remedie whereof Be it enacted by the authoritie aforesaid, That after Execution of Damages by the Partie or Parties so robbed had, it shall and may be lawfull (upon complainte made by the Partie or Parties soe charged) to and for two Justices of the Peace (whereof one to be of the Quorum,) of the same Countie, inhabiting within the saide Hundered or neare unto the same where any such Execution shall be had, to assesse and taxe ratebly and proportionably accordinge to their Discretions all and even the Townes Parishes Villages and Hamlets, aswell of the said Hundred where any such Robberie shall be committed as of the Liberties within the said Hundred, to and towardes an equall contribution to be had and made for the Releife of the said Inhabitant or Inhabitants, against whome the Partie or Parteis robbed before that time had his or their Executione : And that after such taxation made, the Constables Constable Hedboroughes or Hedborough of everie such Towne Parish Village and Hamlet, shall by vertue of this present Acte have full Power and Authoritie, within their severall Limittes, ratably and proportionably to taxe and assesse according to their Abilities everie Inhabitant and Dweller in everie such Towne Parish Villag and Hatnlet for and towards the paiment of such Taxation and Assessment as shalbe so made upon every such Towne Parish Village and Hamlet as aforsaide by the saide Justices ; And that if any Inhabitant of any such Towne Parish Village or Hamlet shall obstinatly refuse and denie to pay the said Taxation and Assessement, so by the said Constables Constable Hedboroughes or Hedborough taxed and assessed, that then it shall and may be lawful to and for the saide Constables and Hedboroughes and everie of them within their severall Limittes and Jurisdictions, to distreine all and everie person and persons so refusinge and denienge, by his or their Goodes and Chattells, and the same Destresse to sell and the Mony thereof comminge to retaine to the use aforesaid ; And if the Goodes or Chatels so distreined and sold shalbe of more Vallue then the said Taxation shall come unto, that then the Residue of thee saide Mony, over and above the saide Taxation, shalbe delivered unto the saide person or persons so distrained.

And be it further enacted, That all and everie the said Constables and Hedboroughes, after that they have within Con,ubI|^'||ul| their severall Limittes [or1] Jurisdictions levied and collectede there saide Rates and summes of Mony so taxed, shall within pay Money to ten dayes after such Collection, paie and deliver the same over unto the said Justices of Peace, or one of them, to the th^pai^o^to Use and Behoofe of the said Inhabitant or Inhabitantes for whom such Rate Taxation and Assessement shall be had or the Party to be made as aforesaide; which Mony so paied shall by the Justices or Justice so receiving the same be delivered over rcimburw<i-(upon request made) unto the saide Inhabitant or Inhabitantes to whose use the same was collected.

Provided also and be it further enacted by the authoririe aforesaide, That where any Robberie is or shall be herafter committed by two or a greater nomber of Malefactours, and that it hapen any one of the saide Offenders to be apprehended, by pursuite to be made accordinge to the saide former mentioned Lawes and Statutes or accordinge to this present Acte, that then and in such case no Hundred or Franchise shall in any wise incurre or fall into the Penalrie Lose or Forfeiture mentioned either in this present Acte or in any the saide former Statutes, although the Residue of the said Malefactours shall happen to escape, and (*) to be apprehended; Any Thinge in this Statute, or in the said former Statutes to the contrarie notwithstanding.

And be it further also enacted by the authoririe of this presente Parliament, That no person or persons that shall hereafter happen to be robbed, shall have or maintaine any Action, or take any Benefite by vertue of the saide Two mentioned Statutes, or either of them, except the saide person and persons so robbed shall, with as much convenient speede as may be, give Notice and Intelligence of the saide Fellonie or Robberie so committed, unto some of the Inhabitants of some Towne Village or Hamlet neare unto the Place where any such Robberie shall be committed; nor shall bring or have any Action, upon or by vertue of any the Statutes aforesaid, except he or they shall first within xx dayes next before such Action to be brought, be examined upon his or their corporall Othe, to be taken before some [[on1] Justice of the Peace of the Countie where the Robberie was committed, inhabiting within the same Hundered where the Robberie was committed or neere unto the same, whether he or they doe knowe the Parries that committed the said Robberie or any of them; And if upon such Examination it be confessed that he or they d :>e knowe the Parties that committed the said Robberie or any of them, that then hee or they so confessing shall, before Die said Action be commenced or brought, enter into sufficient Bond by Recognisance, before the saide Justice before whome the saide Examination is had, effectually to prosecute the same person and persons so knowen to have committed the saide Robberie, by Inditement or otherwyse, according to the due course of the Lawes of this Realme.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Act for revivynge of a former Statute for the true makinge of Maulte.

WHEREAS in the Parliament holden at Westminster upon Prorogation the fourth day of November in the Secound Yeere of the Reigne of the late King of most famous Memorie King Edwarde the Sixt, most deare Brother to our Soveraigne Ladie the Queenes Majesrie that nowe is, there was amongst other Thinges one good and necessarie Acte of Parliament made and established, intituled An Acte for the true makinge of Mault; which saide Statute was after discontinued, and so resteth and remaineth as yet, albeit in trueth during the continuance thereof the same did much good to the Comonwealth and so would it doe still if the same might be revived and stande in force as heretofore it hath done: In consideration whereof may it please her Highnesse, with the Consent of the Lordes Spiritual! and Temporall and the Commons in this preasent Parliament assembled, and by the authoririe of the same, That it may be enacted, That the saide former Acte and Statute above mentioned, and everie Branch Article and Proviso therein conteined, shalbe revived, and from henceeforth continue stande and endure in force and strength to all Intents Constructions and Purposes, and shall be observed and kept in all Thinges accordinge to the Tenor Effect and true Meaninge of the same; This Acte to continue for the time of Three Yeeres nowe next following, after the ende of this present Session of Parliament; and after the ende of the said Thre Yeeres, then to the End of the Parliament then next after following.
