WHEREAS divers Townes situate upon the Sea Coast3 in the Couties of Norfolke and Suffolk being Townes mainteined by fishinge, and have transported and brought very many Herringes and much Fish to the Citie of Yorke, to Boston Grimesbie and Kingeston upon Hull, and divers other Townes upon the North Coast of this Realme, whereby the North Countrey hath bene well served and at reasonable prices, till of late time that the said Coastmen of Suffolke and Norfolke and others weare set at libertie to transporte their Hearrings to what Realme or Kingdome they woulde, to sell at their pleasure without Subsidie or C.ustome paying to your Majestie; so that whereas they did yerely bringe to the Countie of York, and the said Citie of Yorke, to Boston Grimesbie and Kingston upon Hull, not Jesse then a thousande Lastes of White and Redde Herringes, withe greate quandtie of Salt Fishe, besides greate quandde of Fishe and Herrings they brought to divers Townes of the North Coast, wherewith Yorkeshiere Lyncolneshere Nottinghamshiere Derbieshier Cheshiere Lancashiere Cumberlande Westmerlande Northumberland and Bishopricke of Durham were well served with Herrings and Staple Fishe and at reasonable prices, and now they bringe none or a fewe; so that Herrings and Staple Fish is brought and growen to excessive prices, and wilbe greater, for that the saide Coastmen do shippe their reede Herrings to Sealande, & both Reed and White Herrings for Roane Nantes Rochell Burdeaulx and other Places in the Realme of Fraunce, and besides their transporting or shippinge a great nuber is shipped and transported by the Merchants for Portingale, and within the Straites of Marocko for Italie, so that the North partes of this Realme being farre from the Sea have greate scarcide of Fish and Herrings, and shall have greatter, unlese some present Remedie be had for the same: Therefore may it please your Majesde, that it may be enacted by the Lords Spirituall and Temporall and Commons of this present Parliament, That it may be lawful! for any of your Majesdes Subjects of this Realme, for servinge of the saide Counties and North parties, to bringe into this Realme from the partes beyonde the Seas, in English Shippes or Crayers beinge sailed by English Mariners with crosse Sailes, Herings Staple Fish and Linge Fish; as by the same Acte made in the fourth and fifth yeares of King Philip and Queene Mary, amongst divers Clauses Articles and Provisoes therein conteyned more plainely is expressed: Sithence the making of which sayde severall Statutes, although the Makers of the said Clothes have endevored themselves according to their best Skill and Industrie to perforate and fulfill the saide recited Statutes in everie of their Clothes, as much as in them did lie, as touching the Breadth of Clothes, and to that End and Purpose have allowed and doe allowe soe much Yarne and Stuffe to everie such Cloth as might sufficiendy serve to make all the saide Clothes full out in Length and Breadth according to the saide former Statute made in the fifth and sixth yeeres of King Edward the Sixt, and in waight according to the saide Branch of the saide Statute made in the fourth and fifth yeeres of the Reignes of the late King Philipe and Queene Marie: 1

Yet notwithstanding many tymes by reason of the divers Natures in the Wools and by the greate diversities in the Spinning Carding and Milling, many of the saide Clothes made within the said Counties of Wiltshire Gloucester Sommerset and Oxoii, and else where of lyke making, doe not containe full seaven quarters in Breadth, according to the said Statute made in the fifth and sixt yeeres of King Edward the Sixt, and yet doe holde their full Weight or more, according to the former Statute made in the tyme of the saide King Philipe and Queene Mary, and no default touching the Breadth can justly be imputed to the maker thereof, for that the said Clothmakers (as experience daily sheweth) cannot observe the saide former Statutes in all the said Cloths as touching the Breadth, although they endevour themselves never so much thereunto; which Clothes not conteining their full Assise in Breadth as is aforesaid, are many tymes taken and [sized'] by the Searchers of London, when they come to their Market at Blackwelhall, to the greate losse and dammage of the said Clothmakers, and to the greate hinderance of Clothmaking within the saide Countes: In Consideration whereof, albeit it is not hereby intended to repeale or make voyde the saide former recited Estatutes or either of them, otherwise then is hereafter expressed. Yet neverthelesse be it enacted by the Queenes most Excellent Majesde with the Assente of the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall, and the Commons of this present Parliament assembled, and by the Authoride of the same, That noe person or persons shall be hereafter chardged for any such Default, which hereafter shalbe in any of the said Clothes mendoned in this Acte, for want of breadth of Saven Quarters, so that the same Cloth doe conteine in breadth being throughly wet Six Quarters and a halfe at the leaste within the Lists, unwrought and listed according to the ancient Custome ; Any Thing in any of the saide former Statutes mendoned to the contrarie in any wise notwithstanding. Provided alwayes and he it enacted by the Authoride aforesaid, That if any of the saide Clothes shall not conteine Sixe Quarters and a haulfe at the least within the Lists as aforesaid, that then everie person offending in that behalfe shall, for everie such Cloth, be subject to such Paines Penalties and Forfeitures as were, by force of the former recited Statute of the fifth and sixt yeeres of King Edward the Sixt, to have bene forfeited for want of breadth of Seaven Quarters within the Lists.

And be it neverthelesse enacted by the Authoride aforesaide, That if any Cloth be made within any of the saide Counties, or els where of like making, called Narrowlisted Whites, being well scowred thicked milled and fully dried, shal conteine in weight any lesse then lxj ti. at the least, or if any Cloth to be made within any of the saide Counties, or els where of like making, called Broadlisted Whites, being well scowred thicked milled and fully dried, shal conteine in weight any lesse then lxiij ti. at the least; or if any of the saide Clothes called Narrowlisted or Broadlisted Whites, shall conteine in length any more than twentie and eight yardes at the moste, that then everie of the saide Clothiers therein offending shall incurre double such Penalties and Forfeitures, for everie pound so wanting of the severall weightes above limitted, and for everie yarde soe exceeding in length and not weighing after such Rate as is before expressed, as by the said Statute of the fourth and fifth yeeres of King Philip and Queene Mary is provid and appoynted.

This Acte to indure and continue for the space of Five yeeres next after the ende of this Session of this present Parliament, and from the ende of the said Five yeares untill the ende of the next Session of Parliament then next ensuing.

CHAPTER XVIII.

An Acte concerninge makinge of Wollen Clothes in the Counties of Devon and Cornewalle, called Plaine White Straightes and Pynned White Streightes.

WHERE in the Parliament upon Prorogation holden at Westminster the xxiij of Januarie in the fifth yeere of the Raigne of the late King of famous memorie Edward the Sixt, one Acte was made for true making of Woollen Clothes; By which Act amongst other thinges it was enacted, That from and after the Feast of Sainte Michaell the Archangell next ensuinge the makinge of the saide Acte no person or persons shoulde put any Heare Flockes or any Yame of Lambes Wool into any Cloth Carsey Frize or Cotton made ande solde or offered to be solde, as in the saide Acte is expressed; upon paine to forfaite every such Cloth Carsey Frize and Cotton wherein any such Yame Haire or Flocles shoulde be put, or the value of such Cloth Carsey Frize or Cotton; as by the saide Acte it doeth and may appeare: And Whereas by another Acte made in the Parliament holden at Westeminster in the seventh yeere of the Raigne of the saide late King, entituled An Acte for the making of plaine White Straightes and pinned White Straightes in Devon and Cornewall, the saide former Acte was altered, and [at1] libertie given to the Makers of the saide Clothes called plaine White Straightes and pinned White Straightes, to use in makinge of the saide Clothes Flocks Heare or Yeme made of Lambes Wool; and by the saide Statute divers Rules and Orders were appointed for making of the saide Clothes called plaine White Straightes and pinned White Straightes; as by the saide Statute doeth appeare : Nowe for that the Orders and Rules, both by the Statute made in the said fifte yeere as also in the seventh yere of the saide late King Edwarde the Sixt, tende to the utter undoinge and decay of great nombers and multitudes of People which live by the Trade of Clothinge, and are not profitable anie longer to be kepe in theis Countryes and Places where the said Cloths called plaine White Straightes and pinned White Straightes are usually made, the same Clothes beinge but a base and course

CHAPTER XIX.

An Act for the preservacion of Tymber in the Wildes of the Counties of Sussex Surrey and Kent, and for the Amendment of Highe Waies decaied by Carriage to and fro Iron Mylles there.

WHEREAS by the over great Negligence or nomber of Yron Workes, which have bene & yet are in the Wieldes of the Counties of Sussex Surrey and Kent, it is thought that the great Plentie of Timber which hath growne in those Partes have bene greatly decayed and spoyled, and will in short tyme be utterlie consumed and wasted, if some convenient Remedie therein be not tymely provided : Be it therefore enacted by our Soveraigne Ladie the Quenes Majestie the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Commons in this present Parliament assembled, and by the authoritie of the same. That noe person or persons, from and after the Feast of Easter next after the ende of this presente Session of Parliament, shall make erect build or newe set up, at or in any Place within the Countes of Sussex Surrey or Kent, or any of them, any maner of Yron Mills Fomace Finarie or Blomerie for the making or working of any maner of Iron or Iron Mettal, other then either upon such olde and former Bayes or Pennes whereupon hath lately bene or at the tyme of the new Erection shalbe then standing, som Yron Milles Fomace or Hammer, or els in and upon such Lande as the Partie or Parties, so erecting any such intended new Worke, shall continually furnish the same with sufficient supplie of his or their owne proper Woodes, standing or growing in and upon his or their owne proper Soile or Land, being to him or them in Fee Simple, Fee Taile, or for terme of Life or Lives without empeachement of Waste at the least, and not otherwise; nor shall converte or employ, or cause to be converted or employed, to Coales or other Fuell, for the making or working of Yron or Yron Mettall in or about any maner of Yron Milles Furnaces Hammer Finarie Forge or Blomarie, the bodie or bodies of any sound Timber Tree or Trees apt for the making of good and sufficiente Cleftwares or sawing Timber of Oake Ashe or Elme, growing of the breadth or bignesse of One Foote square at the Stubbe, or any parte of the same bodie or bodies of any such Tree or Trees ; upon paine of forfeiture for everie Yron Mille Fomace Forge Finarie or Blomarie, made erected builded or set up contrarie to the tenure and true meaning of this Acte, the summe of Thre Hundered Poundes, and for everie bodie of everie such Timber Tree, so employed or converted to Coale or other Fuell for the making or working of Yron as is aforesaid, the summe of Fourtie Shillings of lawfull Money of England; the one Halfe of which Forfeitures to bee to our Soveraigne Lady the Queenes Majestie her Heires and Successors, and the other halfe to him or them that will sue for the same by originall Writ Bill Plainte or Information, wherein no Essoyne Protection or Wager of Lawe shalbe admitted or allowed.

CHAPTER XX. (')

An Acte for prefvac&n of the Haven of Plymmowthe.

WHEREAS yo' Ma'f Towne of Plymowth in the Countie of Devon being an auncyent Borough Towne W ▼ bordering upon the meane Sea, yet havinge a pleasaunte and safe Harboroughe and Rode for Shipps within or nere the same, comonlye called Plymmowth Haven, wheare aswell yo' Ma'f Shippes as the Shipps and Vessells of dyvers yor Highnes Subjects, tradinge into forren Partes and from Porte to Porte .dthin this Realme, do often upon necessitie and otherwise arrive harboroughe refresshe and vittell themselfes, aswell w® fresshe Water being a thing verey necessarie for them, as withe divers other thinges, hathe for the moste parte of the yere none or at the leaste verey Iitle fresshe Water within a myle of the saide Towne or thereabowt, a Matter verey incomodiouse; By reason whereof yor Ma'f Shippes and the Shippes of yo' Highnes Subjects, arryveng and harbowring in the said Haven as is aforesaide, the Maryners of the same, are manye and often tymes dryven by necessytie to goe a Myle or more from the saide Towne and theire Shippes to fetche fresshe Water for theire necessarie uses: By reason whereof dyvers times they loste dyvers good Wyndes and Oportunyties whiche they might take benefite of, yf they mighte water themselfes nere theire Shippes ; besides the saide Towne being subjecte to fyer, aswell by the Enemye, (for the same was once burned by the Frenche in the tyme of Warre,) as by Negligence and other Mishappe at Home, there is no Water in or nerer the saide Towne for the moste parte of the yere (especiallie in the Sommer tyme when the Daungers bee greateste) then a Myle or sometime more, as the dryeth is: And wheare also the saide Haven of Plymowth, being one of the pryncipall Havens and Harboroughes of the West parts of Englande, dothe daylie querre & fill w,h the Sande of the Tynnewoorcks and Mynes nere adjoyneng to the same, and in shorte tyme wilbe utterlie decayed, yf some Redresse and speedie Remedie be not hadd : And wheare also there is a Water or Ryver within the saide Countie of Devon called the Water or Ryver of Mewe ais Meuye, distaunte from the saide Towne abowte Eight or Tenne Myles, parte of the whiche Water or Ryver w'b some Chardge wilbe brought into the saide Towne of Plymowth, withowt any greate Prejudice or Damage to anye Owner or Owners of any Lande throughe whiche the same shalbe conveied, by reason (the moste parte) in effecte all the same Lande is eyther barren and heathie, or elles hillye & drye Grounds, w61 wilbe bettered and amended by the Water that shalbe brought throughe the same; by bryngeng of whiche Water moste of the Incomodities and Daungers and divers others shall not onlie be remedied, but also some parte of the Chanell of the saide Haven scowred & cleansed by the same Ryver, to the ppetuall Contynew*unce of the same Haven, a Matter moaste beneficiall to the Realme : And wheare also the Inhabitauntf of the same Towne are incorporated by Kinge Henry the Sixte, by the name of The Maio' and Coialtie of Plymowth, whiche is confirmed by yo' Ma,ie and dyvers yor noble Progenito" Kings of this Realme : Maye it therefore please yo' moste excellent Matie of yor moaste noble and aboundant Grace and accustomed Favoure, that yt maye be Inacted by this present Pliament, That yt shalbe lawfull to & for the saide Mayo' and Coialtie, and to theire Successo", at all tymes after the Feaste of Easter nowe next comynge, to digge and myne a Ditche or Trench, conteynenge in Bredthe betwene sixe or seaven foote over in all places, throughe and over all the Lands and Grounds lyeng betwene the saide Towne of Plymmowth and anye parte of the saide River of Mewe als Meuye, and to digge myne breake bancke and cast upp all and all maner of Rockes Stones Gravell Sande and all other Lettf in anye Places or Groundes, for the convenyent or necessarie conveyenge of the same River to the saide Towne; and further from tyme to tyme to doe Repacon and make Weares Banckf and all other Things necessarie, whereby the saide River may be brought & contynewe unto the saide Towne, withowte lett denyall vexacttn or trooble of the Lord or Lords Owner or Owners of the same Grounde, or of any other pson or psons by Suyte in the Lawe or otherwyse, upon payne of xx ii. for everie tyme that they or anye of them do attempte the contrarie thereof; CHAPTER XXL (')

An Act for the preservation of Orforde Haven in the Countie of Suff.

FORASMUCHE as the Haven of Orforde in the Countie of Suff is greatelie shoulded and decaied, by the abuse of certeyne Stallboates and unlawfull Nettf, sett aswell in the saide Haven as also in a place called the Gull being a braunche of the saide Haven, whereby the greate destruction of the Frye of Fisshe there enseweth, by reason of the smallenes of the Maskes of suche Nettf as they use; and also the saide Haven and Gull, by the contynewall standinge of the saide Stalboates & usinge of the saide Nettf, the Course of the Tydes being thereby hyndered, so that the saide Haven and Gull w01 Sande Soyle Sulfe and Pyble Stones, are become of muche lesse depthe then heretofore they have ben, to the greate Pill of Shippes and Vessells usinge that Harboroughe, and likely to be muche more pilouse orells shelved upp, and so the use of the Haven and Gull to be utterlie loste, yf speedie Remedie be not herein provided: Be it therefore Inacted by o' SoPaigne Ladie the Quenes Ma*" the Lords Spuall and Temporall and w* Thassent of the Comons in this present Pliament assembled, and by the Authoritie of the same Pliament, That from the firste daye of Auguste nowe next enseweinge, yt shall not be lawfiill to anye maner of pson or psons whatsoever to sett anye Nett or Nettf, with anye Boate or Boates called a Stallboate or other Boate or Vessell

whatsoever, within the Entrie or Mowth of the saide Haven or in the saide Gull, excepte the Maske or Shale of

everie suche Net, throughowte the whole Nett, do conteyne twoe Inches and a halfe at the leaste in wydnes from knott to knott; upon payne to forfaicte for everie tyme that anye Nett or Nettf shalbe sett or placed in the saide Haven or Gull, not beinge of the Maske or Shale aforesaide, the some of Fyve Powndf of lawfull Englishe Moneye,

together w*1 the Nett or Nettf so sett or the value thereof; the one moytie whereof shalbe to the Queenes Ma1* her

Heires and Successo", and thother moytie to him or them that will sue for the same, in any of her Malf Courts of Recorde at Westm and not elsewheare, by Acc&n Bill Playnte or Informac&n, wherein no Essoyne Protection or Wager of Lawe shalbe admitted or allowed.

CHAPTER XXn. (*)

An Acte for the bringinge of the Haven of the Cittie of Chichester by a newe cut Channell to the Suburbes of

the same Cyttie.

WHEREAS the Cittie of Chichester in the Countie of Sussex ys a verie auncient Cyttie, holden by the Mayo' and Cittizens thereof in Fee Farme of the Quenes Ma,ie, and beinge scytuate nere the Sea Coaste, hath a verie say re Haven, whiche doth ebbe and stowe within one myle of the saide Cittie, whiche Haven is able to harbo' in saftie in extremitie of Tempest and fowle Weather on Flote at Lowe Water, a greate nomber of Shippf, and is therefore verie necessarie & comodious to all her Ma'f Subjects tradinge and travelinge the Seas by that Coaste, eyther in tyme of Warr or Peace, whether yt be to forreine Partes or within the Realme, in so muche that it is taken to be at this present the best Haven betwene Portesmowtlie and the Thames Mowthe; For the better maintenance of wch Haven and the ease of all Merchantf and others havinge accesse thereunto, the Maior and Cittizens of the saide Cittie, (who by the bountifulnes of her Mati" Progenito" likewise have and holde, togeather with the saide Cittie, the saide Haven Waterco'se and Streame theof, with divers other Royalties Liberties Priviledges and Customes thereunto belonginge and therbie arisinge to them and their Successors for ever,) have of longe tyme mainteyned, and yet to their greate Charges Costes and Expences do

C)

An Actb for the Clothyers of Boxsted in the County of Essex.

WHEREAS by a certayne Acte of Pliament begynneng at Westm the twentieth daye of Januarie in the iiijth and fyveth yeres of the Raignes of the late King Phillipp and Quene Marye, and theare contynued untill the seaventh daye of Marche in the saide fourthe and fiveth yeres of the Raignes of the saide late King and ^Juene, amongest other Things yt was Inacted, That from and after the firste daye of Maye then next followinge, no pson or psons whatsoever should use or exercise the Feate or Mysterie of making weavyng or roweing of Wollen Clothes, Longe or Shorte or Karsies, Playne Whites or Playne Streightes, to the Intent to put the same to Sale, but only in a Markett Towne wheare Clothe had contynually bene used to be made by the space of tenne yeres then laste paste, or in a Cyttie Borroughe or Towne Corporate, upon payne of Forfeiture, for everie suche Woollen Clothe or Karsie made woven or rowed owte of suche Cittie Borough Towne Corporate or Markett Towne, fyve pound f : And Wheare also yt is provided in the saide Acte that yt shalbe lawfull to any pson, then usinge or exercizeng the Feate or Mysterie of makinge weaving or roweing of Clothe or Karsie, to inhabite or dwell wheare they then did dwell, and theare to use the making weaving or roweng of Clothe or Karsie as he hathe heretofore; Any Thing in the saide Acte notw^standinge : And Wheare yt is further provided by the saide Acte, that yt shall be lawfull to all & everie pson or p6ons, whiche then did or after that tyme shoulde inhabite or dwell in anye of the Shires of Northwales Chesshier or Lanckashier, Woollen Clothe, owte of a Cyttie Boroughe or Markett Towne, as before they might have doon ; Any Thinge in the saide Acte to the contrarie notw^standinge: And Whereas by one other Acte begynneng at CHAPTER XXIX. (■)

An Acte of one entyer Subsidie and Twoe Fifteenes and Tenthes graunted by the Temporaltie.

MOSTE gratiowse Soveraigne; Having due Considerac&n (as in dutie Wee are bounde) of manye occasions of late yeres offered, and urgentlie constreynynge yow for defence of bothe yor Ma'f Realmes of England and Irelande, whereby great masse of yo' Ma'f Treasure hathe bene ymployed sythence the laste Contribuc&n by Parliament, and namely, in the Prosecuc&n of the Warres in Irelande ; the Chardges also yo' Ma,le hathe very lately susteyned in the repairynge and furnyshenge w*h all kynde of Munytion, the Castles and Fortes alongest the Sea Co6te, for the better w"standinge of forreyne Invasion, the necessary Provision for Store of all kynde of Munytions Powder and suche like, greater then in the tyme of anye of yor Ma'f Predecesso" hathe bene made ; And the greate porcon of Treasure that hathe bene also sythence the saide Pliament most providentlie and necessarilie ymployed in the preventinge of suche intended notoriouse Attemptf, as manyfestlie tended to the Disturbaunce, or rather to the overthrowenge of the present happie state of this yo' Highnes Realme, beinge suche (throughe the speciall goodnes of God and yor Ma"* provident Govemement) as in the tyme of no one of yor Ma'f Progenyto" hathe bene enjoyed; and wayeng also by 6ondrye things latelie discovered that the malice of the Enemyes of yor Ma'" and this Realme dothe not onlie continewe but daylie encrease, and therefore likelie that the saide Mallice wilbe accompanyed w'b moste daungerowse effects, unlesse the same may be by Gods Goodnes and some pollitique foresight prevented, whiche can in no wise be pformed withowt greate and inestmyable Chargf : Wee therefore yor Ma'f most humble loving and obedient Subjects shoulde shewe o'selves not only moste unthanckfull towards so gratiowse a Soveraigne under whome Wee have enjoyed so many and inestymable Benefytes, but also careles of o' owne safetie, yf Wee should not for the cawses above specyfied make offer unto yor Ma"' to yelde to the uttermoste of o’ power such a Contribucbn as the same woulde requyre; And therefore to shewe o'selves aswell thanckfull towards yo' Ma"*, as carefull to provyde that whiche may be for o' owne safetie. Do with all humylytie present unto yo' Highnes, a Subsidie and Twoe Fiftenes & Tenthes towards yo' Highnes greate Chardges: And for the better Assuraunce and levyeng of this o' smalle Contribuc&n of One Subsydie and Twoe Fyftenes and Tenthes, Wee yo' faithfull and obedient Subjects, doe moste humblie beseche yo' Made that yt maye bee enacted by the authoride of this present Pliament, in maner and forme followenge, that is to saye; That yo'Highnes shall have Twoe Fiftenes and Tenthes, to be paied taken and levied of the moveable Goods Cattails and other Things usuall to suche Fiftenes and Tenthes to be contributorie and chardgeable, within the Shieres Citdes Burroughes Townes and other Places of this yo' Majesties Realme, in maner and forme aforetyme used; Except the some of Twelve thowsande powndf thereof fullie to be deducted, that is to saye, Sixe thowsande powndf of either of the saide whole Fiftenes and Tenthes, in Relief Comforte and Dischardge of the poore Townes Cytties and Borroughes of this yo' saide Realme, wasted desolate or destroyed or overgreatly impoverished } after suche Rate as was and hathe afore this tyme ben had and made to everie Shier, and to be dyvided in suche maner and forme as heretofore for one whole Fiftene & Tenthe hath bene had and dyvided; And the saide Twoe Fiftenes and Tenthes (the Excepcon and Deduction aforesaide thereupon had deducted and allowed) to be paied in maner and forme following, That is to saye; The firste whole Fiftene and Tenthe (excepte before excepted) to be paid to your Highnes in the Receipte of yo' Highnes Eschequer, on or before the fowretenthe daye of June next comyng; And the saide seconde Fiftene and Tenthe (except before excepted) to be paid to yo' Highnes in the saide Receipte of yo' Exchequo', on or before the tenthe daye of Maye whiche shalbe in the yere of o' Lorde God One thowsande fyve hundreth fowrescore and syxe.

CHAPTER XXX. (')

An Act for the Queenes Majesties most gracious generall and free Pardon.

THE Quenes most Excellent Matk considering the greate Zeale and Affecc&n w"* her loving and obedient Subjects beare to her Highnes, as by manye wayes they have declared and shewed from tyme to tyme sithens the beginnyng of her Ma*f Reigne, and calling to her most gracius Remembraunce into howe manye Penalties and Daungers of her Highnes Lawes and Statutf sondry of her saide loving Subjects be fallen, from which they cannot anye waye be freed or delivered but by her Maf great Mercye; and considering with all that Mercye doth apperteigne to her Princelye Estate and Calling, to be distributed to her Subjects as occasion shall serve, aswell as Justice; and assuredlye trusting that from hensforthe her Highnes Subjects will endevor themselves to live in dewe Obedience, And according to her Highnes Lawes as they ought to doe : Her Malic ys theirfore mercifullye enclyned and moved to graunt and give unto her saide lovinge Sujectf, a generall free and bneficyall Pardon, and theirby to deliver her said Subjects from the Daungers Penalties and Forfeytures wherew,h they nowe stande charged or chargeable, and weh they have fallen into by reason of their manyfolde Offencf Disobedience and Contemptf : And therefore her Ma,k! ys well pleased and contented that yt be enacted by the aucthoritie of this pnt Parliament, in manner and forme following; That ys to saye. That all and everie the saide Subjects, aswell Spuall as Temporall, of this her Highnes Realme of England Wales the Isles of Jemsey and Gamesey and the Towne of Barwicke, the Heires Successo" Executors and

Administrators of them and everye of them, and all and singter Bodies in anye maner of w.’se corporated, Citties

Burroughes Shires Riedingf Hundredes Lathes Rapes Wapentakf Townes Villagf Hamlettf and Tiethingf, and everye of them, and the Successor and Succeseo" of everye of them, shalbe by the aucthoritie of this pnt Parliament acquieted pardoned released and dischardged against the Quenes' Matlc her Heires and Successors, and everye of them, of all manner of Treasons Fellonies Offences Contemptf Trespasses Entries Wrongs Deceiptf Misdemeaners Forfeitures Penalties and somes of Moneye paynes of Death, paynes corporall and pecuniarye, and generally of all other Things Causes Quarrellf Suetf Judgm'f and ExecucSns, in this present Acte hereafter not excepted nor foreprysed, wch may be or can be by her Highnes in anye wise or by anye meanes pardoned before and unto the firste daye

of November last past, in the six & twentethe yere of her most gracius Reigne, to everie or anye of her said

Subjects Bodies corporated Citties Boroughes Shires Ridingf Hundreds Lathes Rapes Wapentakes Townes Villagf and Tithingf, or anye of them.

And also the Quenes Highnes ys contented that yt be enacted by the aucthoritie of this pnt Parliament, That her said free Pardon shalbe as good and effectuall in the Lawe to every of her said Subjects Bodies Corporate and others

before rehersed in for and against all Things w4 be not hereafter in this present Acte excepted and foreprysed, as

the same Pardon shoulde have bene yf all Offencf Contemptf Forfeitures Causes Matters Suetf Quarrellf Judgementf Execucons Penalties, and all other Things not hereafter in this Acte excepted and foreprysed, had bene pticlerly singlerly spiallie and plainely named rehearsed and spiffed, and also pardoned by proper and expresse Wordes & Names, in their Kindes Natures and Quallities, by Wordes and Termes theirunto requisite to have bene put in and expressed in this pnt Acte of free Pardon; And that her said Subjects nor anye of them, nor the Heires Executo'* or Administrators of anye of them, nor of the said Bodies Corporate and other before named and rehearsed, nor anye of them, be nor shalbe sewed vexed or inquieted in their Bodies Goodes Cattellf Landes or Tenementf, for any manner of Matter Cause Contempt Misdemeaner Forfeiture Trespas Offence or anye other Thinge suffered done or comytted before the saide first daie of Novembre against her Highnes her Crowne Dignity Prerogative Lawes or Statutes, but onlye for such Matters Causes and Offencf as be rehearsed mentioned or in some wise towched in

the Exception of this pnt Acte hereafter mentioned to be foreprised and excepted and for none other; Anye Statute or

Provided allwaies and be yt enacted by the aucthoride aforesaide, That yt shall and maye be lawfiill to all and everye Clarke and other Officers of the Quenes Courtes, to awarde and make Wryttf of Capias Utlagaf, at the Suete of the Parde Playndeff, against suche parsons Owtlawed as be pardoned by this Acte, to the interne to compell the Defendaunte and Defendauntf to make answere to the Playndeff or Playnriefff at whose Sewt he or they were owtlawed; And that everye parson soe owtlawed shall sewe a Wrytt of Scire facias against the Parde or Parties at whose Suet he or they were soe owtlawed, before this Pardon in that Behalf shalbe allowed to him or them that soe ys owtlawed.

And except allso owt of this Pardon, all Offences comitted or done by anye person or persones in newe buyldinge devieding of Tenementes, takinge of Inmates, Newe Inclosures, and other Nusaunces in anye place within the Cittie of London and Subburbes of the same, or within three myeles of the saide Cittie, contrarye to the Lawe or anye her Majesties Proclamac&ns in that Behalf made.

XIV. Proviso for Outlawries on Ca. Sa.

And be yt further enacted, That this Acte of generall Pardon shall not in anye wiese extende to anye parson owtlawed uppon anye Writt of Capias ad satisfaciendum, untill such tyme as the person soe owtlawed shall satisfie or otherwiese agree with the partie at whose Suet the same parson was soe owtlawed or condempned.

CHAPTER XXXI. (■)

An Acte for the good Governement of the Cyttie or Burroughe of Westmynster, in the Cowntie of Midd.

F)RASMOCHE as by erection and newe buyldynge of dyvers Howses, & by the ptinge and dyvidynge of dyvers Tenementf within the Cyttie or Boroughe of Westmynster and the libties of the same. The people thereof are greatelie encreased, 8c beinge for the most parte withowte Trade or Mysterie, are become poore, and many of them gyven whollie to Vyce and Ydienes, lyvinge in contempte of all maner of Officers within the said* Cyttie, for that their power to correcte & reforme them is not so sufficient in Lawe as in that behalfe weare meete and requysite : Be it therefore ordeyned by the Quenes moaste excellent Ma,lc the Lordes Spuall and Temporall, and th* Comons in this present Pliament assembled, dnd by the Authoritie of the same, That the saide Cittie or Boroughe of Westm, the Libties Territories and Precynctf of the same, shalbe and for ever heareafter contynewe severed & divided as yt hathe bene accustomed into xij severall Dyvisions, to be called or knowen by the Names of Wardes ; the same to be and contynewe by suche Lymytes Meates and Dyvisions as heretofore hathe ben comonlie taken or knowen.

And for the better ordering and governement of the people inhabiting and being within all 8c everie the Ward? aforesaide, and for repressinge and rootinge owte of Vice theare used; Be it further ordeyned by the Authoritie aforesaide, That the Deane of the Collegiate Churche of S' Peeter of Westm or his Successo", or the Highe Stewarde there for the tyme being or his lawfull Deputie, shall upon Thursdaye in Ester Weeke nexte after the ende of this Session of Pliament, and so yerlie for ever hereafter, nomynate and electe xij sufficient psons being Merchauntf Artificers or Psons usinge an ye Trade of buyeng or sellinge w'‘‘in the said Cittie or Boroughe, or suche other psons as shalbe willinge thereunto 8c inhabitenge within the saide Cittie or Boroughe and the liberties of the same, whiche shalbe called by the Name of Burgeses ; unto the governement of everie whiche Burges one of the saide xij Wardes shalbe by the saide Deane and Highe Stewarde, or his lawfull Depute for the tyme beinge, appoynted and lymyted; whiche saide xij and everie of them shall accepte theire election, and shall contynewe in his saide Roome for one ycrc next enseweng, and so from yere to yere during his or theire naturall lyevcs, yf they shall so longe inhabite theare -, (Excepte for some Offence or Mysgovernement by them or any of them comytted, and unlesse for cawse reasonable proved, they shalbe displaced by the Deane of Westmynster or Highe Stewarde theare for the tyme beinge;) And yf anye pson or psons resiante and so nomynated shall refuse to accepte the saide Rome, he shall forfeyte the somme of Tenne Poundes, to the use of the Poore within the saide Cittie or Boroughe of Westmynster, and to be levied by the Bailief of the libties of the saide Deane and Chapter by waye of Distresse to be taken and justyfied to the use aforesaide : whiche said xij BurgesS and everie of them shall receave aswell the usuall Oathe of Supremacie, as also a corporall Oathe, to hym to be mynistred by the saide Highe Stewarde or his Deputie in open Courte, to doe and execute all things to them appoynted and authorised by this Acte.

And for the more aide and assistaunce to pforme that whiche by the true intent of this Statute is ment to be pformed; Be it

ordeyned by the Authoritie of this present Pliament, That the saide Deane or his Successo", or the saide Highe Stewarde or his lawfull Depute, w'h the saide xij Burgeses or the more parte of the said Burgeses, shall within tenne daies after the Election and

liberties thereof, being Merchauntf Artificers or usinge any Trade of buyinge or selling within the saide Cittie or Boroughe, or anye other being willing thereunto as aforesaide, to be Assistauntf to the saide xij Burgeses; And that they shall accepte the same Charge, upon payne of vti. to be levied of everie of them that shall refuse the saide Roome in forme aforesaide, to be ymployed as aforesaide; with like Oathes as is aforesaide, and shalbe called by the Names of Assistantf unto the saide xij Burgeses nomynated to the foresaide xij Wardes ; unto everie whiche saide Wardes one of the saide Assistauntf shalbe appoynted, for the Governement of the same w,h the saide Burgese: whiche saide xij Burgeses & the saide xij Assistauntf and everie twoe of them, within the severall Wards to them appoynted 8c lymyted, vz. everie Burges together w,h his Assistante, shall and maye by vertue thereof doe and deale in everie thinge & things as Aldermens Deputies in the Cittie of London lawfullie doe or maye doe; And everie of the saide xij Assistantf shall contynewe in theire saide Offyce for and duringe one whole yere then next ensewenge, yf they shall contynewe theire Habitac8n within the saide Cittie or Boroughe or liberties of the same : And yf any of the saide xij Burgeses or Assistantf shall happen to dye, or otherwise upon reasonable cawse to be removed or displaced from his saide Office, that then the saide Deane or his Successo", and the Highe Stewarde for the tyme beinge or his lawfull Depute, shall from tyme to tyme at their willes and pleasures, nomynate and appoynte any other meete liable pson or psons of like Estate Facultie and Qualitie as aforesaide, inhabitinge within the saide Cyttie or Buroughe 8c the liberties of the same, to supplie the place or places of suche of the saide Burgeses or Assistauntf as shall so dye or' be removed or displaced, and shall contynewe in the saide Roome untill the Thursdaie in Ester Weeke then next followinge ; And be yt further Inacted by the authoritie aforesaide, That the saide Deane and his Successor, or the Highe Stewarde or his lawfull Depute, for ever hereafter yerelie upon Thursdaye in Easter Weeke aforesaide, shall nomynate and appoynte twoe psons owte of the saide xij Burgeses to be called or knowen by the Name of the twoe Chief Burgeses, to contynewe in the Office for one yere then next followeng; whiche Office they and everie of them shall accepte, upon payne of x ti. aforesaide to be paied as aforesaide, and to be levied by waye of Distresse to the use aforesaide as is before lymyted.

And for due Reformaffin of the Inconvenyences 8c Disordres whiche shall or maye happen within the saide Cittie Burroughe or Libertie, Be yt ordeyned by the authoritie of this present Pliament, That aswell the saide Deane or his Successo", the Highe Stewarde aforesaide or his Deputie, as also the saide twoe Chief Burgeses, the other tenne Burgeses, or any sour or three of them whereof the said Deane Highe Stewarde or his Deputie or one of the saide twoe Chief Burgeses to be one, from tyme to tyme for ever hereafter to be appoynted during theire saide Office, shall and maye by vertue of this Acte within the saide Cittie or Burroughe, and the Liberties thereof, heare examyne determyne and punyshe, accordinge to the Lawes of this Realme or the lawdable 8c lawfull Custome of the Cittie of London, all Matters of Incontynences, comon Scoldf, and of Inmates, and comon Annoyaunces; and likewise that they shall have authoritie to comytt to prison suche psons as within the saide Cyttie shall offende against the Peace ; And thereof shall gyve notice within xxiiij'" bowres after, to some Justice of Peace within the Countie of Middlesex.

For the better Government of the City or Borough of Westminster,

It shall continue divided into Twelve Wards.

ii.

The Dean of Saint Peters Westminster, or the High Steward, shall yearly appoint I a Burgesses; one for each Ward.

To continue in Office, from Year to Year, during good Behaviour.

Penalty on refusing to accept the Office, a£io.

Burgesses shall take Oath of Office, and of Supremacy.

III.

Dean, or High Steward, and Burgesses, shall appoint 12 Assistants, yearly.

Penalty on refusing such Office, j£$.

Burgesses and Assistants shall have like Power as Aldermen's Deputies in London.

Appointment of Burgesses, See. in case of Vacancy during the Year.

IV.

Two of the Burgesses shall be appointed Chief Burgesses for each Year.

V.

Dean, or High Steward, Chief Burgesses, &c. empowered to hear and determine Cases of Nuisance, &c. and commit for Breach of the Peace.
